fdd61291-e9d2-50e6-9078-b7370d4dec42.name: Pilgrimage Church of the Scourged Saviour "in der Wies"  ("in the meadow")
fdd61291-e9d2-50e6-9078-b7370d4dec42.description: Embedded in the hilly landscape at the foot of a mountain named Trauchberg, the ensemble is comprised of the church building as well as the U-shaped priory building abutting the chancel. The latter served as living quarters for priests, pilgrim hospice and at the same time, as a summer residence of the abbot of Steingaden. The lay church, arranged in an oval central-plan with an interior processional ambulatory, connects to the chancel which is decorated with gilded Rocaille stucco and brightly coloured imitation of marble and is accompanied by galleries for noble persons. The two-storey pilgrimage altar soars in the chancel, integrated into the column architecture of the galleries. The arcaded zone of the predominantly frescoed vaults is decorated with a fully mature Rocaille stucco. This ornamental structure also forms the arches and windows of the architecture in a unique way which is due to the wooden construction of the vaults. This allows the vaults  to exhaust all rational rules to the extent that the arches in the chancel appear to sag in a statically absurd manner.
fdd61291-e9d2-50e6-9078-b7370d4dec42.short_description: With the so-called Wieskirche, embedded in the hilly landscape of upper Bavarian Alpine upland, the famous church builder and stuccoer Dominikus Zimmermann not only created a major work, but also the Rococo church par excellence, by capriciously making the light-filled architecture subject to the virtuous Rocaille stucco. Additionally, the vaults are decorated with delicately coloured frescoes done by the hand of his brother Johann Baptist.
fdd61291-e9d2-50e6-9078-b7370d4dec42.bibliography:
Bauer, H. and Rupprecht, B. (eds), *Corpus der barocken Deckenmalerei in Deutschland, Vol. 1: Freistaat Bayern, Regierungsbezirk Oberbayern. Die Landkreise Landsberg am Lech – Starnberg – Weilheim-Schongau*, Munich: Süddeutscher Verlag, 1976: 600–623.  
Harries, K., *The Bavarian Rococo Church: Between Faith and Aestheticism*, New Haven/London: Yale University Press, 1983: 94, 139–144.  
Hitchcock, Henry-Russell, *German Rococo: The Zimmermann Brothers*, London: Penguin, 1968: 68–78, 91, 94.  
Petzet, M. (ed), *Die Wies: Geschichte und Restaurierung* (Arbeitshefte des Bayerischen Landesamtes für Denkmalpflege 55), Munich: Lipp, 1992.  
Pörnbacher, H., *Die Wies: Wallfahrtskirche zum gegeißelten Heiland* (Kleine Kunstführer 1), 23rd revised edition, Regensburg: Schnell & Steiner, 2002.
fdd61291-e9d2-50e6-9078-b7370d4dec42.history: The reason for construction was a miraculous weeping of a processional statue embodying the Scourged Saviour, which is supposed to have taken place in the seclusion of Wies on 14 June 1738. As a result, the nearby Premonstratensian Abbey of Steingaden built a Chapel of Mercy which soon became too small because of the increased flux of pilgrims. Therefore, the architect and stuccoer Dominikus Zimmermann was commissioned to construct a spacious church. After the laying of the foundation stone on 10 July 1746, construction was staged in two phases. The first phase, up to 1749, was the chancel building, alone also functioning as a new Chapel of Mercy, together with the abutting priory building. Next was the lay church, designed as a central building, which was able to be consecrated on 1 September 1754.
fdd61291-e9d2-50e6-9078-b7370d4dec42.patrons: Marian Mayr (gov. 1745–72) Abbot of the Premonstratensian Abbey of Steingaden
fdd61291-e9d2-50e6-9078-b7370d4dec42.author: Peter Heinrich Jahn

ff18d270-eb9c-5402-a699-82117263e1b6.name: *Navis nundinaria* (The trading ship)
ff18d270-eb9c-5402-a699-82117263e1b6.alternate_name: A ship-shaped theatre for the roast pork feast of 1657
ff18d270-eb9c-5402-a699-82117263e1b6.description:
The *Insignia degli Anziani Consoli*, bound in 16 volumes and housed in the Archivio di Stato Bologna, are documents on parchment. They were made every two months, from 1530 to 1796, to celebrate the eight Anziani Consoli and the Gonfaloniere di Giustizia, a group of magistrates ruling the city. From the end of the sixteenth-century, the names of the magistrates were depicted flanked by their coats of arms and a significant event that had taken place during the two months of their charge: an extraordinary visual chronicle illustrating more than two centuries of the city's history with six pictures a year.  
This picture (IV bimester of 1657) shows the stage for the roast pork feast. Celebrated every year on the 24th of August, a special installation was ssembled on the main square to host the feast of St. Bartholomew. In 1657 the theatre was shaped as a ship and was occupying nearly all the square, between the palace of the Podestà on the left and the stairs of the basilica of St. Petronius on the right. Along the sides of the ship were the stalls for the feast of the Assumption (from 15th to 24th August) that were going to become on the 24th boxes for the paying audience watching a theatrical representation and taking part in the traditional distribution of roast pork. On the mast waves the flag of the Municipality, under it a standard shows the coats of arms of Pope Alexander VII among those of the cardinal legate and of the archbishop of Bologna. On the aft deck a tent hosts the nine coats of arms of the Anziani Consoli and the Gonfaloniere of the bimester July-August 1657. On top right a Latin inscription in golden ink describes the picture and bears the names of the Anziani Consoli.
ff18d270-eb9c-5402-a699-82117263e1b6.short_description: This illumination represents a theatre in the shape of a ship that was built on the Main Square of Bologna for the feast of the roast pork in August 1657. This was an event that attracted a great number of people every year. The ship sails are the coats of arms of the nine families of the Anziani Consoli and the Gonfaloniere, who ruled Bologna in the bi-mester July-August 1657. On the left side of the ship, is the portico of the Palazzo del Podesta. In the background is the Pavaglione and the Palazzo dei Banchi.  The stairs on the right lead to the church of San Petronio.
ff18d270-eb9c-5402-a699-82117263e1b6.initial_owner: The Anziani Consoli of the town of Bologna
ff18d270-eb9c-5402-a699-82117263e1b6.method_for_datation: The date and the names of the magistrates are inscribed on the top right of the picture.
ff18d270-eb9c-5402-a699-82117263e1b6.obtention: This illumination, like the whole series, has always been housed in the archive of the Bolognese senate, inside the municipal palace. It was transferred to the Archivio di Stato in 1874, when it was created.

ff274184-f67a-583f-9714-b7a7b2f69739.name: Wardrobe
ff274184-f67a-583f-9714-b7a7b2f69739.description:
The massive body of this single-piece wardrobe – veneered, part carved, inlaid and gilded – closes with double doors. Each door has two central, shaped panels with mouldings and inlaid vegetal motifs. The doors –flanked by turned pillars – are supported on carved scrolls in darker wood. The wardrobe stands claw and ball feet, its base decorated with applied carved acanthus leaves, also in darker wood. The richly moulded cornice projections have a square crest above them topped by a fir cone, with facing carved scrolls of acanthus leaves in darker wood.  
The wardrobe, typical of the massive single-piece Baroque clothes presses of south German provenance, furnished the manor of the Counts Drašković from Bisag.
ff274184-f67a-583f-9714-b7a7b2f69739.short_description:
The design of this massive wardrobe with two inlaid-panel doors, twisted pillars and a carved crest is typical of late 17th-, early 18th-century south German production. The wardrobe furnished Bisag Manor in Hrvatsko prigorje, owned by a branch of the Counts Drašković. Jelisaveta Drašković, a descendant of this family that played a very important role in Croatian history, sold the wardrobe to the museum.  
The Germanisches Nationalmuseum in Nuremberg has an identical wardrobe.
ff274184-f67a-583f-9714-b7a7b2f69739.dimensions: H: 214 cm; w: 190 cm; d: 65 cm
ff274184-f67a-583f-9714-b7a7b2f69739.method_for_datation: From analysis of style and comparison with other examples in the available literature.
ff274184-f67a-583f-9714-b7a7b2f69739.provenance: Drašković family of Bisag Manor near Komin
ff274184-f67a-583f-9714-b7a7b2f69739.obtention: Purchased in 1935 from Jelisaveta Drašković (see above).

005e90ce-6216-5bb3-85d1-0c7504f54f18.name: *The triumphal entrance of Pope Paul III in Bologna*
005e90ce-6216-5bb3-85d1-0c7504f54f18.description: The fresco shows the procession of cardinals and knights escorting Pope Paul III Farnese to the Municipal Palace – represented in details in the background – during his stay in Bologna in 1543, before his meeting with the emperor Charles V in Busseto.

01e1c817-734d-5515-87fd-10abc3d72ece.name: Electors’ box with coat-of-arms
01e1c817-734d-5515-87fd-10abc3d72ece.description: The voluminous Elector’s (royal) box, supported by Atlantes-herms, stands out due to its opulent decoration. The box is crowned by putti and the personification of Fama (Fame) as an allegory of glory, surrounding the monogram of Elector Max III Joseph.
01e1c817-734d-5515-87fd-10abc3d72ece.location: Above the entrance on a level with the first and second tiers opposite the stage
01e1c817-734d-5515-87fd-10abc3d72ece.artist: François de Cuvilliés the Elder (1695–1786); Johann Baptist Straub (1704–1784)

022766ef-1e89-5e68-acd0-8d4e3a78cd8a.name: Façade
022766ef-1e89-5e68-acd0-8d4e3a78cd8a.description: The façade, as quite common in Late Baroque buildings in Tyrol, is designed with real architectural elements supplemented with wall paintings. In this case only the mouldings and gable of the cross-section façade are architecturally formed, while the pilasters, entablature, volutes, and window embellishments are painted. The façade’s central motif is an aedicule with a segmental arch above a round window interrupting the entablature. Above the arch the church patron is depicted, originally painted by Bergmüller and subsequently largely renewed.
022766ef-1e89-5e68-acd0-8d4e3a78cd8a.artist: Franz de Paula Penz (1707–1772); Johann Georg Bergmüller (1688–1762)

022c0120-b329-5b4d-8a2d-e8486d754ac9.name: *Angel*
022c0120-b329-5b4d-8a2d-e8486d754ac9.description: The angel rotating in a dance movement, the fluttering ends of the drapery and the idealised, mildly smiling youthful face, is a characteristic piece of the sculptural typology of Alexius Königer.
022c0120-b329-5b4d-8a2d-e8486d754ac9.location: Altar of the Holy Angels, alongside the north side of the triumphal arch
022c0120-b329-5b4d-8a2d-e8486d754ac9.artist: Sculptor: Alexius Königer (1732–1782); painter and gilder: Franz Kochler (active c. 1770s)

02670817-41d7-5797-a20d-2808406b0faa.name: *St. Jacob before God as intercessor for Innsbruck, Tyrol, the Diocese of Brixen and Austria*
02670817-41d7-5797-a20d-2808406b0faa.description: The fresco cycle from Cosmas Damian Asam has the work of the church’s patron saint as its theme. Asam painted illusionistic architecture in the shallow cupolas, a task which he solved differently in each scene. There are no references to real built architecture. In the centre of the perspectively exaggerated depiction a statue of the apostle can be seen. Supplicants from all estates are gathered around him, while Jacob implores God for heavenly assistance.
02670817-41d7-5797-a20d-2808406b0faa.artist: Cosmas Damian Asam (1686–1739); Egid Quirin Asam (1692–1750)

02c7cd31-a334-540d-862c-127ba23ad756.name: Triumphal Arch – detail
02c7cd31-a334-540d-862c-127ba23ad756.description: Basic shapes of the monument refer to Early Baroque architecture with elements of late Renaissance Classicism.

03acf1ee-9509-522b-a745-b53db94bb3d3.name: Celebration of the Premonstratensian Order
03acf1ee-9509-522b-a745-b53db94bb3d3.location:
Premonstratensian Monastery, Hradisko u Olomouce, Chapel of the Abbot  
Olomouc, Moravia, Czech Republic
03acf1ee-9509-522b-a745-b53db94bb3d3.artist: Jan Kryštof Handke (1694 Janovice near Rýmařov – 1774 Olomouc)

03dc4099-756e-55d8-96db-2447147a4e38.name: Noble Room or Room of Battles
03dc4099-756e-55d8-96db-2447147a4e38.description: The Noble Room – also know as the Room of the Battles – is decorated with figurative *azulejos* in blue and manganese depicting the major battles of the Restoration Wars (1641, 1653, 1658, 1659, 1663, 1665, and 1667). Ornamental stucco on the ceiling and walls includes portraits of the owners and celebrate the reacquired independence.
03dc4099-756e-55d8-96db-2447147a4e38.dates: Tiles: 1660–1670; stucco: last quarter of the 18th century

03f0276d-ea71-550e-87b2-3e9d039d58d4.name: Amor and Psyche – Garden
03f0276d-ea71-550e-87b2-3e9d039d58d4.description: During the first stage of the construction of the chateau a park, in the style of French Baroque gardens, was taking shape outside the west wing under the guidance of Dutch experts. The garden casino with Lanzani’s decoration and a fountain by Peter Wiliame, has not survived and only the romantic Chinese pavilion from the 1780s remains. In the mid-19th century the garden, covering 15 hectares, was simplified in the “English” style. A reconstruction in the 1970s partially restored the Baroque appearance of the chateau parterre with pools and fountains and re-installed the mythological and allegorical stone figures.

040b2846-3c5d-576f-85cf-a8f925d606cd.name: Virgin Mary with Child Handing the Order Gown to St. Norbert in the Presence of St. Augustine
040b2846-3c5d-576f-85cf-a8f925d606cd.description: This side altar altarpiece is typical of Leicher, Maulbertsch’s associate and frequent collaborator. The layout, colour scheme and movements of the figures in an S-shaped composition, reflect Maulbertsch’s expressive style although transposed to a softer, more lyrical outcome. The presence of St. Norbert, founder of the Premonstratensian order, refers to the “mother” monastery in Louka. The subject of the picture is the vision of St. Norbert in Prémontré when he saw the Virgin Mary, who gave her blessing to his intention to establish a monastery there, and handed him a white monastic gown.
040b2846-3c5d-576f-85cf-a8f925d606cd.location: Pilgrimage Church of the Scourged Saviour, Dyje, side altar

044291b5-0f3f-5107-908b-3ca119cae2b3.name: Pulpit
044291b5-0f3f-5107-908b-3ca119cae2b3.description: The stucco work, extremely sparse because of the dominant ceiling painting, was carried out by a well-known stuccoer from Wessobrunn, who was only able to reveal his talent as a modeller on the richly ornamental pulpit.
044291b5-0f3f-5107-908b-3ca119cae2b3.location: Right nave wall at the arch of the side chapel

04e7d116-c31a-51d8-ae35-d6c531209e4c.name: Leonhards Altar and Franz-Xaver Altar
04e7d116-c31a-51d8-ae35-d6c531209e4c.description: Two column-less side altars situated near the vestibule illustrate the important Holy Helpers to the rural population. By means of gestures, habits, and contemporary costumes, the multicoloured statues of Saint Notburga, Isidor, Pope Leo IV and Petrus Damiani, carved by Ignaz Günther, are based on folkloric popularity and contrast rural and spiritual status.
04e7d116-c31a-51d8-ae35-d6c531209e4c.artist: Altars and sculptures: Ignaz Günther (1725–75); Altar piece: Franz Anton Höttinger (1722–88)

0513e591-40c9-557a-989a-03bee71d8375.name: Red apartment
0513e591-40c9-557a-989a-03bee71d8375.description: The red living room hosts a bust of pope Benedict XIV, uncle of Carlotta Beroaldi, whose marriage to Francesco Tozzoni was the pretext for a complete renewal of the apartment.
0513e591-40c9-557a-989a-03bee71d8375.location: Palazzo Tozzoni, Imola, first floor, baroque apartment

056db7b3-89b9-5e48-919c-5e2963c5f874.name: Royal crypt with crucifixion group
056db7b3-89b9-5e48-919c-5e2963c5f874.description: Following its demolition in 1677 the crypt chapel of the Prince of Görz-Tyrol was rebuilt and set into the floor of the church so as not to obstruct the view; only the expressive crucifixion group above the crypt altar projects into the space of the church. The masterful craftsmanship of the royal crypt is a major work of the sculptor Andreas Thamasch, a student of Thomas Schwanthaler.

059edbc5-9442-564e-ae32-2efb3b02e0ba.name: Benediction Room
059edbc5-9442-564e-ae32-2efb3b02e0ba.description:
The Benediction Room at the centre of the royal palace appears to be part of the Basilica as it has the same polychrome marble decoration.  
It symbolises the divine origins of Absolute Kingship, to whose authority even the Church submitted. From this room over the Basilica, the Royal Family attended mass, and from the veranda (on the opposite side) opening onto the square, King João V blessed his subjects.
059edbc5-9442-564e-ae32-2efb3b02e0ba.location: In the middle of the Royal Palace

05f34f62-1bb1-5597-b198-6b8eb91197ca.name: Anna altar, high altar statues, baptismal font, Holy Virgin statue, side altars statues
05f34f62-1bb1-5597-b198-6b8eb91197ca.description:
The Anna altar on the left side of the entrance was originally in the former Anna cemetery chapel next to the church. It was created by Michael Zürn the younger, as well as the two statues of Joseph and Mary (originally not placed there) on both sides of the altar. He presumably even did the altar painting. The long and slim statues of St Elizabeth and St Zachariah on both sides of the main altar are also works by Michael Zürn the younger. In the 20th century they were placed in front of windows against strong backlight. This is why mostly only their silhouettes are recognizable.  
  
The baptismal font on the right side of the Anna altar, the remarkable Holy Virgin statue (opposite the pulpit) and the Saints Barbara and Margaret statues on the right side altar date from the 17th century. The two statues of St Peter and St Paul on the left side altar are from a later baroque period.
05f34f62-1bb1-5597-b198-6b8eb91197ca.dates: About 1690; baptismal font: 17th century; statues high altar – St Elizabeth and St Zachariah: about 1690; Holy Virgin statue: first third 17th century; St Barbara and St Margaret statues right side altar: end 17th century; St Peter and St Paul statues lef
05f34f62-1bb1-5597-b198-6b8eb91197ca.artist: Michael Zürn the younger: Anna altar, statues Anna altar, presumably paintings Anna altar and statues high altar (on the left and on the right side); unknown artists: other statues and baptismal font

073a3608-7fb8-5a06-99a1-807b858158d2.name: Chapel of Mercy, interior
073a3608-7fb8-5a06-99a1-807b858158d2.description: At the start of the comprehensive Baroque refurbishment work the master builder Gallus Gratl from Inzig erected a Chapel of Mercy on an oval ground plan at the site where, according to legend, herdsman worshipped the miracle-working image of the Virgin Mary, a small clothed statue of the Mother of God from the period around 1400. Piers with pilaster projections support a domical vault, interspersed with open semi-circular arches; in the cupola there is an oval opening. The Chapel of Mercy is thus to be understood as a homage to the Roman Pantheon which has been a Church of Mary since the 6th century.
073a3608-7fb8-5a06-99a1-807b858158d2.location: West nave, axial in the centre

078016a8-8f27-5a98-ac04-aec12f841ef0.name: The Four Last Things
078016a8-8f27-5a98-ac04-aec12f841ef0.description: Due to John of Nepomuk’s role as the patron saint of the sacrament of confession, the significance of penance is emphasized most notably by a grouping of four confessionals in the vestibule. Their dramatic array of sculptural depictions, being rich in gesture, pertain to the “Four Last Things”: death, judgement, Heaven and Hell. These are represented by the saints Bruno, Hieronymus and Peter, as well as by a beatified believer.
078016a8-8f27-5a98-ac04-aec12f841ef0.location: The partition wall between the vestibule and the nave, both sides above the confessionals.

0791adf8-6e5c-552e-86d8-28d9c5549585.name: Welcoming figure
0791adf8-6e5c-552e-86d8-28d9c5549585.description: Glazed cobalt-blue on white *azulejos* of a welcoming figure. The character wears typical early 18th-century livery, is unarmed, and adopts a reverential attitude, his hat in hand. It is likely that the figure represents a doorkeeper in the service of the Brotherhood.
0791adf8-6e5c-552e-86d8-28d9c5549585.location: Entrance patio at the top of the staircase
0791adf8-6e5c-552e-86d8-28d9c5549585.artist: Architect unknown. Tile-Painting Master P.M.P., probably Padre Manuel Pereira [n.d.]

07c6cafb-a885-50bc-aaa5-99e99c59c913.name: Rosary Altar and Ulrich Altar
07c6cafb-a885-50bc-aaa5-99e99c59c913.description: The two transept arms are predominated by impressive retable altars. The altarpieces were created by a Venetian muralist who was highly sought-after all over Europe and fortunately travelled through. The gifting of the rosary to the Dominican saints, St. Dominic and St. Catherine of Siena, was intended for the local Rosary Brotherhood; St. Ulrich embodies the patron saint of the diocese, waking the dead from their sleep.
07c6cafb-a885-50bc-aaa5-99e99c59c913.location: Transept arms of the monastery church
07c6cafb-a885-50bc-aaa5-99e99c59c913.artist: Altar designs: Johann Georg Fischer (1673–1747); Altarpieces: Giovanni Antonio Pellegrini (1675–1741)

0825097f-68cb-59cd-ad8a-060bcff7b3b5.name: Loggia and arcades
0825097f-68cb-59cd-ad8a-060bcff7b3b5.description: A scenographic view of the loggia shows different points of view obtained through the use of columns, balustrades and arcades. This is typical of the local baroque tradition.

0829f648-7c35-5554-838e-c975a5a23902.name: Ceiling frescos and painted stucco
0829f648-7c35-5554-838e-c975a5a23902.description: Albeit partly painted over and renewed, the ceiling paintings together with the “stucco finto” or painted stucco, form a uniform decorative system. Large rocaille cartouches frame picture panels forming a cycle depicting the Life of Mary (nave: Marriage, Annunciation and Assumption). The sweeping frames connect more than they divide, thus generating flowing transitions between architecture and picture panels.

082ba573-5349-5a5c-b779-c2ec96f62da5.name: General view of the interior: lateral retables
082ba573-5349-5a5c-b779-c2ec96f62da5.description: The lateral gilt wood retables incorporate paintings of the *Stigmatisation of Saint Francis*; *Education of the* *Virgin; Miracle of the Roses; Beatas Mafalda; Teresa and Sancha;* *Saint Michael the Archangel* and the *Assumption of the* *Virgin* by by André Gonçalves. The *Saint Joseph and Infant Jesus* is by André Rubira. The paintings date to around 1730.
082ba573-5349-5a5c-b779-c2ec96f62da5.artist: Architect: João Antunes (1642–1712) and others; Painters: André Gonçalves (1685–1762), André Rubira [n.d.]

082e020f-50f7-57d9-b997-b1311d906e63.name: Plan of the ground and first floors

08354b10-1797-50b3-80a2-2aabc67c1881.name: Church interior viewed from the choir
08354b10-1797-50b3-80a2-2aabc67c1881.description: Gilded woodcarving on the triumphal arch and main altar retable.
08354b10-1797-50b3-80a2-2aabc67c1881.artist: André Soares (1720–1769), Friar José de Santo António Vilaça (1731–1809) and others

086158b7-4dfb-51de-82de-73c1ff47b61f.name: *Assumption of the Virgin*
086158b7-4dfb-51de-82de-73c1ff47b61f.description: One of the first illusionist ceiling paintings in north Croatia, this is the work of the local painter, Blasius Grueber, whose naïve characters are typical of  the artist’s work. The charm and emotional impact of Grueber’s paintings is similar to that of local painters in Tyrol.

090e6d2b-c30e-5e24-add9-f351134c4094.name: *Niche with a flower vase*
090e6d2b-c30e-5e24-add9-f351134c4094.description: A vase with roses, irises and carnations.
090e6d2b-c30e-5e24-add9-f351134c4094.location: Palazzo Miti Zagnoni, first floor, hal of honour, ceiling, corner

091b9985-830d-5a24-aeb3-8b6403f919cf.name: St. Paulo Obelisk Fountain
091b9985-830d-5a24-aeb3-8b6403f919cf.description: From the Mãe d' Água das Amoreiras, a secondary aqueduct spreads out around the city terminating in fountains, many of them like this one still extant. Designed by Reinaldo Manuel dos Santos in 1774, it was not built until 1848, with minor adaptations by Malaquias Ferreira Leal.
091b9985-830d-5a24-aeb3-8b6403f919cf.artist: Design: Reinaldo Manuel dos Santos [n.d.]; adapted by Malaquias Ferreira Leal (1790–1855)

092d3c2e-305d-5a72-89a2-85afc05e6e72.name: *Allegory of Fortune, of Love and of the Four Seasons*
092d3c2e-305d-5a72-89a2-85afc05e6e72.description: Charged by Marc’Antonio Ranuzzi, Marc’Antonio Franceschini and the quadratura painter Enrico Haffner realized the allegorical figures in the ceiling of this room on the first floor of the palace, presumably between 1680 and 1681. Very interesting and original is the allegory in the centre of the vault showing Fortune and her wheel which, moved by the wind, holds Cupid in chains.
092d3c2e-305d-5a72-89a2-85afc05e6e72.location: Ceiling decoration of a room of the first floor of the palace, Palazzo Ranuzzi

093a2210-3ba8-5a5e-89a5-aa9844feba0c.name: Pulpit
093a2210-3ba8-5a5e-89a5-aa9844feba0c.description: The delightful Rococo pulpit in flowing forms, a miniature theatre backdrop, announces the universal claims of the Catholic Church. The open-work construction of the baldachin is crowned by Paul, Apostle to the Gentiles, with four putti symbolising the continents, on the pulpit itself are the personifications of the virtues Faith, Love and Hope as the heart of the Christian message of salvation.

0952e239-ee28-5d99-b908-2b46023f7747.name: High altar
0952e239-ee28-5d99-b908-2b46023f7747.description: The sculpted, distinctly vertical altar, symbolically shaped like a tongue, is placed within a tall arcade that reaches to the gallery on the second floor. Unlike many other constructions of its kind it does not dominate the church interior but symbolically enhances it. There is no ornamental decoration or painting. The building itself, created by matter and the work of light in space, is the sole bearer of meaning. Light is also symbolically divided in the space. In the bottom section the area is illuminated by candles, i.e. fire an earthly light, while on the first floor Divine Light enters the space through mirrors. The symbolic linking and oscillation of rays of light is portrayed in the ribbed walls of the first floor. The second floor and the top of the vaulting, where a symbol of the saint (epitomising a holy miracle) is found instead of the usual symbol of the Holy Spirit, are illuminated by pure light coming through the windows. Without a doubt this horizontal three-part approach also symbolises the Holy Trinity.

09607dac-467d-58f2-9e30-bfb495cee9b1.name: Music loft
09607dac-467d-58f2-9e30-bfb495cee9b1.description: The figurative decoration of the two-manual organ with 24 registers consists of 41 statues representing a celestial ensemble with period instruments.
09607dac-467d-58f2-9e30-bfb495cee9b1.artist: Johann Gottfried Halbich of Králíky, Anton Ricca

09ba891e-91e5-5442-9d3f-f13cb83f8280.name: Alcove
09ba891e-91e5-5442-9d3f-f13cb83f8280.description:
It was probably realised after 1704, surely before 1739, when it is mentioned in a biography dedicated to its author, the sculptor Giuseppe Mazza, here working together with the painter Ercole Graziani senior.  
Coming back from Venice, the artist was probably engaged by the Zaniboni family, owner of the palace, to create this superb nuptial bedroom lavishly decorated with stuccoes and sculptures (among them *Venus* and *Apollo,* allusive to abundance and fertility); every element contributes here to a very dynamic composition inspired by typically baroque concepts.

09d4586b-a36f-5788-ad3c-9a6bd66a0374.name: *Crowning of St. Gaetano*
09d4586b-a36f-5788-ad3c-9a6bd66a0374.description: The saint is lifted heavenwards by the angels. In ecstasy, with his arms open in a gesture of prayer, the saint receives the crown, the blue sash, the lilies and the pale blue scapular.

09e3df49-2f6c-5b50-818a-0273e7daf965.name: Baroque chimney system
09e3df49-2f6c-5b50-818a-0273e7daf965.description: The Baroque chimney system presents a unique approach to vent layout opening into five chimneys. They are also seen as an artwork comparable with modern artefacts.
09e3df49-2f6c-5b50-818a-0273e7daf965.artist: Johann Lucas von Hildebrandt (1668 Genoa – 1745 Vienna)

0a18b18c-28ba-5a3c-9fe9-43418b6ac604.name: Chancel and main altar decoration
0a18b18c-28ba-5a3c-9fe9-43418b6ac604.description: The front of the main altar is composed of ornate, multi-coloured marble and limestone inlay crowned by a phoenix. The *trompe l'œil* ceiling painting depicts the *Coronation of the Virgin*.
0a18b18c-28ba-5a3c-9fe9-43418b6ac604.artist: Design: Carlos Baptista Garvo; stone carvers: António Pereira, Vicente Soares, Manuel Rodrigues; painter: Luís Gonçalves de Sena [dates unknown]

0a72386e-7c5f-545b-9709-c7b0eb095d20.name: *The Creation of Adam*
0a72386e-7c5f-545b-9709-c7b0eb095d20.description: The first story of the cycle, to the left of the entrance represents the Creation of Man as the highest gesture of love of God.

0a801758-209c-55a6-8b1a-e135c565b0ad.name: *Last Supper*
0a801758-209c-55a6-8b1a-e135c565b0ad.description: The Franciscan Monastery in Virovitica accommodated several lay-brother painters, one of them being the Styrian lay-brother painter, Damian Bittner, who painted the *Last Supper* for the refectory together with his associates.

0ae494ef-cd06-5be1-a894-e8f72b874300.name: Holy Trinity Column
0ae494ef-cd06-5be1-a894-e8f72b874300.description: A hexagonal stepped base carries a trilateral concave pedestal the columns of which support a sculpture of God the Father, Christ in heaven, and a pyramid crowned with the symbol of the Holy Spirit on a radial halo. The statues of the Immaculata and the saints are by the court sculptor, Lengelacher, after the painter, A. J. Prenner. The bottom section features allegories of Love, Faith and Hope, and emblems of the patrons.
0ae494ef-cd06-5be1-a894-e8f72b874300.artist: Anton Josef Prenner (1683 Wallerstein – 1761 Wien) – Ignaz Lengelacher (1698 Unter Peissenberg – 1780 Baden)

0b61adbd-97ba-5469-bef9-1a7e071d3e4d.name: Miracle of the Loaves and Fishes
0b61adbd-97ba-5469-bef9-1a7e071d3e4d.description: The central representation space of the abbey, on a rectangular ground plan, has two fireplaces, over which are relief pictures relating to fire as one of nature’s elements, and biblical history (St. Paul Landing in Malta, St. Peter’s Three Denials of Christ). The sculpted decoration is dominated by Old Testament scenes: Samuel Meeting Saul and David Meeting Achimelech. Busts over the entrances represent the seasons of the year; reliefs in the windows portray allegories of the virtues and vices. “Real” architecture is supplemented by illusionary painting, with the subject of Christ at a Common Table culminating in the figure of Divine Providence with a cornucopia. The iconography of the hall – designed to host important guests such as the emperor and his wife – symbolises hospitality and at the same time moderation. Dining was the pivotal element of court ceremonies.
0b61adbd-97ba-5469-bef9-1a7e071d3e4d.location: Refectory, Premonstratensian Monastery, Hradisko u Olomouce
0b61adbd-97ba-5469-bef9-1a7e071d3e4d.artist: Paul Troger (1698 Zell bei Welsberg – 1762 Vienna)

0b97dc8a-3cf2-52e7-ae54-70cec9694c3e.name: Main Altar
0b97dc8a-3cf2-52e7-ae54-70cec9694c3e.description: Two pairs of columns flank the main altar on both sides. According to the church’s patrocinium, the figures of both Johns, the Evangelist and the Baptist, are positioned beside it and are among some of Franz Xaver Schmädl’s best works. In contrast, the altarpiece depicts the Crucifixion of Christ as the beginning of the divine work of salvation. The austere design of the columns around the altar stands in strong contrast to the capriciously arranged side altars, illustrating the hierarchical order between them.
0b97dc8a-3cf2-52e7-ae54-70cec9694c3e.artist: Altar: Thassilo Zöpf (1723–1807); Altarpiece: Johann Baptist Baader (1717–80); Sculptor: Franz Xaver Schmädl (1705–77)

0c30fb7d-3f55-524f-acdd-1883685cccae.name: Stucco ceiling
0c30fb7d-3f55-524f-acdd-1883685cccae.description: The stucco ceiling, presumably also from Gigl, displays slightly different motifs and ornamentation compared to the façades. The border area is composed of intricately intertwined bands with acanthus leaves; in the centre, framed by strap and vine scroll decoration, is a star composed of bands, leaves and shells. Above the entrance to the bay window the coat of arms of the Fischer family.
0c30fb7d-3f55-524f-acdd-1883685cccae.location: Corner room on the third floor (living quarters)

0ca8f01a-192f-5192-af7d-85d181189024.name: *St. Ignatius in Heavenly Glory*
0ca8f01a-192f-5192-af7d-85d181189024.description: For this painting, Garcia was inspired by the composition which Cirro Ferri (1634–1689) painted on the dome of the church St Agnese in Rome. Both works were based on the experience and compositional patterns of Pietro da Cortona (1596–1669).
0ca8f01a-192f-5192-af7d-85d181189024.location: Ceiling of the sanctuary, Jesuit Church of St Ignatius

0d0e56db-22c0-5b6c-94fa-3c424bf11d56.name: The Choir or Sala do Tesouro
0d0e56db-22c0-5b6c-94fa-3c424bf11d56.description: Probably used by the nuns as a meeting place, the floor is of inlaid Brazilian wood. The chapel contains several reliquaries within gilded wooden frames above the choir stalls. Above one of the doors there is a tabernacle with the coat of arms of King José I. The Window bays are adorned with *azulejos*, while the ceiling and walls are decorated with paintings of the Life of Christ and the Life of the Virgin Mary of the 17th and 18th centuries.
0d0e56db-22c0-5b6c-94fa-3c424bf11d56.artist: Marcos da Cruz [n.d.], Bento Coelho da Silveira (1648–1708), André Gonçalves (1685–1762)

0d11fd1e-2845-5a2d-9be0-10b44ca4b3ea.name: View of the exterior
0d11fd1e-2845-5a2d-9be0-10b44ca4b3ea.description: The most significant features of the church, in its picturesque location near the river Inn, are the ridge turret above the choir and the tail gable on the front façade, as well as the skylight turret with onion dome above the crossing. The portal from red marble bears the inscription 1764.
0d11fd1e-2845-5a2d-9be0-10b44ca4b3ea.artist: Franz de Paula Penz (1707–1772); Christoph Anton Mayr (c. 1720–1771)

0d239d25-d965-5b71-8627-0f936291989e.name: Organ Case
0d239d25-d965-5b71-8627-0f936291989e.description: A magnificent organ case produced during the second half of the 18th century. Paintings by Vieira Lusitano hang in gilded frames. Beneath the organ are late 17th-/early 18th-century gilded wood retables.
0d239d25-d965-5b71-8627-0f936291989e.location: Epistle  side, above the two first chapels close to High Choir.
0d239d25-d965-5b71-8627-0f936291989e.artist: Organ maker: unknown; painting: workshop of Francisco Vieira de Matos (known as Vieira Lusitano) 1699–1783.

0d460b15-2345-51b3-8209-f7f723ecea6e.name: Stucchi of Statues gallery
0d460b15-2345-51b3-8209-f7f723ecea6e.description: A quite unique example of Bolognese rococo with its rich stucco decoration.
0d460b15-2345-51b3-8209-f7f723ecea6e.location: Interior, first floor, palazzo Aldrovandi Montanari
0d460b15-2345-51b3-8209-f7f723ecea6e.artist: Alfonso Torreggiani (architecture), Vittorio Maria Bigari and Stefano Orlandi (painted decorations)

0d5965a8-a03d-57bf-8a21-129c9b1fe815.name: Cupola fresco
0d5965a8-a03d-57bf-8a21-129c9b1fe815.description: The ceiling frescos and the wall pictures in the choir are all from the hand of Matthäus Günther and have St. Joseph, the patron of the collegiate church, as their theme. The painting in the cupola crossing depicts the Adoration of the Magi, although the actual theme is the presentation of the Infant Jesus. The focus of the composition is the fresco in the eastern side of the cupola, framed by a picturesque ruin, which is designed to be viewed from the nave.

0db118f6-99b9-55a3-9c4d-d248a7207411.name: Church (architecture and interior)
0db118f6-99b9-55a3-9c4d-d248a7207411.description:
Some years before building the Mausoleum, Pietro de Pomis, the versatile artist at the court in Graz, was involved in the church´s construction. It is documented that the façade, in the style of the then consecrated church San Giorgio Maggiore in Venice by Andrea Palladio, was by him. A hundred years later the style had become old-fashioned, and the church received the new, then typical, two tower-façade of pilgrimage churches. It was decorated with several statues, culminating with the sculptures of St Michael and the devil above the triangular gable between the two towers. All statues were done by Philipp Jakob Straub.  
De Pomis also did the interior´s highlight, the altar painting Mariahilf (Mary´s Help), that gave the church its name. Originally the Virgin and her son wore sculptured metal crowns that were later removed. It is said that the depiction brought about miracles from the very first moment of its existence. The silver frame dates from a hundred years later, and one can imagine how many parts of the painting were cut away because of the new Rococo shape.  
The high-altar´s silver tabernacle was designed by Veit Königer and executed by the goldsmith Anton Römer. If one should question Königer´s authorship, one needs only to compare the tabernacle with that in the former Monastery Church Spital am Pyhrn. It is very similar, four years older and can certainly be attributed to Veit Königer.
0db118f6-99b9-55a3-9c4d-d248a7207411.dates: 1607 laying the church´s and the monastery´s foundation stones; 1609 construction of the monastery building and church; 1627 first façade; 1740 statue of the Miraculous Madonna above the church´s portal; 1742–45 new façade: porch, two towers and statues;
0db118f6-99b9-55a3-9c4d-d248a7207411.artist: Church´s architecture: first façade: Giovanni Pietro de Pomis; allegedly by 1633 construction manager: Pietro Valnegro; (second) two-tower façade: Joseph Hueber; statues at the façade: Philipp Jakob Straub Church´s interior: painting at the high altar: Giovanni Pietro de Pomis; silver tabernacle draft: Veit Königer; execution silver tabernacle and Rococo frame: Anton Römer; sculptures at the high altar´s sides: attributed to Philipp Jakob Straub

0dbd6f4d-41ee-5eab-8782-2834ac28c4e6.name: Staircase
0dbd6f4d-41ee-5eab-8782-2834ac28c4e6.description: Passalacqua inventively reinterpreted the Roman town plan for use in Dubrovnik. With a convex–concave, axially conceived staircase space (in the axis of which is the entrance to the college) he created a deep scenic vista, with which in a distinctive Late Baroque manner, he integrated the Jesuit complex into the structure of the city. Extensive demolition of existing houses was necessary to accommodate the staircase and to widen the street for access. Thanks to Passalacqua’s staircase, the Jesuit complex in Dubrovnik is considered as the highest quality example of Baroque architecture and town planning on the Croatian Adriatic coast.
0dbd6f4d-41ee-5eab-8782-2834ac28c4e6.location: Jesuit Church of St Ignatius, college and Jesuit stairs

0e176e66-89ab-5988-b754-f76492d554b6.name: Rondel
0e176e66-89ab-5988-b754-f76492d554b6.description:
The concept of a garden outside the town walls was probably proposed by F. Luchese. It was executed under the guidance of G. P. Tencalla, with M. A. Lublinský participating in the design. The original state of the gardens is captured in a portfolio by J. van den Nypoort. The ground-plan of the ornamental garden contained a complex water system, feeding ponds, fountains, an aviary, a lake, and a series of “water jets” with which the bishop had become acquainted in Salzburg. The axis of the ornamental garden runs from the skittle-alley entrance that opens onto two “strawberry mounds”. The mounds originate in ancient gardens where they were artificially heaped (Khorsabad) with gazebos, as was the case in Kromeríž. At one time the axis of the garden was flanked by labyrinths and rectangular ponds.  
Rising out of the intersection of paths in the geometrically segmented garden there is a rotunda covered with stucco in high relief. The central space is divided into four grottos and four salons that once featured fountains. Statues and paintings depicting satyrs, allegories of the seasons and stories from Ovid's *Metamorphoses* line the gallery that closes off the front of the garden. The sculptures are modelled on the Villa Pamphilli in Rome. Alternating male and female figures in niches represent ancient gods and goddesses, muses and historical figures from ancient Rome. Side walls once contained grottos with water cascades. A Latin inscription over the main entrance invites visitors to view what was once wetland and wasteland but which now, after many years of hard labour and considerable cost, is a garden designed to delight present and future generations.
0e176e66-89ab-5988-b754-f76492d554b6.artist: Giovanni Pietro Tencalla (1629 Bissone? – 1702 Vienna?), Quirico Castelli (Lugano? active 1658–1672), Carpoforo Tencalla (1623–1685, Bissone), Michael Mandík (? Gdaňsk, worked 1689–1699 in Moravia)

0e7a534f-4091-5533-9e34-fa83788eea0c.name: Chapel of the Sorrowful Mother (Fieger Chapel)
0e7a534f-4091-5533-9e34-fa83788eea0c.description: Built as an extension to the vestibule, it was donated Johann Karl Graf Fieger. Together with the magnificent column altar, the most significant feature is the ceiling frescos from Kaspar Waldmann, a glorification of Mary with the seven founders of the Servite Order and scenes from the life of Mary.
0e7a534f-4091-5533-9e34-fa83788eea0c.location: Northern vestibule, The Servite Monastery Church of St. Charles Borromeo

0e83375b-621c-5113-ac7e-169900faf90f.name: Finding of the Cross by Empress Helena and Trial of the Cross
0e83375b-621c-5113-ac7e-169900faf90f.description: In front of the city scenery of Jerusalem, Empress Helena tries to separate the rediscovered Cross of Christ, relying on its miraculous work, from the two thieves’ crosses. Biographically significant, the already severely sick painter immortalised himself, signature included, as an ailing person amongst a group of people, adjacent to the miracle of the cross, hoping to be healed by the cross relics.

0f34fb84-1a32-5e05-bab6-63b99f2384be.name: Allegory of Beneficent Reign
0f34fb84-1a32-5e05-bab6-63b99f2384be.description: An *Allegory of Beneficent Reign* observes the governor's decisions from above his throne. The original vaulting acquired the symbolic function of a “triumphal arch”. D. Gran was an exponent of Vienna academicism, well versed in producing iconographic programmes on given subjects. Gran's decoration of the Court Library in Vienna inspired M. O. Kounic to commission him rather tha Brno artists Etgens and Eckstein; B. Altomonte also tendered for the commission. Together with the quadraturist G. Fanti, Gran created a mural in the Assembly Hall that sealed his reputation as one of the most sought-after fresco artists of the first half of the 18th century. Several surviving sketches demonstrate the artist's careful preparation for the commission.

0f4907e8-1bfe-5be4-9774-f6308f10d7a4.name: Pulpit
0f4907e8-1bfe-5be4-9774-f6308f10d7a4.description: Dark-bated oak pulpit with busts depicting Jesus Christ, the Virgin Mary and Saints Cajetan and Andreas Avellinus.

0fd664bd-308d-59ad-9fe4-85f50b032730.name: Scenes from the Old Testament
0fd664bd-308d-59ad-9fe4-85f50b032730.description: A local artist created the altarpieces as well as a ceiling painting. The pictures follow the tenets of Czech painting, untouched by the expressive Vienna Academy style. Josef Supper was a leading light in this provincial art centre. The Marian cycle in the nave was completed by his son.
0fd664bd-308d-59ad-9fe4-85f50b032730.artist: Josef Tadeáš Supper (1712 Mohlenice – 1772 Moravská Třebová)

0ffb541c-53f9-50cc-a25b-8099d4c6bfe2.name: Pulpit
0ffb541c-53f9-50cc-a25b-8099d4c6bfe2.description: The markedly elongated proportions of the pulpit match the vertical character of the Gothic nave, while the refined colour harmonies of the marbling and gilding and the dynamically posed sculpture, create an elegant whole that tells of the refined Late Barque language of its creators. The impression of lightness and airiness is accentuated by playful angelic figures in relaxed poses, which are physically independent of the pulpit architecture. Angels with the attributes of Trust and Love are located at the very edge of the *Rocaille* volutes of the pulpit. Effective *putto*, symbols of vanquished disbelief with blindfolded eyes and hands bound in chains, tumble head first from the baldachin. At the top – above the crouched figure of the defeated devil – triumphs an allegorical figure of Faith.
0ffb541c-53f9-50cc-a25b-8099d4c6bfe2.location: Alongside the north wall of the nave
0ffb541c-53f9-50cc-a25b-8099d4c6bfe2.artist: Sculptor: Alexius Königer (1732–1782); painter and gilder: Franz Kochler (active c. 1770s)

1014f7f2-b462-5768-bada-f994085d9729.name: Sacristy cabinet
1014f7f2-b462-5768-bada-f994085d9729.description: There are three stylistically uniform cabinets in the sacristy of the Church of St. Roch, Virovitica, the main one is the largest and most richly decorated, seen here.

102445da-a45f-5b11-ae5e-54f02856f1a4.name: View of the vaulting
102445da-a45f-5b11-ae5e-54f02856f1a4.description: Cross vaulting, which enabled the installation of large basilica windows with frames rich in plastic mouldings.

10b09ae4-8e90-57d0-b70f-35b6ba8fa139.name: Façade with Two Towers and Main Door pediment
10b09ae4-8e90-57d0-b70f-35b6ba8fa139.description: The façade with two towers is peculiar to the architecture of the Congregation of the Eremits of St. Paulo. The main door pediment features the symbol of the Holy Sacrament, the second devotion of the church.

10b5dd9e-da66-5673-82d3-b89488fdaeda.name: The Hill of the Cross
10b5dd9e-da66-5673-82d3-b89488fdaeda.description: The path to a theatrically rendered Calvary includes four chapels of the Stations of the Cross that begin at the parish church. A dramatic Crucifixion scene is introduced by mourning angels. The central, concavely accentuated part consists of the Holy Trinity with God the Father at the top. The impact of the scene derives from the positioning of the group, the contrast of materials, the dynamic postures and decorative elements such as “stones” in the bottom section, and the clouds in the upper one, as well as the placement of the figures of the Virgin Mary and St. John on the consoles.
10b5dd9e-da66-5673-82d3-b89488fdaeda.artist: Jiří František Pacák and workshop (Severin Tischler?)

1174b2ab-da5e-56fc-b6bc-cc3311897b6b.name: Mount of Olives
1174b2ab-da5e-56fc-b6bc-cc3311897b6b.description: Behind the high altar is a grotto, “the Garden of Gethsemane”, with a relief sculpture of Christ and the Apostles on the Mount of Olives before Christ was tortured. A group of sinners suffering in purgatory are depicted on a tomb to accentuate His role as Saviour.
1174b2ab-da5e-56fc-b6bc-cc3311897b6b.location: High altar, Pilgrimage Church of the Elevation of the Holy Cross, Jaroměřice u Jevíčka

11ba5be2-9ef2-554a-855f-c08f25e2d190.name: Gate
11ba5be2-9ef2-554a-855f-c08f25e2d190.description: The triumphal arch with a triangular gable separates the chateau from the town. The original connection by means of the triumphal path was broken and emphasis placed on vistas. The family’s coat of arms is surrounded by the mottos “Kindness is not forgotten” and “the lustre of faith outlasts even a rock”.

120c15e4-f25e-5245-855c-a7af065de45d.name: Imperial Apartment and guest rooms
120c15e4-f25e-5245-855c-a7af065de45d.description: Like almost every monastery, Stift St. Florian provided representative rooms for the Imperial Family when they were traveling. This was a useful facility in times where there were only few hotels/hostels, most of them dirty and unsafe. The 16 guest rooms are still equipped with the original 18th century furniture and fittings, all manufactured by Upper Austrian craftsmen. The sculptures over the doors are remarkable as well as the light carriers and the bed posts in the so-called Prince Eugene room. Sculptures and wall paintings recall his victory over the Ottomans. Statues, furniture, doors and floors in all guestrooms were done by the members of two families, Sattler and Jegg. The most gifted artist-craftsman under them was Leonhard Sattler who made furniture, decoration, all wooden sculptures in the guest rooms, as well as the stone figures and ornaments on the portal.
120c15e4-f25e-5245-855c-a7af065de45d.artist: Leonhard Sattler and members of the Sattler family, members of the family Jegg

121d7b8f-eaf4-5545-aff0-ad69b9902ec1.name: Kings’ Stairway
121d7b8f-eaf4-5545-aff0-ad69b9902ec1.description: The Kings' stairway is furnished with balusters and statues of the Portuguese kings organised chronologically: Count Henrique of Burgundy is followed by his son, the first King of Portugal Afonso Henriques. He is followed by his grandson, the second King Sancho I and, finally, King José I. The kings of the Spanish Habsburg dynasty are represented in slightly smaller dimensions. The effigies were inspired by 17th-century examples owned by Bishop João de Mendonça.

121f0793-9d39-54e5-80a5-b503d8ae19e9.name: Retable of St. Anthony Chapel
121f0793-9d39-54e5-80a5-b503d8ae19e9.description: Example of King João V style woodcarving.

1288aecf-a814-535b-a170-246be71bef2c.name: Painted ceiling and Small Chapel
1288aecf-a814-535b-a170-246be71bef2c.description:
In the first room is a painted wooden ceiling decorated with floral motifs. In the centre, a Portuguese Vessel (Nau) invokes St. Elmo, the patron saint of the Brotherhood.  
The second tempera painted ceiling is in the chapel. The Chapel is completely covered with gold-leaf carving in the “National” style, enhancing the shrines embedded in the walls, and exemplifying space management during the Baroque period. The ceiling depicts scenes from the Life of Saint Elmo.
1288aecf-a814-535b-a170-246be71bef2c.location: Interior rooms, House of the Holy Body (Museum of Baroque)

128ade4a-8221-5910-9ee7-61ede5c15971.name: Portal and façade detail
128ade4a-8221-5910-9ee7-61ede5c15971.description:
Atop the three round arches of the façade are the figures of St. Engrácia, St  
Condestável and St. Isabel, according to the decree of Infanta D. Maria, whose wish was that only Portuguese saints should be depicted here.  
The portal is flanked by two Solomonic columns surmounted by a crown and coat-of-arms.

12b6ef18-d62e-5052-8926-f834733d5460.name: Altar of St. Michael (High Altar)
12b6ef18-d62e-5052-8926-f834733d5460.description: The high altar is impressive not only through the subtle ponderation of a demanding pomp of columns and architectural elegance, but also through its sculptures: A scenic meal of Emmaus in front of the tabernacle as a typological example of the Eucharist, as well as archangel statues of Gabriel and Raphael, whose ironic dialogue with the accompanying cherub are  counted as the highlights of Bavarian Rococo sculpture : The left one performs the Annunciation Madonna, the right one St. Tobias with the fish. In the upper storey of the altar, a third cherub is engaged in horseplay with St. Michael’s weapons. The correlating older altarpiece, which portrays the triumph of the Archangel over Satan, is considered as a major work of Munich Baroque painting.
12b6ef18-d62e-5052-8926-f834733d5460.artist: Altarpiece: Andreas Wolf (1652-1716); Altar and sculptures: Johann Baptist Straub (1704–84)

12e0711b-8fcd-54f5-b3df-b90f0c286076.name: *Peace on Earth* (*The Four Human Temperaments*)
12e0711b-8fcd-54f5-b3df-b90f0c286076.description: The ceiling of the vestibule shows the Four Human Temperaments – *collerico*, *sanguigno*, *flemmatico*, *malinconico* – sitting on the terrestrial globe, seen against the light and alludes to earthly harmony; the allegories of the Four elements – fire, water, earth and air – are painted in the pendentives. The hardy scorcio and the energetic figures sitting on the terrestrial globe give the impression of a vast space, amplified by the light and its movement against the airy background of the sky. The light creates a deep illusive depth in part because of the star architectural frame.

130a251d-cd8c-55de-81ca-2e58a7733c0b.name: St. Gregory
130a251d-cd8c-55de-81ca-2e58a7733c0b.description: Illusionary architecture and ornamentation make up a major part of the church decoration. They also provide a background for one of the Church Fathers in a vault joint. St. Gregory is a crypto-portrait of his namesake, Řehoř Lambeck, a benefactor of the church and art-loving abbot of Louka Monastery. J. Winterhalder Jr., a pupil and close associate of Maulbertsch, participated in the painting of the Church Fathers, Prophets and Evangelists.
130a251d-cd8c-55de-81ca-2e58a7733c0b.location: Pilgrimage Church of the Scourged Saviour, Dyje, detail of the Fresco
130a251d-cd8c-55de-81ca-2e58a7733c0b.artist: Franz Anton Maulbertsch (1724 Langenargen am Bodensee – 1796 Vienna) – Josef Winterhalder Jr. (1743 Vöhrenbach – 1807 Znojmo)

131a9aab-cb29-5c8a-b6c9-6c0c8354e020.name: St. Catherine of Alexandria
131a9aab-cb29-5c8a-b6c9-6c0c8354e020.description: A statue of the Patron Saint of Wisdom, from the altar of the Holy Family, accompanies a canvas by M. Unterberger. W. Träger, who created the sculpted decoration for all the altars in the church, was a lesser-known pupil of O. Zahner with whom he worked from the 1740s. After his teacher’s death, Träger finished the Holy Trinity Column in Olomouc. His work in the Piarist Church in Mikulov complements an interior renowned, in particular, for a fresco by F. A. Maulbertsch. Träger was mainly active in Olomouc where he took over the workshop of J. A. Richter.

1344acc5-88e3-5794-b1bd-e1f3c804fd21.name: High Altar
1344acc5-88e3-5794-b1bd-e1f3c804fd21.description: The Invention of the Cross altarpiece was one of the last works created in Moravia by Franz Anton Maulbertsch, a leading artist of the Habsburg Monarchy during the 18th-century. His canvases are frequently framed by altar architecture and statues by O. Schweigl. In fact, Schweigl was among the first to report on the work of this artist in his treatises on Moravian art; among them, his *History of Art* was a recommended textbook at schools of higher-education. The altarpiece is surrounded by statues of St. Peter with Mary Magdalene, and St. Paul with St. Veronica. Schweigl also created the statues of Saints Barbara and Joseph for the side altars, complementing pictures by Ferdinand Licht (1800), a Brno artist who maintained a late-Baroque style until the early 19th century. The *Invention of the Cross*, already expressively painted by Maulbertsch in Hradište, near Znojmo, is rendered in an objective manner. The miraculous scene is portrayed with light effects accentuated by sculpted decoration. The *chiaroscuro* picture, with its rhetorical gestures, opens with the whitish figures of saints in restricted postures, and classicist flowing gowns. Their faces are full of strong emotional movement. The segmentation and colour scheme of the retable, which is made from imitation marble from a local source used for the construction of the church, blend the late-Baroque altar with the Gothic architecture, producing, despite a variety of styles, a noble and unified interior.
1344acc5-88e3-5794-b1bd-e1f3c804fd21.artist: Ondřej Schweigl (1735–1812, Brno), Franz Anton Maulbertsch (1724 Langenargen am Bodensee – 1796 Vienna)

13b79634-03b0-538a-9826-541612b5cfbc.name: Main Altar
13b79634-03b0-538a-9826-541612b5cfbc.description: The gilded wooden altarpiece in the National style of the Portuguese Baroque.

14756176-c5ce-547a-a93a-d0113a7e9513.name: General View of the Nave towards the Chancel
14756176-c5ce-547a-a93a-d0113a7e9513.description: Although small and low, the true value of the church interior lies in the densely carved and gilded woodwork of the lateral altarpieces, seen most spectacularly in the chancel.
14756176-c5ce-547a-a93a-d0113a7e9513.location: Interior, Sanctuary of Bom Jesus de Matosinhos
14756176-c5ce-547a-a93a-d0113a7e9513.artist: Portuguese woodcarvers: Luís Pereira da Costa (active 1724–?), Domingos Martins Moreira (active 1746–1750)

147bc5f0-6d4a-5622-9f01-e30b4195cabf.name: Ceiling frescos
147bc5f0-6d4a-5622-9f01-e30b4195cabf.description: The central panel in the choir vault with its stucco frame depicts the Holy Family as patron saint of the brotherhood: Mary and Joseph in adoration of the Holy Trinity. Putti present carpenter’s tools as attribute and symbol of the guild. The monochrome spandrel pictures depict Joseph’s Dream, the Flight to Egypt, the Rest on the Flight and the Infant Jesus in the Workshop. On the basis of an analysis of the painting style they are variously ascribed to Paul Zeiller from Reutte or Johann Heel from Pfronten.
147bc5f0-6d4a-5622-9f01-e30b4195cabf.location: Choir, Catholic Guild Church of St. Joseph

14a12f38-87d8-52d7-b640-8b165902a403.name: View of the high altar
14a12f38-87d8-52d7-b640-8b165902a403.description: The later chapels are connected by a passageway. There is a view of the counter façade with the main door flanked by two lions, the only remains of the Romanesque “Door of the Lions”, that now support the stoop.
14a12f38-87d8-52d7-b640-8b165902a403.artist: Domenico Tibaldi; Pietro Fiorini; Floriano Ambrosini; Giovanni Ambrogio Magenta; Alfonso Torreggiani

14cf3ac9-f201-5ffe-96c6-9da83f2f8352.name: Library Façade
14cf3ac9-f201-5ffe-96c6-9da83f2f8352.description: Magnificent Baroque façade in limestone with four huge columns crowned by the royal coat of arms and the phrase “So highly are books praised here in Coimbra that a library crowns the city head”.

15a87fb6-8298-5ff6-a114-ee8cde8ea202.name: Pulpit
15a87fb6-8298-5ff6-a114-ee8cde8ea202.description: A beautiful example of an Early Classicist pulpit in austere forms virtually without ornamentation or pictorial programme. Instead of Baroque rhetoric—which was no longer expected of the preacher—the pulpit was designed to provide a dignified frame for an edifying sermon. The design originates from Hagenauer and Nesselthaler and was executed by Peter Pflauder, a stucco mason and altar carpenter from Thannheim in Tyrol.

15bbc895-ece1-5072-8a0d-58528b3db808.name: Altar of the Holy Cross
15bbc895-ece1-5072-8a0d-58528b3db808.description: The stucco decoration of the altars and the pulpit was created by a prominent Brno artist, previously active in Olomouc. The way in which the artist approaches the spiritual movement of the figures, the non-dramatic gestures, the soft relief shapes and the spatial concept of the sculpture, enhance the effect of an epic scene. The sculptor’s oeuvre includes many altarpieces in Brno and its surroundings, typified by a spectacular form derived from Italian (Bernini) and Viennese (Donner) sculpture. The artist’s stucco work was particularly influenced by B. Fontana.
15bbc895-ece1-5072-8a0d-58528b3db808.location: Minorite Church of Saints John and Loreto, Brno
15bbc895-ece1-5072-8a0d-58528b3db808.artist: Jan Jiří Schauberger (? before 1725 Vienna, active in Olomouc – 1744 Brno)

15d36523-72f6-5f3b-bbf9-9e9553805b24.name: Exterior with lateral terraces
15d36523-72f6-5f3b-bbf9-9e9553805b24.description: Apart from the exchange of the tunnel-vault of the original design with a cross vault, and the introduction of Baroque plasticity in the otherwise early Baroque repertoire of the architectural plastic mouldings, Napoli enriched the cathedral by adding side terraces with balustrades.

16198157-102d-5384-9d69-ee290a4ec9d4.name: Altar of St. Stephen
16198157-102d-5384-9d69-ee290a4ec9d4.description: The lateral altar of scagliola marble is dedicated to the subsidiary patron Saint Stephen, whose stoning is depicted on the altarpiece painting. The altar is flanked by sculptures of the Holy women Mary Magdalene and Afra.

16315802-18c2-5330-ba73-5cd3cfe77f4a.name: *St. Joseph with Jesus and St. John the Baptist*
16315802-18c2-5330-ba73-5cd3cfe77f4a.description: In Croatia and especially in the north, there are a large number of works of the Slovene painter, Valentin Metzinger. An eclectic and accomplished painter, he was inspired by the works of the Bolognese artists Annibale Carracci and Guido Reni, and the paintings of the Venetian Mannerists. From the time of Metzinger’s arrival in Ljubljana in 1727, up to his death in 1759, his name and his works became the trademark of a large number of religious interiors throughout Slovenia and Croatia, particularly within Franciscan churches.

16398617-5dcc-5881-ab36-e46907c727ef.name: *St. Frances Landing at the Adriatic Coast*
16398617-5dcc-5881-ab36-e46907c727ef.description: The scenes painted by Bernardo Bobić are set in contemporary late 17th-century Croatia and Zagreb, although they could only have occurred at the beginning of the 13th century.

169326c2-920f-568e-865b-5feb37a401c0.name: Count’s Study
169326c2-920f-568e-865b-5feb37a401c0.description: The “Chinese” room was adjoined by a library. The floor, inlaid with several kinds of wood, was by the court joiner. The count consulted with the Viennese adviser, Conrad Adolph von Albrecht, who also worked for the Sinzendorfs in Židlochovice in most of his artistic activities.
169326c2-920f-568e-865b-5feb37a401c0.artist: Jacob Prandtauer (1660 Stanz – 1726 St. Pölten), Johann Friedrich Praetorius

16b7443b-221e-5c2f-b518-f5af41d929f0.name: Large Dining Hall (Assembly Hall)
16b7443b-221e-5c2f-b518-f5af41d929f0.description: Due to the death of Bishop Egkh, the Large Dining Hall spanning two floors was not renovated. Some of Maulbertsch's preparatory sketches, with scenes from Ovid's *Metamorphoses* featuring allegories of the times of the day, have, however, survived. The hall was further enhanced in the spirit of Rococo Classicism under Bishop Hamilton, although not with murals but with gilded stuccos portraying allegories of the sciences and arts, together with the canvases *The Trial of Paris* and *The Wedding of Peleus and Thetis*, exemplifying ephemeral vanity, and *Pallas Athena Kidnapping an Ephebus from Aphrodite*, symbolising wisdom and stability. The alternative name of the room, the Assembly Hall, comes from 1848 when an imperial assembly took place there.
16b7443b-221e-5c2f-b518-f5af41d929f0.artist: Franz Adolph of Freenthal (1721–1773), Karl Martin Keller

177f9291-bc9c-5c91-b323-5a7e61e086be.name: *Urban II blessing the Bolognese Crusaders*
177f9291-bc9c-5c91-b323-5a7e61e086be.description: This scene shows the Pope blessing the Bolognese crusaders and their flags before the departure for the Holy Land for the First Crusade (October 1095). The representation, the clothing and the setting are in Baroque style.
177f9291-bc9c-5c91-b323-5a7e61e086be.artist: Giovanni Maria Bibiena (1625–1665) and Bartolomeo Morelli known as il Pianoro (dead 1703)

178756de-2fc7-5c0f-9aeb-af17d4b308f4.name: Diana, Goddess of the Hunt
178756de-2fc7-5c0f-9aeb-af17d4b308f4.description: In accordance with the use of the Amalienburg as a hunting lodge, the stuccoed overdoor of the main portal facing the garden depicts Diana, goddess of the hunt, as a half figure, surrounded with putti, hounds and hunting equipment.
178756de-2fc7-5c0f-9aeb-af17d4b308f4.location: Niche above the central portal of the eastern façade

17c6b768-948a-514c-ad9b-2dc3c8992cd0.name: Side altars
17c6b768-948a-514c-ad9b-2dc3c8992cd0.description: Six virtuosically carved altars mounted in the niches flanking the chancel arch depicting patrons (from left to right: St. Catherine, St. Corbinian, Holy Apostles, Holy Family, St. Benedict, St. Sebastian) as well as the pulpit, are regarded as masterpieces of Johann Baptist Straub. The altarpieces, flanked by sculptures, were made among others by Martin Knoller and Johann Jakob Zeiller.
17c6b768-948a-514c-ad9b-2dc3c8992cd0.artist: Johann Baptist Straub (1704–1784); Johann Jakob Zeiller (1710–1783); Martin Knoller (1725–1804)

1806be4b-9dfd-5bdf-9314-0f98c01bc8cd.name: Chapel of St. Anastasia
1806be4b-9dfd-5bdf-9314-0f98c01bc8cd.description: Marble columns connected elegantly by arches support a vault decorated with virtuous Rocaille stucco, on which is painted the vision of St. Anastasia’s ascension into heaven. The high-quality Venetian altarpiece of the main altar illustrates the intercession of saints to pilgrims with illnesses of the head and mental diseases of all kinds. Capriccio-like  side altars by the hand of the famous sculptor  Ignaz Günther complete the precious decoration.
1806be4b-9dfd-5bdf-9314-0f98c01bc8cd.location: At the north side of the abbey church nearby the chancel and sacristy
1806be4b-9dfd-5bdf-9314-0f98c01bc8cd.artist: Architecture: Johann Michael Fischer(1692–1766); stucco and high altar: Johann Michael Feichtmayr (1696–1772); side altars: Ignaz Günther (1725–75); altarpieces for the altars of St. Anastasia and of the Immaculate Conception: Jacopo Amigoni (1682–1752); ceiling fresco: Johann Jakob Zeiller (1710–83)

185151ef-db66-5040-92c3-fe14c8f0bea2.name: View of the Nave
185151ef-db66-5040-92c3-fe14c8f0bea2.description: Although inspired by Mafra Basilica, the interior design of Estrela Basilica owes more to the interior design of Lisbon churches rebuilt after the 1755 earthquake.
185151ef-db66-5040-92c3-fe14c8f0bea2.artist: Architects: Mateus Vicente de Oliveira (1706–1786), Reinaldo Manuel dos Santos (?–1790)

18b7cc4e-96b8-5108-862c-de91f264ec96.name: Library, Imperial Hall
18b7cc4e-96b8-5108-862c-de91f264ec96.description:
Although the library and the two storey Imperial Hall were built at the end of the 17th century, only the library was finished and equipped before 1700. Typical for the epoch is the deep sculptural stucco decoration framing the ceiling’s fresco paintings. The bookshelves are a masterwork by a cabinet maker from the region. They are crowned by most decorative gilded wood carvings.  
The construction of the Imperial Hall and the fresco paintings with impressive illusionistic columns were finished in 1694 and in 1696. A standstill lasting more than twenty years followed, until the hall was decorated with stucco work and fifteen portraits of emperors, starting with the first sovereign Rudolf I up to Karl VI who was ruling in that era. A charming addition to the room is the (abandoned) fountain in the form of a dog whose mouth poured out the water.
18b7cc4e-96b8-5108-862c-de91f264ec96.dates: 1676–83: construction of the Abbey Wing including the library; 1684: stucco work; n.d. Melchior Steidl’s fresco painting and bookshelves; 1694: the Imperial Hall’s bare brickwork was finished; 1696: fresco painting; 1719: stucco work; 1720: fountain; 1721
18b7cc4e-96b8-5108-862c-de91f264ec96.artist: Carlo Antonio Carlone: abbey wing (including the library and the Imperial Hall); Girolamo Alfieri: stucco work; Melchior Steidl: one fresco painting on the ceiling; Balthasar Melber: bookshelves; Melchior Steidl: fresco painting Imperial Hall; Diego Francesco Carlone: stucco work; n.n.: fountain; Martino Altomonte: emperors' portraits

18b9a5d2-56e7-5160-91ae-9a12388104ed.name: Monumental staircase; entrance
18b9a5d2-56e7-5160-91ae-9a12388104ed.description: Accessible from the atrium of the palace, the staircase is immediately visible thanks to its irregular and dynamic flight. The steps and balustrade immediately draw the sight and the attention of visitors.

18d8c264-d9de-5469-85bc-d0bbaeb6448b.name: *Abraham’s Sacrifice of Isaac* (detail of an angel and Abraham)
18d8c264-d9de-5469-85bc-d0bbaeb6448b.description: Depicting the dramatic peak of the Old Testament story, an angel catches hold of the raised arm of Abraham, stopping him a moment before the sacrifice of his own son Isaac, the crouching figure of whom is on the ready-prepared pyre.
18d8c264-d9de-5469-85bc-d0bbaeb6448b.location: Altar of the Holy Cross (Church of the Holy Cross)

192646de-9480-5ec8-a969-8316a9ee6e28.name: Abbot Loge
192646de-9480-5ec8-a969-8316a9ee6e28.description: The more modest, although no less virtuously modelled and decorated, counterpart to the pulpit forms the loge of the abbot of Steingaden.
192646de-9480-5ec8-a969-8316a9ee6e28.location: Lay church, column pair right of the chancel
192646de-9480-5ec8-a969-8316a9ee6e28.artist: Design: Dominikus Zimmermann (1685–1766) Execution: Pontian Steinhauser (1688–1755)

194f2968-7c68-5b10-86f8-a30372e5853c.name: Nave
194f2968-7c68-5b10-86f8-a30372e5853c.description: The Baroque arrangement of the nave walls is formed by brace-like wall piers composed of three pilasters respectively, of which, the side pilasters are concavely modelled. The side altars at the choir arch and in the middle of the nave, together with the pulpit, are uniformly executed in rich, sweeping Late Baroque forms and were designed by Mölck, who is also responsible for the altar paintings.
194f2968-7c68-5b10-86f8-a30372e5853c.artist: Johann Adam Ritter von Mölck (1718–1794) and others

1991c012-f312-5724-ad34-6745f6148321.name: Angels
1991c012-f312-5724-ad34-6745f6148321.description: The decoration in the chapel originally consisted only of this group of sculpted angels bearing a celestial sphere decorated with five stars and with St. John of Nepomuk standing on top of it. The statues were created by local artists.

19d5aeaa-c02f-5de9-b1ed-729ab86fb294.name: Side Altars of St. Norbert – St. Augustine – St. Joseph – St. John of Nepomuk
19d5aeaa-c02f-5de9-b1ed-729ab86fb294.description: The columned design of the main altars in the choir and in the crossarms contrast the four smaller side altars, only consisting of simple pillar framings, and thus illustrating the hierarchy of the main and side altars in the church. They each are equipped with sculptural arrangements in shallow niches, creating a relief-like effect, and decorated with angels and rocaille cartouches.
19d5aeaa-c02f-5de9-b1ed-729ab86fb294.location: Front and rear side chapels of the nave

19d6827b-60cd-54d1-8560-f7ba5fc8eff1.name: *The Miracle of the Roses* (left) and the *Assumption of the Virgin Mary* (right)
19d6827b-60cd-54d1-8560-f7ba5fc8eff1.description: On the Gospel side of the nave there are two chapels with important paintings by André Gonçalves, including the *Assumption of the Virgin* and the *Miracle of the Roses* depicting the legend of the Life of Queen St. Isabel of Aragão (1270–1336), wife of King Dinis I (1261–1325) of Portugal.
19d6827b-60cd-54d1-8560-f7ba5fc8eff1.location: Lateral chapels of the nave, Gospel side

1a5ad99e-4e60-596e-9113-8c0b78eebfe2.name: Large reading tables
1a5ad99e-4e60-596e-9113-8c0b78eebfe2.description: The six large tables (buffets) in multi-coloured and exotic woods are all slightly different and designed to match each room.
1a5ad99e-4e60-596e-9113-8c0b78eebfe2.location: Interior, Biblioteca Joanina da Universidade de Coimbra

1b3c9fc4-faee-59ed-b3c7-369b7488c0f3.name: Library
1b3c9fc4-faee-59ed-b3c7-369b7488c0f3.description: Above the sacristy and the Chapel of St. Anne is one of a few surviving monastery libraries. The vault features scenes from the life of St. Norbert connected with the celebration of the Eucharist. The painting’s concept, flying in the face of common iconography, was probably by the monastery abbot. The relief decorations of the library cases are symbols of the sciences and arts. A large quantity of the books came from dissolved monasteries in the surrounding area, especially Louka u Znojma; one section was assembled by the abbot of the Cistercian Monastery in Düsselthal in the Rhine basin, which was purchased by the monastery in 1802.

1b76ee67-59f5-5426-ae90-e4aff6200791.name: Electress’s Private Chapel
1b76ee67-59f5-5426-ae90-e4aff6200791.description: Panelled with scagliola marble, the chapel flaunts its sumptuous ornamental decoration. To great effect, the ceiling, decorated with interlacing stuccowork, opens into an oval lantern displaying a fresco of heaven. The valuable altarpiece comes from the workshop of Peter Paul Rubens.
1b76ee67-59f5-5426-ae90-e4aff6200791.location: New Palace, first floor of the north wing

1b9bc4e6-e32d-5048-9385-04be938177c9.name: Monumental staircase
1b9bc4e6-e32d-5048-9385-04be938177c9.description: For this double flight staircase Pietro Canali was inspired by theatrical stage effects. Allegorical statues of *Hercules* and *Atlas* by Gabriele Brunelli (1615–1682) decorate the staircase. The vault was painted by Gioacchino Pizzoli (1651–1731).
1b9bc4e6-e32d-5048-9385-04be938177c9.artist: Pietro Canali; Gabriele Brunelli; Gioacchino Pizzoli

1c0acee7-62a2-5fd2-bde2-c4c712c39be7.name: Ballroom
1c0acee7-62a2-5fd2-bde2-c4c712c39be7.description: Detail of the ballroom with its amazing baroque quadratura framing scenes from Hercules’ life. The coat of arms of the Pepoli surmounted by a swan is continually repeated.
1c0acee7-62a2-5fd2-bde2-c4c712c39be7.artist: Domenico Maria Canuti and Domenico Santi known as Mengazzino

1c18232c-3877-5f00-a0b7-461e6bf058e6.name: Interior opposite the choir
1c18232c-3877-5f00-a0b7-461e6bf058e6.description: The effect generated by the interior in the ideal view from the west is determined by the massive pilasters, which form the support for the pristine semi-circular spans of the double transverse and single longitudinal arches. Their arrangement generates, as is usual for pilaster churches, a coulisse-like prospect, however the room is so short due to the sequence of only three elements (two nave bays and choir) that it almost has the appearance of a central-plan building. The high altar with the miraculous picture, which is situated free-standing in the middle of the choir, thus appears, not as a distant goal, but as quasi the centre of the spatial sequence, especially as the grandeur of its ciborium echoes the four-arched structure of the two-nave bays.

1c762e1a-46e3-5876-b435-e216529f8c0d.name: The Bells of Lisbon and the Sanctus Singing Angel
1c762e1a-46e3-5876-b435-e216529f8c0d.description: Two small frescoes refer to the canonisation of St. Anthony in 1232. The angels invoking him represent the heavenly participation in the pontificial act, while the bells refer to a miracle that occurred at the same time: all of the church bells in Lisbon, hometown of the saint, chimed simultaneously without human involvement. The virtuosic view from below and especially the realism of the bell cage give these images the status of pictorial showpieces.
1c762e1a-46e3-5876-b435-e216529f8c0d.location: Vault of the spandrel spaces between the octagonal and the oval structure

1ccb99e8-d9b9-5a4f-913c-efa249650f37.name: *Grotesco* ceiling painting
1ccb99e8-d9b9-5a4f-913c-efa249650f37.description: *Grotesco* ceiling painting with cartouches over the High Choir depicting the *Holy Trinity*, *Assumption of Our Lady* and *Escape into Egypt.*

1ce65368-cef5-5a21-b4ac-0bc8e7b476f3.name: Tomb of Queen Maria I
1ce65368-cef5-5a21-b4ac-0bc8e7b476f3.description: The Neo-Classical tomb of queen Maria I – made of white, black and pink marble over a plinth – is decorated with two urns and an inscription identifying the queen. The sarcophagus is supported by two lions. At the top is a medallion, containing an effigy of Queen Maria I, presented by Fame and a *putto.*

1d2c211d-2700-5a80-817e-a40c9d14229c.name: Oratories
1d2c211d-2700-5a80-817e-a40c9d14229c.description: Oratory of Our Lady of the Rosary constructed from wood and canvas. There are others dedicated to Our Lady of Mount Carmel, St. Matthew, and St. John the Baptist. With the exception of the Oratory of St. John the Baptist, the outside wings are adorned with paintings.

1d50e49c-ec78-5964-9727-5f82a4990f66.name: Exterior
1d50e49c-ec78-5964-9727-5f82a4990f66.description: Only the curved windows, of a bell-shape on the nave, indicate a building of the Late Baroque period. Everything else is of unimposing design and the former Gothic buttresses have been reduced to bands. The west side has not been designed as an ornamental façade and the gable has even been finished in shingles. The shaft of the Gothic tower with pointed helm roof has remained unrendered.

1d7a5af5-3037-5bd4-8ab2-a42543f3c28c.name: Revelation of St. Joseph Calasanctius
1d7a5af5-3037-5bd4-8ab2-a42543f3c28c.description: The side altarpiece represents the founder of the Piarist order, with his students, worshipping the Virgin Mary. The subject is associated with teaching, one of the chief objectives of the order. The picture complements the *Allegory of Education* by W. Träger.
1d7a5af5-3037-5bd4-8ab2-a42543f3c28c.location: Piarist Church of St. John the Baptist
1d7a5af5-3037-5bd4-8ab2-a42543f3c28c.artist: Josef Stern (1716 Graz – 1775 Brno), Wolfgang Träger (1714 Pilsen – 1763 Olomouc)

1d9489cb-b684-525a-aafd-7aef21007b06.name: *Allegory of Time*
1d9489cb-b684-525a-aafd-7aef21007b06.description: A superb example of “quadratura” by the celebrated Angelo Michele Colonna, a specialist in painted architectures. Giuseppe Alboresi painted the figures inside the large oval at the centre of the ceiling. The scene represents the *Allegory of Time driving away Venus and the Graces*.
1d9489cb-b684-525a-aafd-7aef21007b06.artist: Angelo Michele Colonna (1604–1687) and Giuseppe Alboresi (1632–1677)

1e1c41cd-e203-5847-9534-cb31a2f69f12.name: Monumental staircase
1e1c41cd-e203-5847-9534-cb31a2f69f12.description: The monumental staircase has a complex structure, based on an elliptical plan. Two large flights of stairs embrace, rising, the area where the stair is placed; one more flight rises in the opposite direction driving to the first floor. From the balconies all around it is possible to observe the very suggestive and dynamic development of the stair, where reality and fiction are mixed up thanks to the illusive use of paintings by Ercole Graziani. Many years later Filippo Balugani realized the sculptures representing pagan gods that are placed over the balustrades.
1e1c41cd-e203-5847-9534-cb31a2f69f12.artist: Giovanni Battista Torri; Carlo Fontana; Ercole Graziani; Filippo Balugani

1e3ded35-5fc2-5f5f-b377-ddc4c0c909a6.name: Stucco
1e3ded35-5fc2-5f5f-b377-ddc4c0c909a6.description: The stuccowork was crafted by one of the great masters of the stucco school  in Wessobrunn, where the central themes were snail and shell ornaments. He combined those with traditional motifs from the Early Baroque stucco art in Munich, particularly laurel branches, herms of angels, and strips of stuccowork framing geometrically configured sections. The single motifs are mostly cast with wooden moulds.
1e3ded35-5fc2-5f5f-b377-ddc4c0c909a6.artist: Design: Konstantin Pader; Execution: Matthias II Schmuzer

1e772eff-929b-5a4b-85e1-d834735310d2.name: Apostle statues
1e772eff-929b-5a4b-85e1-d834735310d2.description: The cycle of 14 apostle statues is arranged around the perimeter of the church interior, framed by alcove-like recesses. These remarkable works originate from the workshop of the sculptor Johann Paterer of Lienz.

1e82ff8f-ef07-5744-8db7-50ff944acb83.name: Stiftskirche/Abbey Church, dedicated to the Ascension of Maria and to Saint Jacob/James the Elder
1e82ff8f-ef07-5744-8db7-50ff944acb83.description:
The abbey church was built under abbot Benedikt Rieger. It was also under him that the ceiling and the walls got the rich and artistic sculptural design. There are myriads of stucco garlands made of leaves, flowers and fruits as well as ceiling paintings framed with 3D stucco and umpteen statues of putti (male toddlers), angels and saints.
