No square centimetre was left empty. Nivard II Dierer succeeded as abbot and contented himself with embellishing the interior. He – who had come from a wealthy family and who had seen Versailles Palace – was enthusiastically re-decorating the church. He added a “second layer” of gilded carvings and framed flower still lifes to the pilasters and it was probably he who had coloured and (later) gilded the originally white limed(?) stucco. This was found out recently in thorough analysis with regard to forthcoming restoration works: in Abbot Nivard´s II era all the stucco work on the ceiling as well as the background was light pink, the sculptures – putti and saints – dark pink and the pilasters were marbled grey blue. Probably a bit later, all the stucco of the walls and side chapels was gilded (the abbot may have remembered Versailles Palace). The gold and silver surfaces in the Bernhardisaal (s. Detail 2) give an impression of how the church may have looked when the stucco was gilded.  
The high altar painting is dedicated to the Assumption – the Mother of God, sitting on a cloud, is ascending to heaven. She is surrounded by angels who sprinkle roses into her grave.
1e82ff8f-ef07-5744-8db7-50ff944acb83.location: Almost in the middle of the abbey’s four-wing complex, between the prelate’s court and the cloister.
1e82ff8f-ef07-5744-8db7-50ff944acb83.artist: Stucco figures and fresco paintings: Giovanni Battista Carlone (according to a preserved contract); stucco plants and ornaments: Bartolomeo Carlone; high altar painting: Franz Werner Tamm; side altar paintings: Johann Michael Rottmayr and Johann Karl von Reslfeld; carvings, stucco: Johann Josef Wanscher; statues, high altar: Johann Christoph Jobst?

1ecaa6cc-9678-575c-974d-6bc822ccfe3c.name: *Sala terrena*
1ecaa6cc-9678-575c-974d-6bc822ccfe3c.description: The hall by the passageway to the garden features a segmented vault. It is decorated, like the chateau floors, with stuccowork containing “mirrors” filled with painted scenes from Ovid's *Metamorphoses*, figures of gods and muses.

1ed39711-b2cf-5d1f-b9ad-2e38cdf83f46.name: Plague Column
1ed39711-b2cf-5d1f-b9ad-2e38cdf83f46.description: The column, crowned by the Virgin Mary vanquisher of evil, was erected in gratitude to the end of the plague epidemic. It was among the first columns of its kind in Moravia.

1f032a67-deee-55f1-8090-6e0160ac5a61.name: High Altar of St. Blaise
1f032a67-deee-55f1-8090-6e0160ac5a61.description: A combination of white and polychrome marble make up the altar, conceived as custodial with the statue of the saint. The domed antependium has two angels unveiling a curtain in front of a medallion, while a high niche contains a silver statue of St. Blaise –richly decorated with volutes, acanthus leaves,  figures and heads of angels – rising from the mensa. Two kneeling angels with outspread wings in an emotion-laden attitude of prayer and adoration, flank the central composition. This altar, typical of the Baroque aspiration towards dynamism and opulent colour, is typologically consistent with the group of altars created under the influence of Baltazar Longhena, and his altar in the Church of S. Lorenzo Giustiniani in Venice.

1f6a275f-c79d-5523-8152-e66ee749a6b7.name: Façade
1f6a275f-c79d-5523-8152-e66ee749a6b7.description: The double-tower façade of St. Jacob is a Late Baroque interpretation of a basic plan based on the Salzburg Dome. The projecting towers – which form a unit with the two-storey middle section – are characteristic. In contrast to Salzburg the transitions are more fluent, employing concave wall sections. The vertical oval windows of the upper storeys establish a number of thematic accents. The towers’ upper storeys are also more powerfully built than in Salzburg.
1f6a275f-c79d-5523-8152-e66ee749a6b7.artist: Johann Jakob Herkomer (1648–1717); Johann Georg Fischer (1673–1747)

1f723fe3-b757-5082-bdf0-c8a3679a96b4.name: Main Chapel
1f723fe3-b757-5082-bdf0-c8a3679a96b4.description: The main altar is composed of the tribune and the throne, it includes four figures: St. Vincent Ferrer and St Thomas Aquinas (inferior) and St. Francis of Assisi and St. Dominic (superior). At the top is Christ Crucified. The main chapel ceiling is of gilt wood, carved with geometric motifs based on circles and half circles.

1fd944dc-83c6-5e83-8dba-701c2a61c3e2.name: *Death of the Virgin* (smaller central medallion)
1fd944dc-83c6-5e83-8dba-701c2a61c3e2.description: Small octagonal medallion showing a representation of the Death of the Virgin inspired by the mannerist engravings of Adrien Collaert and Cornelis Galle.
1fd944dc-83c6-5e83-8dba-701c2a61c3e2.artist: António de Oliveira Bernardes (1662–1732) and Pedro Figueira [n.d.]

201812fd-d2db-54ba-a3b4-511d30b9e0b9.name: Church (architecture and interior)
201812fd-d2db-54ba-a3b4-511d30b9e0b9.description:
When a destroyed monastery complex was rebuilt after a war or a fire, they usually started with the church. Or with the church towers, as was done in Lambach, where they put new towers on the three-storey Romanesque base. After a modernization of the cloister and the monks´ cells they built up the church, which has survived as a stylistically pure Baroque building.  
Corresponding with the façade’s double pilasters, there are double pilasters along the nave´s walls. They are crowned by a mighty continuous entablature as well as by fresco paintings and decorative stucco works in the vault. The bright yellow/ochre colour on walls and vault is original. It had been covered with a white layer for many decades and was only some years ago re-painted. The interior is magnificent: the high altar dedicated to the Ascension of the Holy Virgin was probably executed by Antonio Beduzzi, following Fischer´s von Erlach high altar model in the Mariazell basilica. Here and there dominate mighty columns; in Lambach everything is climaxing in the sculptural Holy Trinity scenery above. The huge paintings at the high altar and side altars were executed by Joachim von Sandrart and employees.
201812fd-d2db-54ba-a3b4-511d30b9e0b9.dates: 1639 church towers; 1652–56 church; 1652–61 paintings high altar and side altars; about 1655 stucco work vault; 1662 wrought iron grill; 1698 fresco paintings finished; 1716–17 high altar
201812fd-d2db-54ba-a3b4-511d30b9e0b9.location: In the middle of the South wing
201812fd-d2db-54ba-a3b4-511d30b9e0b9.artist: Possibly Filiberto Lucchese: architecture; Joachim von Sandrart and employees: altar paintings; probably Thomas Zaisel: stucco work vault, unknown: wrought iron grill; Melchior Steidl: most of the fresco paintings; presumably Antonio Beduzzi: high altar

205ab685-f8e2-5231-8359-9f897f061f3f.name: Glory of Moravia
205ab685-f8e2-5231-8359-9f897f061f3f.description: An obelisk, symbol of eternity, carries the emblem of Moravia. The upper section of the main element of the ceiling painting features a zodiac, the eternal cycle of time. The personifications of the sun and moon at the sides accentuate the eternal validity of the central slogan being unfurled by Fame.

205f5fe6-49cb-5a4d-b9c3-c51371b87a31.name: Transfiguration of St. Gordian and Epimachus
205f5fe6-49cb-5a4d-b9c3-c51371b87a31.description: By means of their space-extending illusory architecture, the ceiling frescoes are reminiscent of those of Andrea Pozzo in Sant’Ignazio in Rome, where Franz Georg Herrmann must have visited during a study sojourn in 1712/13. The apotheosis of St. Epimachus with reference to his death in a furnace of fire illustrated in the nave compliments that of St. Gordian including a representation of this previously beheaded martyr. Circular cartouches contain grisaille images of the Four Church Fathers and Twelve Apostles. Parish priest Klein appears, accompanied by the sacristan, on the lower band of the illusory cupola as an observer on a balcony, that is to say, as mediator between heaven and earth. Thus, the devout observer is shown the possibility of reaching heaven for which the illusory cupola symbolically stands. Through the open crown glass window, a bird (whose German compound name “Dompfaff” [bullfinch] ironically alludes to the dome as well as to the priest)  flies to the left of the balcony into the interior of the cupola which provides the illusion of additional closeness to reality by evoking liveliness.

20d4c368-8578-553c-ae8e-72509b27e2b6.name: Interior
20d4c368-8578-553c-ae8e-72509b27e2b6.description: The interior, which is accessed through a small vestibule, is characterised by a sequence of two central spatial units: the congregation room in the form of a rotunda with octagonal arcade and a cupola with skylight turret, and the choir, a transverse rectangular room appended to the eastern arcade. This building design distinguishes the church in Strassen as a later, overall, simplified successor to the Mary Help Church in Innsbruck, and also cites the main features of the Roman Pantheon.

22026d59-be17-5e0a-be64-306b59e6655b.name: Monument to the brothers Giovan Battista and Ippolito Fornasari
22026d59-be17-5e0a-be64-306b59e6655b.description: This double portrait depicts two brothers, both Law professors in the University of Bologna. It hangs over the door, on one side of the Bulgari chapel and dominates the great allegorical fresco representing Dawn and Sunset, Justice and Right, a typical expression of baroque complicated symbolism. It is a typical example of the variety of materials employed to build this sort of monument: pictorial decoration, plaster, metal and sandstone.
22026d59-be17-5e0a-be64-306b59e6655b.location: Palazzo of the Archiginnasio, ground floor

224f5f0e-a3d6-5685-8342-9a71082c79cc.name: Ground plan
224f5f0e-a3d6-5685-8342-9a71082c79cc.description: The principal compositional element is a five-pointed star (five-pointed ground plan, five entrances, five altar niches, ten chapels surrounding the central space, five stars and five angels on the high altar), symbolising the five wounds of Christ, five letters in the Latin word *tacui* (“I was silent”) and, in particular, five stars in the halo of St. John of Nepomuk. Legend has it that the stars appeared in the River Vltava after the martyr had been drowned in it.

235845e0-01ae-56d0-98b0-c0f500d34224.name: Ceiling decoration
235845e0-01ae-56d0-98b0-c0f500d34224.description:
Huge fresco paintings and rich, white or coloured or gilded stucco are the ceiling’s decoration. The fresco paintings were done by Bartolomeo Altomonte (figure) and Francesco Messenta (architecture), the stucco work in the nave was executed by an Austrian plasterer.  
The Austrian War of Succession interrupted the work in the church, the Bavarian elector Karl Albrecht (the enemy) was promptly accommodated in the monastery. It was probably under his influence that Bavarian plasterers, who were familiar with the new Rococo style, came to Wilhering and continued the stucco work in the church. Nonetheless, the abbot insisted that the decoration in the transepts and in the sanctuary had to conform to that in the nave’s vault. Even as there are many different details – the small unit design was given up in favour of a liberal ornamentation, trendy “C” Rocaille ornaments were added and the transition from painting to stucco was done in different ways – the ceiling decoration looks as if it was one harmonious work of art.
235845e0-01ae-56d0-98b0-c0f500d34224.artist: Bartolomeo Altomonte; Francesco Messenta; Franz Joseph Ignaz Holzinger; Johann Georg Üblherr; Johann Michael Feichtmayr

2382fcce-cee1-5bd1-804e-fa17b3a3d4a6.name: Madonna of Old Brno
2382fcce-cee1-5bd1-804e-fa17b3a3d4a6.description: This picture of the Virgin Mary and Child is set inside a stucco frame carried by angels and surrounded by figures of Saints Michael and Sebastian. Similar altars were created for numerous churches and chapels after the coronation of this miraculous picture of the “protectress of the country” in Brno in 1736.
2382fcce-cee1-5bd1-804e-fa17b3a3d4a6.artist: Jan Jiří Schauberger (?, before 1725 Vienna, active in Olomouc – 1744 Brno)

23c2707d-7414-5ebc-9fee-17b21b79755f.name: Ceiling frescos
23c2707d-7414-5ebc-9fee-17b21b79755f.description: The ceiling frescos are an important work of the court painter of Brixen, Franz Anton Zeiller, from 1768. In the cupola he utilised the division into eight panels for the realisation of two cycles: four scenes from the Life of Mary (left) and the Jesuit missionary Francis Xavier (1506–52, right) respectively. The latter depicts the activities of the saint in India, Japan and on the Moluccas as well as his martyrdom above the organ parapet. Despite the different scenes, Zeiller succeeded in lending the cupola a unified overall appearance, effectively uniting events into a single panorama.

24ba5fbf-af5a-56e0-95d5-e55bcb037df9.name: Garden: central level (images 1, 2 and 3) and a 20th-century addition (4)
24ba5fbf-af5a-56e0-95d5-e55bcb037df9.description: In the intermediate rectangular terrace divided into three longitudinal axes with a central lake and four others at the corners, granite sculptures represent the Four Seasons, the Four Continents, the Four Elements, signs of the Zodiac, and the Three Theological Virtues. The 20th-century level is furnished with *azulejos* depicting the Bishops of Castelo Branco.

24ec6e48-1e49-57da-8b31-cb3cc3c40a0c.name: Muse
24ec6e48-1e49-57da-8b31-cb3cc3c40a0c.description: The quadrature contains figures of the Muses, without whose help fame and prosperity are unthinkable. The detail shows the engraved under-drawing.
24ec6e48-1e49-57da-8b31-cb3cc3c40a0c.artist: Daniel Gran (1694 Vienna – 1757 St. Pölten), Gaetano Fanti (1687 Bologna – 1759 Vienna)

2526f022-a75b-57ec-834d-4ab4413501d1.name: Chapel of the Holy Blood
2526f022-a75b-57ec-834d-4ab4413501d1.description: The medieval chapel annex was built before the monastery church in the Baroque style. Of special interest is the cupola structure with shallow tribune erected to replace the former apse. The quarter of the cross vault with chamfered corners and massive piers occupied by pilasters, form four large arcades with wide semicircular arches, which in turn support the cupola. The High Baroque design of the central space is derived from the type of crossing found in St. Peter’s in Rome (cf. Rattenberg).
2526f022-a75b-57ec-834d-4ab4413501d1.location: Chapel annex, southwest of the abbey church

254423af-fde7-552f-b490-c82fbb4023ad.name: High altar
254423af-fde7-552f-b490-c82fbb4023ad.description: The high altar, designed by Schnegg, with its prospect of dark-red marbled pillars, forms the focal point of the enfilade. The altar painting of the highest quality is probably the work of Maulpertsch who painted the Riesensaal in Innsbruck at about this time. The brilliantly polished white sculptures, which stand out from the church’s brightly coloured interior, depict, amongst others, the patrons of the diocese of Brixen. The monumental, but nonetheless elegant figures are of striking quality.

25b397ce-e589-53c6-b2f5-884c9b6d6745.name: Chapel of St. Pauline
25b397ce-e589-53c6-b2f5-884c9b6d6745.description: Andrýsek’s original chapel stood until 1677 but was pulled down during the course of the construction of the new church. The frescos commemorate the origins of the pilgrimage site. The altarpiece represents the Olomouc patroness whose remains were donated to the Olomouc Jesuits by Pope Gregory XV in 1623. The procession held as part of the transfer of the relics was said to have thwarted the plague.
25b397ce-e589-53c6-b2f5-884c9b6d6745.artist: Paul Troger (1698 Zell, near Welsberg – 1762 Vienna)

25d59ad7-f146-5a66-b99c-640d389ce20d.name: Altar of St. Barbara
25d59ad7-f146-5a66-b99c-640d389ce20d.description: Like its match, the Altar of St. Joseph, it is framed with a *trompe\-l'œil* painting of luxurious drapery rather than architectural elements. The role of the structural parts, overtaken by decorative and figural motifs such as volutes and *putti*, makes for the altar's picturesque and extremely dynamic sculptural programme.
25d59ad7-f146-5a66-b99c-640d389ce20d.location: Along the southern side of the triumphal arch, Parish Church of Our Lady of the Snow

25ede1f2-8f70-5252-9d21-3b21a63183bf.name: The Apostle Peter
25ede1f2-8f70-5252-9d21-3b21a63183bf.description: The bust, in relief of the Apostle Peter, opens onto the entrance of the chapel with six reliefs – originally gilded – of Old Testament scenes featuring motifs of sacrifice and thanksgiving by the same sculptor. Sattler also collaborated with V. Render on the Olomouc fountains.

261d6cf2-f4d5-5ea8-a4c4-7c1fe310d8d9.name: Library
261d6cf2-f4d5-5ea8-a4c4-7c1fe310d8d9.description: The library equipment was enabled by a generous donation from Baron Trenck who is mummified in the monastery crypt. The ceiling painting represents John Bonaventura showing a crucifix to Thomas Aquinas in response to a query as to the origin of the sources of his writings. One remarkable item is a human skeleton in a display case amidst the other library cases. The skeleton was used for anatomy studies and also symbolised, within the library iconography, a *memento mori*.
261d6cf2-f4d5-5ea8-a4c4-7c1fe310d8d9.location: Capuchin Monastery and the Church of the Invention of the Holy Cross, Brno
261d6cf2-f4d5-5ea8-a4c4-7c1fe310d8d9.artist: Josef Stern (1716 Graz – 1775 Brno), Ondřej Schweigl (1735–1812 Brno)

26371767-cb3f-5ce5-9d43-eccf210c490a.name: Collateral Altarpiece
26371767-cb3f-5ce5-9d43-eccf210c490a.description: Both collateral altarpieces are very similar, made of gilt carved wood  and flanked by pilasters decorated with acanthus leaves.
26371767-cb3f-5ce5-9d43-eccf210c490a.location: Church interior, Sanctuary of Our Lady of Good Remedy
26371767-cb3f-5ce5-9d43-eccf210c490a.artist: Frei José de Santo António Ferreira (active1764-66)

267869f3-46a7-515e-bdba-038ab6a15510.name: *Glory of the Benedictine Order*
267869f3-46a7-515e-bdba-038ab6a15510.description: The large dome fresco glorifies, approved by the Holy Trinity, the mission of the Benedictine Order in terms of God’s plan for salvation and includes several hundred figures.

272076e8-33b2-5acd-b85d-2a9e6720b295.name: Child Jesus teaching the Virgin
272076e8-33b2-5acd-b85d-2a9e6720b295.description: Focusing on their lesson, Jesus and Mary appear to be engaged in a private interaction but are welcoming the viewer to join them.
272076e8-33b2-5acd-b85d-2a9e6720b295.artist: António de Oliveira Bernardes (1662–1732) and Pedro Figueira [n.d.]

27858881-8a57-5007-898c-050ab30f7f2b.name: Detail of side walls and terrace
27858881-8a57-5007-898c-050ab30f7f2b.location: North, south and east exterior walls

28637f70-e837-5910-a49b-bc2c9584b6d0.name: View of the Sanctuary
28637f70-e837-5910-a49b-bc2c9584b6d0.description: Late Baroque synthesis of a longitudinal and central space.

295ff35d-32e4-5be1-bd84-aedc22f9baff.name: Silver Antependium
295ff35d-32e4-5be1-bd84-aedc22f9baff.description: The antependium is covered with opulent *Rocaille* ornamentation with interwoven volutes and plant motifs. In the central field, there is a depiction of *Christ in Emmaus* in relief.

2998d470-389c-50c8-ac89-55c0122ce826.name: *St. Sebastian*
2998d470-389c-50c8-ac89-55c0122ce826.description: The strongly bent figure of St. Sebastian, shown in agony, fixes his gaze on the sky. This is a perfect example of Marchiori’s flawless mastery of the human figure.

2a8f2ad2-0175-5d0b-b8ba-1b55369ff2d5.name: Façade
2a8f2ad2-0175-5d0b-b8ba-1b55369ff2d5.description: The façade, with its two lightly projecting towers framing the two-storey central section structured in three vertical axes with tail gable, is a later successor to Salzburg Cathedral. However, they are quite different in character – the Early Baroque model appears considerably bulkier and more austere, the Early Classicist successor more two-dimensional and with finer proportions and structure.

2c0658b1-af70-5e4f-a9aa-8724f6488ff4.name: *St Mary of Help*
2c0658b1-af70-5e4f-a9aa-8724f6488ff4.description: The central image – after the well-known “miraculous” icon by Lucas Cranach the Elder – is “carried” by angels over a representation of 18th-century Osijek.

2d0471bd-dce3-5e4b-8f73-fac127443f2d.name: St. John of Nepomuk
2d0471bd-dce3-5e4b-8f73-fac127443f2d.description: Among the Jesuits, the popular confessor and bridge saint enjoyed special reverence as protector of the successful order against hostility based on envy.

2dabfc2d-d0c7-5629-b60d-d85fe2d540f8.name: *The Coronation of the Virgin*
2dabfc2d-d0c7-5629-b60d-d85fe2d540f8.description: Above the frieze decorated with many golden stuccoes opens the dome, decorated with semi columns and rosettes. The open sky frames the Virgin as she is lifted to heaven to be crowned by the angels. The complex spatial articulation along with the violently vertical scene and the rapid succession of grounds achieves perfect foreshortening, a good example of the high level of Mitelli and Colonna’s achievements in decorative painting. The two painters are perfectly at ease working together so it is practically impossible to tell the different hands.
2dabfc2d-d0c7-5629-b60d-d85fe2d540f8.location: Dome of the square antechamber of the chapel of the Rosary, Basilica di San Domenico, Bologna
2dabfc2d-d0c7-5629-b60d-d85fe2d540f8.artist: Angelo Michele Colonna and Agostino Mitelli

2dd05ca7-8405-5c54-83a9-e8196103e37b.name: Altar of St. Benedict (high altar of the abbey church)
2dd05ca7-8405-5c54-83a9-e8196103e37b.description: The high altar, including the interior façade of the sacristy and the monk’s choir through the figure niches, is the oldest part of the valuable furnishing of the abbey church with marble altars. In the course of time, the columned aedicule of the retable was supplemented by a tabernacle and a new altarpiece that shows St. Benedict, the founder of the order, together with his sister Scholastica, as well as by an attic, the large clock of which is a reminder of the passing of time.
2dd05ca7-8405-5c54-83a9-e8196103e37b.dates:
1686 mensa, retable, and sculptures in niches  
1696 tabernacle  
1788 altarpiece  
1790 attic of the retable and tabernacle figures
2dd05ca7-8405-5c54-83a9-e8196103e37b.artist: Architecture of the altar: Johann Georg Guggemos (1636–1703); sculptures in niches and angels: Balthasar Ableithner (1614–1705); architecture of the tabernacle: Abbot Eliland Öttl (gov. 1690–1707); tabernacle figures: Roman Anton Boos (1733–1810); attic of the retable: Franz Edmund Doll (1744–1824); altarpiece: Martin Knoller (1725–1804)

2de50028-8802-5489-81a8-475ca9843c1d.name: Painted ceiling with Hercules in Olympus
2de50028-8802-5489-81a8-475ca9843c1d.description: Inside an architectonic frame with putti and corbels, culminating with a balustraded terrace, opens a square of blue sky. In the middle is Jupiter, sitting on an eagle; beneath him are Hercules and Athena. The goddess introduces the demigod to Jupiter and the father of the Gods gets hold of his wrist and points to the sky; among the clouds, in the background, are visible Neptune, Mars and Venus. The decoration is attributed to the Bolognese painters Agostino Mitelli e Angelo Michele Colonna by a guidebook. In any case the author can be identified with a Bolognese painter of the second half of the sixteenth-century, next to the Rolli brothers or to Domenico Maria Canuti.
2de50028-8802-5489-81a8-475ca9843c1d.artist: Bolognese painter of the second half of the sixteenth-century

2e2ac7b9-9a35-592e-8a89-a59d984fe48d.name: Choir fresco
2e2ac7b9-9a35-592e-8a89-a59d984fe48d.description: The frescos were conceived by Zeiller as a unified system of decoration for the vault zone, including the painted stucco and frames for the picture panels. The relatively small ceiling picture in the choir is surrounded by a broad zone executed in painted stucco (“stucco finto”). It depicts St. Nicholas as helper of the sick, the imprisoned and the destitute, whereby some of the figures are residents of Elbigenalp (the prisoners and a number of the women in the traditional dress of Lechtal).

2e551a44-ed15-554e-b118-1f8beb1b9f7d.name: The Virgin Mary of Old Brno
2e551a44-ed15-554e-b118-1f8beb1b9f7d.description: This picture of the Virgin Mary is named after its second location. It was the palladium of Brno, a miraculous picture (Thaumaturga) of the Madonna and Child donated to the Augustinian Monastery in Brno by Emperor Charles IV. Members of major Moravian aristocratic families were traditionally wedded before the Thaumaturga. The reliquary, originally embedded in the child’s heart, makes up the clasp of the Madonna’s dress. Relief letters, gilded crowns with precious stones, and a chain come from the period of the picture’s coronation and its incorporation into the new altar. The image was credited with the salvation of Brno from the Swedish siege at the end of the Thirty Years’ War, as well as with healing properties and other miracles.

2e812fa6-2d65-5e3f-9d13-bcf1bf2111af.name: Country house
2e812fa6-2d65-5e3f-9d13-bcf1bf2111af.description: The picturesque undulating effects of volute gables and ledges also appeared far beyond the main square, on country houses and farmhouses.

2eb1f102-370e-5a15-aa76-966aead4921b.name: Ceiling fresco of the Great Hall
2eb1f102-370e-5a15-aa76-966aead4921b.description: The ceiling fresco of the Great Hall was once the world’s largest. Illustrating the fight between Aeneas and Turnus for the hand of the king’s daughter Lavinia, Aeneas, it is sometimes said resembles the Elector Max II Emanuel. The use of a painted landscape background instead of *trompe-l’oeil* architectural decoration was novel at the time.
2eb1f102-370e-5a15-aa76-966aead4921b.location: New Palace, first floor of the central wing

2ebf8277-f8ab-5fe5-967c-f6c53d3534cd.name: Façade
2ebf8277-f8ab-5fe5-967c-f6c53d3534cd.description: Of the exterior, executed in the strict forms of North Alpine Early Baroque with little ornamentation, only the front side of the vestibule has been designed as a visible face in the form of a large aedicula, or shrine. Double pilasters of the Ionic order support a wide triangular gable. This form is repeated using simple pilasters in the main portal. The open ridge turret above the vestibule for the chimes is a 19th-century ingredient, although it had a smaller Baroque predecessor.

2f3b7be6-81ba-55c8-a553-1e425e26df8b.name: Cupola painting of the crossing
2f3b7be6-81ba-55c8-a553-1e425e26df8b.description: The large, circular dome fresco is surrounded by four stucco cartouches with pictures of the evangelists that show the wonder of Whitsun and its meaning for the worldwide mission of the church. The architectural scenery of the step-platforms, balustrades and surrounding obelisks is typical of the art of *mise en scène* used for composing ceiling paintings.
2f3b7be6-81ba-55c8-a553-1e425e26df8b.location: Crossing vault of the abbey church

2fdaa7f1-4e56-566b-acd3-10ab6e8daf23.name: Church and mausoleum (architecture)
2fdaa7f1-4e56-566b-acd3-10ab6e8daf23.description:
Because of the Habsburgs’ poor financial situation Hans Ulrich von Eggenberg, archduke Ferdinand´s privy councillor, (co-)funded the complex´s building. Pietro de Pomis, the versatile artist from the court in Graz and architect of the Eggenberg Mausoleum in Ehrenhausen, was commissioned with the construction. He planned a classic façade with three-quarter columns, a triangular gable in the attic area and three huge statues (allegedly by Sebastian Erlacher) on the roof. The narrow building site was even narrower than today: a covered corridor connected the mausoleum with the university opposite. It existed until the 19th century when the staircase was added and from then on one could see the façade.  
De Pomis changed his first draft in 1619/20. He had knocked off a lot of the stucco and added the two segment gables. The larger one is framing the triangular gable, following the *Il Gesù* façade in Rome. The two triumphal arches, lying on top of each other, symbolise the Catholic restoration.  
After the death of Pietro de Pomis, Pietro Valnegro took over the completion of the church and the mausoleum. He built the tower and finished the roofing work. In a final step he crowned the cupolas with symbols of power, and the tower’s highest part with a sceptre. Despite the proximity to the Catholic church this should indicate the secular sovereign’s primacy.
2fdaa7f1-4e56-566b-acd3-10ab6e8daf23.dates: 1614 start of building; after 1619/20 the tower was planned and the façade’s two segment gables were added; 1622 start of the roofing work; about 1635/36 statues on the roof; 1635–36 building of the tower; 1637 roofing work finished
2fdaa7f1-4e56-566b-acd3-10ab6e8daf23.artist: Giovanni Pietro de Pomis: plans church and mausoleum; Pietro Valnegro: new construction manager after de Pomis´ death; (probably) Sebastian Erlacher: statues on the roof

3020bc51-e533-5d86-89b0-6e9d0322a563.name: *The sharing of St. Martin’s coat*
3020bc51-e533-5d86-89b0-6e9d0322a563.description: One of the side altarpieces of the Baroque interior altered in the 19th century, from the Veronese painter Giuseppe Gru. The saint, here on foot and in shining armour, shares his red coat with the beggar; above him three groups of angels are floating, of which two are depicted in the form of busts.
3020bc51-e533-5d86-89b0-6e9d0322a563.location: Altarpiece of the right-hand side altar

3056a9a2-f0a3-5c02-bb5f-90e9ed6e1a41.name: Organ in the High Choir
3056a9a2-f0a3-5c02-bb5f-90e9ed6e1a41.description: In the High Choir there is an Iberian organ with two symmetrical parts: the organ itself on the Epistle side and the organ pipes on the Gospel side. Friar Manuel Lourenço da Conceição from Oporto might have recycled some parts from a pre-existing organ, and Manuel Pinto de Vila Lobos designed the case.
3056a9a2-f0a3-5c02-bb5f-90e9ed6e1a41.artist:
Organ: Frei Manuel Lourenço da Conceição \[n.d.\]  
Organ cases: Manuel Pinto de Vila Lobos \[n.d.\]

30aa54c0-7c8c-5018-a50a-f4a69c3b0d3a.name: Nave ceiling
30aa54c0-7c8c-5018-a50a-f4a69c3b0d3a.description: The *trompe l'œil* ceiling paintings include the *Assumption of Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception* in the central medallion, flanked by allegories of the Four Continents and female figures from the Old Testament.

30d612d9-c8f3-5dd4-bb07-8c2e5ddb2e41.name: Stucco decoration and paintings in the Chapel of St. Anthony
30d612d9-c8f3-5dd4-bb07-8c2e5ddb2e41.description: While the stuccowork in Our Lady of the Scapular Chapel facing it is the work of the  Styrian practitioner, J. A. Quadrio, the Chapel of St. Anthony has stuccowork made later by an unknown author. Interwoven plants and ribbons frame eight medallions depicting the Life of St. Anthony of Padua, painted by Ivan Krstitelj Ranger, in around 1738.
30d612d9-c8f3-5dd4-bb07-8c2e5ddb2e41.artist: Stuccowork: unknown artist; painter: Ivan Krstitelj (Johann Baptist) Krstitelj Ranger (1700–1753)

31608556-6fc2-52c1-ac53-e69ab20e76f6.name: Ceiling fresco: *The Acceptance into Heaven of St. Stephen*
31608556-6fc2-52c1-ac53-e69ab20e76f6.description: The Anras frescos are the earliest independent works of Martin Knoller and are still wholly under the influence of his teacher Paul Troger. The nave fresco depicts the acceptance into heaven of the church patron, St. Stephan, as well as the discovery of his remains. The relatively small fresco panels are framed by “stucco finto” (painted stucco) in the forms of the early Rococo and are also the work of Knoller.

31665f9b-25fe-5a8b-826f-d66f78bb5ec6.name: Altar of St. Ulrich
31665f9b-25fe-5a8b-826f-d66f78bb5ec6.description: The monumental scagliola marble altar is furnished with an anonymous painting depicting the second subsidiary patron the Holy Bishop from Augsburg – St. Ulrich – together with Emperor Otto I riding to battle against the Hungarians and thereby receiving the cross-relic which brings victory.

31788a7e-54f2-5c5b-8dda-c0fc298370ec.name: Side Chapel, left (Holy Sacrament Chapel)
31788a7e-54f2-5c5b-8dda-c0fc298370ec.location: Interior, Sanctuary of Bom Jesus de Matosinhos
31788a7e-54f2-5c5b-8dda-c0fc298370ec.artist: Portuguese woodcarvers: Luís Pereira da Costa (active 1724–?), Domingos Martins Moreira (active 1746–1750)

31a2ed6c-a768-5550-a180-6fecff19b3b0.name: Exterior, south façade
31a2ed6c-a768-5550-a180-6fecff19b3b0.description: Designed by Gumpp in 1754, the Hofgasse Wing was completed according to his plans by 1756. The centre of the wing is composed of a monumental portal projection in the form of a gabled triumphal arch encompassing all four storeys. It is only here that Johann Martin Gumpp’s façade conception has been realised completely in accordance with his ideas. The influence of his brother Georg Anton’s country house façade is evident. The ponderous Late Baroque style has been adjusted to contemporary taste with the addition of rocaille work on the windows.

31a85a61-1ef8-530b-8b89-bfb3cb6f169d.name: Memorial Chapel for Emperor Franz I
31a85a61-1ef8-530b-8b89-bfb3cb6f169d.description: On the order of Maria Theresa the room in which the emperor died in August 1765 was converted into a memorial chapel by Pacassi and an endowment for ladies of rank was founded in his honour. The hall, structured with pilasters, is adorned with gentle rocaille stucco of which the tribune features a painted relief group of God the Father with mourning angels from Franz Anton Leitensdorffer (1721–95).

325eca5c-64d7-58b2-89f1-6abe22c7de12.name: Annunciation to Mary, so-called "Angelic Salutation"
325eca5c-64d7-58b2-89f1-6abe22c7de12.description: In 1764, the graceful wooden sculpture and its counterpart, the pietà, were created as processional statues for the Rosary Brotherhood that had been installed in the abbey church. On a small console, a realistically coloured, life-sized group of sculptures rests with an unobtrusive, yet room-filling presence. The depiction of Mary's humble posture, as Archangel Gabriel is dancingly gliding in, achieves a supreme compositional density.
325eca5c-64d7-58b2-89f1-6abe22c7de12.location: On the left side of the chancel arch
325eca5c-64d7-58b2-89f1-6abe22c7de12.artist: Sculptures: Ignaz Günther (1725–75); painted coating: Nikolaus Nepaur

32a8ad1d-7f6d-50f5-86ce-2904db9b8e81.name: Façade
32a8ad1d-7f6d-50f5-86ce-2904db9b8e81.description: The façade, whose towers, gables and escutcheons were first completed in 1900, i.e. supplemented, most clearly show the influence of the Salzburg Dome. The exterior is maintained in the strict arrangement typical of South German Early Baroque. The towers and the centre of the façade form a unit. The two portal arches, separated by double pilasters (cf. St. Michael’s Church, Munich) already anticipate the configuration of the interior nave walls.

32b1e458-9669-5b2a-91d1-0cb33372a953.name: The lateral altars of the Chapterhouse
32b1e458-9669-5b2a-91d1-0cb33372a953.description: These were perhaps, originally, part of the main chapel and sacristy until the reign of King João III (1521–1557). The two lateral altars were installed during the reigns of King João V (r.1706–1750) and King José I (r.1750–1777). One is dedicated to the Death of Christ the other to Our Lady of Good Death.
32b1e458-9669-5b2a-91d1-0cb33372a953.location: Connected to the nave of the church

338396c3-a01f-5150-a791-09d9535bcffb.name: View of the church from the counter façade
338396c3-a01f-5150-a791-09d9535bcffb.description: The presbiterium (sixteenth century) is connected to the nave (seventeenth – eighteenth centuries) by an imposing triumphal arch, supported by two free standing columns.
338396c3-a01f-5150-a791-09d9535bcffb.artist: Domenico Tibaldi; Pietro Fiorini; Floriano Ambrosini; Giovanni Ambrogio Magenta; Alfonso Torreggiani

33bda0f2-7ee5-5ec5-a93c-d5ad872cb9d3.name: Mausoleum for Archduke Maximilian III, the German Master
33bda0f2-7ee5-5ec5-a93c-d5ad872cb9d3.description: The bronze mausoleum, part of the inventory of the previous building, was designed by Hubert Gerhart from Munich and was completed by Caspar Gras of Innsbruck. It is one of the most important early Baroque mausoleums, with lifelike expressiveness, above all in the depiction of the Archduke who was Grand Master of the German Order of Knights, and St. George, the order’s patron saint. The superstructure is formed of four spiral columns ranked with vines, populated by all manner of animals.
33bda0f2-7ee5-5ec5-a93c-d5ad872cb9d3.location: Left transept apse, St. Jacob’s Cathedral
33bda0f2-7ee5-5ec5-a93c-d5ad872cb9d3.artist: Hubert Gerhard (c. 1545–1623); Caspar Gras (1585–1674); Heinrich Reinhart (1575–1629)

33e67493-5004-5c1c-a3c3-fa98674ddebb.name: Marin and Anian Altar (High Altar)
33e67493-5004-5c1c-a3c3-fa98674ddebb.description: The high altar is the focal point of the spatial sequence, with its mighty columned retable confidently expanding over the pilaster arcade intended as its frame. In addition to the thematised Martyrdom of the church patrons within the fresco cycle, the altar piece displays their glory. Famous examples of Rococo sculpture are the standing figures due to their exalted, elegant poses and hidden irony: near the south German diocesan patrons, the Corbinian associated bear senses the fish attribute of Ulrich. In regard to the holy imperial couple, Heinrich II turns away jealously from his wife, Kunigunde, because she was accused of adultery. Insultingly, she absolves the test of virtue imposed on her by casually tapping a smouldering ploughshare with her bare foot.
33e67493-5004-5c1c-a3c3-fa98674ddebb.artist: Altar and Sculptures: Ignaz Günther (1725–75); Altar piece: Joseph Hartmann

340f6fef-9b1b-5389-8915-7000eae390e7.name: *Mercy*
340f6fef-9b1b-5389-8915-7000eae390e7.description: In a niche above the pulpit sits the allegorical figure of *Mercy*, moulded in stucco by Angelo Gabriello Piò.
340f6fef-9b1b-5389-8915-7000eae390e7.location: Interior, Church of Sant'Agostino in San Michele

34bb86f6-37dc-5242-9419-abe2436ed8e4.name: Stairway (general view)
34bb86f6-37dc-5242-9419-abe2436ed8e4.description: The design for the staircase was drawn up in 1777. Building began in 1781 and continued until 1969.
34bb86f6-37dc-5242-9419-abe2436ed8e4.location: Exterior, Sanctuary of Our Lady of Good Remedy

35987b22-22f6-548e-b0dc-11837fe3e5cf.name: Ceiling fresco and stucco
35987b22-22f6-548e-b0dc-11837fe3e5cf.description: The ceiling paintings from Joseph Adam Mölck (inscribed and dated 1761) depict the acceptance into heaven of St. Andrew who is simultaneously presented as the intercessor for the city of Lienz, surrounded by the four evangelists in the vault caps. Thus, together with the altarpiece, the path of salvation is illustrated on the basis of the legend of the church patron. The fresco opens up a view of heaven as a history of the saint as well as a vision of the end of time. The Late Rococo stucco establishes flowing transitions between the lunettes above the high pointed arch windows and the fresco panels, as well as between the fresco panels themselves, thus forming a vivid whole.

36237c2b-4693-554b-a692-0f69275b2d84.name: Ground Plan
36237c2b-4693-554b-a692-0f69275b2d84.description: The new façade designed by André Soares was attached to the existing church designed by Manuel Fernandes da Silva, and which had an exquisite ground plan combining a square and a lozenge.
36237c2b-4693-554b-a692-0f69275b2d84.artist: Manuel Fernandes da Silva [n.d.] and André Soares (1720–1769)

3636a025-d6fb-5112-aadf-5dc2f03d7988.name: Parish Church of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary
3636a025-d6fb-5112-aadf-5dc2f03d7988.description: F. A. Rottal recruited leading artists in his services. The high altar does not feature an altarpiece but, instead, there is a sculpture of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary by J. J. Schauberger. The precious sculpted decoration of the church is complemented by a baptismal font by O. Zahner with a sculpture of Christ’s Baptism on Earth, and side altars and statues on the frontage. The sculptors joined forces in other commissions also.
3636a025-d6fb-5112-aadf-5dc2f03d7988.artist: Filiberto Luchese (1606, Melide – 1666, Vienna), Jan Jiří Schauberger (?, before 1725 Vienna, active in Olomouc – 1744 Brno), Ondřej Zahner (1709 Ettershausen – 1752 Olomouc)

36eb8438-4ed4-581c-8b45-b9a32a850141.name: Nave and Chancel
36eb8438-4ed4-581c-8b45-b9a32a850141.description: View of the main altarpiece with gilt wood carving.

37077acc-2bd2-556b-ada4-0cdd3f56fffb.name: Rua das Amoreiras Arch
37077acc-2bd2-556b-ada4-0cdd3f56fffb.description: Thanks to the architectural risk-taking of Carlos Mardel, the Rua das Amoreiras arch was built between 1746 and 1748. Two things make this monumental structure particularly notable: its innovation, for over the final perpendicular branch of the aqueduct the water galleries from Alcântara run and this had never before been seen; and the engineering – from here the aqueduct turns sharp right to the Mãe d'Água reservoir. The Amoreiras Arch frames the Rua das Amoreiras and represented at one time an “entrance”, as if it were an arch in a defensive wall, highlighting both the exceptional status of this hydraulic masterpiece and its setting.

37d69274-1d0d-51a0-8b8a-bd4be92b778e.name: Paintings and *azulejos* of the nave and main chapel
37d69274-1d0d-51a0-8b8a-bd4be92b778e.description:
The 20 ceiling paintings depicting the Life of the Virgin are by the Marcos da Cruz workshop. The walls are adorned with paintings by Bento Coelho da Silveira. They depict the Life of St. Claire (upper register) and the Life of St. Francis (lower register). Paintings by André Gonçalves decorate the triumphal arch. These feature the Coronation of the Virgin by the Holy Trinity. Paintings of St. Claire and St. Francis flank the archway. The nave *azulejos* are by the Dutch artist, Willem van der Kloet; they were commissioned in Holland. Close to the *rocaille* pulpit are *azulejos* featuring Franciscan monks praying. The *azulejos* in the main chapel are by Jan van Oort.  
These depict the vision of Pope Nicholas V when standing by the body of St. Francis.
37d69274-1d0d-51a0-8b8a-bd4be92b778e.dates: Ceiling paintings: c.1675–1690; triumphal arch paintings: c.1740–50; *azulejos*: 1698–1707; pulpit: 1747–1759; main altar: after 1755
37d69274-1d0d-51a0-8b8a-bd4be92b778e.location: Nave and main chapel, Church and Convent of Madre de Deus
37d69274-1d0d-51a0-8b8a-bd4be92b778e.artist: Painters: Marcos da Cruz [n.d.], Bento Coelho da Silveira (1648–1708), André Gonçalves (1685–1762); tile painters: Jan van Oort [n.d.], Willem van der Kloet [n.d.], Gabriel del Barco (1649–c.1703); woodcarver: Félix Adauto da Cunha (1649–c.1703)

3833a71f-0ae4-54fa-a584-49250b36be5a.name: High Altar of St. Catherine of Alexandria
3833a71f-0ae4-54fa-a584-49250b36be5a.description: The illusionist fresco St. Catherine Among Alexandrine philosophers and Writers is a quality *trompe l'oeil* painting displaying illusionist architecture of the Alexandrian temple with the huge figures of St. Catherine and her collocutors occupying the central part of the composition. The painted space spreads towards the background in almost accurate central perspective. On the sides, just above eye level, are St. Paul on the left and St. Peter on the right, while the attic is dedicated to the Holy Trinity accompanied by angels.
3833a71f-0ae4-54fa-a584-49250b36be5a.location: The sanctuary, eastern wall, Academy Church of St. Catherine

3872b95b-f605-5d55-a762-172880091112.name: The Good Government of Urban VIII
3872b95b-f605-5d55-a762-172880091112.description: The Good Government of Urban VIII, with Dignity in the centre flanked on the left by Prudence and on the right by the Delegated Power which receives a letter and is preparing to leave on a mission; on the left, the Forge of Vulcan, and on the right Peace and Fame.

38a5bbd4-6960-5ff5-882d-383729be2fff.name: *The Miracle of St Servulus*
38a5bbd4-6960-5ff5-882d-383729be2fff.description: Despite moderate *chiaroscuro*, the intense colours of Camerata's painting indicate acceptance of the stylistic features of Rococo.

38ad57d4-b61f-536a-8b64-9601d38d1e4e.name: Courtyard
38ad57d4-b61f-536a-8b64-9601d38d1e4e.description: The ceremonial courtyard is closed off by low out-buildings joined by the entrance gate. In the frontage, by the entrance to the chateau, are allegorical female figures bearing the coats of arms of the Sinzendorfs and Valdštejns. Archduke Friedrich of Habsburg demolished the existing fortifications, filled the moats and reconstructed the chateau in the Empire style. Parts of the side wings of the ceremonial courtyard were lowered and the frontages unified in a Neo-Baroque style. The statues of Saints Anne and Joachim, along with the Virgin Mary and St. Joseph, originally adorned the chapel entrance.

38f8230e-0728-5617-bd21-ae2887da3089.name: St. John of Nepomuk
38f8230e-0728-5617-bd21-ae2887da3089.description: St. John of Nepomuk was a popular saint frequently considered protector of roads and particularly bridges, marking the manner of his death. He was thrown in the Vltava from Charles Bridge in 1393. One obvious difference between the statues by Jelínek and Winterhalder is the relief-segmented cloak, which creates movement and disturbance in order to stir the viewer’s emotions.

39832be8-c5b7-5cfe-931f-9f739df8c80b.name: Organ
39832be8-c5b7-5cfe-931f-9f739df8c80b.description: The relief-shaped organ case is decorated with carved drapery, angels and *putti* playing musical instruments. The Brno master was one of the best-known organists in Moravia.

39c1e1c9-f718-5118-9432-f7a5dd662a06.name: Alcove
39c1e1c9-f718-5118-9432-f7a5dd662a06.description: Made for the marriage of Francesco Tozzoni and Carlotta Beroaldi, the bedroom (alcove), with its yellow tapestry has homogeneous furniture. Former seventeenth-century pieces perfectly match with those made especially for this room.
39c1e1c9-f718-5118-9432-f7a5dd662a06.location: Palazzo Tozzoni, Imola, first floor, baroque apartment

3a82940b-0422-54ce-94e9-7b0610d5dd16.name: Cupola
3a82940b-0422-54ce-94e9-7b0610d5dd16.description: This was the first cupola built in Portugal, similar to that of St. Peter’s in Rome. Sixty-two metres high, it is marble outside and with polychrome marble inside. The cupola has an eight-sided form and eight windows, above which are the sculpted litanies of the Virgin Mary. Forty-one men worked simultaneously on the decoration “very well and at ease”, according to a testimony in contemporary sources.

3a980bd0-16f1-5f78-a2c6-a7b42ae9476d.name: Altar of St. John of Nepomuk
3a980bd0-16f1-5f78-a2c6-a7b42ae9476d.description: An elegant combination of violet and white marble gives the impression of lightness despite the strict classical architectural elements of this altar. Pairs of columns support the architrave and the attic. The central niche, flanked by a pair of columns, holds the sculpture of St. John of Nepomuk while the side sculptures personify Hope and Faith and are much smaller in scale. It is thought that the altar design was from Vienna and the marble imported from Italy. Master sculptors also came from Venice, but it is still uncertain who they were.

3a98ccd2-7a4a-590a-bab6-e7dbee8acf4a.name: *Angels*
3a98ccd2-7a4a-590a-bab6-e7dbee8acf4a.description: An opening shows the viewer the angels of Paradise.

3ada43e4-57c6-5bbc-9913-92e6edad63c2.name: *Penitence*
3ada43e4-57c6-5bbc-9913-92e6edad63c2.description: The figure of *Penitence* was moulded in stucco by Angelo Gabriello Piò.
3ada43e4-57c6-5bbc-9913-92e6edad63c2.location: Interior, Church of Sant'Agostino in San Michele

3b19208b-10e2-5a60-9070-af5dd1de98cb.name: *God the Father in Glory with Angels*
3b19208b-10e2-5a60-9070-af5dd1de98cb.description:
This glory was originally made for the main altar of the dismantled church of St. Gabriel in Bologna. When the religious orders of the church were suppressed (1810) the group was moved to the parish church of Minerbio. Neo-classic architect, Angelo Venturoli managed to preserve the baroque effect of dramatic light “alla Bernini” by opening two hidden side windows. The group was arranged with the help of a nineteenth-century sculptor, Giacomo De Maria, who added some of the angels and clouds.  
This is probably the second experiment of Mazza with the Roman baroque effects of light invented by Bernini and employed in his St. Teresa in Santa Maria della Vittoria in Rome, where a dramatic light coming from a hidden window, sometimes through a coloured glass, emphasises statues in a theatrical way. Mazza had already tried this technique in the small chapel of the Grassi family residence in Bologna (1704), where altar and altarpiece are made of stucco.
3b19208b-10e2-5a60-9070-af5dd1de98cb.location: Upper part of the high altar of the church of St. John the Baptist
3b19208b-10e2-5a60-9070-af5dd1de98cb.artist: Giuseppe Maria Mazza, Angelo Venturoli, Giacomo De Maria

3ba969a6-b8d7-5978-b6e8-6a6fa0e0f59c.name: Fig house and Mosque (pavilion)
3ba969a6-b8d7-5978-b6e8-6a6fa0e0f59c.description:
As typical Baroque building projects, green- and garden houses became fashionable during the 17th century. Long before King Louis XIV of France had the famous orangery built, there was a fig house and a garden pavilion in Kremsmünster. The fig house is said to be the oldest preserved greenhouse in Europe. It is a simple construction of walls (with huge windows in the South and West) and pillars. It was heated by two stoves. In the ground were plant beds framed by stones. The roof was removed in summer.  
The so-called Mosque is an octagonal, single-storey building with a dome and a crescent moon, a corridor of pillars, two aisles and two towers on both sides. Under the room is a water fed grotto with a grid on top for the cooling upwards. The oriental appearance of the building was typical for the passion for the exotic at that time.
3ba969a6-b8d7-5978-b6e8-6a6fa0e0f59c.location: East and opposite of the observatory
3ba969a6-b8d7-5978-b6e8-6a6fa0e0f59c.artist: n.n.: fig house; Pater Aegyd Everard von Raittenau: Mosque

3c4ef2fa-2d0c-53ea-a254-7f42269d568c.name: Sculpture of the Crucifixion
3c4ef2fa-2d0c-53ea-a254-7f42269d568c.description: The monumental bronze sculpture of the Crucifixion once belonged to the former Altar of the Holy Cross, where the mass for the people was read. Thematically, it completes the life-story of Christ narrated in the other altars. The Virgin Mary and John the Evangelist standing beside the cross, as well as Mary Magdalena kneeling at its foot, are shown in lamentation expressed through gestures of grief.
3c4ef2fa-2d0c-53ea-a254-7f42269d568c.location: In front of the choir / behind the modern altar

3c569a1e-c412-5ccf-b034-acfc029ba2ad.name: Interior
3c569a1e-c412-5ccf-b034-acfc029ba2ad.description: The simple sequence of the nave and choir rectangle is accentuated and given life by slanted corners. The powerfully built arcade-above-pilaster piers between nave and choir provide a perspectival frame for the ostentatious high altar. The extremely small frescos do not form a “heaven of the saints” being restricted to delimited areas. The remaining surfaces are neither filled with frescos or stucco. While the Holy Family is depicted in the choir the pictures in the nave feature scenes of the Resurrection of Jesus, distinguished in rank by the monochrome and polychrome execution.
3c569a1e-c412-5ccf-b034-acfc029ba2ad.location: View towards the choir, Catholic Guild Church of St. Joseph

3d279afa-014f-54de-b5b3-c820b9b5e080.name: Grand Hall
3d279afa-014f-54de-b5b3-c820b9b5e080.description: The most significant and artistically most important room in the building is the Grand Hall on the second floor, designed after the fire of 1785. Stucco decorations on the walls imitate grey marble with dark veins, while at one time those of the vault were painted light yellow. Architectural decoration powerfully articulates the surfaces.
3d279afa-014f-54de-b5b3-c820b9b5e080.location: Second floor, Palace of the Sugar Refinery

3e066392-a6df-54b7-a168-ff25ae805497.name: View from the high altar
3e066392-a6df-54b7-a168-ff25ae805497.description: The eight beautiful free standing columns, instead of the more common lesene or half columns, mark the progression of the nave.

3e274dad-a65b-5160-a9e1-d5f8cc5ac311.name: Monumental staircase
3e274dad-a65b-5160-a9e1-d5f8cc5ac311.description: Restored by the architect Francesco Tadolini, this staircase connecting ground and first-floor is decorated with architectural motives, typical of the so called ‘quadratura’ genre; this technique, based on very sophisticated perspective skills and strictly linked to the making of theatrical sceneries, was typical of the Bolognese school during baroque age. Their author, Pietro Scandellari, had been one of the first and most appreciated pupils of Ferdinando Galli, called Bibiena, who, together with his brother, sons and nephews, excelled in those fields all over Europe. The decoration is characterised by the opening of illusive views, which expand the space of the real architecture thanks to the virtual dimension of painting.

3e3d9ee3-a05b-5877-b95d-8cf4890f89db.name: *St. Paul in Athens*
3e3d9ee3-a05b-5877-b95d-8cf4890f89db.description:
St. Paul is represented pointing to the Athenians a ray of light that symbolises God coming to enlighten the people.  
Giuseppe Rolli painted the figures, Antonio the architectures.

3ea84492-2f0d-59cf-aec2-c0b1aefd137a.name: Crucifix altar
3ea84492-2f0d-59cf-aec2-c0b1aefd137a.description: The side-altar, which according to documents was donated in 1754, was built by Johann Mussack the younger in stucco marble. The column superstructure with entablatures placed at an angle and a sweeping altar crown incorporates a Late Gothic crucifix attributed to Hans Klocker from the period around 1500. This has been extended to form a crucifixion group with the addition of figures of John, Mary and Mary Magdalene, supplemented by statues of Moses and Aaron as well as angel figures with instruments of Christ's torture and a relief of the *Sacrifice of Abraham* in the altar crown, all of which are the work of Johann Paterer. The crucifix, venerated as a devotional image, thus becomes the focus of the Baroque presentation and additionally, as a result of the Old Testament figures, is placed in the context of a typological history of salvation.
3ea84492-2f0d-59cf-aec2-c0b1aefd137a.location: Nave, eastern end wall of the southern side-aisle
3ea84492-2f0d-59cf-aec2-c0b1aefd137a.artist: Johann Mussack the younger [n.d.]; Johann Paterer (1712–1785)

3f0a1c3d-1c6e-578a-909f-f74f5146fd83.name: High altar
3f0a1c3d-1c6e-578a-909f-f74f5146fd83.description: Following a Venetian type, the high altar does not feature a retable, favouring a tabernacle flanked by statues and crowned with a ciborium. The marble statues of saints of the Benedictine Order, St. Scholastica, St. Gallus, St. Columbanus and St. Benedict, are masterpieces of the sculptor, Franz Anton Sturm, and rank among his best works.
3f0a1c3d-1c6e-578a-909f-f74f5146fd83.artist: Design: Johann Jakob Herkomer (1652–1717); Sculptures: Franz Anton Sturm (1690–1757)

3f371b7c-e6f8-56ea-ad51-4698c54c3ba9.name: St. Barbara
3f371b7c-e6f8-56ea-ad51-4698c54c3ba9.description: In the 1760s the altars were supplemented with predella paintings by J. Jablonský, who settled in Brno. In the final phase of works he echoed painters from the Vienna Academy circle, collaborating with the artist, J. Stern.
3f371b7c-e6f8-56ea-ad51-4698c54c3ba9.location: Pilgrimage Church of the Virgin Mary of Dolours, Side altar
3f371b7c-e6f8-56ea-ad51-4698c54c3ba9.artist: Johann Jablonský (1737 Rychnov nad Kněžnou – after 1774 Brno?)

3f3dd440-a378-5215-abad-afdbb7bd5887.name: Façade of the Asamhaus
3f3dd440-a378-5215-abad-afdbb7bd5887.description: Egid Quirin Asam’s house-turned-atelier is distinguished by its rich, figurative stucco façade. In a sense, it constitutes the secular counterpart to the sacred theme of the church façade. Its content centres on the journey of an artist’s soul in the home of the Muses on Mount Parnassus, with Athena Pallas as its guide.
3f3dd440-a378-5215-abad-afdbb7bd5887.location: To the left of the church

3fe5563b-80f9-52a9-8802-38778459ad4f.name: *God the Father in Glory with Angels*, detail of the right side
3fe5563b-80f9-52a9-8802-38778459ad4f.description: The group was arranged with the help of a nineteenth-century sculptor, Giacomo De Maria, who added some of the angels and clouds.
3fe5563b-80f9-52a9-8802-38778459ad4f.location: Upper part of the high altar of the church of St. John the Baptist
3fe5563b-80f9-52a9-8802-38778459ad4f.artist: Giuseppe Maria Mazza, Angelo Venturoli, Giacomo De Maria

4017c5f2-8879-55a2-83f3-1a52477c3b70.name: Altar and choir
4017c5f2-8879-55a2-83f3-1a52477c3b70.description: The choir, oriented to the west, was renewed in 1730 in the contemporary Rococo style. On the occasion of the centennial of the Peace of 1648 a new gallery for the organ was installed. The slightly curved stucco is captivating in its simple elegance, its colour highlighting the choir. Although the gallery continues in the choir, the coloured Regency and Rococo stucco establishes a discrete, almost scenographic quality. The fresco on the ceiling shows the three theological virtues: Faith, Hope and Charity. Around the altar, as at the pulpit, paintings depict scenes from the Life of Christ: the Baptism, Resurrection, Pentecost and Last Supper. The two most important ritualistic elements in the church – altar and pulpit – together harmonise in form and content, dedicated fully to the teachings of Christ.
4017c5f2-8879-55a2-83f3-1a52477c3b70.dates: c. 1653: retable; 1673/74: paintings; 1730: organ and decoration of the vault; 1748: renovation of the gallery and organ; 1767: altar
4017c5f2-8879-55a2-83f3-1a52477c3b70.artist: Johann Heiss (1640–1704), Johann Ulrich Mayr (1630–1704), Johannes Spillenberger (1628–1679), Josef Werner (1637–1710); Johann Georg Bergmüller (1688–1762); Johann Esaias Nilson (active 1721–1728); Ignaz Wilhelm Verhelst (1729–1792)

40401d8d-14cf-5acd-a731-f9dfdb35baa6.name: Façade West wing and portal
40401d8d-14cf-5acd-a731-f9dfdb35baa6.description:
At the end of the 17th century the West wing and its tower with curved hood roof were built. As one enters the monastery complex at this side, the wing has the main façade with an interesting pilaster order: on the middle part with the tower and on the right side of the building they are perfectly arranged. Two pairs frame the tower´s middle axis, three pairs of double pilasters and three single pilasters separate the five windows on the right. On the left side there are only three window axes, maybe there were at some time four, the distribution of the pilasters is – probably because of that – irregular. The interval between the three double pilaster pairs varies from pair to pair. The two single pilasters on the far left could be a double pilaster pair with a big space between, but they could also be two single pilasters framing a no longer existent window. Who knows if this pilaster order was the original idea of the architect(s)?  
Hardly anyone will notice the pilasters´ irregular order as the façade´s artistic highlight, the marble portal with the crowning statue of the Holy Virgin and the Baby Christ, will captivate the viewer. Two saints (Adalbero and Kilian) are at their sides. The sculptor had a great sense of humour (the abbot must have had too): unimpressed by the holy society above, angels and putti are frolicking around abbot Severin Blass´s crest. A naughty one is playing with a mitre; two others help him to put it on. Every detail on the portal is finely carved out, the thing is as a whole a baroque masterwork.
40401d8d-14cf-5acd-a731-f9dfdb35baa6.dates: End of 17th century West wing; 1693 marble portal
40401d8d-14cf-5acd-a731-f9dfdb35baa6.artist: Unknown: West wing; Jakob Auer: marble portal

4062b5e3-511d-575d-83b1-5710e5352283.name: *Divine Wisdom hovering over Human Wisdom*
4062b5e3-511d-575d-83b1-5710e5352283.description: The scene celebrates Divine Wisdom through bold perspective and the supernatural light around the figures.

414c7c6c-2207-59d9-bb8a-cc731e96b803.name: Entrance frontage
414c7c6c-2207-59d9-bb8a-cc731e96b803.description: Construction of the college started in around 1593 and continued throughout the 17th century. The church tower was left unfinished for some time and so that on entering the church the visitor may note its two major building phases and changes of style spanning some 150 years.
414c7c6c-2207-59d9-bb8a-cc731e96b803.location: Jesuit Church of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary
414c7c6c-2207-59d9-bb8a-cc731e96b803.artist: Antonio Gabri, Mořic Grimm (1669 Achtdorf – 1757 Brno)

41e9c7e4-cfb4-54eb-8001-37ef0aec887d.name: Revelation: Joshua and Angel
41e9c7e4-cfb4-54eb-8001-37ef0aec887d.description: The left-hand chapel was once a sacristy for the Carthusian priests. The altarpiece, worshipped by gilded angels by O. Schweigl, represents Archangel Michael (M. J. Schmidt). The marble slab in the floor covers the tomb of Moravian Margrave of the *Prokop* (district) of Luxembourg. The interior is adorned with frescos featuring revelations – angels as God's messengers in scenes from both the Old and New Testaments – such as dreams, revelations and annunciations.
41e9c7e4-cfb4-54eb-8001-37ef0aec887d.artist: Franz Anton Maulbertsch (1724 Langenargen am Bodensee – 1796 Vienna)

422c7b42-221d-51e6-9da7-fd1c3d2f7f80.name: *St. Francis stripped of His Secular Clothes* and the *Death of St. Francis*
422c7b42-221d-51e6-9da7-fd1c3d2f7f80.description: The polygonal chancel has a marble framed retable either side of which are two paintings in marble frames: *St. Francis* *stripped of His Secular Clothes* by Francisco Vieira Lusitano (c.1730) and *Death of Saint Francis* by Francesco Pavona (c.1736–1740).
422c7b42-221d-51e6-9da7-fd1c3d2f7f80.artist: Francisco Vieira de Matos (Vieira Lusitano 1699–1783) and Francesco Pavona [n.d.].

423dd37f-2b1c-55e1-9492-76c6ad265c77.name: Reliquary of Dubrovnik Cathedral
423dd37f-2b1c-55e1-9492-76c6ad265c77.description: Death is one of the central motifs of Baroque art. It is also the motive of this huge reliquary, which belongs in a room decorated by several artists including the Venetian sculptor and architect, Marino Gropelli, the stuccators, Carlo Deli Franghi and Valentino Vissani, and the Dubrovnik painter, Petar Matej.
423dd37f-2b1c-55e1-9492-76c6ad265c77.artist: Marino Gropelli (1662–1728); Carlo Degli Frangi [n.d.]; Valentino Vissani [n.d.]; Petar Matej [n.d.]

4245f4f1-ced8-58b2-8737-09920f72fa22.name: Interior
4245f4f1-ced8-58b2-8737-09920f72fa22.description: General view of the interior of the church. There is a huge representation of Calvary with life-size figures at the main altar.
4245f4f1-ced8-58b2-8737-09920f72fa22.location: Bom Jesus Church, Bom Jesus de Braga Sanctuary (Bom Jesus do Monte)

42f3e619-7f2e-5807-987f-322644ef856c.name: High altar
42f3e619-7f2e-5807-987f-322644ef856c.description: The architect of the church, Konstantin Pader, also provided designs for the stucco and the altars, which creates homogeneity of both structure and decoration. The high altar is characterised by an enhanced plasticity of its elements and can be attributed to the High Baroque. The imitating ebony and marble colour scheme and gold-plated ornamental applications were typical of that era. The altarpiece, framed by an aedicula attached to a tall pedestal, depicts Christ's Deposition from the Cross and therefore conveys the biblical scene necessary for the interpretation of the miraculous image. Beneath is an opening that allows the visitor to glance at the miraculous pietà and the remains of the pear tree trunk.
42f3e619-7f2e-5807-987f-322644ef856c.artist: Design: Konstantin Pader; Altarpiece: Johann Hehrl

432eb32a-5dbe-51f2-bd94-bbb4fc20e188.name: *King Francis I heals the People affected by Scrofula*
432eb32a-5dbe-51f2-bd94-bbb4fc20e188.description: In the Middle Ages people believed that the kings of France and England had a special power that could heal scrofula by just touching those afflicted with the illness. Here the king of France, Francis I, is shown healing the people affected by scrofula during his visit to Bologna in 1515.

4362690b-8bce-5978-8be2-ef7d62b6ca6f.name: Memory Hermitage
4362690b-8bce-5978-8be2-ef7d62b6ca6f.description: The small Hermitage is isolated. It is quadrangular in shape with a reverse ogee dome crowned with a rounded pinnacle. Despite its popularity it is very difficult to define the Memory Hermitage in chronological terms. Its “cubic” form and bulbous dome undoubtedly remind us of the ancient Muslim *qubba.*

43735349-37aa-5e8a-a34a-c8f426840f79.name: The Life and Veneration of St. John of Nepomuk
43735349-37aa-5e8a-a34a-c8f426840f79.description: The ceiling fresco spans the entire length of the church and is located behind an indirectly lit ledge which appears to be an opening in the ceiling vault. This creates the illusion that one is peering into the eternal heavenly realms. Around the periphery of the vault is a fresco depicting scenes from the life of St. John of Nepomuk and his subsequent veneration.

439142cf-eadb-561b-b568-5ee2993b4f57.name: Allegory of Hope
439142cf-eadb-561b-b568-5ee2993b4f57.description: The staircase is an important ceremonial element in such residences. In religious circles, it is likened to the ascension to heaven, with individual steps associated with penitence. Niches in the vestibule contain life-size stuccoed sandstone statues, allegories of the virtues. Above them are scenes from the life of St. Norbert and his predecessors, including according to an idealised genealogy, the founders of Hradisko Monastery. The whole thus makes up a gallery of ancestors through the mirror of virtues and glory, peaking in the apotheosis of St. Norbert, founder of the Premonstratensian order, on the vaulting. The allegory of Hope, facing the corridor, personifies the power and strength of Christ’s sacrifice and faith in his Resurrection.
439142cf-eadb-561b-b568-5ee2993b4f57.location:
Premonstratensian Monastery, Hradisko u Olomouce, Staircase  
Olomouc, Moravia, Czech Republic

43a75426-3216-5cbd-9ee9-f0c92937c066.name: *St. George*
43a75426-3216-5cbd-9ee9-f0c92937c066.description: The youthful figure of St. George with a tender and melancholic expression is shown in elegant movement. The careful shaping of the opulent costume together with the surface worked with particular sensitivity to the effects of light make this work a characteristic example of the style and sculptural capacities of the Tagliapietra workshop.
43a75426-3216-5cbd-9ee9-f0c92937c066.artist: Alvise Tagliapietra (1670–1747) and his son Ambrogio (b. 1701)

43b951e7-d8bb-5eb9-ba51-a66bdd187d0a.name: Fresco painting
43b951e7-d8bb-5eb9-ba51-a66bdd187d0a.description:
The church´s artistic highlight is the fresco painting in the choir. It shows the Mother of God ascending towards heaven. She is surrounded by angels and awaited by the Father, Son and Holy Spirit. The scenery is – typically baroque – accompanied by a concert of angels.  
Further down are the apostles finding the tomb empty, but according to legend laid out with roses. Maybe the little angels (to the right of the Madonna and below) who are sprinkling flowers allude to this.  
The fresco painting is considered Altomonte´s masterpiece. Art historians even refer it as the most important illusionistic artwork in Austria. But it was Francesco Messenta who did the illusionistic architectural painting – such as the columns in 3D-effect and the balustrades on the ceiling. It is remarkable how the painted architecture is a continuation of the real architecture.  
The whole composition refers to Figura 47 in Andrea Pozzo´s *Perspectiva pictorum et architectorum* (Perspective in Architecture and Painting, vol. II).

43c6d616-3140-55ee-a6e8-3280cf935f70.name: Altar of the Birth of the Virgin Mary (high altar)
43c6d616-3140-55ee-a6e8-3280cf935f70.description: The high altar, Schmädl’s first large scale piece, is impressive due to its extensive architecture of grandiose column clusters and a canopy in the form of a drapery held by angels, with which the stage of a sacred act is architecturally framed in accordance with the Baroque Theatrum Sacrum. Including its uncommon three-dimensional representation of the birth of the Virgin Mary, the Rottenbuch example is designed according to the archetype represented by Egid Quirin Asam’s theatrically sculpted altars.

44049e01-31b1-5474-82f2-065f4c10101e.name: *Pauline Monk and a Man (Confession?)*
44049e01-31b1-5474-82f2-065f4c10101e.location: Presbytery (left, north, wall), Church of St. George in Purga Lepoglavska

44556ac2-dd90-5636-a742-fb5719f64f4a.name: View of the Choir
44556ac2-dd90-5636-a742-fb5719f64f4a.location: Parish Church of St. Mary Magdalene

4460c0bd-4e29-5dc4-9802-1d885df92d37.name: *St. Peter*
4460c0bd-4e29-5dc4-9802-1d885df92d37.description: An elongated and elegant saintly figure with his head thrown back, it is a characteristic example of Königer’s sculptural idiom with its typical lyricism, suffusing the usually more robust figures of the two leading apostles with a pronounced spirituality.

4460d659-be3c-5edc-a835-cb31775cb892.name: Façade
4460d659-be3c-5edc-a835-cb31775cb892.description: Despite the dominant horizontal façade, the two towers are thin and crowned with the reverse ogee pinnacles that are typical of regional Portuguese Baroque.

44cfc923-4530-5e47-9070-2ca89dd2d65e.name: Transfiguration of the Lord on Mount Tabor
44cfc923-4530-5e47-9070-2ca89dd2d65e.description: The church presbytery was rebuilt after an earthquake in 1763 and provided with a new fresco. Although the artist took over the position of J. J. Etgens in Moravia in the second half of the 18th century, he went on to execute commissions mainly of a decorative nature.

451de532-a903-5a8c-9c94-39a46adafd1f.name: *Presentation of the Miraculous Picture*
451de532-a903-5a8c-9c94-39a46adafd1f.description: The fresco depicts the Abbey’s foundation legend, as in Pisa the donor Emperor Ludwig (Louis) the Bavarian receives the miraculous picture from an angelic-looking monk.

4538f38d-a64f-5f64-ba07-d2b5bab3e669.name: Riesensaal
4538f38d-a64f-5f64-ba07-d2b5bab3e669.description: The “Riesensaal”, whose name is derived from an earlier cycle of Hercules paintings, together with the court chapel, is the second room dedicated to the memory of Emperor Franz I and designed according to the model of the Grand Gallery in Schönbrunn Palace. The banqueting hall extending across the whole width of the wing on Rennweg encompasses two storeys and seven window axes. It is furnished in honour of the House of Habsburg. The huge fresco panels depict allegories, the oil paintings the family of the imperial couple.

4627664d-6522-539e-8981-4f06294692e3.name: Mary Immaculata
4627664d-6522-539e-8981-4f06294692e3.description: The statue of the Virgin Mary from white marble at the top of St. Anne’s Column was replaced by a copy in 1958 for conservation reasons. The original is now located in the collegiate church of Fiecht near Schwaz as a loan of the Provincial Government of Tyrol. (The figures on the plinth were also replaced with copies in 2009; the originals are now located on the first floor of the Old Federal State Parliament in Innsbruck).
4627664d-6522-539e-8981-4f06294692e3.location: Monastery Church of St. Joseph in Fiecht; side altar (former statue on St. Anne’s Column)

46629869-175a-5ce1-8e92-45a1b32d5f70.name: Hall of the Ancestors
46629869-175a-5ce1-8e92-45a1b32d5f70.description: The wainscoting, a copy of the imperial office in Vienna, features family portraits by leading Viennese portraitists including J. Kupecký. The vaulting is decorated with the painting *The Celebration of Jaroměřice*, framed by illusionary architecture.
46629869-175a-5ce1-8e92-45a1b32d5f70.artist: Josef Emanuel Fischer von Erlach (1656–1742 Vienna?), Tobias Gravani, Johann Gotfried Auerbach, Johann Baptist Glunck, Martin Meytens (1695 Stockholm – 1770 Vienna), Domenico Maria Francia, Alessandro Ferretti

4692d873-94e6-59eb-9dc0-1830c1081690.name: Ceiling fresco
4692d873-94e6-59eb-9dc0-1830c1081690.description: Guglielmi’s high-grade ceiling fresco depicts allegories of the Four Continents but doesn’t leave any doubt about the supremacy of Europe. Again, the topic shows a clear connection to the life and work of the patron. In the centre of the painting stands Mercury, the god of trade, with a cornucopia. The theme is trade and its worldwide power spreading European comforts, announced by Fame, all over the world. The accentuated exotic design of the figures corresponds with the painted over-doors in the ballroom.

46b1a9f3-2b23-572f-becd-4572b3354cf4.name: High altar and eastern side altars
46b1a9f3-2b23-572f-becd-4572b3354cf4.description: The high altar together with the two side altars, are arranged as a coulisse-like ornamental screen extending across the whole width of the flat choir termination, thus forming a magnificent concluding prospect. The ornamental screen, structured by columns, includes three altarpieces as well as two large statues and is surmounted by a protruding altar crown above the high altar with a stucco glory of the Holy Trinity.
46b1a9f3-2b23-572f-becd-4572b3354cf4.artist: Johann Perger (1729–1774); Johann Joseph Karl Henrici (1737–1823)

46bb4fb6-c314-5cbe-a7dc-30c998b1dfb1.name: Garden frontage
46bb4fb6-c314-5cbe-a7dc-30c998b1dfb1.description: The garden was designed as part of the chateau reconstruction. The French architect, Charbonier, worked on the site in 1714–15. The chateau frontage opened onto the garden through a terrace with a three-shouldered staircase with statues that also decorated the garden. Today they are found in the niches of the stereotomous frontage with sharp linear elements. The axis parterre was lined by double pathways and the chateau was encircled by a moat. The garden, with a conservatory, was considered one of the most beautiful in the country. The local gardener, Hatzl, was summoned to the court of Maria Theresa and put in charge of the Schönbrunn gardens in Vienna. The first hot-air balloon in Moravia was launched outside the Židlochovice Chateau in 1784.
46bb4fb6-c314-5cbe-a7dc-30c998b1dfb1.artist: Ernst August Charbonnier (1677–1747 Hannover?), Ludwig Sebastian Kaltner

4721206d-edec-5f4f-8475-830cfd0d5bb0.name: Crucifix
4721206d-edec-5f4f-8475-830cfd0d5bb0.description: The cross, created by the sculptor of Stams Monastery, Andreas Thamasch in the year of his death, is a “wound” or “Blutheilands” crucifix and is also referred to as a “Plague Cross”. With his last work Thamasch succeeded in creating an especially expressive example of this type; the stirring face wracked with torment, the body covered with wounds.

473330fa-5960-51e1-a666-631b6d56dfc2.name: Nave fresco
473330fa-5960-51e1-a666-631b6d56dfc2.description: The large ceiling picture is entirely devoted to the glorification of faith and the church. In the centre a triumphal chariot with Christ and the ecclesia in papal regalia, pulled by the four evangelist symbols, i.e. apocalyptical beasts led by John the Baptist. In addition, symbols of redemption (the cross and the lamb), the end of time (Chronos) and the Last Judgement (the angel of judgement, penitence) which allude to the fulfilment of God’s plan of salvation. Using luminous colours, Zeiller succeeded in creating a figurative composition of great plasticity and forcefulness which fills the Baroque pictorial rhetoric with life.

475ce502-c96b-5741-bb58-ee8eb89c4993.name: Plans from the founding charter: Holy sepulchre with “Schlupfwallfahrt”
475ce502-c96b-5741-bb58-ee8eb89c4993.description: The plans from Johann Jakob Herkomer contained in the founding charter envisaged a special feature, a holy sepulchre in the crypt, a so-called “Schlupfwallfahrt”, as built by Herkomer in his own private chapel in Sameister. Access was to be provided by a low passage. Although Herkomer’s ideas found their way into the founding charter they were not realised, possibly on cost grounds, and were replaced by the simpler revised plans from Hafenegger.

4794de30-313e-53cb-8def-1b482c7a40ea.name: *Sanguinic*
4794de30-313e-53cb-8def-1b482c7a40ea.location: Wall of the working cabinet, Ratkaj Palace

47ae5572-acbf-57a2-be11-0e35cf01e522.name: *The Glory of St. Ignatius of Loyola*
47ae5572-acbf-57a2-be11-0e35cf01e522.description: The glory of the founder saint of the Jesuits dominates the middle of the vault of the chapel. It is inspired by the great decoration with the same subject painted by Andrea Pozzo in Rome.
47ae5572-acbf-57a2-be11-0e35cf01e522.location: Chapel of the Jesuit novitiate, vault

47aeefc2-2cb5-5035-8113-5799de8577ea.name: High altar
47aeefc2-2cb5-5035-8113-5799de8577ea.description: The high altar, the work of master carpenter Johann Laufer from Innsbruck, incorporates a Late Gothic statue of the Virgin Mary. The Baroque altar constitutes the frame for the staging of the older devotional image and thus forms the centrepiece of the church’s entire pictorial inventory. The raiseable altarpiece depicting the Assumption of Mary originates from Mölck. It finds its continuation in the ceiling frescoes depicting the Mariological cycle.
47aeefc2-2cb5-5035-8113-5799de8577ea.artist: Johann Adam Ritter von Mölck (1718–1794); Johann Jaufer [n.d.]

47be1ddd-0ecd-5944-937b-603bf7067790.name: The Virgin Mary as Queen of Heaven
47be1ddd-0ecd-5944-937b-603bf7067790.description: In 1736–1745 the church was redecorated. The vaults are covered with fresco paintings. The Coronation of the Virgin Mary (Queen of Heaven) is in the chancel while in the naves are the Celebrations of Christ, the Holy Spirit and the Virgin Mary along with other works. The artist was a pupil of C. D. Assam, a leading south-German fresco painter who was active in Munich in around 1720. He came to Silesia and Moravia through the Order of German Knights and in 1743 he became court painter to Count Filip Ludvík of Sinzendorf.
47be1ddd-0ecd-5944-937b-603bf7067790.location: Jesuit Church of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary

483269b7-dbdb-5903-9179-333113251b69.name: High altar
483269b7-dbdb-5903-9179-333113251b69.description: The high altar in front of the choir wall in the southern cross arm with columns in bright coloured stucco marble and white figural decoration is the work of an unknown master craftsman. The venerated miraculous crucifix has been inserted in place of an altarpiece, a work of the 17th century.
483269b7-dbdb-5903-9179-333113251b69.location: Choir (southern cross arm), Catholic Pilgrimage Church of the Holy Cross

48d6ab89-fd69-5029-ab77-89ea887fd268.name: Façade
48d6ab89-fd69-5029-ab77-89ea887fd268.description: The side façade with its five axes and window axes at irregular intervals only has one central polygonal bay window. Horizontally it is concluded by an eaves cornice. The stucco, forming an embellishment around the window openings, has more room to unfold than on the main façade. The architectural forms of the décor, such as the window moulding, are overshadowed by the vigorous outgrowth of ornamentation.

48fb8493-9f5a-5ea7-895d-1ffecd02f2af.name: The Lambertini altar of the Sacrament
48fb8493-9f5a-5ea7-895d-1ffecd02f2af.description: In 1734 Cardinal Prospero Lambertini commissioned Torreggiani with the completion of the Cathedral. The restoration of the cardinal’s chapel, the second on the left, dedicated to the Holy Sacrament, is the most significant example of the work of Torreggiani.
48fb8493-9f5a-5ea7-895d-1ffecd02f2af.location: Cattedrale di San Pietro, interior, left nave

49f2b9ac-02d2-5d5a-b795-331d46920de1.name: Altar of St. Cajetan
