49f2b9ac-02d2-5d5a-b795-331d46920de1.description: The altar bears a masterpiece of German Baroque painting dedicated to the founder of the Theatine order.

4a57faf0-598d-578a-ae25-67d5b5d35328.name: Pulpit
4a57faf0-598d-578a-ae25-67d5b5d35328.description: The pulpit, decorated in slender *rocailles*, is positioned prominently within the church *vis-à-vis* the gallery according to its role in the Lutheran rite. A life-size wooden crucifix above the pulpit and two paintings of Christ’s Passion by Johann Heinrich Schönfeld at either side complete the Christological ensemble.
4a57faf0-598d-578a-ae25-67d5b5d35328.location: Wall on the right-hand side, Evangelical Lutheran Church of the Holy Cross
4a57faf0-598d-578a-ae25-67d5b5d35328.artist: Johann Esaias Nilson (1721–1728); Ignaz Wilhelm Verhelst (1729–1792); Johann Heinrich Schönfeld (1609–1684)

4ad97887-f621-598c-8c7f-52693a816738.name: St. Felix of Cantalice
4ad97887-f621-598c-8c7f-52693a816738.description: The entrance of the church, in sloping terrain, was adjusted by a terrace with statues of Capuchin saints. The sculptor, who trained in the Rhine Basin region, worked in the Brno workshop of J. J. Schauberger. His compact figures are noteworthy for their expressive faces.
4ad97887-f621-598c-8c7f-52693a816738.location: Capuchin Monastery and the Church of the Invention of the Holy Cross, Brno

4b13da99-6999-503a-b4bc-3a583fb6e0dc.name: Altar of the Holy Cross
4b13da99-6999-503a-b4bc-3a583fb6e0dc.description: The three parts of the Holy Cross altar embody the sanctuary of the pilgrimage. Within elaborate niches of stucco marble on the corners of the choir arch, one finds the assistant figures of the central crucifix: the miraculous *Mater Dolorosa* on the left-hand side, and on the right, the *Apostle St. John*. The gilded *rocaille* elements, as well as the many different and lively putti, are considered masterpieces of Üblher.
4b13da99-6999-503a-b4bc-3a583fb6e0dc.location: Choir and choir arch, Catholic Parish and Pilgrimage Church of the Exaltation of the Cross and Our Lady of Sorrows

4b86710e-568a-5cec-95d8-65d5bb9609bd.name: Sacristy (general view)
4b86710e-568a-5cec-95d8-65d5bb9609bd.description: The sacristy owns what can be considered a complete and unique – both in terms of iconography and style – series of *rocaille* wood-carved and Baroque sculptures, and also a series of Benedictine figures.
4b86710e-568a-5cec-95d8-65d5bb9609bd.artist: Friar José Cipriano da Cruz Sousa (c. 1645–1716) and others

4bdace62-bc43-503d-9780-29b787d8dbe1.name: Hall of Mirrors
4bdace62-bc43-503d-9780-29b787d8dbe1.description: As the heart of the small palace , the Hall of Mirrors functioned as a ballroom, concert hall or as a place of relaxation for the court society following a hunt. Mirrors inside the hall are applied to the wall sections between the windows. The interplay of real and reflecting windows appears to dissolve the surface of the walls and blurs the boundaries between the inside and the outside. The  windows and mirrors are framed with sophisticated Régence style décor and silver-plated carvings. Zimmermann's capriccio-like stuccoes of the ceiling transforms it into an Eden-like landscape by depicting trees, putti, divine figures and birds. This theme of the décor is used to connect the interior of the Amalienburg with its formerly surrounding French formal  garden.
4bdace62-bc43-503d-9780-29b787d8dbe1.artist: Design: François de Cuvilliés the Elder (1695–1768); Stucco: Johann Baptist Zimmermann (1680–1758); Ornamental carvings: Johann Joachim Dietrich (1690–1753)

4c4b0392-7206-5523-9fd7-760883134905.name: Façade
4c4b0392-7206-5523-9fd7-760883134905.description: The curved profiles of the towers and the wavy cornice look like details more usually seen on furniture.

4dd9e779-97fc-5d96-b3d0-9cbecf9a92c0.name: View of the right nave
4dd9e779-97fc-5d96-b3d0-9cbecf9a92c0.description: Side chapels and small domes with baroque decorations. Especially impressive is the third one, painted by Angelo Michele Colonna, and the fifth one decorated by Burrini and Chiarini.
4dd9e779-97fc-5d96-b3d0-9cbecf9a92c0.artist: Angelo Michele Colonna; Giovanni Antonio Burrini and Marcantonio Chiarini

4dec7c99-613e-59ef-83b0-ed79acbd070f.name: Monumental arch so called ‘del Meloncello’
4dec7c99-613e-59ef-83b0-ed79acbd070f.description: This ingenious structure links the side of the portico coming from the city to the one climbing up the hill, as a sort of overpass. The monumental arch was built under the direction of the same architect who designed the new church; he was probably charged with the building of a project by a great protagonist of the European baroque age, Francesco Galli, known as Bibiena, whose education as a theatre architect and stage designer influenced the general idea and the decorative features of the work.
4dec7c99-613e-59ef-83b0-ed79acbd070f.location: Exterior, Santuario della Beata Vergine di san Luca

4e21d747-872b-5b6e-941c-e4be1506d6b9.name: Pulpit
4e21d747-872b-5b6e-941c-e4be1506d6b9.description: Ornamental structures populated by cherubs as emissaries of the Heavenly Host overrun the foot of the pulpit and pile up on the sounding board. The Old Testament tablets of the Ten Commandments refer to the word of God as well as symbols of the four Latin Church Fathers to its theological interpretation. A boy riding a fish symbolises  the baptized soul as the recipient of the homily-conveyed messages of salvation.
4e21d747-872b-5b6e-941c-e4be1506d6b9.location: Lay church, column pair left of the chancel
4e21d747-872b-5b6e-941c-e4be1506d6b9.artist: Design: Dominikus Zimmermann (1685–1766) Execution: Pontian Steinhauser (1688–1755)

4e2c1b12-21c6-58e5-bf20-cdc0eb585033.name: Saints John and Paul
4e2c1b12-21c6-58e5-bf20-cdc0eb585033.description:
The side-altar painting commemorates the penultimate abbot of the Premonstratensian Monastery (and possibly also the creator of the complex iconography of the ceiling paintings) whose tomb lies in front of the altar. A picture of Roman martyrs, protectors from unfavourable weather, is framed by an altar by O. Schweigl. The function of the saints as the country’s protectors may also be understood symbolically: a 1772 decree considerably restricted the organisation of pilgrimages, while an imperial patent from 1783 prohibited them completely.  
The picture in the attachment is of St. Gilbert, the abbot’s favourite saint.

4e8a7718-f219-5f1d-baf0-f5d5f51bee94.name: Plague Column
4e8a7718-f219-5f1d-baf0-f5d5f51bee94.description: A plague epidemic struck the town in 1681. Construction of the column began in 1700 opposite the house of the burgher Z. Hodová whose inheritance financed the project. A sculptor from Brtnice was chosen for the job; Brtnice was a renowned centre of arts and crafts. The cloud-like column, surrounded by volute pedestals with statues of the saints, is crowned with the figure of the Virgin Immaculata. The base is furnished by grottos within which are St. Rosalia and Mary Magdalene. The burgher’s legacy inspired other inhabitants to civic generosity and their donations paid for many of the sculptures adorning the town, including the Chapel of the Virgin Mary (1719).

4f5cb1b8-e3a4-57ad-af75-9eeb25ded3f1.name: Hunting scene
4f5cb1b8-e3a4-57ad-af75-9eeb25ded3f1.description: *Azulejos* representing an early 18th-century gallant deer-hunting scene with an elegant lady and gentleman riding what seem to be Lusitano horses. This panel is one of a set of gallant hunting scenes that decorate the entrance room on the first floor. Note that the frame, with typical Baroque architectural and decorative elements, is a tapestry.
4f5cb1b8-e3a4-57ad-af75-9eeb25ded3f1.artist: Tile-Painting Master P.M.P., probably Padre Manuel Pereira [n.d.]

4fa9f786-cb2b-50f5-adc6-97d7af192089.name: Side-altar
4fa9f786-cb2b-50f5-adc6-97d7af192089.description: The three altars were created as an ensemble by an unknown master in 1770. The right-hand side-altar is completely dedicated to Jesuit saints: the altarpiece, painted in 1778 by Carl Henrici from Bozen depicts Saint Francis Xavier (corresponding with the fresco cycle); the statues depict Ignatius of Loyola and Aloysius Gonzaga, the most important of the order’s saints.
4fa9f786-cb2b-50f5-adc6-97d7af192089.location: South-eastern section of the rotunda wall in the congregation room

4fb258af-9fed-50d6-bfc4-da833a1c858a.name: Ceiling frescoes
4fb258af-9fed-50d6-bfc4-da833a1c858a.description:
The expressive ceiling frescoes in the Schutzengelkapelle (originally the provost´s sacristy) were done by Wolfgang Andreas Heindl, who was then better known than Bartolomeo Altomonte. Regarding the painted architecture, Heindl was, like most painters, oriented towards Andrea Pozzo´s work about perspective (such as Altomonte and Francesco Messenta). He brought this art to a high level by creating perspective rooms complicatedly placed behind each other, as can be seen on some of the paintings. The frescoes in the chapel are dedicated to the Sacrifice of Isaac and to the Inauguration of the Temple by King Solomon.  
Right opposite the chapel is the priest´s sacristy, originally the canons´ sacristy. The ceiling frescoes – representing the High Priest offering David the Shewbread for Reception and the Israelites´ Easter Lamb Meal before leaving Egypt – were also painted by Wolfgang Andreas Heindl. All paintings in both rooms are surrounded by delicate stucco work.
4fb258af-9fed-50d6-bfc4-da833a1c858a.location: In the Chapel dedicated to the Guardian Angels, the former provost´s sacristy, and in the sacristy – both to the left and to the right of the sanctuary

4fe53e71-5945-5d6a-9e28-e7a34d244285.name: Freemasons’ Room
4fe53e71-5945-5d6a-9e28-e7a34d244285.description: The decoration of the chateau was completed in the early 19th century, in the spirit of the “spiritual alchemy” of the late Enlightenment. The Mniszeks finished the Empire-style construction of the stable frontage and made minor Neo-Gothic and Romantic adjustments to the frontages. They also built chapels, crosses, obelisks and family memorials in the park. In 1816 Stanislav Mniszek purchased a stoneware factory and turned it into a famous manufactory.

500bb353-5c8f-5d23-a0c9-9b97e34a6259.name: The martyrdom of St. Laurence
500bb353-5c8f-5d23-a0c9-9b97e34a6259.description: Cobalt-blue on white painted and glazed tiles, *azulejos*. The Italianate Baroque style of the painting is due to the interpretation of Italian prints by the artist.

50647a20-01f3-57bc-8f5f-7e46ecf4d6a4.name: Altar of St. Cross
50647a20-01f3-57bc-8f5f-7e46ecf4d6a4.description: The story of Redemption through the sacrifice of Christ is represented by burning souls behind the bars of the altar cavity; *Supper at Emaus,* modelled in low relief on the doors of the *tabernaculum*; the huge sculptures of St. Veronica and St. Barbara on either side; St. Mary, Mary Magdalen and St. Joseph standing in front of the painted *Crucifixion* and, finally, God surrounded by angels in the attic.
50647a20-01f3-57bc-8f5f-7e46ecf4d6a4.location: The Chapel of the Holy Cross

50970b92-85d1-59d1-b583-3cd3eb00cd42.name: Detail of the Fortress
50970b92-85d1-59d1-b583-3cd3eb00cd42.location: Built of clay, brick, wood and some stone, the fortress complex was designed to accommodate 4,000 soldiers and 150 cannons.

50b2d233-8179-54ab-9a65-4f12378d21af.name: Parliament hall
50b2d233-8179-54ab-9a65-4f12378d21af.description: The central hall, the parliament’s assembly hall, extends over one and a half floors and is the representative highpoint of the interior. Following the model of Italian galleries, it is situated on the second as opposed to the first floor (cf. Augsburg Town Hall). The excellent interior design work pursues the idea of the state’s political self-representation. Statues of princes and regents, attributed to Nikolaus Moll, depict Tyrol’s rulers and regents, the frescos from Asam present the state and its history in connection with biblical scenes, placing it under the protection of divine providence, the putti from Lechleitner display the symbols of the estates.
50b2d233-8179-54ab-9a65-4f12378d21af.location: Centre of the second floor in the main wing, (Old) Federal State Parliament
50b2d233-8179-54ab-9a65-4f12378d21af.artist: Georg Anton Gumpp (1682–1754); sculptural work: Ingenuin Lechleitner (1676–1731); Nikolaus Moll (1676–1754); Cosmas Damian Asam (1686–1739)

50b56dcf-06cd-51c0-a478-2ba2d18b7a16.name: *St. George*
50b56dcf-06cd-51c0-a478-2ba2d18b7a16.description: The saint, shown as he transfixes the dragon writhing under his feet, along with the figure of St. Martin on the same altar, has similarities with the statues of Filip Jakob Straub on the High Altar of Welsche Kirche in Graz, which probably served Weinacht as an inspiration.
50b56dcf-06cd-51c0-a478-2ba2d18b7a16.location: Far-left intercolumniation of the High Altar, Parish Church of Our Lady of the Snow

5103c1d7-7cdc-5cd7-a8b3-15573cb52a74.name: Interior
5103c1d7-7cdc-5cd7-a8b3-15573cb52a74.description: In contrast to its plain exterior the building interior surprises with its ambitious combination of architecture and interior work and a magnificent prospect with the high altar at its centre. At the transition of the somewhat wider nave to the choir, projecting pilasters form the frame for the view in the direction of the altar. In the foreground rounded niches housing the side altars form the transition from nave to choir. Choir and niches form a triad at whose zenith the high altar with the Notburga shrine is staged like an oversized monstrance.
5103c1d7-7cdc-5cd7-a8b3-15573cb52a74.location: View from the nave into the choir

514d8dc0-868f-5204-a073-0bc44b2dabbb.name: Robillion Pavilion
514d8dc0-868f-5204-a073-0bc44b2dabbb.description: Designed by Robillion, the Pavilion is sometimes considered one of Portugal's first Neo-Classical buildings. However, it is no more than an expression of the *French* Baroque – obviously more “Classical” – attached to the overall palace form. It has two floors and a considerable monumentality, emphasised by the Stairway of the Lions.

5189e709-985a-5612-9c80-28cf963cf0c0.name: *Christ*
5189e709-985a-5612-9c80-28cf963cf0c0.description: With a prominent diagonal axes, both groups at the ends of the altar direct the viewer’s gaze towards the central motif – the redemptive sacrifice of the Crucified Christ. Carved in white marble, yellow marble frames the figure of the dying Christ. Additional emphasis is achieved by a pair of volutes that edge the upper part of the frame and stand out against a background of black marble drapery, the folds of which are arranged in rays.

5192e45b-8f0a-579c-8621-8835ab5c086e.name: Fresco paintings in choir and antechoir, altar paintings
5192e45b-8f0a-579c-8621-8835ab5c086e.description:
As a typical Cistercian monastery most of the (fresco) paintings are all about the glorification of the Holy Virgin with her in the centre of the composition. In Wilhering the figures on the rectangular ceiling are in groups, arranged step-like, towards the Virgin, in Engelszell there is a dome with the Mother of God at its centre and the figures surrounding her in a circle. Herewith, Altomonte alluded to an earlier fresco painting by himself in Spital am Pyhrn in one of the dome´s cupolas. An illusionistic base is transitioning from the architecture, via a balustrade to the celestial scene. While in Wilhering the painting is framed by stuccowork, there is an area-wide painting in the Engelszell church.  
Engelszell is a good example of how an over-occupied artist like Altomonte carried out his commissions. For the painting of the Guardian Angel on a side altar he re-used a composition from an altar painting in Wilhering done by his father Martino. Interestingly, there is a third and later version in the Chapel of the former monastery church in Spital am Pyhrn. Martino Altomonte had painted a Death of St. Joseph for Wilhering whose composition Bartolomeo re-used in Engelszell in a slight variation and mirror-inverted. As his father Martino was Bartolomeo´s teacher and his consistent example, he once again followed his draft in the Ascension of the Virgin on the main altar. Bartolomeo left his mark in form of a slim pyramid on the left as he had done on the huge fresco painting of the Ascension in Spital am Pyhrn, on a painting in St. Florian Abbey, on another in the Hagenberg parish church and on others more.
5192e45b-8f0a-579c-8621-8835ab5c086e.location: In the dome, in the pendentives and on the altars

52383801-0cd8-5000-8d48-ffc62ed390a0.name: *St Michael Overthrows the Fallen Angels and the Coronation of Mary the Virgin*
52383801-0cd8-5000-8d48-ffc62ed390a0.description: As counter-reformatory Catholic propaganda linked to the iconography of the Jesuit church St Michael in Munich, the main fresco addresses the victorious battle of the Archangel Michael against the apostate angels, who blatantly  represent Protestantism. Crowned by the Trinity, Mary, as the Queen of Angels, oversees the happenings that are surrounded by Marian Symbols.

528f12d4-5b9e-5f75-a717-5d6b25977d21.name: Pagan gods
528f12d4-5b9e-5f75-a717-5d6b25977d21.description: Although these are reminiscent of antique statues, the gods fit perfectly in the illusionistic architecture, painted by the artist to create artificial effects in order to amaze the visitors.

52d56c38-4a81-5355-bc6c-d0f037719582.name: High Altar of St Jerome
52d56c38-4a81-5355-bc6c-d0f037719582.description: The altar belongs to the monstrance-like type of altars, characterised by a specific form, narrow in the lower part and round in the main, upper part.

5306c69e-1796-5ac2-951a-f0b0a93b2822.name: Revelation of Virgin Mary of the Snows
5306c69e-1796-5ac2-951a-f0b0a93b2822.description: The picture at the high altar was supplied by a Viennese artist. The demanding oval composition depicts the Virgin Mary appearing before a pope. She showed him a place covered in snow, where he was supposed to build her a temple.
5306c69e-1796-5ac2-951a-f0b0a93b2822.artist: Johann Georg Schmidt known as Wiener-Schmidt (1685 Bohemia – 1765 Vienna)

530f92d7-28b1-5d2b-a2fa-26fbedb036ab.name: View of convent buildings and church
530f92d7-28b1-5d2b-a2fa-26fbedb036ab.description: Although the façade of the convent and the church originate from the first building phase they are largely characterised by the stuccowork from the end of the 17th century. Nevertheless, documents confirm that the church portal forms part of the original inventory from Alexander Colin. The tri-axial church façade with Ionic colossal order is crowned by a curved and stepped gable which is largely composed of three massive alcoves for statues.
530f92d7-28b1-5d2b-a2fa-26fbedb036ab.artist: Giovanni Lucchese [n.d.], Alberto Lucchese [n.d.]; Alexander Colin [n.d.]

5356a6b6-e734-542a-9ab6-73a3c0d9aadd.name: The Life of St. John the Baptist
5356a6b6-e734-542a-9ab6-73a3c0d9aadd.description: Johann Baptist Baader’s ceiling fresco spans an area of over 160 square meters above the nave. A natural landscape in the foreground and an architectural backdrop impressively envelope the depictions of the life of St. John the Baptist, providing structure for their arrangement at the same time. In the spirit of enlightenment, allegories are omitted here in favour of historical topics. From the design of the powerful trompe l’oeil architecture, Baader was clearly inspired by the style of Andrea Pozzo’s dome frescoes, which his Augsburgian teacher Johann Georg Bergmüller conveyed to him. Moreover, some of the staffage figures illustrate how Baader was greatly influenced by Neapolitan ceiling frescoes during a sojourn in Italy lasting several years.

535dd005-986e-56bc-8767-b42ad5c5bcc1.name: Burial chapel and crypt interior design
535dd005-986e-56bc-8767-b42ad5c5bcc1.description:
Interestingly, Johann Bernhard Fischer von Erlach’s first draft for the cupola – one fresco painting over the entire area – was criticised and declined. The inspiration might have come from Andrea Pozzo. He was then working on the ceiling fresco of San Ignazio, the second Jesuit church in Rome, from where Fischer had arrived. Fischer´s second plan showed a divided ceiling surface: seventeen small fresco paintings framed by rich stucco decoration. Matthias Echter did the paintings on which emperor Ferdinand´s II virtues and his Catholic deeds are symbolised. Marx Schokotnigg created the stucco figures in the niches; Joseph Antonio Serenio did the stucco work.  
The Holy Sepulchre with gilded figures surrounding and crowning the scaffolding was designed by Veit Königer. Through a circular opening in front of it a red marble sarcophagus can be seen in the crypt below. It is not Ferdinand´s II tomb, but that of his parents archduke Karl II and his first wife archduchess Maria Anna (though Karl´s II body is buried in the Seckau basilica). Ferdinand´s and his wife´s coffins are in niches embedded in the wall and marked with tablets bearing their names. The stucco work in the crypt – putti, insignia and coats of arms representing the lands and hereditary lands ruled by emperor Ferdinand II – was firstly done by Mattia Camin and later replaced by Josef Antonio Serenio.
535dd005-986e-56bc-8767-b42ad5c5bcc1.dates: 1640 stucco work crypt; 1687 interior design burial chapel; as from 1688 ceiling frescoes and stucco work in the chapel; 1694 the stucco work in the crypt was replaced; 1695–96 stucco figures in the chapel´s niches; 1768–69 Holy Sepulchre
535dd005-986e-56bc-8767-b42ad5c5bcc1.location: Southern part of the building complex
535dd005-986e-56bc-8767-b42ad5c5bcc1.artist: Mattia Camin: stucco work crypt; Johann Bernhard Fischer von Erlach: interior design burial chapel; Matthias Echter: fresco paintings in the burial chapel; Joseph Antonio Serenio: replaced the original stucco work in the crypt; Marx Schokotnigg: stucco figures in the niches; (probably) Sebastiano Carlone the elder: marble sarcophagus in the crypt

539aa4cf-42d9-5596-9e53-4495b36a2b5b.name: Exterior (façade and tower)
539aa4cf-42d9-5596-9e53-4495b36a2b5b.description: The imposing building displays a continuous pilaster arrangement. At the centre of the northern nave wall is the tower, the lower sections of which were retained from its Gothic predecessor. Thus the rhythmical structure of the nave wall was also designed with respect to the position of the tower. The cross section façade to the west is distinguished by a massive aedicule with a segment pediment surmounting the main portal.
539aa4cf-42d9-5596-9e53-4495b36a2b5b.location: View of the exterior from the northwest
539aa4cf-42d9-5596-9e53-4495b36a2b5b.artist: Abraham Millauer (c. 1680–1758), Philipp Millauer (1710–53), Leonhard Millauer [n.d.]

53a5bd73-a238-53c4-81c9-59518376497e.name: Coronation Monstrance
53a5bd73-a238-53c4-81c9-59518376497e.description: The radial monstrance is decorated with vine leaves and grapes, the Eucharist, symbol of Christ’s blood. Below the casket is a relief of the Madonna and Child; at the top, under a baldachin, is God and the dove of the Holy Spirit. Cartouches on the richly wrought pedestal feature paintings on enamel: the Madonna of Old Brno and half-figures of the order’s saints.

53f0ae70-9e34-55bc-bbcb-4ee9c86e09a0.name: Stucco
53f0ae70-9e34-55bc-bbcb-4ee9c86e09a0.description: The stuccowork, executed during 1634–7, is the work of Georg Braun of the Wessobrun school according to designs from Hans Schor and Florian Nut. Panels, vases, festoons, and draperies, framed by rod motifs, underscore the structural elements in emulation of the austere panelled stucco of the South German (Munich) style. The transept and choir also contain ornaments in the emerging scrollwork style, designed c. 1640/50 by Oswald Kaiser.
53f0ae70-9e34-55bc-bbcb-4ee9c86e09a0.artist: Georg Braun [n.d.], Hans Schor (1585–1674), Florian Nut [n.d.], Frair Oswald Kaiser [n.d.]

542f882d-f0f2-5fe9-acfb-9ba0da1c097f.name: Staircase
542f882d-f0f2-5fe9-acfb-9ba0da1c097f.description: The stone cantilever staircase is decorated with sculptures of *putti* holding components of the family's coat of arms and representing allegories of the Senses. Cartouches in the parapet feature scenes from Virgil's *Aeneid*. The monumental staircase hall closes with a fresco of Odysseus presenting the Trojan horse. The entrance space portrays the family as protectors of Christianity and patrons of the arts.
542f882d-f0f2-5fe9-acfb-9ba0da1c097f.artist: Johann Christian Pröbstl, Josef Tadeáš Rotter (1701 Opava – 1763 Brno)

5440bc4b-65aa-5aaa-a46d-9a40f7e60b5d.name: Choir window
5440bc4b-65aa-5aaa-a46d-9a40f7e60b5d.description: For the decoration of the choir Kleinhans designed three-part curved windows in the style of Dominikus Zimmermann set into the side walls. The window functions as an ornamental feature, the original form of the antique thermal window is deconstructed and enhanced. As the remaining windows are only in the form of semi-circular arches, the contrasting character of the choir is especially marked.

547c3e10-f334-55ad-84da-873152b39f6d.name: Transfiguration on Mount Tabor
547c3e10-f334-55ad-84da-873152b39f6d.location:
Premonstratensian Monastery, Hradisko u Olomouce, Representations’ Room  
Olomouc, Moravia, Czech Republic

547f4652-cadb-535f-a3e5-1f8c723e719b.name: Monumental staircase
547f4652-cadb-535f-a3e5-1f8c723e719b.description: The double flight monumental staircase planned by the architect Angellini is a good example of the so called senatorial type. It is distinctive because of the balanced insertion of decorative elements.

5545cb27-0785-507a-9024-c4b15d333e54.name: Monumental staircase; Statue of Sisyphus
5545cb27-0785-507a-9024-c4b15d333e54.description:
Sisyphus, the son of Aeolus and King of Corinth, is represented carrying a rock towards a mountain. This is the punishment he was condemned to after his death.  
His presence, should be considered along with Athena, the symbol of Learning in the niche above. This may be alluding to the struggle of the Human race for the conquest of Wisdom.
5545cb27-0785-507a-9024-c4b15d333e54.artist: Giovanni Carlo Sicinio Galli Bibiena (architect), Filippo Scandellari (sculptor), Giovan Battista Canepa (sculptor's aid)

55470828-abb3-50d6-b682-ff639cac44ee.name: Monastery buildings
55470828-abb3-50d6-b682-ff639cac44ee.description:
When the Baroque era began, most of the buildings still were Romanesque or Gothic. The former cloister was at the beginning of the 17th century the first to be demolished and replaced by a two storey, U-shaped cross-vaulted wing.  
The new convent building with three-storeys and four wings kept the Gothic walls, got four identical open arcade-facades in all floors and looks more Renaissance than Baroque. Therein is the refectory, the one and only room at the original location, nowadays a Baroque Hall with paintings by Joseph Adam von Mölck.  
In the East wing was the former library, during the Baroque era transformed into the chapter hall with a ceiling painting by Joseph Amonte. Under abbot Placidus Mally freestanding independent structures in the East of the complex were connected and, like the East wing on the outside, unified in the high Baroque epoch.  
The three storey North wing is characterized by the protruding seven-axis Avant-Corps, including the monastery´s main entrance with three gates. The high one in the centre (with rusticated arch, columns at both sides and crowned with a crest) is for carriages, while the two smaller ones are for pedestrians.
55470828-abb3-50d6-b682-ff639cac44ee.dates: Beginning of the 17th century new cloister; refectory paintings 1767; 1628–32 new convent building; 1720 North wing and renovation of the monastery´s building complex in the East
55470828-abb3-50d6-b682-ff639cac44ee.artist: Cloister, refectory paintings: Joseph Adam von Mölck; new convent building: Bartolomeo di Bosio; baroquization of North wing and Eastern part of the monastery´s building complex: probably Johann Georg Stengg

5581753a-eaef-56a7-aafa-55998200dcf9.name: High altar
5581753a-eaef-56a7-aafa-55998200dcf9.description: The high apse windows allow light to shine upon the imposing high altar; marble columns wind their way up into the heights, clearly alluding to the choir of the Theatine Church in Munich. Between the columns are the statues of Zacharias and Joachim as well as Anna and Elizabeth, relatives of the Virgin Mary whose Ascension to Heaven is depicted on the altarpiece. The scene develops into a sculptural medium depicting Christ recieving his mother with open arms beneath a glory of rays.
5581753a-eaef-56a7-aafa-55998200dcf9.artist: Egid Quirin Asam (1692–1750); Thomas Schaidhauf (1735–1810); Johann Nepomuk Schöpf (c. 1735–after 1785)

563c5781-e08e-5f36-b59b-bbc28044b3ab.name: View of Brno and the Premonstratensian Monastery in Zábrdovice
563c5781-e08e-5f36-b59b-bbc28044b3ab.description: The church galleries contain a number of votive pictures brought by pilgrims. This monumental canvas depicts the Brno Basin with the Zábrdovice Monastery which administered the pilgrimage site. The picture was donated by the canonry as an expression of thanks for the protection of Brno during the siege by Prussian and Saxon armies in 1742.

5645191d-dd08-5956-93d5-cbb42d7972b6.name: Arts’ Terrace
5645191d-dd08-5956-93d5-cbb42d7972b6.description: The Arts' terrace is totally covered with figurative and ornamental *azulejos* painted in blue and manganese on a white background. The terrace is named on account of the *azulejos* depicting Poetry and the Seven Liberal Arts. Marble life-size statues, placed in niches, depict pagan gods. Over the niches are medallions in the '*della Robbia*' style in which are several busts of Roman Emperors. At the end of the terrace is the chapel.

564b795c-c024-5183-8ef7-83ea55c2e465.name: Christ Appears on the Sea of Galilee
564b795c-c024-5183-8ef7-83ea55c2e465.description: The cartouche is in the Rococo style. The central area, in low relief, presents the miraculous catch of fish described in the Gospel of St. John (21: 1–14).

56957b4a-772d-5e30-9bf7-57cd1b52eb92.name: Church‘s architecture
56957b4a-772d-5e30-9bf7-57cd1b52eb92.description:
As the church is on three sides surrounded by old dwelling houses, standing next to each other, and narrow streets it is therefore not easy to capture it, neither with the eyes nor with a camera. With a building core from the 14th century, the church was inside and outside gradually baroquised from the 17th century, including the decoration of a single vaulted bay on the North side of the church. Possibly the annex building on the presbytery’s North side, today the sacristy, dates from this era.  
In the 18th century a popular architect built the tower; some years later the entrance hall was added. The tower’s two storey façade is on its four sides structured with pilasters on the corners and a continuous cornice. It frames the oval windows (in the lower storey) and the clocks´ lower halves (in the storey above). The continuous entablature above the clocks breaks through the roof, builds triangular gables and climaxes in an onion-shaped roof with lantern.  
The tower is running parallel to the chapel’s tower on the Kalvarienberg and ends in the same height. Even as the latter is a 19th century building (on the place of a 1740s chapel), one may assume that this didn’t occur by accident.

5718ac81-d92d-51a8-a1ec-2e1b0253d7a9.name: Theatre room
5718ac81-d92d-51a8-a1ec-2e1b0253d7a9.description: The theatre room was used for the performance of spiritual enactments.
5718ac81-d92d-51a8-a1ec-2e1b0253d7a9.location: North wing (3rd floor), Benedictine Abbey of St. Theodor and Alexander

571b4393-48a0-5d36-b275-9a37e8ea9df6.name: Coronation Paraments
571b4393-48a0-5d36-b275-9a37e8ea9df6.description: Fabrics were essential elements of the coronation ceremony. Viennese embroiderers frequently worked for the monastery. In comparison with other preserved Paraments these appear rather poor. The most spectacular part of the coronation set was the altar with an altarpiece. Accompanying elements were subordinated to it through their reduced decorativeness.

57410af1-c860-5014-8639-e6bbd059adc1.name: *Felsina between Peace and War*
57410af1-c860-5014-8639-e6bbd059adc1.description: The fresco in the Audience Room (today the Fireplace Room) was painted by Marco Antonio Franceschini and  shows Felsina (Bologna's name in Latin) between War and Peace. The scene is framed by “quadrature” (architectural illusionistic paintings) by Enrico Haffner. Felsina is crowned with laurels by Fame, while below them a lion and a lamb represent the desire of peace.
57410af1-c860-5014-8639-e6bbd059adc1.location: Fireplace Room, first floor, Palazzo Marescotti Brazzetti

57d49d32-78d5-547d-87e6-2b2f82733699.name: *Ecstasis of St. Paul*
57d49d32-78d5-547d-87e6-2b2f82733699.description:
Also known as the “Glorification of St. Paul”, the fresco represents the Saint carried to heaven by the angels.  
Around the dome, in the pendentives, the four continents (Europe, Asia, America, and Africa) symbolise St. Pauls’ universal message spreading throughout the world.

58029e88-155f-5398-871d-c04bac23385d.name: Church doorway
58029e88-155f-5398-871d-c04bac23385d.description: A Rococo doorway dating to 1755. The lintel is decorated in high relief with flower garlands, palms and shells, and is crowned by a Marian monogram.

5828d034-3839-538e-a971-84b96d302fc5.name: The staircase of the so called “Artists” (right branch), leading to the first floor
5828d034-3839-538e-a971-84b96d302fc5.description: The walls and ceiling are decorated with coats of arms and symbols of the memories which celebrate the most significant events of the history of the Studio.

5842aabd-e2d2-5fed-b156-c2aae539180c.name: Statues of the Founders
5842aabd-e2d2-5fed-b156-c2aae539180c.description: The two monumental statues of the founders, the Bavarian Duke Ludwig (Louis) II and his son who shared his name and was promoted to Emperor of the Holy Roman Empire, testify to the relevance of the medieval founding of the monastery up until the end of the Baroque period.

58796dab-18c0-5c82-8173-c5e543e4c87a.name: Celebration of the Virgin Mary
58796dab-18c0-5c82-8173-c5e543e4c87a.description: The monumental fresco is by C. F. Sambach, a pupil of P. Troger and G. R. Donner and later a rector at the Vienna Academy. The central scene, placed in an illusionary architectural frame, is supplemented with allegories of the Virtues in pendentives. The bottom section features the coats of arms of the benefactors and angels spreading pilgrimage devotionalia from a cornucopia. Sambach also created the pictures for the side altars. This series of large paintings is among his best work.
58796dab-18c0-5c82-8173-c5e543e4c87a.location: Pilgrimage Church of the Virgin Mary of Dolours

58b70fd0-9fb0-5e67-9831-8c61eaa6f8dd.name: Pietà
58b70fd0-9fb0-5e67-9831-8c61eaa6f8dd.description: Based on a type of traditional devotional image, the artist managed to create a perfectly shaped pyramidal composition of Mary's graceful mourning pose and the weightless Body of Christ, elegantly outstretched in an S -shape. An also mourning putto is decorating the scene and lends a folksy counterbalance.
58b70fd0-9fb0-5e67-9831-8c61eaa6f8dd.location: On the right side of the chancel arch
58b70fd0-9fb0-5e67-9831-8c61eaa6f8dd.artist: Sculptures: Ignaz Günther (1725–75); painted coating: Nikolaus Nepaur

58db5d91-9a5a-5cc7-993f-9e9b4c91e765.name: Inscription on the entrance doorway
58db5d91-9a5a-5cc7-993f-9e9b4c91e765.description: The detail shows the inscription above the entrance to the Chapel of Bones. It addresses those who enter the chapel, reminding them of the folly of vanity and concentration on mundane affairs, which must give way to an exemplary life and to the denial of earthly belongings. The inscription reads: “*Nós ossos que aqui estamos pelos vossos esperamos*” (“We bones lying here are waiting to be joined by yours”).

58dd5f59-71f0-5f4d-bc1e-ecd6fcdecdae.name: High Altar
58dd5f59-71f0-5f4d-bc1e-ecd6fcdecdae.description:
Sculptures of St. Peter and St. Paul, St Ignatius and St Frances Xavier standing in shallow niches furnish the lower side sections of the high altar. At either side of the retable are sculptures of *St. John Nepomuk* and *St. Donat Martyr*. In the attic, the *Annunciation* accompanied by saints and angels, is divided into two zones.  
In around 1737, the sculptor, Ivan Walz, was working in Varaždin having taken over the workshop of the Reiss-Schoy family in Maribor, thus it is probable that this altarpiece is his work.

58fa3a97-2ab3-5a6d-aeef-3f7f461c21ff.name: The Triumph of Peace and Justice
58fa3a97-2ab3-5a6d-aeef-3f7f461c21ff.description: The Triumph of Peace and Justice, with the flying figures of Justice, holding the fasces, and of Abundance, with the fruits.

59c51cf5-bbb6-53c6-b4c9-b11995b0abfd.name: Ulrich Altar
59c51cf5-bbb6-53c6-b4c9-b11995b0abfd.description: With its elegant Rococo shapes, the side altar, crafted by the great master of the local guild of sculptors at that time, is dedicated to St. Ulrich as the diocese patron and shows his apotheosis in the medium of sculpture.
59c51cf5-bbb6-53c6-b4c9-b11995b0abfd.location: Middle side chapel on the left

5a0ce955-8a25-5f7e-af4e-1e515760b5aa.name: Detail of carved stone ornamentation
5a0ce955-8a25-5f7e-af4e-1e515760b5aa.description: The *concheado* or shell-like style, which in Portugal corresponds to *Rocaille* with its asymmetry, is overdone here as the granite becomes ductile and plastic.

5a414632-5957-5804-9e90-cd85d42a99f3.name: High Altar of the Church of St. Anne
5a414632-5957-5804-9e90-cd85d42a99f3.description: F. A. Rottal was a prominent investor. He built and restored churches (Hostýn) in his demesne, founded a Trinitarian Monastery in Holešov and reconstructed the Church of St. Anne. A lesser-known artist, J. F. Pilz’s paintings were a tour de force.
5a414632-5957-5804-9e90-cd85d42a99f3.artist: Ondřej Zahner (1709 Ettershausen – 1752 Olomouc), František Antonín Palko (1717 Breslau – 1767 Vienna)

5b042fed-0778-5fb0-9fbd-bea71502dbf8.name: High altar
5b042fed-0778-5fb0-9fbd-bea71502dbf8.description: The high altar in the form of a freestanding, four-columned ciborium is the work of Franz Karl Fischer, the son of the master builder Johann Georg Fischer of the Füssen school. The altar, in which in all likelihood the four columns of its predecessor from 1728 have been integrated, was designed by Joseph Stapf.  The columns are arranged in a trapezoid form, whereby the two rear columns frame the mensa with tabernacle, and form the rear wall of the structure. Above the tabernacle is a miraculous picture in an aureole, a Gothic Madonna with child. According to records a picture of the Virgin Mary was displayed under four columns in Wilton as early as 1311. The two angel candelabra which flank the altar are works of the late 17th century, presumably from Andreas Faistenberger.

5b082eee-cf48-5ef3-91b2-aa3a2ddd577a.name: High altar
5b082eee-cf48-5ef3-91b2-aa3a2ddd577a.description: The high altar, with its Classicist design from Urban Klieber, features an early Baroque painting depicting the vow made by the estates on 1 February 1647. Representatives of the estates and bishops kneel before the church and pay homage to the picture of the Virgin Mary, supported by angels. The copy of Cranach’s miraculous picture from St. Jacob, painted in 1654 by Michael Waldmann, is integrated in a frame in the main picture, in imitation of Rubens’ Madonna in the Chiesa Nuova in Rome. The map, unrolled by a putto under the miraculous picture shows that the entire county of Tyrol had placed itself under the protection of the Virgin Mary.
5b082eee-cf48-5ef3-91b2-aa3a2ddd577a.artist: Johann Paul Schor (1615–1674); Urban Klieber (1741–1803); Michael Waldmann the elder (c. 1605–1658)

5b66ccc1-4f4e-5e59-afac-9cb5613ba254.name: Staircase
5b66ccc1-4f4e-5e59-afac-9cb5613ba254.description: The Italian artists were part of the D. Martinelli circle, participating in the construction of the Liechtenstein palace in Vienna. The stucco artist, Bussi, also worked with Fischer von Erlach and J. L. Hildebrandt.

5bab92c3-59a2-5508-84dd-c3ea097dc2d5.name: Façade
5bab92c3-59a2-5508-84dd-c3ea097dc2d5.description: Of Christoph Gumpp’s plans for a double-tower façade only the north tower was completed by 1667. The forebuilding in the form of a monumental portico was completed by Gumpp’s grandson, Georg Anton, under Abbot Gregor von Stremer. This High Baroque forebuilding of Roman monumentality opens at its centre to form a large niche framed by an aedicule. The statues of the legendary giants Haymon and Thyrsus, as well as the figures from the upper balustrade, are early, somewhat crude works from Nikolaus Moll.
5bab92c3-59a2-5508-84dd-c3ea097dc2d5.artist: Christoph Gumpp the younger (1600–1672); Georg Anton Gumpp (1682–1754); Nikolaus Moll (1676–1754)

5bc76a0c-5131-5c24-99d0-666fd90caf59.name: Allegory of Salvation
5bc76a0c-5131-5c24-99d0-666fd90caf59.description: The middle section of the vault is the centre of the longitudinal building and the principal part of its iconography. Adam and Eve embody the burden of eternal sin and mortality. Archangel Gabriel wreathed in flower garlands bears the Divine message of the salvation of mankind – the birth of Christ and his sacrifice – symbolised by a cross and the marks of Christ’s torture. The scene of the Supreme Divine Secret – where the Word becomes the body – closes with Archangel Michael weighing souls on Judgement Day. The arrival of the Saviour as foretold by the prophets is represented in the joints of the vault with Moses, Abraham, Noah and Enoch.
5bc76a0c-5131-5c24-99d0-666fd90caf59.location: Pilgrimage Church of the Scourged Saviour, Dyje, detail of the Fresco
5bc76a0c-5131-5c24-99d0-666fd90caf59.artist: Franz Anton Maulbertsch (1724 Langenargen am Bodensee – 1796 Vienna)

5bf676b7-c1ac-53ed-8e80-eafc74f0d3c4.name: The portico
5bf676b7-c1ac-53ed-8e80-eafc74f0d3c4.description: The construction of the long and sinuous portico in its actual shape started in 1674, thanks to the contributions of religious orders, noble families, guilds and private citizens. The project, made by Camillo Saccenti (already presented in 1655 but at that time thought to be too expensive) was modified by the architect Gian Giacomo Monti at the beginning of the eighteenth-century.  Based on the advice provided by the archbishop’s architect Giovanni Antonio Conti the work started from the portico next to the shrine and ended in 1721.
5bf676b7-c1ac-53ed-8e80-eafc74f0d3c4.location: Exterior, Santuario della Beata Vergine di san Luca
5bf676b7-c1ac-53ed-8e80-eafc74f0d3c4.artist: Camillo Saccenti; Gian Giacomo Monti; Giovanni Antonio Conti

5c1e94cf-ce7a-5555-9256-3d473268fb97.name: Portal
5c1e94cf-ce7a-5555-9256-3d473268fb97.description: The college complex was pulled down in 1904 during the redevelopment of Brno. Only a photographic record and a portal from the Cardinal’s Courtyard, found today next to the church presbytery, has survived. The statue of Archangel Michael on the ledge holds cartouches with the coat of arms of Cardinal František of Dietrichstein. On the sides are statues of Saints, Ignatius of Loyola, founder of the Jesuit order, and Francis Xaverius. A plaque installed later commemorates the academy of 1778.
5c1e94cf-ce7a-5555-9256-3d473268fb97.location: Jesuit Church of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary
5c1e94cf-ce7a-5555-9256-3d473268fb97.artist: Jan Křtitel Erna (1625?, Brno – 1698, Brno) – Jan Kašpar Pröbstl (? – 1729, Brno)

5c4e21c7-caf1-59f7-973d-709acd6289a4.name: Venus Garden
5c4e21c7-caf1-59f7-973d-709acd6289a4.description: Access to the Venus Garden is via a staircase decorated with *azulejos*. At the south side of the garden stands a pavilion (*casa do fresco* in Portuguese), with an extremely rare decorative scheme of figurative *azulejos* and ornamental grotto-work. The façade is completely covered with grotto-work, creating a porch with a central pediment on top of which there are two pinnacles either side and a cartouche with the coat of Arms of the Marquis' wife, Madalena de Castro. Facing the pavilion stands the S-shaped lake flanked by walls and covered with *azulejos*. The tiles depict satirical scenes in which monkeys and cats represent everyday life.

5c94a693-94d2-5ebe-82b9-608c53f0f3fd.name: High altar
5c94a693-94d2-5ebe-82b9-608c53f0f3fd.description: The imposing high altar with six columns above a concave ground plan was altered considerably in the late 19th century and subsequently returned to its original form during restoration work concluded in 1982. The original altarpiece, the *Assumption of Mary* painted by Franz Laukas in 1724, was also reinserted. The two masterfully executed statues of St. Joseph and Joachim, the work of Andreas Köll (c. 1720) were also repainted white.

5d026b9e-4028-590c-984e-d857427cc68e.name: Water Tank and the Moses Cascade
5d026b9e-4028-590c-984e-d857427cc68e.description: At the upper level are the Water Tank and the Moses Cascade, which is a purely decorative feature.

5d2048c3-7fc9-5226-968c-556eab5c57e0.name: Archangel Gabriel
5d2048c3-7fc9-5226-968c-556eab5c57e0.description:
The figure of the Angel of the Annunciation closes a series of statues lining the route from Telč to Staré Město where the Chapel of the Virgin Mary can be seen with decoration by J. L. Daisinger, an assistant of P. Troger.  
K. Ober’s work is seen chiefly in Jaroměřice nad Rokytnou. In Telč he is also responsible for the sculpted decoration on the frontages of two houses in the main square.

5d384b4b-2125-59b9-a241-75c9c513995b.name: Stucco ornamentation
5d384b4b-2125-59b9-a241-75c9c513995b.description: The decoration consists of floral ornamentation, angels, and figurative representations depicting scenes from St Frances Xavier’s missionary activities and his dying vision on Shangchuan Island in China.
5d384b4b-2125-59b9-a241-75c9c513995b.location: The Chapel of St. Francis Xavier

5d883aff-c791-5728-975f-c3f848744787.name: Upper Synagogue
5d883aff-c791-5728-975f-c3f848744787.description: Form the 15th century onwards, part of the area below the chateau became a cultural and spiritual centre for the Moravian Jewish community. There was a Talmudic school, 12 synagogues and other places of worship. In the second half of the 16th century the legendary Rabbi Löw, allegedly the creator of the Prague golem, worked there. After a fire, the buildings and the synagogue were restored by master builders of the court. The synagogue is the only extant example of a “Polish-style” temple in Czech lands. It features four cupolas supported by four columns standing in the centre of a hall. The adjacent Jewish cemetery is among the largest and oldest in the Czech Republic.

5da28193-df85-5125-983e-01722d0be0e4.name: *The fall of Phaeton*
5da28193-df85-5125-983e-01722d0be0e4.description: Burrini is considered the most “baroque” Bolognese painter for his dynamic and fluid painting style. He represents the myth of Phaeton, who is falling down from the sky with his chariot and horses in a sort of vortex.

5da360c8-1992-5262-82c8-43e5fdfbccd1.name: Ground-floor Windows
5da360c8-1992-5262-82c8-43e5fdfbccd1.artist: Architect: André Soares (1720–1769), possibly in association with the decorative artist, Bartolomeu Antunes (1688–1753)

5dcb2629-41cc-5771-865e-799a7eb11951.name: Pulpit
5dcb2629-41cc-5771-865e-799a7eb11951.description: The basket and sounding board of the pulpit show a spirited moulding as was typical  of the era. Highly gesturally executed sculptures of the four evangelists are mounted in pairs to the basket, while at the very top, an angel with the commandment tablets establishes a typological reference to the Old Testament.

5e5ff728-46b9-5dbd-a88e-16ce672bc4f4.name: Chapel of the Holy Cross
5e5ff728-46b9-5dbd-a88e-16ce672bc4f4.description: A court architect who trained in Vienna and in Rome continued the construction of the chateau and completed the rectangular chapel in the south wing. The relief decorations, with the *Laying of Christ in His Grave* on the high altar, and the *Madonna of Old Brno* and the *Death of St. Francis* on side altars, were created by court sculptor Johann Stern, brother of the painter Josef Stern. The chapel portal, designed by Grimm, was executed by the Brno stonemason Joachim Günther.
5e5ff728-46b9-5dbd-a88e-16ce672bc4f4.artist: František Antonín Grimm (1710–1784, Brno), Johann Stern, Joachim Günther

5f26136b-1267-5ef4-9888-5bee5a1fa737.name: Nave vault and transept
5f26136b-1267-5ef4-9888-5bee5a1fa737.description: Stucco work in the nave and transept representing the Holy Trinity.

5f3390bb-5bf1-5895-b59d-b1ec1f2825e9.name: Ceiling painting *Last Supper*
5f3390bb-5bf1-5895-b59d-b1ec1f2825e9.description: The cupola above the choir depicts the last supper as the origin of the Eucharist sacrament. Illusionistic architecture, open at the top, in the form of an oval building with arcades, provides the setting for the scene which is presented on a narrow stage at the top of steep stairs. The scene of the Last Supper has genre-like additions. The cool colours, the relatively sober depiction of the scene and the austere architecture are clear features of the Early Classicism which Keller, drawing on Martin Knoller, was far more indebted to than the other two fresco artists.

60118261-bf39-5b51-becf-89deec2d3d9c.name: Invention of the Holy Cross
60118261-bf39-5b51-becf-89deec2d3d9c.description: The Counter-Reformation activities of the Capuchin order are reflected in this sizeable picture for the high altar. It depicts a key scene in the legend of the Invention of the Holy Cross on which Christ was crucified, showing Empress Helen, the mother of Constantine the Great, as she witnesses the Cross's authenticity; that the touch of the cross brings a dead youth back to life and cures a terminally-ill woman. Behind the empress stands Bishop Makarios. The use of light within the picture makes much of the resurrection, while the rhetorical gestures, artistic rendering of richly varied surfaces and a monumental compositional structure, make for an impressive painting. The canvas, considered the first Baroque painting in Moravia, originated at the same time as the *Crucifixion* Sandrart painted for the Cathedral of St. Stephen in Vienna, which was said to have been commissioned by Count Václav Eusebius of Lobkowitz, one of the most powerful men in the Viennese imperial court.
60118261-bf39-5b51-becf-89deec2d3d9c.location: Capuchin Monastery and the Church of the Invention of the Holy Cross

60296dc5-8d61-56ba-bc2f-3edce00a1d4f.name: The Capture of Christ and Peter’s Repentance
60296dc5-8d61-56ba-bc2f-3edce00a1d4f.description:
In the background from right to left, the soldiers carry Jesus away. In the foreground St. Peter holds his hands and cries when the cock sings as he realizes he has denied Christ three times as his master foretold.  
This fresco is generally attributed to Francesco Albani, a pupil of Calvaert and of the Carraccis. Along with Guido Reni he moved to Rome 1601 and abandoned the sadness of the late Ludovico and adopted a sensuous and happy style.

604cc244-889a-5a66-aacc-7f2528ae03e7.name: High Altar
604cc244-889a-5a66-aacc-7f2528ae03e7.description: The sculptural figures of *St. Rosalie*, *St. Sebastian* and Franciscan saints accompanied by a playful group of angels within the opulent attic of the Church of St. Roch, are the work of Josip Holzinger from Maribor. The chronology of Holzinger's work in north Croatia represents all the stylistic stages of his almost 40 year-long career. They also reflect the dominant stylistic influences to which his individual, highly developed formal language was exposed – that of Josip (Jožef) Straub (1712–1756) and Veit Königer (1729–1792).

607f2261-ddcf-5352-a0ee-33f57d581ee2.name: Cemetery Cloister
607f2261-ddcf-5352-a0ee-33f57d581ee2.description: The Monastery includes two cloisters: the Refectory Cloister ruins; the Cemetery Cloister, in the classical style, comprises arched galleries richly decorated with tiles that are incomplete. The monastic areas or adjoining wings include the Jericho Garden; the Courtyard of St. John in its original state as far as its structure and design are concerned, and complete with a small garden and monumental fountain at the centre and the Wine Cellar Courtyard.

61064b4e-4c79-5abe-a9ae-05568f433736.name: Ground Plan
61064b4e-4c79-5abe-a9ae-05568f433736.description: The building is organised on an axis plan, leading from the stairway through to the oval nave, the chancel and the offices, up to the bell tower.

6110f5b1-3f44-5eb5-b9ee-45cff6f20302.name: Relief cycle, *Life of the Virgin Mary*
6110f5b1-3f44-5eb5-b9ee-45cff6f20302.description: Ten oval, gilded lead reliefs with pictures depicting the Life of the Virgin Mary are mounted on the marble high altar.

61326b88-96a4-5ced-9671-1bceca375464.name: The Saints in Heaven (so-called Heaven of Dießen)
61326b88-96a4-5ced-9671-1bceca375464.description:
In this dome fresco, innumerable saints and beatified persons from the various branches of the founding noble family, the Counts of Dießen-Andechs, form a group amassed around Christ. As being such, they exemplify the cardinal virtues which are depicted in the pendentives.  
Having been carefully calculated both narrationally and perspectively, the oldest locally revered members of the Dießen-Andechs family (Rasso, Rathard and Mechtildis) are the first to catch the eye of those entering the church.

6133a83a-0997-5190-b0b2-40bcced633e0.name: Interior facing the high altar
6133a83a-0997-5190-b0b2-40bcced633e0.description: The iconographic and symbolic plan guiding the 17th century renovation culminates in the altarpiece for the high altar, representing the *Holy Saviour*, by Guido Reni and Francesco Gessi (1620) and surrounded by paintings by Giacomo Cavedoni (1622) hanging on the apse walls and depicting the *Story of the Beirut Crucifix*.
6133a83a-0997-5190-b0b2-40bcced633e0.artist: Guido Reni, Francesco Gessi, Giacomo Cavedoni

6170eca7-efbd-5cb1-8474-f0ef9b1c591c.name: Carillons
6170eca7-efbd-5cb1-8474-f0ef9b1c591c.description: A Flanders-made ensemble of two carillons with 92 bells commissioned by King D. João V, representing the world’s largest historical set. The north tower carillon has 45 bells and the south tower carillon 47 bells. The bells are made of bronze and their total weight is 217 tons. According to tradition, when the king was told the astronomic price of only one carillon, he answered "I didn't expect it to be that cheap, I'll have two."

6174afaa-9d22-5990-a88e-438c271eaecb.name: Trophy
6174afaa-9d22-5990-a88e-438c271eaecb.description: Four magnificent stucco trophies decorate the corners of the ballroom ceiling. They represent a unicorn head surrounded with arms and flags, creating an elegant composition.

62b3a30a-96c4-5dc1-863f-09b18e3e6d90.name: *The Archangel Michael Defeating the Devil*
62b3a30a-96c4-5dc1-863f-09b18e3e6d90.description: *St. Michael Defeating the Devil* is made of stucco and stands over the main door, in the counter façade.
62b3a30a-96c4-5dc1-863f-09b18e3e6d90.location: Interior (above the doorway), Church of Sant'Agostino in San Michele

632ade3d-0ea4-5615-a757-c3571c4ba4b4.name: Pulpit
632ade3d-0ea4-5615-a757-c3571c4ba4b4.description: One of the most important sculptural centres in Adriatic Croatia during the 18th century, Rijeka boasted Baroque churches that today form a thesaurus of Baroque sculpture of both known and anonymous masters. Between 1733 and 1772 Antonio Michelazzi’s sculpture workshop in Rijeka employed many altar makers and sculptors from Friuli and Gorica. This pulpit – with the seated figures of the four evangelists Matthew, Mark, Luke and John and bearing Christ’s monogram on the concave front – is supported by two massive volutes. It represents a strong plastic accent in the church since all the other altarpieces are within the radial chapels.

6332aef6-0e61-5535-815a-05022a32411f.name: St. Laurence
6332aef6-0e61-5535-815a-05022a32411f.description: Stone medallion from the medieval period that ornaments the outside sacristy door and is a vestige from the old chapel.

638b8d0b-c143-5fcb-b7eb-99c572ca9cf5.name: Cartouche with inscription
638b8d0b-c143-5fcb-b7eb-99c572ca9cf5.location: Central part of the arch below the niche

64257b77-a47c-5cac-9408-48a93277530e.name: Façade
64257b77-a47c-5cac-9408-48a93277530e.description: Entrance to the building is through two lateral doors at the top of the stairway. In the middle of the stairway there is an axial door that gives way to a chapel, which sits below the ground floor of the church. The axial door is topped by an oval panel and a large window with a curved frame; a form that will continue in the chapel interior. The large Classical pilasters flanking the central axis appear to dematerialise as they rise and the Baroque stone carving is enhanced.

64b1529f-4194-5ba5-ba30-0bd0414b0c72.name: Nativity
64b1529f-4194-5ba5-ba30-0bd0414b0c72.description: Portugal’s largest monumental late Baroque Nativity scene (3 x 5 x 4 x 5 meters), it contains around 500 figures depicting six biblical narratives, the Nativity, Annunciation to the Shepherds, Adoration of the Magi, Adoration of the Shepherds, Massacre of the Innocents and Presentation in the Temple.
64b1529f-4194-5ba5-ba30-0bd0414b0c72.artist: Joaquim Machado de Castro (1731–1822) and his workshop

6569b90f-9302-59c0-b1b9-bd845a85d868.name: Choir
6569b90f-9302-59c0-b1b9-bd845a85d868.description: The choir, built on an almost quadratic ground plan, forms the highpoint of the spatial arrangement. Separated from the nave by a massive, deeply retraced triumphal arch, it is designed as a centralised building, whereby the lengthwise oval design of the domical vault is only apparent on entering the space. Massive bevelled piers provide the support for the shallow barrel vaults which form short cross-arms to the north and south as well as the niche for the high altar to the east.

65803034-8993-5d4f-bda7-d5181acd7eec.name: Garden frontage
65803034-8993-5d4f-bda7-d5181acd7eec.description: The eleven-axis garden frontage was inspired by one designed by Hildebrandt for Count Archbishop Franz Anton Harrach in his Mirabell summer palace in Salzburg. Its frontage decoration escalates towards the central axis, with a portal and a middle-floor window crowned with a triangle, and peaking in a parapet of sinuous shape, so typical of Hildebrandt. The reception area of the palace is accentuated by the rhythm of tall pilasters and a balustrade with sculpted decoration.
65803034-8993-5d4f-bda7-d5181acd7eec.artist: Johann Lucas von Hildebrandt (1668 Genoa – 1745 Vienna)

65b630ff-6806-578e-b37c-687287b4028b.name: Attica
65b630ff-6806-578e-b37c-687287b4028b.description: As proposed by Hildebrandt, six decorative statues were supplied for the garden frontage attica in 1729 by an unknown Olomouc sculptor.

65e0961f-c135-53b7-936d-31d97f565267.name: Ceiling fresco: *The Veneration of St. Charles Borromeo*
65e0961f-c135-53b7-936d-31d97f565267.description: The frescos in Volders are among the most important of Knoller’s works. The apotheosis of the church patron in the main cupola is the high point of the programme, surrounded by scenes from his life. As an important representative of the Counter Reformation his veneration goes hand in hand with the victory of Catholicism. Knoller’s clear composition with monumental figures already contains elements of Classicism.
65e0961f-c135-53b7-936d-31d97f565267.location: Main cupola, The Servite Monastery Church of St. Charles Borromeo

65eba8ae-f9a2-5fc2-94ef-563d44d65d3f.name: *Azulejos* depicting the 14 Acts of Mercy
65eba8ae-f9a2-5fc2-94ef-563d44d65d3f.description: *Azulejos* representing the 14 Acts of Mercy cover the walls of the nave. On the Gospel side are the Spiritual Works and on the Epistle side the Corporal. In the central arch, a large *azulejos* panel depicts Our Lady of Mercy, who with her open veil, appears as if protecting the visitors.
65eba8ae-f9a2-5fc2-94ef-563d44d65d3f.artist: Attributed to António and Policarpo de Oliveira Bernardes [n.d.]

663341fb-1727-5934-b72b-3a793d3acfc9.name: The Glory of St. John of Nepomuk
663341fb-1727-5934-b72b-3a793d3acfc9.description: This aedicula façade, inspired by Roman Baroque architecture, appears like a triumphant, altar-like monument in honour of Saint John of Nepomuk. His admission into Heaven, symbolized by the canopy over the entrance adorned with gilded stars, is depicted in the medium of a three-dimensional stone sculpture supported compositionally and iconographically by the building’s architectural motifs.
663341fb-1727-5934-b72b-3a793d3acfc9.artist: Architecture: Cosmas Damian (1686–1739) and Egid Quirin Asam (1692–1750) Stucco and Sculpture: Egid Quirin Asam

663effd7-2e63-5a2c-a696-83675cd1674c.name: *Angel Musician*
663effd7-2e63-5a2c-a696-83675cd1674c.description: Angel musicians playing their instruments in the painted windows all around the dome represent a vivid and dynamic element of this eloquent illusionist painting.

666bff86-ca66-563d-a8c1-4a4350c7023d.name: Low-Choir, Tomb of Princess Santa Joana
666bff86-ca66-563d-a8c1-4a4350c7023d.description: The monastery’s low choir is decorated with gilt wood carving, tiles and marble. Above is a painted Baroque ceiling. The monumental sarcophagus of Princess Santa Joana is made of multi-coloured inlaid marble.

667bd081-852f-55d6-9cc7-bc832e3888f1.name: Christ Collapsing under the Cross
667bd081-852f-55d6-9cc7-bc832e3888f1.description: Havelka’s artistic expression and exaggeration of shape was rooted in F. A. Maulbertsch’s style, which was possibly mediated by J. Winterhalder Jr. or J. W. Bergl. Havelka developed his style to the full in the dramatic Stations of the Cross cycle. F. A. Sebastini, an associate of Maulbertsch, worked on the decoration of Count Salm’s residence in Sloup at the same time.
667bd081-852f-55d6-9cc7-bc832e3888f1.artist: Josef Ignác Havelka (1716 Ústí nad Orlicí – 1788 Brno)

66dfc443-c601-5b54-a7ec-cc7138d5f3ff.name: View of the choir with side altars
66dfc443-c601-5b54-a7ec-cc7138d5f3ff.description: The prospect of the choir is formed by the side altars placed at an angle, the curved triumphal arch and the illuminated transept. The former focal point, the Baroque high altar, was dismantled in the middle of the 19th century and redesigned in 1968/69 with the inclusion of a statue of St. Nicholas (c. 1680, supposedly from Ettal Monastery). The magnificent prospect is now primarily a result of the two side-altars whose imposing figures are the work of Maximilian Hitzelsberger.

66f63eaa-f1a5-5dad-8430-57fbeee250e2.name: Library
66f63eaa-f1a5-5dad-8430-57fbeee250e2.description: Of the original monastery interior only the library, decorated by J. T. Rotter, has survived. The monks transferred the shelves, made by a lay brother, to their new monastery in Old Brno. Corner niches are filled with allegories of continents by Josef Leonard Weber, whose family were sculptors active in Trnava, Slovakia, and in Budapest and whose statues can be found in the Znojmo region in particular. Some of the library folios actually originated in the monastery. J. G. Mendel, a member of the Augustinian order and a founder of genetics, also studied there.
66f63eaa-f1a5-5dad-8430-57fbeee250e2.location: Augustinian Monastery, Hermits of St. Thomas the Apostle
66f63eaa-f1a5-5dad-8430-57fbeee250e2.artist: Josef Leonard Weber (? Svidnica – after 1766 Trnava), Bernard Stettener

68654a80-6367-5fad-a886-df3ed8762563.name: Stucco cartouche
68654a80-6367-5fad-a886-df3ed8762563.description: The authorship of the excellent stuccowork has not been recorded although, undoubtedly, the master craftsman was a member of the Wessobrunn school. The attribution to Franz Xaver Feichtmayr, possibly with the involvement of his brother Johann Michael, is considered reliable. It is composed of rocaille stucco of the greatest refinement, which in parts has been executed in free sculptural forms and open work. As they ascend, the broad, bold forms in the lower section of the spandrel become increasingly delicate, and against the background of the main fresco dissolve into fragile vegetative tendrils, whose free play of forms also disrupts the symmetry of the cartouche. The rear-view figure in the spandrel fresco is reputedly a self-portrait of Matthäus Günther.
68654a80-6367-5fad-a886-df3ed8762563.location: West nave bay, southeast vault spandrel
68654a80-6367-5fad-a886-df3ed8762563.artist: Franz Xaver Feichtmayr the elder (1698–1763, attributed) and his brother Johann Michael Feichtmayr (1696–1772, attributed)

68e9823a-426f-5c71-85b6-2202e4741be6.name: The Altar of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary (high altar)
68e9823a-426f-5c71-85b6-2202e4741be6.description: The grandiose high altar, measuring 14 x 20 metres, depicts the Assumption of the Virgin Mary into Heaven through the media of painting and sculpture. The altarpiece can be retracted, revealing interchangeable backdrops which are used to assist with the theatrical displaying of salvation history on different feast days. Four larger-than-life statues of the Church Fathers flank the high altar on both sides – truly they are crowning achievements of Bavarian Baroque sculpture on account of their solemn expressionalism.

6963f2e6-4bc1-5d5d-9766-4c5b468084d6.name: Retable of the Jesse Tree
6963f2e6-4bc1-5d5d-9766-4c5b468084d6.description: A staging of Christ and the Virgin Mary's genealogy in polychrome wood. On the base, the figure of Jesse from which stems a trunk – Christ's genealogy – with the most ancient ancestors of the Holy Family among whom are King David and King Solomon.
6963f2e6-4bc1-5d5d-9766-4c5b468084d6.artist: Carving: António Gomes [n.d.]; Filipe da Silva (active 1718–?); sculpture: Manuel Carneiro Adão (active 1719–?)

69cdf891-6e4a-541f-80fe-030af8f5ae79.name: St. Vincent Ferrer
69cdf891-6e4a-541f-80fe-030af8f5ae79.description: Reinforcement work included construction of a terrace, lined with statues by J. Winterhalder Sr. and O. Zahner. The sculptor, J. A. Nessmann, came to Brno from Mainz and worked initially in the workshop of J. J. Schauberger. His statues in wood and stone are typified by soft modelling and compact outlines, giving them an air of urgency. The terrace once housed shops.

6a6d110d-3b84-5e46-a4e1-e3d49f9a2245.name: *The Martyrdom of St Servulus*
6a6d110d-3b84-5e46-a4e1-e3d49f9a2245.description: Late Baroque dynamics and pathos are characteristics of this painting depicting the early Christian martyr, saint protector of Buje.

6a906d8b-0bc1-5f1f-959d-21eda46497c4.name: Gilded carvings
6a906d8b-0bc1-5f1f-959d-21eda46497c4.description: Vine leaves, bunches of grapes, plumage-shaped acanthus leaves and *phoenixes*, combined with seraphs and musician angels, frame not only the exuberant oval frame of the High and Low Choir but also the six oil on canvas paintings and the two large windows placed each side of the nave.

6b1e3b8c-0d8c-5527-b9d3-642e4b7b458f.name: Bethlehem Chapel
6b1e3b8c-0d8c-5527-b9d3-642e4b7b458f.description: The Burial Chapel of the Virgin Mary is followed by a two-storey building loosely designed after Christ’s tomb in Jerusalem. On the ground floor are marble reliefs of the Birth of Christ, the Adoration of the Magi and the Flight into Egypt; on the first floor there is a chapel featuring Mary Magdalene and the corpse of Christ.
6b1e3b8c-0d8c-5527-b9d3-642e4b7b458f.location: Pilgrimage Church of the Elevation of the Holy Cross, Jaroměřice u Jevíčka

6b3927f1-b04e-5f3a-a184-d24f0c3ed3fe.name: Ceiling *quadratura*
6b3927f1-b04e-5f3a-a184-d24f0c3ed3fe.description: The wooden ceiling of the nave bears a perspective painting or *quadratura* with fake architectural elements, and in the central panel, the *Apotheosis of Saint Francis*.
6b3927f1-b04e-5f3a-a184-d24f0c3ed3fe.artist: Jerónimo da Silva, Vitorino Manuel da Serra, João Nunes de Abreu. [dates unknown]

6b44fe59-7a74-52bd-b3df-12c9adba8bba.name: *St Michael the Archangel and the Battle for the Liberation of Osijek from the Turks*
6b44fe59-7a74-52bd-b3df-12c9adba8bba.description: The compositional structure of the painting skilfully combines two themes: the *Fall of the Angel* in the upper part, and a depiction of the battle for the liberation of Osijek from the Turks, in the lower part. The traditional apocalyptic scene with fallen angels lying beneath the feet of the archangel – the victor – is replaced in this rendition by a depiction of the liberation of Osijek from the Turks. The artist based the symbolism of the victory of Good over Evil – of the archangel over Lucifer – with the victory of the Catholic Church over Islam. This was entirely appropriate for the environment intended, for Osijek had been under Turkish siege for 160 years (1526–1687).
6b44fe59-7a74-52bd-b3df-12c9adba8bba.location: High Altar, Parish Church of St. Michael

6b4d1462-1c3f-5d42-b337-330d26caf4c6.name: Cupola
6b4d1462-1c3f-5d42-b337-330d26caf4c6.description: The magnificent cupola, inspired by that of Mafra Basilica, is inspired by Rococo design.
6b4d1462-1c3f-5d42-b337-330d26caf4c6.artist: Architects: Mateus Vicente de Oliveira (1706–1786), Reinaldo Manuel dos Santos (?–1790)

6be16235-7200-5556-9bd2-0e18c38a6fca.name: St. Norbert
6be16235-7200-5556-9bd2-0e18c38a6fca.description: The painting of a side altar altarpiece is dedicated to the founder of the Premonstratensian order, St. Norbert, set into an illusionary painted altar with other “statues” of saints. The scene, climaxing in the Host, symbol of the Lord’s body, opens with the figure of an angel in counter-light. The light emanates from inside the picture and the viewer, deceived by the optical illusion of altar architecture, is pulled into the scene – a celestial sphere with glorified saint.

6be75fcb-c136-5464-b836-1965beae6a26.name: Façade
6be75fcb-c136-5464-b836-1965beae6a26.description: The entire idiosyncrasy and fancy of the Early Baroque building can be best seen on the façade which appears as if it was pieced together from a construction kit composed of the most bizarre forms. The departure from the classical theory of form shows that the dilettante architect (= enthusiast) was still an adherent of Mannerism, drawing his vocabulary of forms from religious tracts. Little of the often classical austerity of German Early Baroque is in evidence here. The chapels at the sides of the façade were added later in accordance with the existing design.

6c2db2b6-bf95-5968-8435-b88d7d3acfd9.name: High Altar
6c2db2b6-bf95-5968-8435-b88d7d3acfd9.location: Sanctuary, Votive church of St. Mary of Jerusalem, Trški Vrh, near Krapina

6c85a65f-6ff4-5d91-8ae5-f984c4d54097.name: Chapel of St. Joseph
6c85a65f-6ff4-5d91-8ae5-f984c4d54097.description: The altarpiece represents St. Joseph, husband to the Mother of the Lord. The artist, who trained in Swabia, settled in Vienna after a journey to Italy and supplied altarpieces for Moravian churches. The tabernacle and reliquaries were originally part of the high altar. The glass case (1750) contains a wax figurine with relics of St. Liberata, donated by Pope Benedict XIV.

6d5d6c37-c76c-5c00-aa84-68da154b6726.name: Burial Chapel of St. Ulrich
6d5d6c37-c76c-5c00-aa84-68da154b6726.description: The decoration of the crypt, dedicated to the patron saint of the diocese St. Ulrich, is a prime example for the local variant of the Rococo style in Augsburg, characterised through its playfulness and ornamental abundance. By contrast, the sarcophagus with the figure of the saint stands fully within the tradition of Baroque sepulchre culture.

6d626c54-3bed-51af-abd9-dd1ddb58f977.name: Allegory of Hope
6d626c54-3bed-51af-abd9-dd1ddb58f977.description: The dynamic figure “in a purely Baroque style” (parsonage chronicle) acts as a counterpart to the allegory of Faith, either side of the Altar of the Holy Cross. Each part of the figure is set in motion with marked exaggeration. The drapery segmentation follows the spiral movement of the figure but its main purpose, together with the facial expression of the statue, is to highlight ecstatic spiritual experience. The sculptures draw on the expressive style of M. B. Braun, under whose guidance Pacák worked.
6d626c54-3bed-51af-abd9-dd1ddb58f977.artist: Jiří František Pacák (around 1670, Starý Rokytník near Trutnov – 1756, Litomyšl)

6e4db345-1b0a-556e-bbd5-bd88afa359ae.name: The Marriage of St. Catherine
6e4db345-1b0a-556e-bbd5-bd88afa359ae.description: The frescos from the Veronese painter Giuseppe Gru form the vault’s only system of decoration, including painted stucco (“stucco finto”). This generates a uniform impression in harmonious colours, although the illusionistic architecture and the stucco of the ceiling paintings tend to vie for attention. The scene in the cupola is designed to be viewed from the congregation room and is composed of bouffant clouds interspersed with architectural embellishments. The actual event, the marriage of the saint to the Infant Jesus surrounded by angels, is depicted on the front edge of the shallow cupola and overlaps the base moulding in the form of angels, painted on overhanging pieces of wood, which appear to glide down into the room.

6e5aafb7-e8b9-5072-b2ae-7378c0d99a0e.name: Chapel of Our Lady of the Good Death
6e5aafb7-e8b9-5072-b2ae-7378c0d99a0e.description: Marble side altar with the Tomb of Our Lady of the Good Death, decorated with angels and garlands of flowers. On the tomb there is a marble bas-relief representing the Death of Our Lady in Jerusalem, which is surmounted by her Assumption.
6e5aafb7-e8b9-5072-b2ae-7378c0d99a0e.artist: Sculptor: João António Bellini of Padova [n.d.]

6f0f07b0-eee8-503e-a5b8-02651b202a00.name: General view of the Stairway of the Five Senses and the Fountain of Vision  and of  Taste
6f0f07b0-eee8-503e-a5b8-02651b202a00.description: This stairway continues the theme of the hierarchy of the five senses, as if revealing in the ascending course the degree of corporeity that should be attributed to each of the senses. The mythological figures found at the axis of the fountain were re-“Christianised” by order of the Censorial Court in 1774 having previously been considered “indecorous” due to their proximity to the biblical figures. The figures – whose original denominations are well known – were maintained and only the inscriptions were changed.
6f0f07b0-eee8-503e-a5b8-02651b202a00.location: The Stairway of the Five Senses, Bom Jesus de Braga Sanctuary (Bom Jesus do Monte)

6f14b3df-f1ed-5a46-bf19-8c72f314230c.name: *Allegory of Four Continents and Virgin Mary the Queen of the Universe*
6f14b3df-f1ed-5a46-bf19-8c72f314230c.description: The low ceiling is covered with illusionistic paintings: personifications of the Four Continents and allegories of the Four Elements; the Four Stages in man’s life. The Virgin Mary dominates the composition sitting on a rainbow almost in the centre of the ceiling.
6f14b3df-f1ed-5a46-bf19-8c72f314230c.location: Ceiling in the former apothecary of the Franciscan Monastery of St John Baptist

6f69a47e-294c-59c1-8a2b-a6157999fccc.name: Pulpit
6f69a47e-294c-59c1-8a2b-a6157999fccc.description: The richly decorated pulpit in the scrollwork style, donated by Claudia de’ Medici c. 1640 (monogram “C” with crown), is attributed to the Jesuit Friar Oswald Kaiser.

6fccc8a5-19f7-5482-b69d-9f79881ef1ac.name: *Hope*
6fccc8a5-19f7-5482-b69d-9f79881ef1ac.description: Figure of a woman holding in her left hand her attribute of a large anchor.

7015959d-b802-5549-a4a7-81818e774e68.name: *St. Joseph’s Dream*
7015959d-b802-5549-a4a7-81818e774e68.location: Altar painting, court chapel, Oršić Castle

7097bc44-e9d6-5417-8da4-35e4e2b28e0a.name: Monumental Staircase
7097bc44-e9d6-5417-8da4-35e4e2b28e0a.description: The double flight staircase was built between 1726 and 1738; the statues in the foreground are by Francesco Janssens.
7097bc44-e9d6-5417-8da4-35e4e2b28e0a.artist: Domenico Trifogli; Francesco Janssens; Giambattista Verda

70ec2281-ef4e-50b0-8303-a3fb3481192a.name: Pulpit
70ec2281-ef4e-50b0-8303-a3fb3481192a.description: The pulpit with rich, extremely delicate and intricate rocaille ornamentation and volute ribbons on the baldachin are the work of an unknown master craftsman. The wealth of figures and ornamentation appears almost overcrowded. The side figures of Moses and Peter represent the old and the new union: Mosaic Law and Peter’s Power of the Keys.

7135ec66-10c1-53a9-ba84-370a2120ea93.name: General View with Staircase
7135ec66-10c1-53a9-ba84-370a2120ea93.description: This beautiful staircase, designed by André Soares, was rebuilt in 1958.

718b140c-3c37-56e7-9342-578e4be4a043.name: Main façade
718b140c-3c37-56e7-9342-578e4be4a043.description: Four storeys, each with three window axes, extend above two compact Late Gothic access arches, with the central axis symmetrically framed by two polygonal bay windows. The building is crowned by a Baroque valley roof gable with volutes and a vertical oval window in the centre. The bold stucco composed of garlands of flowers and fruit, festoons, shells and putti, linked by foliage and strapwork, establish an unusually sculptural accent, thus giving expression to the wealth and prestige of the building’s owner.

71df805f-1b7b-5911-adcc-427480fc234a.name: View of the Monastery
71df805f-1b7b-5911-adcc-427480fc234a.description: The picture shows the monastery and church on the outskirts of Brno, and a village green with the small Church of St. Vitus restored after the ravages of the Swedish campaign. The church is adjoined by cells where one church father lived in each. Outside the cells were gardens demarcated by a two-storey-high wall that made the communication between neighbouring monks impossible (part of their asceticism), and thus guaranteed absolute privacy. The cells contained a room for sleeping, studying and praying and a workshop. These areas were connected by a cloister that closed off the courtyard of reclusion.

71e649d1-8512-5c78-b45e-dbe9c62e5ac6.name: Ceiling fresco: *Glorification of Mary*
71e649d1-8512-5c78-b45e-dbe9c62e5ac6.description: The choir fresco depicts a pristine Heaven of the Saints devoid of architectural set pieces or landscapes. The composition of the venerated Mary in the midst of the Fourteen Holy Helpers consists of groups of figures arranged on the clouds like spectators on the tiers of a theatre, as opposed to tracing a circular form. Here we have left the earthly sphere of the two western frescos and the glory of heaven is expressed in bright, airy colours.

720a6202-279b-5f2f-a279-276e169fe85c.name: Miracle of the Virgin Mary of the Snows
720a6202-279b-5f2f-a279-276e169fe85c.description:
The dedication of the church is associated with a story from the life of St. Ignatius of Loyola, the founder of the Jesuit order, who held his first service in the Sta. Maria Maggiore Church (Church of the Virgin Mary of the Snows), in Rome. The scene illustrates a plague epidemic averted from Rome in 590: Pope Gregory the Great leads a procession to the basilica, praying to the miraculous picture of the Madonna. When the picture was lifted an angel appeared above Saint Angelo Castle; put his sword in its sheath, and the plague subsided.  
The church presbytery contains a scene of the Apotheosis of the Virgin Mary, Queen of Heaven. The relief decoration was created by the Italian stucco artist, A. Ricci, to the designs of K. J. Harringer, who sent the altarpieces to Olomouc from Vienna.

7212b05e-72ab-5a3f-96b6-a69fb2c79452.name: Minorite Church of Saints John and Loreto, Brno
