7212b05e-72ab-5a3f-96b6-a69fb2c79452.description: The vault of the single-nave building opens onto a celestial sphere with a monumental fresco and scenes from the lives of the Saints John and Loreto. The illusionary architecture graduates into genuine pilasters and stucco decoration. The main section depicts the Birth of St. John the Baptist, while the presbytery vault, separated by a “triumphal arch”, features the signs in the sky described in the Revelation of St. John.
7212b05e-72ab-5a3f-96b6-a69fb2c79452.location: Minorite Church of Saints John and Loreto, Brno

724ecf67-8522-5e73-9afd-9978350e2c01.name: Hall of the Ancestors
724ecf67-8522-5e73-9afd-9978350e2c01.description:
Chancellor Václav Antonín completed reconstruction of a former garden room with a ceiling painting of the Gods on Mount Olympus and displayed larger-than-life portraits of his parents, grandparents and his wife.  
The Hall of the Ancestors is connected to the oval Historical Hall by illusionary painted architecture. It was here that the truce between Austria and France was signed after the Battle of Austerlitz.

73405eca-5c23-5cd2-a06a-559a0200f6cd.name: The Observatory
73405eca-5c23-5cd2-a06a-559a0200f6cd.description: According to Anna Maria Matteucci, when Carlo Francesco Dotti was appointed to the Institute – where he also designed the Library – he modified the plan of his predecessor, Giuseppe Antonio Torri. In particular, consistent with his architectural style, he simplified the baroque motifs giving the tower a severe, neo medieval look.
73405eca-5c23-5cd2-a06a-559a0200f6cd.artist: Giuseppe Antonio Torri; Carlo Francesco Dotti

746b9a00-54e3-5a9c-ad36-ed683d252746.name: Main Door and Bay Window
746b9a00-54e3-5a9c-ad36-ed683d252746.description: Central axis of the building decorated with *Rocaille* motifs.
746b9a00-54e3-5a9c-ad36-ed683d252746.artist: Architect André Soares (1720–1769), possibly in association with the decorative artist, Bartolomeu Antunes (1688–1753)

74c6cc96-1064-598d-8fdd-a09d0c9171cf.name: Chapel of St. John the Baptist
74c6cc96-1064-598d-8fdd-a09d0c9171cf.description: The Chapel of St. John the Baptist, with its lavishly ornamented surfaces in coloured marble and other stone facings, is in the Roman Baroque style. The bronze gates of the front balustrade and the bronze side doors display the monogram of King João V. The side panels – the Annunciation (right) and Pentecost (left) – and the central panel – The Baptism of Christ – as well as the floor (displaying an armillary sphere), are mosaics. Several types of ornamental stone are used in the chapel. An important collection of liturgical objects was produced as part of the interior decoration project: gold-embroidered vestments, several metal objects – candleholders, reliquaries and crucifixes – and also books for the Mass.
74c6cc96-1064-598d-8fdd-a09d0c9171cf.dates: The interior decoration of the chapel was commissioned from Rome in 1740 by King João V (1706–50) and constructed between 1742 and 1750, when it was officially inaugurated in Lisbon.
74c6cc96-1064-598d-8fdd-a09d0c9171cf.location: Church Interior, Church of São Roque
74c6cc96-1064-598d-8fdd-a09d0c9171cf.artist: In Rome architects Luigi Vanvitelli (1700–1773) and Niccolò Salvi (1697–1751) directed hundreds of artists and craftsmen; Mosaic: Agostino Masucci (1691–1758) and Mattia Moretti (d. 1779); Floor mosaic: Enrico Enuo.

74d429db-0e98-5a57-908f-8cf2399a89f7.name: Loreto and the so-called Náchod Chapel (St Anna church)
74d429db-0e98-5a57-908f-8cf2399a89f7.description: The Cardinal had a pilgrimage chapel built within the Capuchin Monastery in 1622. The chapel, modelled on an Italian Loreto to symbolise the Holy stable, the birthplace of Christ, was the first of its kind in Czech lands. In 1636 the Church of St. Anne was constructed next to the chapel, with a statue of the Black Madonna the scourge of the heretics. The complex was richly decorated with statues and stuccos. The church and the Loreto were destroyed by fire; only the chancel and the Náchod Chapel survive.

75199fa6-69bb-5d9b-b18f-1369a12f7cc8.name: The Holy Trinity
75199fa6-69bb-5d9b-b18f-1369a12f7cc8.description: The topmost sculpture of Christ the Saviour and God the Father, the ruler of the world, opens with the Archangel Michael, symbol of the eternal struggle against heresy. The dove of the Holy Spirit on a sunburst has its eminence underlined by the rays of the rising sun. Even the Augsburg masters took an interest in the gilding of the copper statues.
75199fa6-69bb-5d9b-b18f-1369a12f7cc8.artist: Ondřej Zahner (1709 Ettershausen – 1752 Olomouc), Jan Šimon Forstner (1714? Salzburg – 1773 Olomouc)

755d9e28-1614-5e7a-abb4-064ce943bbfb.name: Stuccowork
755d9e28-1614-5e7a-abb4-064ce943bbfb.description:
Most remarkable is the white stuccowork that can be found on the pulpit, on the altars and on the walls. The altars made of stucco lustro are richly decorated with saints, putti and ornaments. The white figures on the abat-voix over the pulpit made of black and red marble are brilliant works of art. On the top is St. Bernard who defeats Abelard, both performing dynamic movements and gestures corresponding to their dispute.  
The statues on the high altar (presumably) represent Pope Eugen III and Bishop Peter of Tarentaise in the middle and Archbishop Konrad of Salzburg and Bishop Otto of Freising on both sides of them. In their slight movements and in the breeze that blows through their clothes one can experience the dynamic of the Baroque era.  
Not to be forgotten, the statues on the side-altars and the excellent Rococo decoration on altars, columns and walls, are all beautiful examples of 18th century stucco art.

759ac58d-d5a3-5acd-ba7a-9d489af7bf33.name: Vaulting
759ac58d-d5a3-5acd-ba7a-9d489af7bf33.description: The symbol of St. John of Nepomuk at the top of the vaulting is the central motif of the church interior. It is a symbol repeated in the shape of the pointed windows; their incorporation into “lantern” chapels above the entrance vestibules, resembles a sword in a sheath. The metaphor also appears in the legend of St. John of Nepomuk; he refused to break the confidentiality of the confessional, his tongue being like a sword in a sheath.
759ac58d-d5a3-5acd-ba7a-9d489af7bf33.location: Interior, Church of St. John of Nepomuk

763c1dc5-b3ae-5fc9-b99e-a58d295dd192.name: Life and Work of St. Augustine and the Founding of the Monastery Weyarn
763c1dc5-b3ae-5fc9-b99e-a58d295dd192.description: The colourful ceiling frescoes are characterised by decorative elements of courtly genre paintings. They show three pivotal life stages of St. Augustine: converter, founder of the order and theologian. In front of the chancel arc, the fresco depicts the monastery foundation as a result of his merits.

76789659-5402-53ca-bb05-6967a2feb46c.name: Church´s architecture
76789659-5402-53ca-bb05-6967a2feb46c.description:
Curiously enough for a basilica of that dimension – with three storey-façade, two 80 m high towers crowned with domes and lanterns –, one cannot get a full view of its main façade. A near wall opposite forces the spectator to stand close to it (even on the terrace) so that one can only perceive a small part of the architecture with the eye.  
The church´s interior with its gigantic white half-pedestals and winding entablature appears mighty, festive and noble. The cornice with rich stucco work dominates the room so that the slightly prominent choir organs appear almost insignificant. In contrast to the architecture are the unpretentious fresco paintings in the vaulting, in some places illusionistically continuing the interior´s main motif of the columns.
76789659-5402-53ca-bb05-6967a2feb46c.location: In the Northwest of the monastery (on Romanesque/Gothic floorplan, incorporating parts of the old architecture)
76789659-5402-53ca-bb05-6967a2feb46c.artist: Architecture: Carlo Antonio Carlone; stucco: Bartolomeo Carlone; fresco paintings: Johann Anton Gumpp and Johann Melchior Steidl

767b259b-ec09-5677-98c7-f929983f4b2b.name: Drawing of  Pombaline Façades
767b259b-ec09-5677-98c7-f929983f4b2b.description:
Fire became a major concern after the earthquake of 1755 when tightly packed downtown Lisbon was consumed by fire that swept through the narrow streets and quickly destroyed buildings that were built closely together.  
Henceforth, buildings were separated by stone walls in order to isolate them. The uniform, multi-storey Pombaline façades (with shops, three domestic floors and an attic) are unique, constructed at a time when the focus was on safety and cost was a priority.  
The uniformity of the façades and windows is linked to the cost controls that dictated reconstruction: installation of the doors and windows were straightforward once all the stone frames had been made with identical measurements. The addition of a coat of arms was not allowed.

76936470-37f5-5740-97e3-6a78439dffef.name: Abbot’s Coronation Sceptre
76936470-37f5-5740-97e3-6a78439dffef.description: The spiral part of the sceptre is covered with acanthus leaves and multi-coloured cut glass. In the central halo there is an image of the Madonna of Old Brno transferred into relief form as a cast statue.

7701e3b1-be74-5694-b46e-d3d7094df40f.name: Main Chapel, interior
7701e3b1-be74-5694-b46e-d3d7094df40f.description: Main altarpiece with a huge retable decorated in *azulejos* in the so called National style. In the centre of the retable there is a reliquary in gilt silver donated by the pilgrims of Lisbon in 1680, it holds the image of Our Lady of Cape Espichel.
7701e3b1-be74-5694-b46e-d3d7094df40f.location: Sanctuary of Our Lady of Cape Espichel

773672e7-c81d-5cd0-bedd-93bea7b36705.name: *Allegorical celebration of the thermal water in Porretta*
773672e7-c81d-5cd0-bedd-93bea7b36705.description: This painted decoration was created to celebrate the family by enhancing the therapeutic properties of the thermal water which springs in Porretta, a small village on the mountains around Bologna, a feud of the Ranuzzi from 1482. Girolamo Ranuzzi asked the poet Pier Jacopo Martello to create an iconographic programme to translate in painting. Vittorio Bigari and Stefano Orlandi painted the ceiling between 1724 and 1725.
773672e7-c81d-5cd0-bedd-93bea7b36705.location: Ceiling decoration of the so-called ‘Galleria’, Palazzo Ranuzzi

77da7614-9b91-52f9-a8f6-51683004bb06.name: Panelled ceiling
77da7614-9b91-52f9-a8f6-51683004bb06.description: Presumably the work of master craftsmen schooled in secular architecture, the nave features a wooden panelled ceiling composed of rectangular and octagonal panels and gilded rosettes. Due to the intricacy and interlacing of the panels it was never intended for a programme of pictures. Nevertheless, it lends the space the character of a festive hall and heightens the impression generated by the altars.

792acd8a-ec3d-58f9-aac4-9e904aebd7b3.name: Altar of St. Ignatius
792acd8a-ec3d-58f9-aac4-9e904aebd7b3.description: Archbishop Emerik Esterhazy was the donor for the marble Altar of St. Ignatius. In its architectural structure, the altarpiece belongs to a type designed for jesuit churches by Andrea Pozzo. The two side sculptures represent the two Jesuit saints, St. Frances Regis and St. Frances Xavier.
792acd8a-ec3d-58f9-aac4-9e904aebd7b3.location: The first side chapel of St. Ignatius on the left-hand (north) side of the nave

795a67c4-4c3c-5df0-8c64-eacfd926fc71.name: Main Chapel exterior
795a67c4-4c3c-5df0-8c64-eacfd926fc71.description: The element of surprise, a major component of the project, continues to impose itself on all those that walk the labyrinthine streets surrounding the cathedral.
795a67c4-4c3c-5df0-8c64-eacfd926fc71.artist: Johan Friedrich Ludwig (João Frederico Ludovice, active 1718–1746)

798b4fa0-3381-5e10-8b2c-ebe673128ec2.name: Mercury Fountain
798b4fa0-3381-5e10-8b2c-ebe673128ec2.description: Mercury, the Roman god of trade, blesses the town's prosperity at the intersection of two streets. He is depicted with three basic attributes symbolising his vocation: he is wearing a *petasus* (hat to keep off the rain), in his raised right hand he holds a caduceus (a sceptre with a pair of intertwined serpents; a messenger's emblem), and has *talaria* on his feet (winged sandals to enable speedy travel). Mercury was equivalent to the Greek god Hermes, guide to the souls of the dead. The fountain thus features three serpentine dolphin gargoyles, symbolising three underworld rivers, the Lethe, the Styx and the Acheron.
798b4fa0-3381-5e10-8b2c-ebe673128ec2.artist: Václav Render (1669–1733 Olomouc), Filip Sattler (1695 Wenns, Tyrol – 1738 Olomouc)

79ee1d89-b25b-54b7-9f77-22260ee5d520.name: Vault of the Grand Hall
79ee1d89-b25b-54b7-9f77-22260ee5d520.description: The vault is divided into four sections by diagonal strips. In between each section, there are round medallions with scenes from Roman military history, as well as emblems with the motifs of antique military equipment: shields, torches and flags.
79ee1d89-b25b-54b7-9f77-22260ee5d520.location: Second floor, Palace of the Sugar Refinery

7a265b3f-2b51-5ca3-916a-6ac872b18851.name: St. Barbara
7a265b3f-2b51-5ca3-916a-6ac872b18851.description: Side altars dedicated to Saints Barbara and Tecla, Apollonia and Catherine feature paintings by F. I. Leicher, Maulbertsch’s associate, and statues of the saints by O. Schweigl.
7a265b3f-2b51-5ca3-916a-6ac872b18851.artist: Felix Ivo Leicher (1727 Bílovec – 1812 Vienna), Ondřej Schweigl (1735–1812, Brno)

7a442db3-4954-5129-a8ef-ef640fd2ef00.name: The first appearance of the Archangel Michael and pilgrimage to Monte Gargano
7a442db3-4954-5129-a8ef-ef640fd2ef00.description: The ceiling frescoes typologically illustrate the founding legend of Western Christianity’s most important sanctuary of St. Michael in southern Italy’s Monte Gargano. Typical to the era of a sophisticated 18th century is the circular landscape strip, on which Zimmerman settles his colourful figure scenes. The nature decorations are based on the French Rococo painting of François Boucher.

7b24d963-dbed-5062-9184-43967c49d4a8.name: Atrium
7b24d963-dbed-5062-9184-43967c49d4a8.description: Painted in the same style as the walls of the staircase, the atrium introducing to the main apartment on the first floor was originally decorated with sculptures, today missing.

7bb2bdb2-91ed-584a-9b73-434103abc508.name: *Sala terrena*
7bb2bdb2-91ed-584a-9b73-434103abc508.description: Of the 17th-century interiors, only a hall opening to the garden and flanked by two grottos has survived the many fires. Stuccos frame allegorical pictures of Earth and Heaven, the Four Seasons and the Elements, symbolised by mythological figures. The decoration is the work of M. A. Lublinský, artist, canon, and advisor to the bishop.
7bb2bdb2-91ed-584a-9b73-434103abc508.artist: Baldassare Fontana (1661–1733, Chiasso), Paolo Pagani (1655 Castello Valsolda – 1716 Milan)

7bb44db4-3bdf-59d8-a571-b142ef6d20a2.name: Lamentation of Christ
7bb44db4-3bdf-59d8-a571-b142ef6d20a2.description: The affecting  painting with Ettal Monastery as provenance is related to the Roman influenced classicism of Knoller’s academic colleague, Anton Raphael Mengs (1728–79), and is thus compositionally close to corresponding depictions from Annibale Caracci (1560–1609).
7bb44db4-3bdf-59d8-a571-b142ef6d20a2.location: Altar of the middle side chapel on the right

7bdc50c1-c5b6-5f3d-a9fb-5eab3d2363fe.name: *Mark the Evangelist*
7bdc50c1-c5b6-5f3d-a9fb-5eab3d2363fe.location: Pulpit, Parish Church of Our Lady of the Snow

7bfae956-1b6f-569b-bb35-b579c1e19ea0.name: View of the Choir
7bfae956-1b6f-569b-bb35-b579c1e19ea0.description: Interior with square bays of baldachin vaults.

7c25f7e8-78b1-5829-95c7-616fc23652e8.name: Chapel of the Annunciation
7c25f7e8-78b1-5829-95c7-616fc23652e8.description: Only fragments of the original paintings in the Chapter Hall survive. The subjects involve the Life of the Order (allegories of the Church, Taciturnity and Saints Bruno and Jerome), the Monastery and Czech History (Margrave Jan Jindrich, founder of the monastery; St. John of Nepomuk and Queen Žofie; St. Wenceslas), *Exempla* and Visions.
7c25f7e8-78b1-5829-95c7-616fc23652e8.artist: Franz Anton Maulbertsch (1724 Langenargen am Bodensee – 1796 Vienna)

7c3e742f-cfd4-500e-8e4d-e525b24f1214.name: Side altar
7c3e742f-cfd4-500e-8e4d-e525b24f1214.artist: Josef František Wickart (1691 Vienna – 1729 Brno), Augustin Jan Thomasberger, Jan Sturmer (1675 Königsberg – 1729 Olomouc)

7d2b3ac8-5006-5bd9-839b-0e54084544a5.name: Marble Hall and Staircase
7d2b3ac8-5006-5bd9-839b-0e54084544a5.description:
After the death of Carlo Antonio Carlone, who had been commissioned to (re)build the church and the abbey buildings, Jakob Prandtauer assumed the construction works. He was a well-known architect and conferred of course his personal character. He added an emphasizing, three storey portal to the infinite-seeming west wing, reworked the staircase and its façade and accentuated the south wing with a prominent middle part, the Marble Hall.  
Going up the staircase – a typical Baroque construction – one passes through different parts with different views to the courtyard. It culminates in a set back terrace in the second floor, a kind of imperial loggia with a magnificent view. Provost Johann III Födermayr had built it. He loved palace-like architecture, such as the prominent Marble Hall also erected under him. The façade is characterized by very large windows and pilaster arrangements (over three storeys) and a mansard roof, mostly used for palaces (the same provost had built a small castle nearby with another mansard roof). The Marble Hall´s richly decorated interior with oil and fresco paintings is praising Prince Eugene of Savoy who won the war against the Ottomans and secured therewith peace in the Holy Roman Empire for a very long time.
7d2b3ac8-5006-5bd9-839b-0e54084544a5.dates: 1706–14 west wing/staircase and portal, 1718–24 south wing/Marble Hall
7d2b3ac8-5006-5bd9-839b-0e54084544a5.artist: Architecture, staircase: Carlo Antonio Carlone and Jakob Prandtauer; architecture, Marble Hall: Jakob Prandtauer; oil and fresco paintings: Bartolome Altomonte

7d79aec6-af13-5110-a27e-45a7ec8a4d19.name: Fountain of the Five Holy Wounds
7d79aec6-af13-5110-a27e-45a7ec8a4d19.description: The motto for the theme of the senses is given by the first fountain, which refers precisely to the Suffering of Christ, and presents the symbolism that summarises the *Via Crucis*: The Five Holy Wounds Fountain. The fountain tablet presents in relief the instruments of the Passion of Christ.
7d79aec6-af13-5110-a27e-45a7ec8a4d19.location: The Stairway of the Five Senses, Bom Jesus de Braga Sanctuary (Bom Jesus do Monte)

7e5a4283-522d-5505-981d-d1cf2b78769d.name: Slope and Ditch with Bulwark and Ravelin
7e5a4283-522d-5505-981d-d1cf2b78769d.description: Besides its military efficiency, the large earthworks and buildings were important to social cohesion. The bulk of the architecture was a rhetorical statement that the country could face any menace from foreign armies. The fortification was, therefore built both symbolically and practically to discourage further enemy actions.

7fe4d5db-8af3-5754-8d9b-bd7179d3b9bd.name: Egypt
7fe4d5db-8af3-5754-8d9b-bd7179d3b9bd.artist: Johann Bernhard Fischer von Erlach (1656, Graz – 1723, Vienna), Anton Riga (around 1660, Královec – 1728, Brno)

8040d180-a30b-5c06-b882-58cee878370d.name: *St. Stephen* (Altar of St. Stephen)
8040d180-a30b-5c06-b882-58cee878370d.description: The young deacon, Stephen, is shown in a scene of apotheosis, surrounded by a wreath of clouds and a halo.
8040d180-a30b-5c06-b882-58cee878370d.location: Central inter-columnation of the Altar of St Stephen (south chapel), Parish Church of Our Lady of the Snow
8040d180-a30b-5c06-b882-58cee878370d.artist: Circle of the sculptor, Filip (Philipp) Jakob Straub (1706–1774)

8070db7b-4bbf-58ff-8f55-6d5199922b61.name: Cartouche with coats of arms of the owners
8070db7b-4bbf-58ff-8f55-6d5199922b61.description: The chateau was built by Countess Marie Eleonora of Harrach – daughter of Count Antonius Florian of Liechtenstein – and her husband Friedrich August Harrach. They purchased the demesne in 1723. The couple’s coats of arms adorn the chateau’s garden frontage. The drawing of the cartouche, executed by an unknown Olomouc sculptor, was supplied by Hildebrandt in 1728. The Harrach family was, together with Prince Eugene of Savoy and the Counts Schönborns, among Hildebrandt’s main benefactors and clients. Hildebrandt worked for the family for a full 30 years. His designs included the reconstruction of the chateau in Bruck an der Leitha, a garden palace in Vienna, restorations of a palace in Freyung and the Episcopal residence in Salzburg. The Kunín Chateau is among only a few buildings designed by this architect in Czech lands.

80903990-ddf3-5c36-bb78-e716a6d2f404.name: Congregation room
80903990-ddf3-5c36-bb78-e716a6d2f404.description: The double-pilaster motif of the façade is repeated in the rotunda, exemplified by the supporting walls between the arcades. Six uniform pier arcades open up between theme-generating archways. A circumferential cornice, which has been executed as a full entablature above the pilasters, unites the room. The vaulting extends above a narrow attic zone, divided by bands which continue the vertical of the pilasters. The large vertical oval fresco panels, which, so to speak, open the dome-shaped shell, thus echo the archways of the arcades.

80a1b956-25ac-5fbb-95b6-df261b896bca.name: Church of the Name of the Virgin Mary with residence of the Premonstratensian order
80a1b956-25ac-5fbb-95b6-df261b896bca.description: The model shows the ideal appearance of the church and residence that were not completed. Santini’s original design did not include a tower in the frontage, while the shape of the church held more true to the Marian star, as in other of the architect’s designs. The complex came into existence through the construction of the new church and its link with the Chapel of St. Anne; the chapel opposite was to be dedicated to St. Joseph.

8108fdce-e8a6-5545-97ae-8f3a83cc9a5b.name: Main altar
8108fdce-e8a6-5545-97ae-8f3a83cc9a5b.description: The main altar, in the centre of the chancel, has been placed beneath a cupola that has four large windows and some in *trompe l'oeil* windows too. The altar has Rococo spiralling pilasters and a gilt wood carved baldachin that crowns the image of Nossa Senhora de Aires.
8108fdce-e8a6-5545-97ae-8f3a83cc9a5b.dates:
c. 1751–1760  
The image of Our Lady dates to the late 15th century

811c78b3-34d9-54df-bc61-6623d14d26f2.name: Pulpit
811c78b3-34d9-54df-bc61-6623d14d26f2.description: The pulpit from the sculptor Moll from Innsbruck is an especially opulent example of a Baroque pulpit. The richly curved forms of the foot, parapet and baldachin feature a wealth of figures and symbols, including personifications of the divine virtues at the foot of the cupola and evangelist symbols on the baldachin.

812197e2-6d09-587c-afc4-a0c15fcc3d62.name: The Entombment
812197e2-6d09-587c-afc4-a0c15fcc3d62.description: Against a realistic landscape, several characters move dramatically gathering in foreground. One of the Maries’ is kneeling while eloquently pointing out to the viewer the figure of Christ, held by the Virgin.

8128a2ad-ec2b-5fac-8598-45527014f650.name: View to the Sanctuary
8128a2ad-ec2b-5fac-8598-45527014f650.location: Votive church of St. Mary of Jerusalem, Trški Vrh, near Krapina
8128a2ad-ec2b-5fac-8598-45527014f650.artist: Architect: Josef Hoffer (1700–1764); builder: Josip Javornik (active c. 1750); painter: Anton Joseph (Jožef) Lerchinger (Lerhinger) (c. 1720–after 1787)

81361e9e-cd2c-5f12-afd9-bc76a3a86457.name: The Annunciation
81361e9e-cd2c-5f12-afd9-bc76a3a86457.description: The niches in the side naves contain a series of eight pictures with scenes from the Life of the Virgin Mary. This was commissioned for the newly built Jesuit church and Marian congregation by the Count of Dietrichstein. The Marian congregation was originally to consist of Italian craftsmen and merchants. Domestic artistic output was unable to comply with the demands of the donors and the new functions of the commissions, however, so the gap was filled by Italian stonemasons and sculptors arriving in Moravia from the late 16th century onwards, and artists of Flemish origin whose style was informed by P. P. Rubens, and who met the requirements of Re-Catholicization. The monumental *Madonna* (1670) in the Chapel of the Virgin Mary is by Jan van der Furth, a Flemish sculptor, active in Brno.
81361e9e-cd2c-5f12-afd9-bc76a3a86457.location: Jesuit Church of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary
81361e9e-cd2c-5f12-afd9-bc76a3a86457.artist: Baldissere di Anna (1560, Venezia – after 1639, Venezia)

8145d2c1-7c14-5207-8402-31352fd57971.name: Represented music
8145d2c1-7c14-5207-8402-31352fd57971.description:
In the Baroque era there was a strong interplay of the arts. As contemporary music played an important role, it soon became a topic in the visual arts. In Wilhering there are many angels – painted, statues or on reliefs – concerting and singing for the glory of the Madonna.  
Painted angel musicians under the organ gallery welcome those entering the space. Above them there are stucco reliefs in white and gold representing music instruments, concerting putti and a painting of King David with the harp. Further up on the organ case, art culminates in an angels’ concert with gilded instruments.  
Another King David with a harp, like all statues in the church made of stucco, is standing on the choir’s organ and points the musical way towards the sanctuary. A fresco painting on the ceiling above the presbytery closes symbolically the round – a painted orchestra and a choir are playing the background music during the Assumption of the Mother of God.
8145d2c1-7c14-5207-8402-31352fd57971.artist: Bartolomeo Altomonte; Johann Georg Üblherr; Johann Michael Feichtmayr

81b4bb52-8b07-5a5b-88b7-ddd086e84db0.name: High altar
81b4bb52-8b07-5a5b-88b7-ddd086e84db0.description: The high altar with a height of almost 19 metres forms the focal point of the prospect which opens up when entering the church. As in a processional way, the sequence of altars leads to this central point. The altarpiece shows Mary as the Queen of the Rosary with the church’s two patrons. A special feature of the altar is the altar crown, a stage-like, perspectively designed Solomonic lion’s throne on which Christ is seated: “Ecce plus quam Salomon hic” (See more than Solomon). The statues (St. Augustine, Norbert as well as Vigilius and Cassian) were modified by Josef Stapf in 1768.
81b4bb52-8b07-5a5b-88b7-ddd086e84db0.dates: 1662–1665: ciborium; 1671: altar painting; 1768: modification of the mensa/statues
81b4bb52-8b07-5a5b-88b7-ddd086e84db0.location: East wall of the choir, Catholic Collegiate Church of St. Lawrence and St. Stephen
81b4bb52-8b07-5a5b-88b7-ddd086e84db0.artist: Paul Huber [n.d.]; Josef Stapf [n.d.], Ferdinand Fries [n.d.]; Johann (Hans) Schor (1615–1674); Egid Schor (1627–1701)

821cd765-2d08-5e55-ab82-e653efb6cb1a.name: Stucco
821cd765-2d08-5e55-ab82-e653efb6cb1a.description: The stucco of the Wessobrunn school, whose individual motifs have a playful aspect and overall create a harmonious impression of restrained elegance, largely contribute to the structuring of planes as well as the accentuation of edges, vault arches, and lunettes, occasionally lightly masking the borders. In the choir, symbols of the church, the papacy, and the celebration of Mass, presented in a trophy-like manner, are integrated into the ornamental system of decoration.

8277ff67-ae58-5300-9fc6-c53e66fabfca.name: Stairway
8277ff67-ae58-5300-9fc6-c53e66fabfca.description: The Tibães Stairway was built almost simultaneously with the first phase of construction of Bom Jesus de Braga in around 1725. It can be considered as part of the baroque “fashion” of stairways.

82817bab-a50a-5ce1-8f65-0d7b359e74ee.name: Chapel of St. John Nepomuk (Sacrament Chapel)
82817bab-a50a-5ce1-8f65-0d7b359e74ee.description: The chapel of the popular patron saint of Bavaria, St. John Nepomuk (today, known as the Sacrament Chapel) was designed in 1737/38 by Egid Quirin Asam. The dynamically curved architecture and the ecstatic sculptures of the patron and his namesakes, John the Baptist and the Evangelist, refer clearly to designs of the Roman High Baroque.

8335d26b-5dea-5502-948b-ed9fdba57da6.name: *Ensemble d’époque*: Dining-Room
8335d26b-5dea-5502-948b-ed9fdba57da6.description: Like the bedroom, the re-creation of an 18th-century dining-room is located in the east wing of the palace. Again worthy of mention are the *azulejos* that line the walls depicting rural themes, romantic scenes and *chinoiseries* most of which date to 1746.

83a35999-406e-5ef3-a9b6-1e038d1d60e2.name: Three out of the six original plans with a new layout sympathetic to the old one; final plan and orthophoto of Lisbon
83a35999-406e-5ef3-a9b6-1e038d1d60e2.description: Following the earthquake of 1755, the Marquis of Pombal rapidly ordered a competition for the design of *Baixa Pombalina*. Six plans were submitted from which he would select the winner. On 4 December 1755, Manuel da Maia and Eugénio dos Santos presented plans that proposed replacing Terreiro do Paço (Palace Square) with Praça do Comércio, conceived as a monumental entrance into the town through the Cais das Colunas (Columns Quay).
83a35999-406e-5ef3-a9b6-1e038d1d60e2.artist: Military engineers: Manuel da Maia (1677–1766), Eugénio dos Santos (1711–1760)

83aa2430-712c-51df-90c4-780d33fa5d69.name: *St. Apollonia*
83aa2430-712c-51df-90c4-780d33fa5d69.description: This opulently clad saint holds in her hands the attributes of her the martyrdom, the palm and pincers, which enables us to recognise her as St. Apollonia. Like her companion piece, *St. Barbara*, she is a characteristic work of Ivan Rosemberger. Rosemberger was prolific, making sculpture of a specific typology and careful in his choice of ornaments. His work set a distinctive stamp on the sculpture of the whole Varaždin region in the first half of the 18th century.
83aa2430-712c-51df-90c4-780d33fa5d69.location: Altar and Chapel of St. Barbara

83b6729d-7c75-5598-b935-15ef40ebd71d.name: Ancient Ruler
83b6729d-7c75-5598-b935-15ef40ebd71d.description: The impressive chateau entrance is rich in sculpted decoration. The bridge opens with sphinxes and the parapet is lined with vases with *putti*. The entrance gate is flanked by personifications of Strength and Power, symbolised by the mythological figure of Hercules and the figure of a ruler with the coat of arms of the investors. The gate pillars carry winged horses. The artistic ideas culminate in statues of ancient gods on the parapet: Hera, Zeus, Pallas Athene and Apollo, epitomising Good Government, Wisdom and the Arts (J. C. Pröbstl).

83bec619-3cc0-5537-81cf-5de75419f325.name: *Azulejos* depicting the legend of the Miraculous Finding of the Image of Our Lady
83bec619-3cc0-5537-81cf-5de75419f325.description: These 18th-century panels recall the legend of the Miraculous Finding of the Image of Our Lady at the site.
83bec619-3cc0-5537-81cf-5de75419f325.location: Memory Hermitage, interior, Sanctuary of Our Lady of Cape Espichel

83c8fa85-4413-5d4d-90af-066b8e8a993e.name: The Stigmatisation of St. Francis
83c8fa85-4413-5d4d-90af-066b8e8a993e.description: Rotter, who specialised in altarpieces, easel paintings, frescos and decorative wall paintings, was a major figure within the Brno guild of painters. His oeuvre is known from the 1740s, when he worked for the Augustinians and Premonstratensians in Hradisko near Olomouc, although the frescos are not preserved. The side-altar picture comes from Rotter’s late phase, when he embraced closed shapes and more simple colour schemes.
83c8fa85-4413-5d4d-90af-066b8e8a993e.location: Capuchin Monastery and the Church of the Invention of the Holy Cross, Brno

83d3decd-9c3a-5aca-8af7-4d9325db876f.name: Right hand-side altar
83d3decd-9c3a-5aca-8af7-4d9325db876f.description: The artistic highlight of the ensemble is the right hand-side altar from unpainted Swiss pine wood, probably the work of the carver Michael Lechleitner from Grins. The altar, which according to the inscription was donated by Susanne Kolp and Elisabeth Linser in 1652, is one of the most important German Early Baroque altars. In continuation of Late Gothic traditions it is covered in rich ornamental carvings from the repertoire of the Late Renaissance, while the overall form – a column aedicule raised on a high plinth with a vertical oval altar crown – is already characterised by Baroque forms.
83d3decd-9c3a-5aca-8af7-4d9325db876f.location: Southeast nave on the triumphal arch wall

83f00d04-322f-5906-895c-fe49ae869ea2.name: Formal or Grand Garden
83f00d04-322f-5906-895c-fe49ae869ea2.description: The Grand Garden, is flanked to the south by a monumental lake with a wall and upper gallery. The wall is divided into several arches, three of which lead to grottos. The other arches are covered with *azulejos* depicting noble horsemen. On top of the wall, the king's gallery has niches and busts representing the kings of Portugal. On either side of the King's Gallery two monumental staircases lead to the main garden.

84149fe6-4a0e-5c7e-942e-8173633f866e.name: *Gaiolas* Building Structure
84149fe6-4a0e-5c7e-942e-8173633f866e.description: *The Gaiola Pombalina* is a remarkable symmetrical structure built from wood to distribute and balance the forces of an earthquake. All buildings in downtown Lisbon were built according to this system, and this is the world's first anti-seismic structure. This prototype, built by the fire department at the beginning of the 20th century, is used for fire-fighting training.
84149fe6-4a0e-5c7e-942e-8173633f866e.location: *Baixa Pombalina* or downtown Lisbon. These drawings are displayed in Museu da Cidade and a prototype is in the Museu dos Bombeiros.
84149fe6-4a0e-5c7e-942e-8173633f866e.artist: Eugénio dos Santos (1711–1760); Carlos Mardel (c. 1695–1763), Manuel da Maia (1677–1766)

84897501-b74e-51a6-8afc-b37c98e434cb.name: Sketch of the frontage
84897501-b74e-51a6-8afc-b37c98e434cb.description:
The building, designed by Santini, was executed by local master bricklayers.  
The sketch shows that a double staircase in the front leading to the gallery opposite the high altar was dropped. The basic layout and volume of the building were thus geometrised into perfect symmetry – situated on top of a hill – between heaven and earth.

8510bddb-6669-55e4-b55b-9aa81ce25268.name: Stucco
8510bddb-6669-55e4-b55b-9aa81ce25268.description: With the brothers Feichtmayr and Johann Georg Üblhör, Abbot Höllerer succeeded in attracting artists of the Wessobrun school, who, collectively, had already proved themselves in the monastery church of Diessen am Ammersee. The ceiling stucco in the nave, largely applied in the form of cartouches, is characterised by fine rocaille figures which fill areas in some parts while establishing playful transitions between the architecture and ceiling pictures in others.
8510bddb-6669-55e4-b55b-9aa81ce25268.dates: 1743/44 and 1751 (reconstruction following collapse of the nave vault)
8510bddb-6669-55e4-b55b-9aa81ce25268.artist: Franz Xaver Feichtmayr (1698–1763), Johann Michael Feichtmayr (1696–1772), Johann Georg Üblhör (1700–1763)

8514c9c2-742c-59b9-b32a-26fca7a59c83.name: Main entrance
8514c9c2-742c-59b9-b32a-26fca7a59c83.description: The presence of two imposing figures (telamones) supporting the balcony of the first floor characterises the portal of the palace. Work of Gabrielle Brunelli and Francesco Agnesini, the telamones are made of local but very friable sandstone, called ‘macigno’. Thanks to the telamones the building is also known as the ‘palace of the giants.’ (il palazzo dei giganti).

8535523a-7de1-5689-8812-034669b2237f.name: *St. George Slaying the Dragon*
8535523a-7de1-5689-8812-034669b2237f.location: Church of St. George in Purga Lepoglavska

857d8aa6-3634-546c-83be-046a850d2c59.name: Altar of the Mourning Mary
857d8aa6-3634-546c-83be-046a850d2c59.description: Commissioned by the noblewoman, Judita Balagović Japranska, the altar is a showcase by the Varaždin sculptor Ivan Jakob Altenbach. Like his other altarpieces, it was probably created in collaboration with the Varaždin cabinetmaker, Toma Derwant, and painted and gilded in what was for the time a characteristic contrast of colours for altar architecture: dark paintwork on which gilt ornamentation shines out brilliantly.

85ccf86f-1deb-5026-b557-514be192d4e5.name: St. John of Nepomuk Worshipping the Virgin Mary
85ccf86f-1deb-5026-b557-514be192d4e5.description: The church altars were decorated by the leading Brno artists, J. V. Korompay, J. T. Rotter, I. Raab, O. Schweigl and J. Stern. The diagonal composition is characteristic of 17th-century Roman Adoration paintings (P. Cortona, G. B. Gaulli). The sketch for the side altarpiece is held in the Moravian Gallery in Brno.
85ccf86f-1deb-5026-b557-514be192d4e5.location: Dominican Church of St. Michael, Brno

85d4ddf7-7782-5fd0-9f12-244d2aa92c0b.name: Jesuit College and the Church of the Name of Jesus
85d4ddf7-7782-5fd0-9f12-244d2aa92c0b.description: The construction of both college and church are associated with the Counter-Reformation and the active approach of the Jesuits after the Battle of White Mountain in 1620. The management of the Jesuit College in Jindřichův Hradec made the best of their influence with the owner of the demesne and, after purchasing several houses in the town, they established a seat of the order there. In the west section of the square the original narrow frontages of burgher houses were broken by a monumental two-floor construction and with a church in a new style, styles which influenced all further building in Telč. The church was decorated by various European artists: V. Kovanda, F. J. Hamb, K. Škréta, J.  J. Heinsch, D. Gran and I. Raab.

86945764-6ee6-5a39-8aa8-6d6d98fb73a2.name: Church of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary
86945764-6ee6-5a39-8aa8-6d6d98fb73a2.description: Italian architects and stucco artists came to Moravia from royal service in Poland. In Valtice they created the first buildings in the early Baroque style. The original cupola on a drum, the first of its kind in Central Europe, was pulled down shortly after its completion due to its instability. Statues of saints were inserted into the church frontage, while the sculpted interior decoration gained importance dominated by heavy stuccowork. Artists participating in the decoration included G. da Cremona from Italy, the Flemish artist F. de Neve, I. Lengelacher and others.
86945764-6ee6-5a39-8aa8-6d6d98fb73a2.artist: Giovanni Battista Carlone I (before 1590–1645), Giovanni Giacomo Tencalla (c. 1600–c. 1650), Giovanni Tencalla, Giovanni Pietro Tencalla (1629 Bissone? – 1702 Vienna?)

87188e70-5901-5074-a091-18da8ed50017.name: High altar
87188e70-5901-5074-a091-18da8ed50017.description: The Baroque modification of the church was preceded by the exhumation of the remains of St. Notburga. The bones, in the form of a whole-body relic with rich garments housed in a glass shrine, were integrated into the altar in 1740. The bulky, two-storey altar with free-standing columns and a baldachin in the altar crown served as a form of triumphal gate between earth and heaven with the saint as mediator. Two of the outer saintly figures, Leopold and Emperor Heinrich II are attributed to Franz Xaver Nißl.

873474e2-e2a6-57ee-9fc2-5d408be01607.name: Angel
873474e2-e2a6-57ee-9fc2-5d408be01607.description: Monumental statues of angels on the perimeter ledge bear symbols of the Virgin Mary invocated by the Litany of the Virgin Mary.
873474e2-e2a6-57ee-9fc2-5d408be01607.artist: Anton Schweigl (1700 Gaiming in Tirol – 1761 Brno)

873719b6-be77-587a-8bfa-0e77decf061d.name: Plan of Slavonski Brod Fortress
873719b6-be77-587a-8bfa-0e77decf061d.description:
A regular star-shaped fortress (1691-1731) with the church of St. Anne (1743)  
in the middle. Placed at the centre of the Fortress, the pavilion style church was designed to stand over an independent tabernacle-altar situated at its centre.

874da6da-0212-5f0e-8a01-ffb1b3349b5b.name: Paintings from the Life of the Virgin Mary
874da6da-0212-5f0e-8a01-ffb1b3349b5b.description: On the wall are a series of paintings depicting scenes from the Life of the Virgin Mary, probably by the workshop of Bento Coelho da Silveira. Directly below, the chest of drawers has a gilded and carved back with panels representing scenes from the Life of St. Ignatius. The ceiling is decorated with acanthus, *putti* and Marian symbolism.
874da6da-0212-5f0e-8a01-ffb1b3349b5b.artist: Attributed to the workshop of Bento Coelho da Silveira (1648–1708)

8817f196-3685-51fa-b249-38607df00ba9.name: Northern side façade
8817f196-3685-51fa-b249-38607df00ba9.description: Religious motifs are no longer to be found on the side façades instead they are completely devoted to the amusement of the viewer. While the south side features a false window with a woman looking out, the north side is largely decorated with exotic animals in accordance with the fashion of the time. Three monkeys are sitting on the cornice with a basket of fruit, above them a parrot on a stick and a cat at the other end of the cornice.

8876c18d-f3ae-5f68-8a86-50eabdc4d86a.name: Retable of Nossa Senhora do Socorro
8876c18d-f3ae-5f68-8a86-50eabdc4d86a.description: Example of King João V style.
8876c18d-f3ae-5f68-8a86-50eabdc4d86a.artist: Architectectural design: Francisco do Couto e Azevedo [n.d.]; carver: Manuel da Costa Andrade (active 1740–1743)

889f8782-5e62-5b11-89a5-a0f388893265.name: Chancel fresco
889f8782-5e62-5b11-89a5-a0f388893265.description: The choir fresco depicts the Virgin Mary with the corpse of Jesus under the cross, as well as angels and God the Father breaking the arrows of wrath.

88c7204a-23d1-51ef-a375-c6869cf50789.name: General view
88c7204a-23d1-51ef-a375-c6869cf50789.description: The rich iconographic decorative program of the oratory celebrates the Trinity with stories from the Old and New Testament.
88c7204a-23d1-51ef-a375-c6869cf50789.artist: Lionello Spada, Francesco Brizio and Lucio Massari

88e757c8-ca10-5fb1-967b-a65fdddec865.name: Ceiling painting *Veneration of the Holy Trinity*
88e757c8-ca10-5fb1-967b-a65fdddec865.description: In his rendering of a heaven of the saints in the western cupola, the otherwise little known fresco artist Franz Joseph Haller has largely dispensed with painted architecture, with the exception of a few transitionary steps at the bottom edge. Instead, its effect is achieved through the luminous colours used to depict clouds suffused with light, against which the magnificent robes of the saints stand out dramatically. The composition is designed less with reference to the circular form than staggered from the eastern edge to the centre, thus oriented towards the entering visitor.

89542836-1bd2-508a-9e55-b7f2185eb881.name: Monumental staircase
89542836-1bd2-508a-9e55-b7f2185eb881.description:
Around 1688 Annibale Ranuzzi commissioned the construction of a monumental staircase for his residential palace in Bologna. The presence of a monumental staircase was a very important element in the baroque ceremonies connected with Bolognese senatorial class political and social activities.  
It is not possible to identify the creator of the staircase. Some believe he must be identified with Giovanni Battista Torri, who paid for the wood model of the work. Others believe he must be identified with the famous Carlo Fontana, who was contacted by the patron together with other architects.  
The work was finished around 1695.
89542836-1bd2-508a-9e55-b7f2185eb881.artist: Giovanni Battista Torri (?), Carlo Fontana (?), Ercole Graziani; Filippo Balugani

89c05fc9-f779-5631-bd7e-77ed9cf6185a.name: Altarpiece: *Baptism of the Indian Nobleman* and *St. Francis Xavier’s Miracle of the Crab*
89c05fc9-f779-5631-bd7e-77ed9cf6185a.description: The altarpieces of the side chapel dedicated to St. Francis Xavier, glorify him as the most important missionary of the Jesuit order, who, like Ignatius, was conferred sainthood in 1622. The painting depicting the baptism of the Indian nobleman is attributed to Johann Heinrich Schönfeld, together with the scene on the rear wall of the miracle of the crab in which Francis Xavier received his crucifix back from the sea. The images refer to the Jesuit order as the main bearer of the missionary counter-reformation.
89c05fc9-f779-5631-bd7e-77ed9cf6185a.location: First right-hand side chapel, Jesuit Church Innsbruck

89f1df55-2357-58fe-bc86-45fa395f58bf.name: The *Baptism of Christ*
89f1df55-2357-58fe-bc86-45fa395f58bf.description: The Baptism group, conceived as a counterpart to the pulpit, belongs among the major works of Swabian Rococo for, among other reasons, the sensitive gestures of the sculptures and the capricious form of the altar-like framing.
89f1df55-2357-58fe-bc86-45fa395f58bf.location: Northeast crossing pillar of the abbey church, above the baptismal font
89f1df55-2357-58fe-bc86-45fa395f58bf.artist: Johann Michael Feichtmayr (1696–1772); Johann Joseph Christian (1706–1777)

89fc8bb9-22fe-56d2-9d2a-03c49de73797.name: Pulpit
89fc8bb9-22fe-56d2-9d2a-03c49de73797.description: The long body of the pulpit is articulated by the sequencing of little columns, in between which there are niches with figures of Christ and the apostles. The copious employment of ornamental motifs on all surfaces of the pulpit and baldachin, along with the rich, gleaming gilding on the dark ground, are characteristic stylistic features of Late Mannerist Central European woodcarving.

8aaa5906-7f55-546c-b7da-d0174d9c8d33.name: Painted ceiling (central medallion)
8aaa5906-7f55-546c-b7da-d0174d9c8d33.description: A type of ceiling painting known as *di sotto* *in sù* (“above from below”), designed to create the illusion that the figures are suspended above the viewer when seen from below. The Ascension of the Virgin is influenced by Rubens' *di sotto* *in su* ceilings. The Triumph of the Mother of God oval medallion is contained within *ferronneries*.

8abb8c3e-33ea-5e72-82b2-aa08a95b720e.name: Library/Bibliothek
8abb8c3e-33ea-5e72-82b2-aa08a95b720e.description:
Surprisingly there was no library planned as an extra building at the start (but there must have been a room for the book collection), maybe it was planned and could not be constructed for some reason. It was added 40 years later to the east wing in two floors and in the form of an irregular cross. A gallery with a balustrade grid of wrought iron with gilded leaves and flowers is sitting on wooden and marbled pillars with Corinthian capitals. The window soffits and the corner pillars are decorated with stucco works (plants, ornaments and putti). There are frescoes all over the ceiling, in the cupola roof in form of an illusionistic architecture. All the fresco paintings show scenes that have a context of content with books.  
As the library wing is located next to a hill, there has often been damage after heavy rain and landslides; once it was totally buried. In the 19th century the building was sinking and almost collapsed. In 1894 parts of the fresco paintings fell down or were damaged by the rain. From 1969 to 1974 the library was completely refurbished and the foundation rebuilt.
8abb8c3e-33ea-5e72-82b2-aa08a95b720e.location: East wing, next to the church’s tower
8abb8c3e-33ea-5e72-82b2-aa08a95b720e.artist: Architect(s): Carlo Antonio Carlone (plans?); construction: Johann Michael Prunner(?) (and gallery?)

8abd269a-1a28-5ed5-b924-14d950ea3615.name: Invention of the Cross
8abd269a-1a28-5ed5-b924-14d950ea3615.description: The artist of the original altarpiece for the high altar came to Moravia via Vienna. He worked for the Bishop of Olomouc as a copyist and collaborated on the decoration of the Provincial Books. He settled in Brno, where, commissioned by the Augustinians, he created a sizeable *veduta* of the town (1675). A comparison with the present altarpiece shows a change in style within a single century.

8ac4cf22-50d5-5b6f-aa87-7f91455fb3ac.name: Water House
8ac4cf22-50d5-5b6f-aa87-7f91455fb3ac.description: Hexagonally shaped, the interior of the water house has running benches and is decorated with *azulejos*, the narrative of which involves scenes of leisure and pilgrimage (today completely destroyed). At the far end, there is a small house-shaped fountain decorated in smooth relief and with a protruding key. It is surmounted by a triangular pediment with a valve in the fauces of a stone lion.
8ac4cf22-50d5-5b6f-aa87-7f91455fb3ac.location: Sanctuary of Our Lady of Cape Espichel, East end

8aeeb74e-0d4f-5071-922e-9d1cbcceeefc.name: View to the Choir
8aeeb74e-0d4f-5071-922e-9d1cbcceeefc.location: Votive church of St. Mary of Jerusalem, Trški Vrh, near Krapina
8aeeb74e-0d4f-5071-922e-9d1cbcceeefc.artist: Architect: Josef Hoffer (1700–1764); builder: Josip Javornik (active c. 1750); painter: Anton Joseph (Jožef) Lerchinger (Lerhinger) (c. 1720–after 1787)

8b35ea4f-b3dc-5188-83e9-65b089384de4.name: Chancel
8b35ea4f-b3dc-5188-83e9-65b089384de4.description: The chancel is completely covered with gilded and carved woodwork. In the centre of the altar stands the miraculous image of Our Lord of Matosinhos flanked by Late Renaissance stone figures.
8b35ea4f-b3dc-5188-83e9-65b089384de4.location: Interior, Sanctuary of Bom Jesus de Matosinhos
8b35ea4f-b3dc-5188-83e9-65b089384de4.artist: Portuguese woodcarvers: Luís Pereira da Costa (active 1724–?), Domingos Martins Moreira (active 1746–1750)

8b8d95b0-01c3-5050-9691-e08552b65528.name: Scourged Christ
8b8d95b0-01c3-5050-9691-e08552b65528.description: The miraculous statue was brought by a monk to Louka Monastery from the Steingaden Monastery in Bavaria. It is a replica of an Adoration statue in the local *Wieskirche*. The statue was first placed on a side altar in the old Church of St. Lawrence where it was believed to heal the sick and enjoyed enormous respect. When a new church was built on the site the statue was installed at the high altar. The church decoration was determined by the new dedication to the Scourged Christ.
8b8d95b0-01c3-5050-9691-e08552b65528.location: Pilgrimage Church of the Scourged Saviour, Dyje

8b96a363-f446-5109-9d02-c46824b4fd8c.name: Entrance portal
8b96a363-f446-5109-9d02-c46824b4fd8c.description: The chateau was renovated under K. Liechtenstein-Castelkorn, at first to a design by F. Luchese, but after his death, to the designs of G. P. Tencalla. The current state of the facades (largely respecting Tencalla’s approach) is the result of a restoration, following a fire in 1752, by Cyrani of Bolleshaus and later F. A. Krzoupal. The courtyard was approached in the same manner as the external facades while the courtyard arcade has been walled-up. The facade features tall pilasters alternating with continuous window axes.

8c54f38e-a3cf-5faf-b07b-5c9551b5fb78.name: Choir
8c54f38e-a3cf-5faf-b07b-5c9551b5fb78.description: Detail of one of the small choirs. Its elegant and curvilinear profile and its stucco frame remind other creations of Alfonso Torreggiani. Choirs were usually built in churches to allow nobles families, or other noteworthy individuals, to take part to the mass without being seen. In small churches like this one, choirs were usually fake ones and couldn’t be used.

8c5e9db1-f7d8-5032-8c56-6187b6c635db.name: Neptune Fountain
8c5e9db1-f7d8-5032-8c56-6187b6c635db.description: The oldest of the series of Olomouc fountains is dedicated to the water god, believed to protect the town from the watery elements. Its counterpart is the Jupiter Fountain (1707), invoking the ruler of the heavenly pantheon.

8c6e7a5a-f8b4-50cb-b4d1-b5bba30ca387.name: Dominik Ondřej Kounic with the Order of the Golden Fleece
8c6e7a5a-f8b4-50cb-b4d1-b5bba30ca387.description: The spur for the spectacular reconstruction of a Renaissance palace for the Kounic family came from Dominik Ondřej of Kounice, Imperial Vice-Chancellor. Kounic first commissioned the Bavarian architect Zuccali and later D. Martinelli, who had worked for the family in other parts of the demesne (Uherský Brod). Only the west wing was completed. The bust was created by Jan Blommendael, portraitist of William III Oranje-Nassau (Mauritshuis). Kounic stayed in the Hague during the peace negotiations that took place between 1695 and1697. He was also portrayed by Hyacinth Rigaud.

8ce1345f-9a1d-5d72-9553-3b644103bd1d.name: *Phlegmatic*
8ce1345f-9a1d-5d72-9553-3b644103bd1d.location: Wall of the working cabinet, Ratkaj Palace

8ce91db9-f083-5822-bb05-df6162f52108.name: High Altar
8ce91db9-f083-5822-bb05-df6162f52108.description: The monumental altar, erected the full width of the chancel, originally had three mensas. The Varaždin Franciscans owed this stylistically up-to-date and, in the context of Baroque altarpiece making in northern Croatia, exceptional, altar plan to the engagement of the altar-maker, K. Zettl, who came from the distant artistic centre of Munich. The stylistic contemporaneity in the context of woodcarving in the sub-alpine area is evident in the characteristics of the sculpture, suffused with a moderate Baroque emotionality and typical of the work of Maribor sculptor F. K. Reiss, whose development in sculpture and his style was helped by his family links with the Schoy family of sculptors in Styria.
8ce91db9-f083-5822-bb05-df6162f52108.artist: Altar builder: Kristofor Zettl (active c. 1700); sculptor: Franjo Krištof Reiss (d. 1711)

8ce96854-8c7d-59a9-952c-b295df7f550a.name: *Glorification of the Miti family*
8ce96854-8c7d-59a9-952c-b295df7f550a.description: the ceiling is decorated with a motive of niches with cartouches and corbels; in the middle is represented an allegorical scene.
8ce96854-8c7d-59a9-952c-b295df7f550a.location: Palazzo Miti Zagnoni, first floor, hall of honour, ceiling

8d3b4ed2-289b-509f-9057-e51b50094952.name: Celebration of the Virgin Mary
8d3b4ed2-289b-509f-9057-e51b50094952.description: The ceiling painting blends in with the architecture illustrating apocrypha from the Book of Sirach. The painting is a metaphorical celebration of the Virgin Mary as the embodiment of Divine Wisdom: angels with mirrors serve to enlighten visitors.

8da4bfa4-102e-544c-8d43-38afff470b75.name: Congress hall
8da4bfa4-102e-544c-8d43-38afff470b75.description: The congress hall, as a second, far less intricately designed festive hall, was installed in the north wing and served as a counselling room. Its Rococo stuccowork on the ceiling was completed around 1758, in all likelihood by Franz Singer. The stucco is of extreme elegance and delicacy and lends the hall the character of an intimate chamber, which, while hardly in accordance with the original intention, reflects the declining political importance of the representatives of the estates.

8e028480-2139-5321-be75-aa5ace6155c1.name: The boxes
8e028480-2139-5321-be75-aa5ace6155c1.description: The boxes are supported by mermaids and caryatids all represented in different attitudes.
8e028480-2139-5321-be75-aa5ace6155c1.artist: Bolognese sculptors, probably Camporesi or Balugani

8e48c406-81de-53cf-94cd-3dd8775f331d.name: Pulpit
8e48c406-81de-53cf-94cd-3dd8775f331d.description: The pulpit, with its wooden core freely ornamented with stucco is one of the most remarkable Rococo pulpits in the entire south German-speaking region. An exemplary feature is the towering baldachin with its rocaille work ascending freely like waves, a masterpiece of the stucco mason’s art. The rocaille work of the baldachin contains symbols of the sermon – Tablets of the Law, flaming sword and the holy spirit in the form of a dove – while the pulpit itself has a purely ornamental design.
8e48c406-81de-53cf-94cd-3dd8775f331d.location: East side of the nave, central pillar

8ef6164d-8b25-56fd-9a75-9a922be66c14.name: Mass Chalice and Jugs
8ef6164d-8b25-56fd-9a75-9a922be66c14.description: Apart from the chalice decorated with half-figures of the order’s saints painted on enamel, and jugs for Abbot Zirckl, there were two other chalices for assisting priests, with scenes from the Lfe and Torment of St. John of Nepomuk and the Passion, created in the Augsburg workshop for the coronation.

8ef9bfb4-d3b4-5ef0-87cf-354fa15fff3a.name: Summerhouse, interior, festive hall
8ef9bfb4-d3b4-5ef0-87cf-354fa15fff3a.description: The building erected in the convent garden by Hall’s master builder Simon Gremblich in 1715/16, served the ladies of the endowment as a summer residence. At its centre is located the festive hall extending across seven window axes with its important wall and ceiling frescos from the hand of Kaspar Waldmann. Here the painter operated, in a manner of speaking, as both architect and sculptor, structuring all the walls in illusionistic depictions of High Baroque architectural forms. These form a framework for the theological programme of images of female biblical figures – role models for the ladies of the endowment – while in the ceiling panel, the benefactress herself, Archduchess Magdalena appears before the Holy Trinity.

8efd1f12-5052-51ee-9e54-57876db45757.name: Chapel of All Saints
8efd1f12-5052-51ee-9e54-57876db45757.description: Under a stuccoed baldachin, lifted by angels, the altar of relics is presented to the believers. To its sides, the skeletons of the Four Holy Abbots: Wigpertus, Nidgarius, Adalbero and Thosse are presented in showcases. The connection of their dead bodies with an image of the Crucifixion suggests their successful emulation of Christ.
8efd1f12-5052-51ee-9e54-57876db45757.artist: Matthias Lotter [n.d.]; Johann Georg Knappich (1637–1704); Johann Georg Schmierer [n.d.]

8f913dd6-44f7-5383-a80c-856aa602cf61.name: Interior, facing east
8f913dd6-44f7-5383-a80c-856aa602cf61.description: The spatial image, dominated by the Early Baroque fittings, is divided into two zones, a lower with side chapels and altars and an upper with choir lofts and vault, which are characterised by the bold, heavy stucco and the colourful fresco panels. The altars are arranged according to the strict Early Baroque aedicula scheme and are all framed in black and gold. The high altar with its triumphal altar crown forms the connection between the two zones. The indirect light falling on chapels and choir lofts plays a decisive role in generating the atmosphere of a scared theatre.
8f913dd6-44f7-5383-a80c-856aa602cf61.location: Catholic Collegiate Church of St. Lawrence and St. Stephen
8f913dd6-44f7-5383-a80c-856aa602cf61.artist: Christoph Gumpp the younger (1600–1672); Bernardo Pasquale [n.d.]; Kaspar Waldmann (1657–1720)

8fa2cd8d-b816-515a-9e0d-d37d36b4f317.name: Ceiling fresco
8fa2cd8d-b816-515a-9e0d-d37d36b4f317.description: According to Gumpp’s plans the large hall was originally intended to be decorated exclusively with stucco, however this was abandoned. A competition was announced, which was won by Asam. The ceiling picture, largely depicting the glorification of the state of Tyrol and its various regions, was designed and painted by Asam according to a conceit from Stickler, the Abbot of Wilten.

8fe0581a-5b87-5ce5-b038-f57ad44a0666.name: The Re-establishment of the Dießen monastery by the Counts of Andechs
8fe0581a-5b87-5ce5-b038-f57ad44a0666.description:
Contrary to custom, it is not St. Augustine, the founder of the order of the Augustinian Canons, who dominates the series of frescos, but rather the history of the Dießen monastery itself. This was done to remind the House of Wittelbach as contemporary rulers of Bavaria of its responsibility to care for the monastery as the legal successors of the founding family which had died out in the Middle Ages.  
The main fresco recalls the re-establishment of the former double monastery by Count Berthold II of Andechs in this way: Under celestial auspices, papal confirmation is given to the men’s convent of St. Mary in 1132 against the backdrop of the Lateran Palace in Rome. On the other side, the admission of Mechtildis, the Count’s juvenile daughter, into the short-lived women’s convent of St. Stephen in 1139 is depicted against an imagined backdrop of the medieval local monastery church, typologically referring to Mary’s entrance into the Temple.

90011718-442c-5028-93d5-960d464ee51f.name: Façade of the Church of St. Engrácia

914274d1-3d96-57be-befe-0bf0a94e33ac.name: *Vojslava of Hrádek*
914274d1-3d96-57be-befe-0bf0a94e33ac.description: Legend has it that the monastery was founded in 1211 by Markvard of Hrádek and his wife Vojslava. Their fictitious portraits originally decorated the refectory. The couple is represented in 17th-century attire. Their spiritual intentions made clear by their gestures, their majestic posture illustrates their determination in the execution of theose intentions. The composition, a richly ornamented table and background covered in drapery, is a traditional painting scheme.

9159ffdd-4a9a-524e-8b47-9e3d2e15912a.name: Plan of the Cathedral of St. Theresa, Požega
9159ffdd-4a9a-524e-8b47-9e3d2e15912a.description:
Late Baroque longitudinal, centralised type with curved lateral chapels  
positioned on a transversal axe.

916476d2-c19c-58a3-8bc7-4dbd353724d6.name: Parnassus Fountain
916476d2-c19c-58a3-8bc7-4dbd353724d6.description: “Art monuments” have their clients and designers as well as those who build them, the stonemasons, builders and other craftsmen, and sometimes bureaucrats as well. The construction of the fountain was administered by the Senator of Brno, J. I. Dechau. He supervised the architect and managed the builders and, when it was completed, he had a print engraved in which he proudly stated his name under the picture. He may be the man depicted here explaining the fountain’s symbolism to a group of aristocrats.

9177ddb1-aa6a-5f3f-9e90-4bcc20f58655.name: Chapel of St. Magnus
9177ddb1-aa6a-5f3f-9e90-4bcc20f58655.description: Designed as an oval mausoleum rotunda, the Burial Chapel of St. Magnus legendarily goes back to his foundation of the church and is, therefore, a pilgrimage destination as well as a traditional site for the abbey itself. The dignified marble decorations include sculptures of Magnus of Füssen and saints of the Benedictine Order: St. Benedict, St. Scholastica, St. Gallus and St. Columbanus.
9177ddb1-aa6a-5f3f-9e90-4bcc20f58655.dates:
1712: construction  
1717: altar, including the sitting figure of St. Magnus  
1724: statues of saints  
1751/52: decoration of the vaults
9177ddb1-aa6a-5f3f-9e90-4bcc20f58655.location: Facing south, below the organ loft of the monastery church
9177ddb1-aa6a-5f3f-9e90-4bcc20f58655.artist: Architectural design and altar design: Johann Jakob Herkomer (1652–1717); Sculptures: Franz Anton Sturm (1690–1757); Stucco: Joseph Fischer; Ceiling paintings: Franz Anton Zeiler (1716–93/94)

926bb9de-1635-5964-8408-1522672f9fdd.name: Church's architecture and interior
926bb9de-1635-5964-8408-1522672f9fdd.description:
Standing in front of the Engelszell abbey church one perceives the similarity with the façade of the abbey church in Wilhering: both main façades have the tower in the centre and are divided into zones – there is the base storey, the zone with the giant pilasters, the attic and tower storey (in Wilhering there are two). In addition, both have a high and richly curved roof and inside the nave’s walls the pilaster order is alike. As a creative addition, the ground floor is shaped as a slightly curved ellipse in the Engelszell church, unlike the rectangle ground floor in Wilhering.  
The fresco paintings and the stucco work in Wilhering and in Engelszell were done by the same artists, in Engelszell the fresco painter also did all the altar paintings. Furthermore the team was extended by a Tyrolian wood and stone carver who was then very popular in Lower Bavaria. He created the church´s portal decoration, the choir stalls, the organ case and four statues of angels in the choir niches.  
When the defective vault´s masonry in the nave was restored in 1839 the ceiling´s fresco painting was destroyed and afterwards painted white. In the 1950s it was re-painted by an artist. The then-ruling abbot chose *The Angels´ Choirs and the Holy Virgin as their Queen* as the topic and only asked the artist to adapt the artwork in colour and style harmoniously to the Altomonte fresco paintings.
926bb9de-1635-5964-8408-1522672f9fdd.location: In the North of the monastery buildings

92a08715-2350-530f-b788-77727a9408e0.name: Sculptures of the chancel screen
92a08715-2350-530f-b788-77727a9408e0.description: Towards the end of World War II the entire choir area was destroyed by fire, including the high altar, the choir screen and the tabernacle. Of the four evangelist figures flanking the passageways through to the choir, only Marcus, John and Lucas have remained intact. They are counted among the most accomplished Baroque sculptures in Bavaria.

93e214a2-7f15-5e87-87e8-625bd4fe8857.name: High altar
93e214a2-7f15-5e87-87e8-625bd4fe8857.description: The three altars, built in 1770, are still entirely in the tradition of the Late Baroque. The high altar with its column superstructure and the towering altar crown completely fills the east wall of the choir. The large altarpiece depicts the Coronation of the Virgin Mary by the Holy Trinity, a formidable work of the artist Johann Mitterwurzer from Mühlbach, painted in 1778 and drawing on the altarpiece from the predecessor building. The statues, Jacob the Elder, the patron of the parish, Peter, Paul and the missionary Francis Xavier, are executed employing the majolica technique.

94031aeb-2e89-58b2-8d43-398dcb900c96.name: Altar of the Eleven Thousand Virgins
94031aeb-2e89-58b2-8d43-398dcb900c96.description: This gilt wood retable with three levels of round-arch niches containing busts and relics is surmounted by a frieze with cherubs. Above it is a painting of the Virgin Mary by Martim Conrado.

9457f0e4-3fcf-50a6-aec1-b755319d7119.name: Ground-plan reconstruction
9457f0e4-3fcf-50a6-aec1-b755319d7119.description: The original ground plan was altered by the construction of the sacristy and oratory. The symbolic design of a four-apse central construction is an allusion on the “double” temple in Jerusalem, close to the Holy Grave.
9457f0e4-3fcf-50a6-aec1-b755319d7119.artist: František Benedikt Klíčník? (1677 Ivanovice na Hané – 1755 Brno)

9472b01a-4d61-5273-a492-4252a74c1f5d.name: Souls in Purgatory
9472b01a-4d61-5273-a492-4252a74c1f5d.description: The altarpieces originated in parallel with the wall paintings. Leicher had studied in a Piarist school in Příbor, and worked for the order in Mikulov. He probably mediated commissions in Mikulov and Kroměříž to his friend, F. A. Maulbertsch with whom he collaborated, and whose specific style became the cornerstone of his work. The dramatic air of the predella picture derives from its subject. Leicher, influenced by M. Unterberger rather than the expressivity of P. Troger, usually opted for a more classical, lyrical approach.

948b8793-f65d-5074-831e-9d04a6833408.name: Holy Stairs
948b8793-f65d-5074-831e-9d04a6833408.description: A three-shouldered staircase is the conceptual climax of the Loreto Chapel. Praying on their knees, worshippers ascend to an Ecce Homo group, stopping at the symbols of Christ’s suffering. The 28 steps recall the stairs climbed by Christ in the Palace of Jerusalem after his condemnation by Pontius Pilate. The entrance portal of the Loreto stable is guarded by a pair of angels, and a relief of the Transfer of Santa Casa (Holy House) with the Virgin Mary at the centre, surrounded by the patron saints of the church. The vaults of the gallery around the Holy House and above the stairs, placed in front of the presbytery, were painted by F. Ř. I. Eckstein, and feature scenes from the Life of the Virgin Mary. They are framed by illusionary architecture graduating into grisaille paintings, also covering the Holy House. The chapel contains a number of pictures by Brno artists, among whom, J. I. Havelka, who created a great number of paintings for the Minorite order and probably lived in the monastery.
948b8793-f65d-5074-831e-9d04a6833408.location: Minorite Church of the Saints John and Loreto
948b8793-f65d-5074-831e-9d04a6833408.artist: Mořic Grimm (1669 Achdorf – 1757 Brno), Anton Johann Ospel

949beb48-45b8-5856-b363-32eb9f163579.name: Frescos of the *Virtues of St. Corbinian*; the *Apotheosis of St. Corbinian*; *Theological Virtues*; the *Enthroned Mother of God*; *Adoration of the Lamb*
949beb48-45b8-5856-b363-32eb9f163579.description: The Asam's paintings and stucco form an inseparable symbiosis; even the frescos participate in a decorative system, unfolding in front of a painted ground of brocade. The impetus to unite the genres becomes most apparent in the painted *trompe l'oeil* cupola, following the style of Roman examples (S. Ignazio and Il Gesù). While the high altar is dedicated to the Virgin Mary, the ceiling represents the second patron, St. Corbinian. The frescos show (starting in the west): the *Virtues of St. Corbinian Annihilating the Vice* and *The apotheosis of St. Corbinian*; followed by: *Theological Virtues*, framed by the coat-of-arms of the bishops of Freising; *The Enthroned Mother of God* (in the *trompe l´oeil* cupola); and the *Adoration of the lamb*.
949beb48-45b8-5856-b363-32eb9f163579.artist: Egid Quirin Asam (1692–1750); Cosmas Damian Asam (1686–1739)

94e616f1-2015-5f83-a8bb-76438726f9d0.name: *Souls in Purgatory*
94e616f1-2015-5f83-a8bb-76438726f9d0.description: The dynamic contour lines and the sharp edges stress the drama of the scene: souls in the flames of purgatory, and hovering above them, the redemptive figure of an angel.

95109161-87b5-5953-88a1-413967eb4236.name: Ceiling Painting
95109161-87b5-5953-88a1-413967eb4236.description: The original ceiling painting comprising architectural elements was made by the Spanish painter Francisco Venegas at the end of the 16th century. The Triumph of the Holy Cross, among other scenes from the bible, were mostly inspired by engravings from Antwerp and added in the early 17th century by the Portuguese painter, Amaro do Vale.

962e003b-defe-58d1-85ea-6105adc77f5a.name: *St. Charles Borromeo* (detail)
962e003b-defe-58d1-85ea-6105adc77f5a.location: Upper inner rim of the monument

965899fc-aa3e-5147-ae6e-550eff2b95c8.name: Loggia and arcades
965899fc-aa3e-5147-ae6e-550eff2b95c8.description: A scenographic view of the loggia shows different points of view obtained through the use of columns, balustrades and arcades. This is typical of the local baroque tradition.

9683c02e-cb4c-54e9-994d-daff1aae6652.name: Exterior
9683c02e-cb4c-54e9-994d-daff1aae6652.description: The imposing building together with those surrounding it forms an impressive ensemble. The church is surmounted by a tower on the west wall which was retained from the Gothic predecessor. The high Gothic helm-roof contrasts with the subdued design of the rest of the building with uniform pilaster arrangement and a cornice as the sole unifying element. The arrangement of the windows corresponds to the multi-storey configuration of the interior walls.

9767c365-8093-52c3-83c1-3946d0072faa.name: View from the east
9767c365-8093-52c3-83c1-3946d0072faa.description: Although the arrangement of the rest of the building is not as closely crowded as the façade, the walls are still un-classical in their configuration. The superstructure with perimeter pilasters throughout and an attic zone is modelled on St. Peter’s in Rome, as is the building’s basic design with domed tri-conch. The tower, expressing the motif of the Trinity, was originally designed with a spiral-shaped pinnacle.

976874d7-3e8f-5368-ba10-5054c2f2a238.name: Oil paintings
976874d7-3e8f-5368-ba10-5054c2f2a238.description: Three examples of the six oil paintings that make up the Cycle of the Life of the Virgin and the Childhood of Jesus.
976874d7-3e8f-5368-ba10-5054c2f2a238.artist: Attributed to Bento Coelho da Silveira's workshop, Lisbon (1648–1708)

977620b0-e9c5-5c9f-a82f-14e43800712f.name: Pompeo Aldrovandi reconciles the Papal Estate with the Reign of Spain
977620b0-e9c5-5c9f-a82f-14e43800712f.description: A very significant episode in the career of Pompeo Aldrovandi as a diplomat.
977620b0-e9c5-5c9f-a82f-14e43800712f.location: Interior, first floor, palazzo Aldrovandi Montanari
977620b0-e9c5-5c9f-a82f-14e43800712f.artist: Vittorio Maria Bigari and Stefano Orlandi

9779dbd4-5cc7-5f2e-8017-625b454897d3.name: High altar
9779dbd4-5cc7-5f2e-8017-625b454897d3.description: The powerful, Early Baroque high altar, which was reworked in the 18th century, is one of the earliest two-leveled conceptions in Bavaria serving a pilgrimage cult. Statues of the bishopric patron, St. Ulrich, and the order’s patron, St. Augustine, stand between pillars. A fold-away altarpiece painting referring to the legend of the pilgrimage once stood at the centre of the altar, behind this would have been an upper altar that was reserved for a spiritual dignitary. The miraculous, legendarily supposed Thassilo-Crucifix which replaced the painting in reality dates from about 1230. The front of the crucifix shows an image of Christ crucified covered with horse skin. This originally would have been placed near to the pilgrims on the lower altar. In the 18th century, Johann Baptist Straub used the space vacated by the crucifix for a marvelous tabernacle with figures of the Holy Emperor Heinrich and his wife Kunigunde as well as allegories of Faith, Hope and Love. Sensitively rendered reliefs appear typologically on the sacrifice of the mass: the Harvest of Manna, the Last Supper and Supper at Emmaus.
9779dbd4-5cc7-5f2e-8017-625b454897d3.artist: Hans Krumpper (1570–1634); Benedikt Meggas; Bartholomäus Steinle (1580–1628/29); Johann Baptist Straub (1704–1784)

9786138c-911e-5c83-bbbc-1f79f78efc26.name: Patio with stairs to the first floor
9786138c-911e-5c83-bbbc-1f79f78efc26.description: The patio, with stairs to the first floor, creates a refined entrance space decorated with figurative *azulejos*: a welcoming figure stands at the top of the staircase, which throughout its course is decorated with designs of architectural balusters, *putti* and vases of flowers.
9786138c-911e-5c83-bbbc-1f79f78efc26.location: Entrance to the building, House of the Holy Body (Museum of Baroque)
9786138c-911e-5c83-bbbc-1f79f78efc26.artist: Architect unknown. Tile-Painting Master P.M.P., probably Padre Manuel Pereira [n.d.]

97b7bc59-bda4-53ec-9bcc-8d85ce39a695.name: The Saint
97b7bc59-bda4-53ec-9bcc-8d85ce39a695.description: The sculpted decoration of the church was created by a leading Brno sculptor Ondřej Schweigl, a graduate of the Vienna Academy. The surface finish is by the master gilder V. Kutálek, the artist’s son-in-law, and with whom he collaborated in, for example, nearby Křtiny.
97b7bc59-bda4-53ec-9bcc-8d85ce39a695.location: Pilgrimage Church of the Virgin Mary of Dolours

97fcd65c-140e-5f02-af6d-be912af1408c.name: *Glorification of the Miti family*
97fcd65c-140e-5f02-af6d-be912af1408c.description: Justice holds the scale while Right lays a lily on it.
97fcd65c-140e-5f02-af6d-be912af1408c.location: Palazzo Miti Zagnoni, first floor, hall of honour, ceiling

97fe6083-dbd1-5242-b2e0-5e77a101a930.name: Eternal light
97fe6083-dbd1-5242-b2e0-5e77a101a930.description: Reliefs in gilded copper represent St. John the Baptist, St. John the Evangelist, St. Francis of Assisi, and others. The lamp’s summit consists of the Holy Trinity and the Virgin Immaculata, patron saint of the Minorites. The eternal light is usually hung in front of the high altar as a symbol of the Lord’s presence.
97fe6083-dbd1-5242-b2e0-5e77a101a930.location: Minorite Church of Saints John and Loreto, Brno

9809408c-d76c-58f4-9fb9-a3cc8351b641.name: Main Altar
9809408c-d76c-58f4-9fb9-a3cc8351b641.description: Relief decorations are symbolically connected with the paintings and the light: a choir of angels in heaven, with God the Father on the wall behind the main altar, and a statue of the Virgin Mary of Rajhrad; statues of St. Peter and St. Paul; bas-reliefs representing the Annunciation, the Crucifixion of St. Peter and the Decapitation of St. Paul; a pulpit with a pelican symbol, symbols of the Evangelists and four Church Fathers; a wood carving in the gallery and stone vases on supporting pillars outside the church, which were executed in the workshop of  I. Lengelacher, the court sculptor of the Dietrichsteins.

9825e4cf-984d-54fe-be91-fec38216c23f.name: Glory of the Benedictine Order
9825e4cf-984d-54fe-be91-fec38216c23f.description: The main fresco is oriented toward those entering  the church so that what first catches the eye  is, as admonition to repentance, the fall of evil powers and theological heretics. In general, the fresco evokes the visionary spectacle of a heaven of saints. The Holy Trinity appears in the middle of concentric cloud rings populated with saintly figures. Underneath, Maria is carried upward by angels. Extending from her are rays of grace, which are aimed over the order’s founders Benedikt and Scholastika to the church patrons Marin and Anian, so that the work of the order universally, and especially in Rott am Inn, are made understood as evidence  of grace.
9825e4cf-984d-54fe-be91-fec38216c23f.location: Dome of the central octagonal room

9834f4df-4ac2-5b3d-9e01-415aa52a8d3b.name: Front Façade of the Church
9834f4df-4ac2-5b3d-9e01-415aa52a8d3b.description: The façade has some new features when compared with other projects of the Society of Jesus, including the removal of the two usual towers. The Jesuit symbol “IHS” remains.

983963e7-fc19-5d7d-8898-e4698259d642.name: Detail of ceiling
983963e7-fc19-5d7d-8898-e4698259d642.description: Wooden ceiling with a *trompe l´oeil* vault.

9893bb4f-5bee-56e3-82dc-7febef951947.name: Immaculate Conception
9893bb4f-5bee-56e3-82dc-7febef951947.description: In 1646, on restoration of Portugal’s Independence from Spain, King João IV officially consecrated Portugal to the Virgin of the Immaculate Conception. Depictions of scenes from the Life of the Virgin go back to the earliest days of Christian art but it is unusual to see this particular scene depicted.

990449da-d78b-5865-9816-b5be7b3e9f0e.name: Monumental Staircase
990449da-d78b-5865-9816-b5be7b3e9f0e.description: The double flight staircase was built between 1726 and 1738 by Domenico Trifogli following the model of Bolognese senatorial residences staircases; the sculptures are by Francesco Janssens and the stucco decorations by Giambattista Verda.
990449da-d78b-5865-9816-b5be7b3e9f0e.artist: Domenico Trifogli; Francesco Janssens; Giambattista Verda

9907ee8c-c9bc-5075-a64d-986d4821b30a.name: Vault with stucco and ceiling paintings
9907ee8c-c9bc-5075-a64d-986d4821b30a.description: The ceiling frescos, framed by delicate strapwork stucco, were painted by Franz Laukas from Prutz. The five large panels depict scenes from the life of Mary, accompanied by eight smaller Mariological pictures and six scenes depicting the legend of the pilgrimage. Laukas’s painting style displays a clear folk art element – in particular the smaller panels with their charming naivety reminiscent of votive painting.
9907ee8c-c9bc-5075-a64d-986d4821b30a.artist: Franz Laukas (1690–1765); Anton Gigl (1700–1769), Augustin Gigl (dates unknown, active in the first half of the 18th century)

9927d984-2b47-57ca-b768-827d5abf75c0.name: High altar and miraculous picture
9927d984-2b47-57ca-b768-827d5abf75c0.description: The high altar is one of the most important examples of the Baroque staging of an older sacred picture.
