The miraculous picture *Mariahilf* from Lucas Cranach was originally housed in Dresden and found its way to Innsbruck as a gift to Archduke Leopold V. It has been on display in the parish church since 1650. It became the most widespread picture of the Virgin Mary in the alpine region. It was integrated into the high altar, built in 1726, as a “picture within a picture” (with exchangeable frames, which during Lent displays a picture from Josef Schöpf, at all other times a silver frame). The high altar is flanked by statues of the patron saints of the Diocese of Brixen, Ingenuin and Albuin.
9927d984-2b47-57ca-b768-827d5abf75c0.artist: Lucas Cranach the Elder (1472–1553); Cristoforo Benedetti (1660–1735), Theodor Benedetti [n.d.]; Josef Schöpf (1745–1822)

9945fbfe-1d4b-5e33-a105-610f2f4a3994.name: Model of Lisbon before the earthquake of 1755
9945fbfe-1d4b-5e33-a105-610f2f4a3994.description: A large-scale model of Lisbon’s city centre before the earthquake of 1755.
9945fbfe-1d4b-5e33-a105-610f2f4a3994.artist: Gustavo Matos Cerqueira, Vieira da Silva and others

9972577e-63e0-5aa2-b411-009561d6a3ae.name: The Vision of St. Norbert
9972577e-63e0-5aa2-b411-009561d6a3ae.description: Designed with elements from palace architecture, an architectural capriccio with a scenic background depicts St. Augustine presenting the monastic rules to St. Norbert as the founder of the order. Landscape, architecture, and affected-acting figures create an atmosphere that follows the model of French Rococo Style. This is a characteristic example of the concentration of courtly painting motifs.

997f7ad0-fb6e-54d0-81cc-7b436458c50b.name: Bernhardisaal (hall dedicated to saint Bernhard, the Cistercian order’s founder)
997f7ad0-fb6e-54d0-81cc-7b436458c50b.description:
The Bernhardisaal, a typical baroque imperial hall (a splendid room to receive the emperor and his family when they would pass by), is the most ornate in the abbey. Thanks to a restoration not long ago the hall reappears in its original magnificence. Gilded stucco work, the huge gilded coat of arms (Abbot Nivard II’s) and the silver-plated putti clambering on walls and ceiling as well as the colourful frescoes with allegorical scenes and gold frames make of the hall a baroque work of art. The room gets much light from several windows lying on top of each other on both longitudinal sides. And there are windows with illusionistic views on both narrow sides. Typical witty baroque detail - the portrait of a shooter, above the marble mantel piece, that aims at the spectator.  
Between the real windows there are paintings representing historical and church historical scenes, above flower still lifes. The doors are marble framed.

99d3e111-7860-5e69-a3b1-666ee0d16242.name: Pulpit
99d3e111-7860-5e69-a3b1-666ee0d16242.description: The gently curved pulpit and baldachin in the Late Baroque tradition was completed in 1784 and is the work of three artists, the carpenter Michael Hueber, the stucco mason Graßmayr and the sculptor Paterer who crowned the baldachin with the figures of a good shepherd and four angels.
99d3e111-7860-5e69-a3b1-666ee0d16242.artist: Michael Hueber [n.d.]; Franz Graßmayr [n.d.]; Johann Paterer (1712–1785)

9a119226-14e5-5c76-9358-4559912ca023.name: Chapel of Our Lady of the Doctrine
9a119226-14e5-5c76-9358-4559912ca023.description: The main image of this chapel represents Our Lady of the Doctrine (St. Ann with the Virgin Mary in her arms). Although the chapel was built in the 17th century, the decoration is typical of the Portuguese Baroque “National style”, which developed during the late 17th and early 18th century. This side chapel is the only one where gilded woodwork covers the whole of the interior surface including the barrel-vaulted ceiling.
9a119226-14e5-5c76-9358-4559912ca023.dates: Work on the chapel began on 1 April 1634 and it was used by the Brotherhood of Our Lady of the Doctrine as their headquarters. The stonework was finally completed in 1690.
9a119226-14e5-5c76-9358-4559912ca023.location: Church Interior, Church of São Roque
9a119226-14e5-5c76-9358-4559912ca023.artist: The woodwork is by José Rodrigues Ramalho (1660–1721) according to a contract dated 1688 between him and the Brotherhood. The stonework was executed by master masons, Manuel Antunes and João Teixeira, whose exact dates are unknown.

9ae03881-78f0-5e63-bd66-5bb57bff8346.name: Monk’s Choir
9ae03881-78f0-5e63-bd66-5bb57bff8346.description: Because of its stuccoed  stellar vault the oratory of the monks is counted as one of the most beautiful early Baroque rooms in Old Bavaria. A round dance of angels in its centre presents the instruments of passion of Christ.
9ae03881-78f0-5e63-bd66-5bb57bff8346.location: First floor of the chancel building
9ae03881-78f0-5e63-bd66-5bb57bff8346.artist: Architecture: Marx Schinnagl (1612–81); Stucco: Kaspar Feichtmayr the Elder (1639–1704)

9ae9fc2b-3bed-5ffe-b81b-cb6a18a7f879.name: “Noble” or first-floor windows
9ae9fc2b-3bed-5ffe-b81b-cb6a18a7f879.artist: Architect: André Soares (1720–1769), possibly in association with the decorative artist, Bartolomeu Antunes (1688–1753)

9be0039d-e38c-5148-9a95-774d967994a4.name: Cupola
9be0039d-e38c-5148-9a95-774d967994a4.description: The hemispheric cupola is illuminated by four large windows and some other *trompe l'oeil* windows too. It is decorated with Rococo flower valances and colourful stucco. In cartouches painted on the pendentives are the Evangelists: St. Hieronymus, St. Augustine, St. Ambrose and St. Gregory.
9be0039d-e38c-5148-9a95-774d967994a4.artist: Father João Baptista and Manuel Gomes [dates unknown]

9c061ec9-c566-5a43-ac42-9667454b892a.name: Homage Hall and Library
9c061ec9-c566-5a43-ac42-9667454b892a.description:
Above the main entrance there is the two storey Homage Hall. It was decorated by Joseph Amonte. Walls and ceiling are completely covered with fresco paintings. The overall scheme was inspired by the paintings in the festival hall of the Troja palace in Prague. The illusionistic architecture follows the drawings in Andrea Pozzo´s manual *Perspectiva pictorum et architectorum.*  
A bit westward – separated by a staircase and one floor higher – there is the library. In the state room there are bookshelves in front of marbled walls. They are separated by marbled columns from each other. The ceiling is divided into three parts and was painted by Joseph Amonte. The topics are theological – Christ and Moses are represented in the centre, they are surrounded by paintings in medallions representing Jesuit martyrs, Pope Benedict XIV with two cardinals and the Prince Archbishop Sigmund III of Salzburg with a bishop and an abbot. The latter is the most interesting detail of the painting as it relates to a contemporary occasion. The Prince Archbishop of Salzburg was elected in the very year when Amonte painted the ceiling. And what had he to do with an abbey in Styria? Styria had been since the Middle Ages until the end of the 18th century under the ecclesio-political rule of the Salzburg bishopric.
9c061ec9-c566-5a43-ac42-9667454b892a.dates: From the year 1720: construction North wing; 1740: fresco paintings in the Homage Hall; around 1753: state hall of the library and fresco paintings on the ceiling
9c061ec9-c566-5a43-ac42-9667454b892a.location: In the North wing (above the entrance) and in the West of it, both separated by a staircase
9c061ec9-c566-5a43-ac42-9667454b892a.artist: Architecture: construction and baroquization of the North wing: probably Johann Georg Stengg Homage Hall and library fresco paintings: Joseph Amonte

9c12405d-2e2a-59f6-85f0-cd79f698c73d.name: Chapel of St. Anne
9c12405d-2e2a-59f6-85f0-cd79f698c73d.description: The chapel protrudes from the otherwise smooth façade of the east wing of the monastery, adjoining the sacristy. In 1639 a crypt was built there to contain the tomb of Provost Plocar who commissioned the construction of the monastery. The chapel vaults and walls are covered with illusionary painting. The coats of arms are associated with the “mother” monastery in Brno-Zábrdovice. The richly carved retable from 1702, holding an image of God the Father, frames a Gothic statue of St. Anne.

9cf9544c-47c2-5741-bf3e-5d928fd5cfa2.name: Chapel of Our Lady of Piety
9cf9544c-47c2-5741-bf3e-5d928fd5cfa2.description: The design for the retable is centred on a representation of Calvary. A 17th-century sculpture of the Pietà completes the tribune. The wood carving is exuberantly multi-coloured as a result of the variety of gold leaf that covers it.
9cf9544c-47c2-5741-bf3e-5d928fd5cfa2.dates: The construction and decoration was overseen by the Brotherhood of Our Lady of Piety. According to an inscription, work began in September 1686 and was completed by 1711. The retable dates from 1708. The gilding was added in 1716.
9cf9544c-47c2-5741-bf3e-5d928fd5cfa2.location: Church Interior, Church of São Roque
9cf9544c-47c2-5741-bf3e-5d928fd5cfa2.artist: The retable was made by the 18th-century master carver Bento da Fonseca de Azevedo

9d1b3ddb-6a64-5dc1-ae7b-afa6d1da6b9b.name: Exterior, east façade
9d1b3ddb-6a64-5dc1-ae7b-afa6d1da6b9b.description: The Hofburg’s main façade differs significantly from that facing the Hofgasse. The wing was erected between 1766–80 according to plans from Pacassi and under the direction of the Viennese military architect Constantin Walter von Pfeilsberg. Gumpp’s plan was abandoned in favour of a new conception. The elongated, lightly curved front is designed along the lines of the Viennese palace built at the same time. It has a high basement storey and colossal order, with two seven-axis portal projections and rounded corner pavilions composed of existing towers.

9d1f5f8c-ef4a-5842-b57a-0d05acb3531b.name: Ceiling frescos: *St Gall during the building of the monastery*
9d1f5f8c-ef4a-5842-b57a-0d05acb3531b.description: The sequence of ceiling pictures – three illusionistic cupolas and corresponding spandrel pictures – begin with the story of the church patron Gall executed in subdued colours which become increasingly brighter in the two subsequent cupola frescos. The saint, situated in a landscape scene, is depicted as the abbot (which he never actually was) of the monastery of St. Gallen under construction. The presentation of the building plan effectively represents the act of founding. The cupola fresco, partly situated above the organ loft, is designed to be viewed facing west.

9dddcf81-e7ef-57de-826f-00c891445be3.name: Imaginary cityscape in the Salon with Panoramic Views
9dddcf81-e7ef-57de-826f-00c891445be3.description: The wall paintings of imaginary cityscapes reveal the influence of the architectural drawings of Giovanni Battista Piranesi.
9dddcf81-e7ef-57de-826f-00c891445be3.location: Second floor, west salon, Palace of the Sugar Refinery

9df17b0c-56ba-5fdc-8d9a-c7177fbc1afc.name: Casemates for the Military
9df17b0c-56ba-5fdc-8d9a-c7177fbc1afc.description: A row of buildings to accommodate military casemates. Eighteen of the twenty underground rooms have ventilation, access to a well, a water mine and a water-drainage system. In case of attack, the townspeople would seek refuge in the underground rooms, which also served as military lodgings, a warehouse and even as hospital in critical periods.
9df17b0c-56ba-5fdc-8d9a-c7177fbc1afc.artist: Pierre Gilles de Saint-Paul,Manuel de Azevedo Fortes  and others

9e276d65-268c-5885-a7c1-1b671be8c8e8.name: View of the sanctuary
9e276d65-268c-5885-a7c1-1b671be8c8e8.description: The architect of the Church of St. Ignatius in Dubrovnik, Andrea Pozzo, envisaged a fresco painting for the sanctuary, dividing it with pillars into three parts – as he had done in his own painting in the church of the same name in Rome – and setting the iconographical programme. The programme was perceived as the *Apotheosis of the Work of St. Ignatius* in the central field of the sanctuary, the *Encounter of St. Ignatius with St. Francis Xavier and St. Francis Borgia* in the side fields and *St. Ignatius in Heavenly Glory* on the ceiling of the sanctuary. The wall paintings were executed by the Sicilian painter of Spanish descent (who trained in Rome and Naples), Gaetano Garcia. Looking to show case patterns from Rome, like Pozzo's St. Ignatius and the Church of St. Agnese in Agone (with dome frescos painted by Carlo Ferri), Garcia achieved an impressive High Baroque composition, with a pronounced dynamic, opulent colouring and an effective play of light and shadow. The largest Baroque fresco cycle in Dalmatia, it gives some inkling of the splendour intended for the interior of the Dubrovnik Jesuit church, had the painting programme – which probably included the ceiling of the nave – been carried out to the end.
9e276d65-268c-5885-a7c1-1b671be8c8e8.location: Walls and ceiling of the sanctuary, Jesuit Church of St Ignatius

9e2fc162-268d-5843-8639-395c51330ad4.name: Flower decoration
9e2fc162-268d-5843-8639-395c51330ad4.description: The festive atmosphere of the interior is enhanced by the rich decoration and flower ornamentation of the quadraturist, Greiner, and the still-life painter, Zagelmann.
9e2fc162-268d-5843-8639-395c51330ad4.location: Pilgrimage Church of the Virgin Mary of Dolours, Detail of the Fresco
9e2fc162-268d-5843-8639-395c51330ad4.artist: Johann Zagelmann (1720 Těšín – 1758 Vienna), Anton Greiner

9ef848af-7443-53bc-a4ff-279d68aba619.name: Gateway with bastions
9ef848af-7443-53bc-a4ff-279d68aba619.description: In 1664/65 work was begun on the reinforcement of the eastern fortified gateway with the addition of two extensive polygonal bastions, which, together, were designed to protect access to the fortress. Thanks to their polygonal form, an all-round defence of the walls, without blind spots, was possible through the deployment of canons. In front are deep trenches. The bastions enclose a gate with aedicula frame, which, in accordance with Italian models, displays its defensive character through the use of bold rustication.
9ef848af-7443-53bc-a4ff-279d68aba619.artist: Christoph Gumpp the younger (1600–1672), Elias Gumpp (1609–1676)

9f686f76-730a-5310-83dc-4ed16a53c99a.name: Proscenium
9f686f76-730a-5310-83dc-4ed16a53c99a.description: The facade-like arch-shaped structure near the front of the stage is supported by two colossal columns either side with the proscenium boxes between them. Above the centre of the stage the crest of the alliance of Bavaria–Saxony is prominently displayed.

a0121cc0-20a3-5469-8da2-4993a1e95a3a.name: Main façade
a0121cc0-20a3-5469-8da2-4993a1e95a3a.description: The end side facing the Untermarkt is the magnificently decorated main façade of the house with a central bay window. Architecture paintings form the structure and frame for the images. At the bay window the central motifs are presented, in the middle below the window the Mary Help picture from Innsbruck carried by putti, above it God the Father and the Holy Ghost. On the side walls further putti are depicted playing with a wind wheel and bird cage, while the putti to the side of the bay window present the Tablets of the Law with the Ten Commandments, the Cross of Christ and a chalice. The gable zone features a peacock. The overall appearance is primarily a result of the virtuoso rocaille frames around the windows. Cornice and gable, both painted, form the upper termination.

a079adb4-175d-5bd2-96ab-5385a891031d.name: Herm pair: Autumn
a079adb4-175d-5bd2-96ab-5385a891031d.description: The herm pairs allegorise the seasons, this one showing an allegory of autumn.
a079adb4-175d-5bd2-96ab-5385a891031d.artist: François de Cuvilliés the Elder (1695–1786); Johann Baptist Straub (1704–1784)

a087cbc7-2a72-565a-9130-17dbf4bd2cf2.name: Side chapel, right (Our Lord of Passos Chapel and Our Lady of Soledad)
a087cbc7-2a72-565a-9130-17dbf4bd2cf2.location: Interior, Sanctuary of Bom Jesus de Matosinhos
a087cbc7-2a72-565a-9130-17dbf4bd2cf2.artist: Portuguese woodcarvers: Luís Pereira da Costa (active 1724–?), Domingos Martins Moreira (active 1746–1750)

a141a2a7-c77e-5121-9c0d-10970929fb2e.name: Chateau design
a141a2a7-c77e-5121-9c0d-10970929fb2e.description: The design followed an existing building which on the north side was to be flanked by ground-floor side-wings ending in prismatic constructions. The main frontage is made more striking by a protruding circular hall. Older fortifications prevented the completion of all but the east wing. The “correspondence plan” from the royal court architect in Paris was adjusted to local conditions by the builder Ludwig Sebastian Kaltner.
a141a2a7-c77e-5121-9c0d-10970929fb2e.artist: Robert de Cotte (1656–1735, Paris), Ludwig Sebastian Kaltner

a1ef0742-6721-5a62-b45f-58953a49f528.name: Ceremonial courtyard
a1ef0742-6721-5a62-b45f-58953a49f528.description: The completion of the residence was chiefly an urban logistical task. The outbuildings were already standing in the 17th century, as well as a riding hall on the right and a theatre on the left. The style of the Viennese engineer and decorator A. J. Ospel, followed in the footsteps of F. Borromini and F. G. Galli-Bibiena. The contrast between simple shapes and impressive stonemasonry detail is typical of the artist. The majority of Ospel’s works for the chateau interiors have not survived (for example, an elaborate ceramic stove). The space opens with telamons by G. Giuliani.
a1ef0742-6721-5a62-b45f-58953a49f528.artist: Ondřej Erna, Jan Křtitel Erna, Anton Josef Ospel (1677–1756)

a250e219-36b1-5af4-998b-4d66ef54d879.name: Library
a250e219-36b1-5af4-998b-4d66ef54d879.description: The library was established shortly after the foundation of the monastery and some of the manuscripts were produced here. A number of important figures, mainly historians, are associated with the library. In the mid-18th century the idea of publishing Czech chronicles found roots here (B. Piter). G. Wolný subsequently wrote 15 volumes of Moravian topography and his work became a cornerstone for the history of Moravia. Dr. B. Dudík, a prominent Moravian historiographer, published over 70 scholarly works and must be given credit for the return of large quantities of ancient manuscripts carried off to Sweden during the Thirty Years’ War. The fresco represents the merits of the Benedictines in the development of the sciences. The library now houses the National Literature Archive.

a2714513-34b3-581b-8817-44074b61fd72.name: Frescos on the ceiling of the cupola
a2714513-34b3-581b-8817-44074b61fd72.description: The frescoes on the crossing cupola form an organisational system which simultaneously blends with and transcends the architecture. Free-standing columns appear to support a type of dome which encloses the base of the skylight turret. Between the columns a central scene from the Legend of the Cross is depicted in each of the four axial directions respectively: the “bronze serpent”, as well as the discovery, raising and veneration of the cross by the martyrs.
a2714513-34b3-581b-8817-44074b61fd72.location: Crossing cupola, Catholic Pilgrimage Church of the Holy Cross

a2e43246-4b4d-5e5d-8850-938cd4037e12.name: Autumn
a2e43246-4b4d-5e5d-8850-938cd4037e12.description: The entrance vestibule of a triple nave features personifications of the four seasons, a frequent subject for Baroque residences, including gardens and *salla terrenas*, symbolising the earthly sphere of the world and the passage of time. The figure, of striking volume, is typical of G. Heintz, paraphrasing Michelangelo's Bacchus known from graphic reproductions.
a2e43246-4b4d-5e5d-8850-938cd4037e12.location:
Premonstratensian Monastery, Hradisko u Olomouce, Entrance Vestibule  
Olomouc, Moravia, Czech Republic

a32a2915-2855-5d07-8732-65d0e36b429e.name: The Bell Tower known as “Torre dos Clérigos”
a32a2915-2855-5d07-8732-65d0e36b429e.description: The tower has six floors and is 75.6 m high. The floors vary in width, narrowing like a telescope. The balconies on the top floor help to create the illusion that the top of the building is dematerialising, thus increasing the rhetorical power of the building as a “lighthouse of faith” that hovers over the city.

a3be46cc-799f-5f24-bbf9-715af2876ed1.name: High altar
a3be46cc-799f-5f24-bbf9-715af2876ed1.description: The high altar, possibly a work of Johann Georg Pauer from Tannheim, was built around 1710. Its massive, completely gilded superstructure with projecting strutted pediment above spiral columns is one of the most important achievements of High Baroque altar-construction in Außerfern. The altarpiece from the Baroque painter Johannes Heel from Pfronten in Allgäu depicting the Adoration of the Shepherds is situated beneath the ceiling fresco of the *Adoration of the Holy Trinity*.
a3be46cc-799f-5f24-bbf9-715af2876ed1.location: Choir, Catholic Guild Church of St. Joseph

a3c72600-46fb-5ac2-b8e9-785b043b34d5.name: Interior (nave and choir)
a3c72600-46fb-5ac2-b8e9-785b043b34d5.description: The interior of the monastery church is an exquisite example of a Baroque prospect. The view through the wide, three-bayed nave hall with shallow groined vault and wide fascia experiences a decisive caesura at the retracted triumphal arch. The powerful pilaster arcade with semi-circular arches provides an unobstructed view of the centre of the choir, of which only the eastern arcade framing the high altar and part of the domical vault with the fresco is visible from the nave. Thus the high altar and the eastern section of the ceiling painting appear to be placed in direct relation to one another.
a3c72600-46fb-5ac2-b8e9-785b043b34d5.artist: Unknown Lombardian master builder; Diego Francesco Carlone (1674–1750), Paolo d’Allio (1655–1729)

a3f46d26-44e7-58fe-98bf-abbe1a6305e7.name: Pulpit
a3f46d26-44e7-58fe-98bf-abbe1a6305e7.description: The pulpit architecture is completely obscured by sculpted decoration. Roofing is absent, replaced by a group of dynamically rendered figures headed by Archangel Gabriel, fighter against the Antichrist and with Divine Providence in the background. The platform is lined with statues of the saints Vincent Ferrer and Thomas Aquinas, while a relief depicts the founder of the Dominican order. Reliefs on the ambo represent New Testament scenes from Christ Tempted by the Devil. The expressively executed coloured pedestal is made up of a host of fallen angels in desperate postures. Winterhalder was inspired by a similar base by B. Permoser in Dresden, with which he had became acquainted in the 1730s. The illusionary architecture of the high altar was executed by the Dominican brothers.

a4957036-5b31-596c-980c-cb78a45dd4a3.name: *Archangel Raphael with Little Tobias*
a4957036-5b31-596c-980c-cb78a45dd4a3.description: Black gilded side altars pose a contrast, together with a pulpit, to the white vaulting decorated with simple stucco featuring vegetal motifs. The figure of Tobias personifies count Dietrichstein, whose coat of arms is on the boy’s shoulder. The guardian angel accompanies him on the journey to the divine light, leading him on the path of virtue and protecting him from sins and vices. M. A. Lublinský is also attributed with the replica of a picture by P. P. Rubens on the opposite altar.
a4957036-5b31-596c-980c-cb78a45dd4a3.location: Augustinian Monastery, Hermits of St. Thomas the Apostle
a4957036-5b31-596c-980c-cb78a45dd4a3.artist: Ferdinand Pfaundler, Jan Krtitel Speiss (? Sterzing – 1688 Brno), Martin Anton Lublinský (1636 Lesnica – 1690 Olomouc)

a4fc9e31-68fa-54b9-af64-b54cda00cfe4.name: Pews
a4fc9e31-68fa-54b9-af64-b54cda00cfe4.description: The church pews, with their 80 dividing panels decorated with carvings, are the work of the sculptor Franz Xaver Nißl from Fügen in Zillertal, a student of Johann Baptist Straub. The shorter, front convent pews are decorated with symbols of Christ, Mary and the clergy, the rear pews feature, amongst other motifs, the life of St. Benedict and Joseph and a number of Holy Helpers alongside the coat of arms of the benefactor.

a510d0cb-7ef9-570d-8610-ec9568ed5fcb.name: Celebration of Emperor Charles VI
a510d0cb-7ef9-570d-8610-ec9568ed5fcb.description:
Governor Kounic was a follower of Charles VI and a promoter of the “pragmatic sanction”. He systematically addressed the modernisation of the country and reforms in public administration. With the emperor’s support Kounic unified the administration and the royal tribunal into a Provincial Governorate, which spurred the construction of a new entrance wing by M. Grimm, its central bay with two passageways symbolising the new office. The staircase and the new Assembly Hall were decorated by local artists.  
The artist, F. Ř. I. Eckstein also tendered for the commission to decorate the Assembly Hall but he was spurned and left Brno to work for the Jesuits in Lviv where he later died.
a510d0cb-7ef9-570d-8610-ec9568ed5fcb.artist: František Řehoř Ignác Eckstein (1689? Židovice u Žatce – 1741 Lviv)

a567bfc0-3ec2-5307-8a47-ec8ecae7cc75.name: Hercules
a567bfc0-3ec2-5307-8a47-ec8ecae7cc75.description: Hercules, symbol of strength and courage, holds Cerberus, the guardian of the underworld, in chains.
a567bfc0-3ec2-5307-8a47-ec8ecae7cc75.artist: Johann Bernhard Fischer von Erlach (1656, Graz – 1723, Vienna), Tobias Kracker (1658, Vienna – 1736, Vienna)

a57f3c15-9662-5e36-8cd0-ac76848e3b6b.name: High altar
a57f3c15-9662-5e36-8cd0-ac76848e3b6b.description: The powerful column structure of the high altar in red marble completely fills the choir’s eastern alcove. The altarpiece depicting the Transfiguration of St. Augustine is overshadowed by a large stucco statue of Mary Immaculate in front of an aureole window. In addition, the church patron is flanked by the two Johns (Evangelist and Baptist).
a57f3c15-9662-5e36-8cd0-ac76848e3b6b.artist: Diego Francesco Carlone (1674–1750); Jakob Zanusi [n.d.]; Lorenz Wieser [n.d.]

a6ec6fee-8f25-562d-81df-4adbcf12d051.name: Pulpit
a6ec6fee-8f25-562d-81df-4adbcf12d051.description: The pulpit forms a contrast to the remaining interior work in ponderous Late Baroque style with its intimations of austere Early Classicism. The baldachin’s filigree, freely soaring rocaille stucco, similar to that in Götzen, lends a certain accent to the space’s remaining stuccowork, also executed in the forms of the Late Rococo, which contributes little in the way of expressiveness.

a7199e6e-f09c-553d-bbf6-ec8f5ca91e89.name: Lake of the Crowns and Overflow Garden (Jardim Alagado)
a7199e6e-f09c-553d-bbf6-ec8f5ca91e89.description: The Lake of the Crowns is built on a rectangular plan with three fountains topped by crowns. In this level there are several trapezoidal lakes integrated with flowerbeds and a central fountain, amongst which is the *Jardim Alagado*, (3rd image) which acted as an overflow garden.

a72619dd-8151-59b9-940a-aea86096b247.name: Altar of St. John of Nepomuk
a72619dd-8151-59b9-940a-aea86096b247.description: The essential features of the sculptures are in the independently decorative luxuriance of the drapery, which in places grows into abstractly dramatic labyrinths, hiding in its mass the body of the saints; a plastic mass of clothing that with its abundance of folds and deep shadow hides its volume. The expressive faces, with deep, emphatic lines on the noses and eyelids, correlate well with this overall modelling.
a72619dd-8151-59b9-940a-aea86096b247.location: Right-hand side altar in the main nave, Franciscan Church and Monastery of Our Lady of Trsat

a77ef2d9-10e4-5afc-a3ae-c7088cf25f5a.name: Statues at high altar
a77ef2d9-10e4-5afc-a3ae-c7088cf25f5a.description:
The Adoration of the Magi group was created for an earlier high altar that was shortly thereafter replaced. The six statues were later taken apart and transferred to places between the high altar and the side altars. In the 19th century the high altar was restored and modified and the statues were again placed on it. It looks as if then a higher (third) platform for the Virgin with Child was added as – in the actual installation – St Joseph’s and the kneeling king’s looks don´t meet the baby Jesus which was quite sure the basic idea.  
The sculptor Thomas Schwanthaler was the artist who created the Adoration group. The expressive lengthened figures, in concern to his own development, usher in a new artistic era. Most remarkable are the figures’ realistic looking hands with a richness of detail and gesture.  
The Gmunden Adoration group has become a model for many nativity scenes up to our present day.

a7d38155-17fa-5bba-9425-30187706f79f.name: Cupola
a7d38155-17fa-5bba-9425-30187706f79f.description: The pillars continue in four pendentives with allegories of Europe, Asia, Africa and America (J. K. Handke, 1731); the niches feature statues of the Evangelists. The stucco decoration divides the vaulting into six cartouches, the frescos of which represent Old Testament accounts of Sara, Rebecca, Abigail, Bathsheba, Judith and Ester – prototypes of the Virgin Mary. The upper third of the cartouches contain invocations of the prayer *Salve Regina* (Steger, 1677). The cupola, centralising the longitudinal building, is crowned with a lantern and a dove, symbol of the Holy Spirit.
a7d38155-17fa-5bba-9425-30187706f79f.artist: Baldassare Fontana (1661–1733, Chiasso), Jan Kryštof Handke (1694 Janovice u Rýmařova – 1774 Olomouc)

a835eb0b-d481-5e55-87e0-9378c9200c20.name: Cabinet
a835eb0b-d481-5e55-87e0-9378c9200c20.location: Sacristy, Church of St. George in Purga Lepoglavska
a835eb0b-d481-5e55-87e0-9378c9200c20.artist: Pauline carpenter; painter: Ivan Krstitelj (Johann Baptist) Ranger (1700–1753)

a86530f8-03b2-599f-9c61-5d3eb621bc7f.name: Exterior
a86530f8-03b2-599f-9c61-5d3eb621bc7f.description: The plain exterior of the building is characterised by a mixture of Gothic and Baroque stylistic forms, most clearly evidenced by the façade with painted pilaster arrangement and tail gable as well as the curved windows on all sides.

a93a44e4-31d3-5087-ab94-f1ff9655efb5.name: Balustrade
a93a44e4-31d3-5087-ab94-f1ff9655efb5.artist: Architect: André Soares (1720–1769), possibly in association with the decorative artist, Bartolomeu Antunes (1688–1753)

a95515d5-18b6-558f-b87d-d9d3eeff31fe.name: *The Bronze Serpent*
a95515d5-18b6-558f-b87d-d9d3eeff31fe.description: An Old Testament scene of powerful dramatic charge, the dynamically composed sculptural group is organised around a diagonal line. The ornamental articulation of the drapery of Moses’ cloak is a recognisable feature of Robba’s stylistic language.
a95515d5-18b6-558f-b87d-d9d3eeff31fe.location: Altar of the Holy Cross (Church of the Holy Cross)

a9e8aaa6-04ad-5a03-89b4-55c42fe97bbd.name: Burgher House No. 59/I
a9e8aaa6-04ad-5a03-89b4-55c42fe97bbd.description: The frontages of almost 50 per cent of the houses were re-plastered in the first quarter of the 18th century, not purely for decorative reasons but also because the requirements placed on housing had changed. New larger windows made the interiors considerably lighter. The houses began to feature elements of the Radical Baroque, lacking completely the basic architecture of Telc, and generally rather scarce in Moravia in contrast to Bohemia. The undulating effect of the frontages is enhanced by diagonally positioned pilasters reaching up to the gable tops that are crowned with a window and a vase.

aa5845ce-589a-5523-b9b6-1dd7e994fc46.name: The Altar of St. Peter and Paul (High altar)
aa5845ce-589a-5523-b9b6-1dd7e994fc46.description: The magnificent high altar, put up with red Veronese marble, fills out the central axis of the chancel and is flanked by large windows. A series of elegant columns dramatically envelope the mensa and retable. As emissaries of the Heavenly Hosts, angels with harps stand beside the attic storey which inside bears a halo of light (so-called gloriole) representing God. They look upon Günther’s altarpiece, which displays the glory of the church’s patrons. Flanking the columns  four statues represent other saints who are important to the parish.
aa5845ce-589a-5523-b9b6-1dd7e994fc46.artist: Designer unknown; altar painting: Matthäus Günther (1705–88)

aaa73ab6-82bc-549b-89fe-7ef1622228fa.name: Altar of St. Dionisius (Altar of the Holy Martyrs)
aaa73ab6-82bc-549b-89fe-7ef1622228fa.description: The Altar of St. Dionisius combines sculptures by the early Baroque sculptor from Varasdin, Ivan Jakob Altenbach, and paintings by the Slovenina painter, Hans Georg Geiger. The first domestic sculptor of major artistic note, Ivan Jakob Altenbach appeared in the mid-1670s. His work shows essentially that he overcame the surviving forms of Mannerism to achieve the stylistic features of the Baroque. The Jesuit church in Leoben, Styria, influenced the conservative, two-storey structure of the wooden retable.
aaa73ab6-82bc-549b-89fe-7ef1622228fa.location: The side chapel of St. Martyrs (St. Dionisius) on the right-hand (south) side of the nave
aaa73ab6-82bc-549b-89fe-7ef1622228fa.artist: Ivan Jakob Altenbach (active c. 1675–d. before 1692), Hans Georg Geiger (active 1639–d. 1681)

aad909a1-b106-56bf-86ee-b7aee4a41eef.name: Central ceiling fresco in the Riesensaal
aad909a1-b106-56bf-86ee-b7aee4a41eef.description: The painted ceiling, including the painted stucco, covers an area of c. 500 square metres and is one of Franz Anton Maulbertsch’s major works. The empress personally contributed to its design. The central fresco shows an allegory of the union of the royal houses of Austria and Lorraine, the flanking ovals depict the regalia of Tyrol. The marriage of the houses of Austria and Lorraine is depicted as a chariot, accompanied by personifications of the sovereign’s virtues.

ab501a21-ec14-5a97-af8f-4cbadd1c1cc2.name: The Altar of St. Agatha
ab501a21-ec14-5a97-af8f-4cbadd1c1cc2.description: The side altar made of stucco marble is dedicated to St. Agatha, a patron of farmers. Instead of a painting, an alcove holds Schmädl’s sculpture of the martyr. The scroll-shaped volutes to the sides lend the altar an extremely ornamental character. Symbolic of the opening of Heaven, a golden circlet sits above the altar behind which an obelisk crowned with a vase towers as a Christian symbol of victory.
ab501a21-ec14-5a97-af8f-4cbadd1c1cc2.artist: Altar: Thassilo Zöpf (1723–1807); Sculptor: Franz Xaver Schmädl (1705–77)

ab9ca50b-155a-5181-83a8-a7d112c0581e.name: Figure of the Divine Emperor
ab9ca50b-155a-5181-83a8-a7d112c0581e.description: A harmonious sculpture representing Christ Crucified, of which the anchor and sceptre are of filigree silver.

ac0222e4-7fae-5d3e-bc11-b8b5d0857467.name: High Altar
ac0222e4-7fae-5d3e-bc11-b8b5d0857467.description: Two sculptures from the Pacassi workshop: *St. Francis* on the left and *St. John the Evangelist* on the right.
ac0222e4-7fae-5d3e-bc11-b8b5d0857467.location: Presbytery, Franciscan Church and Monastery of Our Lady of Trsat

acbcd2fe-73a5-5680-ae25-a6b4c595a3b1.name: *Sala Terrena*
acbcd2fe-73a5-5680-ae25-a6b4c595a3b1.description: The space is decorated with illusionary ornamental painting evoking an overgrown pergola. The adjoining lounge contains Japanese genre scenes and “Roman” baths with stucco ornamentation decorated with shells and stones.
acbcd2fe-73a5-5680-ae25-a6b4c595a3b1.artist: Giovanni Michele Fontana, Johann Wenzl Bergl?

acbef11a-4848-5569-876c-c3b3f5bd5ca0.name: Cycle of the Apostles
acbef11a-4848-5569-876c-c3b3f5bd5ca0.description: In a host of Apostles on a side wall of the nave, the image of Judas is replaced with St. Paul.

acdb77c0-0663-595b-975d-8751bfd3847c.name: Old Festival Hall
acdb77c0-0663-595b-975d-8751bfd3847c.description: The early Baroque festival hall, adorned with two magnificently columned doorways, underwent a reworking in the high Baroque style by means of fully plastical stucco. The allegorical ceiling paintings, complexly mirroring life, deal with the seasons; the elements of fire, water, air and earth; the animal, plant and mineral worlds; the eternal circle of virtue and vice; the work of Christ interpreted as hunter, fisherman and gardener; as well as the resulting triumph of the rational believing soul.
acdb77c0-0663-595b-975d-8751bfd3847c.dates:
1672–75 establishment  
Around 1690 replenishment of ceiling stucco
acdb77c0-0663-595b-975d-8751bfd3847c.location: Second floor of the convent floor west wing
acdb77c0-0663-595b-975d-8751bfd3847c.artist: Architecture: Marx Schinnagl (1612–81); Stucco: Kaspar Feichtmayr the Elder (1639–1704), Nicolò Perti or Prospero Brenno; ceiling paintings: Stephan (1622–1700) and Michael Kessler (born 1649)

ad7a69b4-51ae-5bed-922f-f95d07fa6ad4.name: Retable of Nossa Senhora da Soledade
ad7a69b4-51ae-5bed-922f-f95d07fa6ad4.description: Wood carved retable in the *Rocaille* style.

ad94253e-58eb-5964-86d8-0901c5ccbeaf.name: View of the inside of the church
ad94253e-58eb-5964-86d8-0901c5ccbeaf.description: The church is divided in three naves. The light comes in through the ample windows and shines on the gilded decorations of the columns and arches.

add54831-b132-5b1c-9ed1-5c4eec59a759.name: Praça do Comércio
add54831-b132-5b1c-9ed1-5c4eec59a759.description: Praça do Comércio overlooking the River Tejo is an emblematic part of the *Baixa*. According to the engraving attributed to Gaspar Froes Machado, the initial plans were not entirely fulfilled; the triumphal arch was finally built in 1873 according to the design of Veríssimo José da Costa.
add54831-b132-5b1c-9ed1-5c4eec59a759.location: Facing the estuary of the River Tagus
add54831-b132-5b1c-9ed1-5c4eec59a759.artist: Initial plans of Praça do Comércio: Manuel da Maia (1677–1766), Eugénio dos Santos (1711–1760); Carlos Mardel (c. 1695–1763); triumphal arch: Veríssimo José da Costa [n.d.] assisted by Vítor Bastos (1830–1894) and Anatole C. Calmels (1822–1906)

ade4aee1-0543-5bda-bcdc-10aeda05e8ed.name: Altar of Grace
ade4aee1-0543-5bda-bcdc-10aeda05e8ed.description: The church’s lattice wall — common in Loreto chapels to separate the praying individuals from the miraculous image — had been reintroduced as a Marian picture wall. The lattice was removed to allow an unobstructed view of the devotional picture, which was reinterpreted as an image of The Madonna of Loreto. It is framed by a nimbus. In combination with the set of angels, it evokes an appearance of Mary as the Queen of Heaven. This takes place in the presence of the Trinity, as archangels stick out from the heavenly hosts, whereby Christ is depicted as a child. Above the doors, Archangel Gabriel carries out the proclamation. The door panels are painted with images of St. Joseph and St. John the Baptist. The antependium, on the other hand, displays a painting of The Birth of Mary. The figures of the tabernacle stand for the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit: Wisdom, understanding, counsel, fortitude, knowledge, piety, and fear of the Lord; in accordance with Proverb 9:1 from the Litany of Loreto: “Wisdom has built her house; she has set up her seven columns.”
ade4aee1-0543-5bda-bcdc-10aeda05e8ed.artist: Sculptures of the Archangels, Proclamation, and Trinity: Joseph Götsch (1728—93); angel figures: Josef Anton Fröhlich; paintings: Sebastian Troger (c. 1745—92)

ae77a293-7b0e-5067-bde6-8ea3bbcc4d01.name: *Ensemble d’époque*: Bedroom
ae77a293-7b0e-5067-bde6-8ea3bbcc4d01.description: Installed in the east wing facing the Buxo Garden is a re-creation of an 18th-century bedroom. It is worth mentioning in particular the *azulejos* that line the walls depicting rural themes, romantic scenes and chinoiseries most of which date to 1746.

aea13279-eedb-5f94-9955-da7b4271af44.name: The High Altar
aea13279-eedb-5f94-9955-da7b4271af44.description: Made of Carrara marble with polychrome incrustations, in its dimensions the high altar dominates the other six altars placed in six radial chapels. Extending towards the vault of the chapel with its high central attic “inhabited” with small angels and a central figure of the Holy Father surrounded by rounded clouds, its slanted side “wings” with side passages in the lower part, fills the whole of the sanctuary forming a concave. There is a central wooden Gothic crucifix and in the side-niches are sculptures of St. Vitus and St. Modest.

af670ccd-204f-5459-abf8-9e8b73bfa098.name: High Altar
af670ccd-204f-5459-abf8-9e8b73bfa098.description: Built thanks to the generosity of Viceroy Baltazar Bedeković and his wife, Helena Rozalija Somogy, the main altar's massive construction meets the full width and height of the sanctuary. According to the inscription on the cartouche at the top of the retable the altar was completed in 1743, although the sculpture of *Immaculate Mary* at the centre belonged to the old dismantled main altar made in 1729.
af670ccd-204f-5459-abf8-9e8b73bfa098.location: Presbytery, Parish Church of Our Lady of the Snow
af670ccd-204f-5459-abf8-9e8b73bfa098.artist: Circle of the sculptor  Filip (Philipp) Jakob Straub (1706–1774)

af7ed7f2-fbcb-55f0-b2b4-8482fde079df.name: *Titus Flavius Josephus and Titus Livius*
af7ed7f2-fbcb-55f0-b2b4-8482fde079df.description:
This representation is depicted in one of the seven lunettes of the main room. In this room the central theme is the *Ascension to the Mountain of Knowledge*. The allegories of several disciplines (Philosophy, Mathematics, Moral Philosophy, Theology, History and Law) are flanked by pairs of their significant representatives. The lunettes allude to the books held in the bookshelves below.  
In the middle, standing on a basis inscribed in capital characters: PEPLUM MINERVA / D.D.D. / A: T: P, a crowned female figure leans with her shoulder against a great fasces (around which twines a cartouche with the words VERITAS and VIVIT) and shows a book. At her feet are two busts of Roman emperors. On the right, a massive masculine figure (reminiscent of the gigantic characters in Pellegrino Tibaldi's frescoes in palazzo Poggi) turns towards the statue, holding in his hand a medal with a man's portrait. On the left Titus Flavius Josephus reads and at the same time unrolls a scroll written in Jewish characters.

afa63df6-92d1-5fda-adee-1fb5ac15e24c.name: High altar
afa63df6-92d1-5fda-adee-1fb5ac15e24c.description: The Early Baroque high altar built for the medieval monastery church by the sculptor Steinle from Weilheim is of special art-historical significance. The altar screen, architecturally formed by two columns, is overgrown with thick tendrils, a “Root of Jesse” or “Tree of Life”, springing from the base of the altar with the figures of Adam and Eve ascends via the central figure of the salvational “Immaculata” to the crucifixion as a symbol of redemption. The tradition of Late Gothic branch-motif ornamentation is here combined with Early Baroque forms. Stucco curtain and baldachin from Franz Xaver Feichtmayr added in 1731.
afa63df6-92d1-5fda-adee-1fb5ac15e24c.artist: Bartholomäus Steinle (c. 1580–1628/29); carpentry by Wolfgang Kirchmayr (dates unknown, working up until 1600)

afd811b1-ad49-5351-8f64-cc37ff31078e.name: *Our Lady of the Snow hovering over the Church of Kutina and inhabitants of the city*
afd811b1-ad49-5351-8f64-cc37ff31078e.description: In the *trompe l'œil* *rocaille* framework there is a representation of Vicar Antun Pozojević and Count Karlo II Erdödy with the newly erected church of Kutina, surrounded by its covered walkway. The Immaculate Virgin Mary with a scapular on her arm hovers above them.
afd811b1-ad49-5351-8f64-cc37ff31078e.location: Sanctuary ceiling, Parish Church of Our Lady of the Snow

b06f52e2-cfcb-5f2c-8057-5b7d801c7bd4.name: Interior
b06f52e2-cfcb-5f2c-8057-5b7d801c7bd4.description: Following a number of restorations during the 20th century, the overall impression of the interior has largely been restored to that of the mid-18th century. The choir prospect is dominated by the crossing as the focus of the spatial sequence: four bevelled pilaster piers support a shallow cupola above pendentives. The perspectively graduated prospect is introduced by a massive arcade with semi-circular arches above pilaster piers at the transition to the nave and crossing. The focus is the high altar, which fills the whole width of the apse.
b06f52e2-cfcb-5f2c-8057-5b7d801c7bd4.location: View in the direction of the choir

b0b74c0a-ea2d-5127-a642-8a836ff47fcb.name: Loggia
b0b74c0a-ea2d-5127-a642-8a836ff47fcb.description: Central view of the loggia on the front with the so called serliana or Palladian window.

b1230e81-eafc-5132-aed0-e2361753686f.name: Retable of Moroccan Saints and Martyrs
b1230e81-eafc-5132-aed0-e2361753686f.description: Example of the late King João V style.

b194640b-e18f-56a3-a553-f1b273892d94.name: High altar
b194640b-e18f-56a3-a553-f1b273892d94.description: The high altar, framed by the choir’s double arcades when viewed from the nave, is composed of a six-column superstructure above a lightly curved ground plan and is executed completely in accordance with the style of Bavarian altars. Figures and paintings were first added around 1780, the altarpiece with the beheading of the church’s patroness is a copy of Martin Knoller’s altarpiece painting in Ettal.

b1a77d33-eb7b-5b94-86ac-a5048091f551.name: *Transverberation of the Heart of St Teresa*
b1a77d33-eb7b-5b94-86ac-a5048091f551.description: The ecstasy or rapture of St. Theresa is represented here by use of intensive colour contrasts and dynamic light and shadow throughout the vertical composition. The cheerful atmosphere of the painting does not suit the mystical subject matter – the vision of St. Theresa, a Seraph driving the point of a lance through her heart repeatedly, causing her both spiritual and physical pain.

b1a77da8-c428-593d-a327-c702cc601914.name: Staircase
b1a77da8-c428-593d-a327-c702cc601914.description: A staircase of great scale and ostentation it is fixed in the nucleus of the palace.
b1a77da8-c428-593d-a327-c702cc601914.location: Interior of the palace, Pimenta Palace

b1dd8d6f-0a1e-5d0a-9dd4-32bf8cee812d.name: Ceremonial Hall
b1dd8d6f-0a1e-5d0a-9dd4-32bf8cee812d.description: Designed in the colonnade type, the magnificent reception hall of the church demonstrates the highest level of splendour. Several elements of the interior reflect the high educational standards of the monks, such as the stucco decor that possesses a great deal of symbolism and the allegorical ceiling painting with a wind rose in its centre as a showpiece of Baroque metrology.
b1dd8d6f-0a1e-5d0a-9dd4-32bf8cee812d.location: Monastery building, on the first floor of the west wing
b1dd8d6f-0a1e-5d0a-9dd4-32bf8cee812d.artist: Interior design and stucco: Andrea Maini (b. 1683); Ceiling fresco: Franz Georg Hermann (1692–1768)

b1f0dda2-237e-58d7-b2ae-dbd6e459db34.name: Interior, nave wall
b1f0dda2-237e-58d7-b2ae-dbd6e459db34.description: The structure of the nave walls is orientated on the central tribune which protrudes into the building line. This crosswise symmetrical axis centres the nave. Pilasters, entablatures and arcades form a protruding enclosure, a bold accentuation of the side altars. The pictorial programme composed of alcoves for statues and ceiling frescos is also oriented towards this central point; only the pulpit sets an asymmetrical accent.
b1f0dda2-237e-58d7-b2ae-dbd6e459db34.artist: Abraham Millauer (c. 1680–1758), Philipp Millauer (1710–53), Leonhard Millauer [n.d.]

b2980c5d-4b8e-5737-b1bd-ebbf38274aad.name: High altar
b2980c5d-4b8e-5737-b1bd-ebbf38274aad.description: The high altar, which according to an inscription on the predella was built in 1651 as an endowment of the Weinzierl family, is the oldest of the three altars in the Church. It is an aedicula altar with a broken segmental pediment and an openwork altar crown. At the centre of the programme of figures are the church’s three patron saints, all of whom are invoked as protection from the plague.

b3326d33-a792-54b2-b4b4-828dbbb5989d.name: *Angel with Banderola*
b3326d33-a792-54b2-b4b4-828dbbb5989d.artist: Alvise Tagliapietra (1670–1747) and his son Ambrogio (b. 1701)

b3631ca4-4c40-5863-ad39-0d6734c902ed.name: Blackamoor
b3631ca4-4c40-5863-ad39-0d6734c902ed.description: The figure of an adoring Blackamoor complements the iconography of the altar in the side chapel of St. Francis Xaverius added in 1670. The allegories of America and Asia symbolise the outreach of the Jesuit order. The ceiling painting features scenes from the saint’s missionary activities and is a sequel to the painting in the vault of the main nave: Ignatius of Loyola Spreading the Flame of Christ’s Faith to the Four Continents.
b3631ca4-4c40-5863-ad39-0d6734c902ed.location: Jesuit Church of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary

b3dc84c7-1930-5b07-b085-55d198c770fa.name: St. Vincent and St. Sebastian
b3dc84c7-1930-5b07-b085-55d198c770fa.description: Depicting the Martyrs St. Sebastian and St. Vincent, these sculptures represent just two pieces from The Royal Commission, which includes among other precious items 56 Italian sculptures, representing the most important collection of Italian Baroque sculpture outside Italy. The two sculptures illustrated here are made from marble; each one is 3.58-meters tall.

b409179d-6059-59d1-be2e-d8d52c3ce402.name: St. Thomas Aquinas
b409179d-6059-59d1-be2e-d8d52c3ce402.description: A shallow, theatrical scene depicts the Dominican theologian Saint Thomas Aquinas (d.1274) at prayer, in the course of which Christ appeared before him. J. L. Kracker was active in the Brno workshop of J. T. Rotter, having studied in Vienna. He made several drawings of the interior decoration of the church which are now preserved in Hungarian art collections. In 1749 he moved to Znojmo and through the Premonstratensians in Louka Monastery entered service with the Bishop of Jager.
b409179d-6059-59d1-be2e-d8d52c3ce402.location: Dominican Church of St. Michael, Brno

b478afb3-6caa-520b-bcbb-1a527eca0896.name: St. John the Baptist
b478afb3-6caa-520b-bcbb-1a527eca0896.description: The individual, larger-than-life figures are veiled in light, airy cloaks. Their austere gesticulation and postures correspond with their spiritual facial expressions. The picturesque outlines of the figures enhance the aesthetic impression of a pyramid-like whole. Following Zahner’s death the sculptural decoration was completed by W. Träger and J. M. Scherhauf. They continued with the sculptor’s initial concept and achieved features typical of Zahner in a side-altar figure for the Místek Church.

b48cb5d9-82ce-54c1-ab46-61d861c8e0cc.name: Loggia and arcades
b48cb5d9-82ce-54c1-ab46-61d861c8e0cc.description: A scenographic view of the loggia shows different points of view obtained through the use of columns, balustrades and arcades. This is typical of the local baroque tradition.

b4d6753b-ee3a-5120-a57e-e35af32589c1.name: Hall of the Ancestors
b4d6753b-ee3a-5120-a57e-e35af32589c1.description: The monumental and technically demanding building on an unusual elliptical ground plan, celebrates a Swabian-Bavarian dynasty that settled in Moravia in the second half of the 16th century. Statues in the niches represent real and mythical family figures. Erlach followed in the footsteps of Bernini in the design. The memorial building changed function in the mid-18th century when the Hall, with its pre-Romanticism terraces, became a viewing point for surveying the beautiful countryside around the chateau.
b4d6753b-ee3a-5120-a57e-e35af32589c1.artist: Johann Bernhard Fischer von Erlach (1656 Graz – 1723 Vienna), Tobias Kracker (1658–1736, Vienna)

b5374d8c-6eef-522b-8e1c-30b80526f11b.name: Library and refectory
b5374d8c-6eef-522b-8e1c-30b80526f11b.description:
Standing in the library one is astonished by the proportions. There are extensive fresco paintings on the ceiling which is measuring 21.4 m x 10.8 m. Though the room is only 4.8 meters high. It seems that there were originally two storeys as were in most libraries of that era. There are two architectural signs: a staircase leads to a lower situated small room (with a later drawn wall), and the adjacent library is in a later added wing. It was possibly built to replace the (earlier) lower situated one. – The topics on the ceiling´s paintings are very different: on the largest in the centre twelve-year-old Jesus can be seen in the temple. Around there are portraits of the four Fathers and the four Doctors of the Church, allegoric scenes, the dedication of the abbey to the Holy Virgin and the foundation legend of the Lambach, Göttweig and Admont abbeys by three friends – the later saints Adalbero and Altmann, bishop of Passau, and archbishop Gebhard of Salzburg.  
The refectory on the ground floor of the North wing is a highly decorated room. Walls and ceiling are covered with stucco garlands of fruits and leaves, busts and reliefs, some of them gilded. On the freshly coloured fresco paintings (end walls and ceiling) one can see the monastery´s dedication to the Holy Virgin and biblical scenes: an angel serves Jesus food after he had fasted in the desert for forty days and forty nights, the rain of manna, Christ at the Pharisee Simon´s banquet and Moses knocks water out of the rock. Pulpit and tables (the latter now in the ambulatory) with inlay were done by a regional artist.
b5374d8c-6eef-522b-8e1c-30b80526f11b.dates: End of 17th century fresco paintings ceiling and stucco work library West wing; 1706/1707 construction North wing; 1708 stucco work refectory; 1709 pulpit refectory and tables (the latter now in the ambulatory); 1720 fresco paintings refectory
b5374d8c-6eef-522b-8e1c-30b80526f11b.artist: Library: Melchior Steidl: fresco paintings; (associated with) Wenzel Halwax and his workshop: allegoric scenes Refectory: Diego Francesco Carlone: stucco work; Andreas Heindl: fresco paintings; Balthasar Melber: pulpit and tables with inlay (now in the ambulatory)

b636a313-8aa8-5184-b365-a6f872984266.name: *God the Father in Glory with Angels*, detail of the upper part
b636a313-8aa8-5184-b365-a6f872984266.description: The group was moved to the parish church of Minerbio by a neo-classic architect, Angelo Venturoli. He managed to save the baroque effect of dramatic light “alla Bernini” by opening two hidden side windows.
b636a313-8aa8-5184-b365-a6f872984266.location: Upper part of the high altar of the church of St. John the Baptist
b636a313-8aa8-5184-b365-a6f872984266.artist: Giuseppe Maria Mazza, Angelo Venturoli, Giacomo De Maria

b669842e-6ceb-5465-9eca-126b151afac3.name: *Assumption and Heavenly Reception of the Virgin Mary*
b669842e-6ceb-5465-9eca-126b151afac3.description: The complex Neoclassical dome fresco depicts Christ’s reception of the Virgin Mary in heaven together with biblical figures. It is clearly related to the high altarpiece depicting the *Assumption of the Virgin Mary*.
b669842e-6ceb-5465-9eca-126b151afac3.location: High altar and dome of the chancel

b7aa2d97-f660-5f39-a7c3-53ec68eec878.name: Victory Hall
b7aa2d97-f660-5f39-a7c3-53ec68eec878.description: The Regency-style panelled hall shows in its paintings, reliefs, concave moulding and ceiling fresco scenes of war, which refer to the Elector’s military success in the Turkish Wars. Scenes of the unsuccessful War of the Spanish Succession were deliberately avoided.
b7aa2d97-f660-5f39-a7c3-53ec68eec878.location: New Palace, first floor of the central wing
b7aa2d97-f660-5f39-a7c3-53ec68eec878.artist: Johann Adam Pichler (c. 1690–1761); Charles Dubut (c. 1687–1742): Jacopo Amigoni (c. 1682–1752); Joachim Beich (1665–1748)

b7c0b98d-c15d-53e7-87ca-e9455c41bd5a.name: Choir and crossing
b7c0b98d-c15d-53e7-87ca-e9455c41bd5a.description: Located at the centre of the building is the crossing, above which rises an octagonal cupola. A special feature is formed by the transitional pendentives, which here are filled in as opposed to being concavely arched. The tambour, studded with large windows, has an eight-sided cloister vault above it. The choir, considerably lower than the cross-arms due to its apse, has been under reconstruction since 2004 as part of the work on the high altar (from 1757) which was destroyed in 1943. The original altarpiece has been replaced by a work from Antonio Balestra from the story of St. Jacob. The straight-sided choir is flanked by two choir lofts, supported by stucco angels.

b7c10224-4a94-5164-8f2e-460a85f3a197.name: What remained from Marie Antoinette´s stay at Lambach abbey: a theatre decoration and a bed
b7c10224-4a94-5164-8f2e-460a85f3a197.description:
When Marie Antoinette travelled from Vienna to Versailles to become the wife of the later king Louis XVI, she had to go on a long journey. Since in these times there were no hostels along the roads, she travelled from monastery to monastery. When she arrived at Lambach abbey she was welcomed with many festive events. A monk had written a humorous stage play that was performed in the newly arranged theatre. Original stage decorations and the stage wall are still there. The latter is framing the stage with painted columns, statues (more figurines than statues, drawing the spectators´ eyes to the stage) and entablature. On the balcony on the right sits a man with a letter in his hands who is said to be the artist of the illusionistic painting. Through the curtain of the left door somebody is peeping out, which is typical before the beginning of a theatre piece to see how many spectators have arrived.  
And there is still the bed in which the later queen of France had slept. It is decorated with a carving on the headboard and inlays on the footboard.
b7c10224-4a94-5164-8f2e-460a85f3a197.location: Theatre; the bed is actually exhibited in the so-called Musician´s Corridor
b7c10224-4a94-5164-8f2e-460a85f3a197.artist: Johann Wenzel Turetschek (stage wall), unknown artist (bed)

b8200398-9bb1-5c02-923f-c8bdfc9fc5cf.name: The so called Spellati (the Ripped off)
b8200398-9bb1-5c02-923f-c8bdfc9fc5cf.description: These two statues, from the original wax models by Ercole Lelli, were carved in limewood by Silvestro Giannotti. They represent two male figures naked and skinless in order to show their muscles. They hold a canopy standing over the anatomy professor while he is teaching. Over the canopy sits an allegorical female figure representing Anatomy. She is receiving her typical attributes, a bone and a scroll, from a genius.

b83ce496-5956-54df-b73a-f5033db4841f.name: The Twelve Tablets of the Law
b83ce496-5956-54df-b73a-f5033db4841f.description: The Hall, containing the provincial tablets of the law, is decorated with scenes featuring *Emperor Ferdinand II*, *Moses' Decalogue*, the *Defence of the Provincial Tablets* and the *Guardians of the Public Trust*, represented by the figures of an aristocrat, a clergyman and a burgher, as well as a scrivener. The tablets, introduced in 1348, were a code of law that preceded the [land books](http://cs.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pozemkov%C3%A1_kniha "Pozemková kniha") where all enactments of [provincial assemblies](http://cs.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zemsk%C3%BD_sn%C4%9Bm&action=edit "Zemský snem") were recorded. [Joseph II's](http://cs.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josef_II. "Josef II.") reform of [1783](http://cs.wikipedia.org/wiki/1783 "1783") abolished the tablets' office, and legal authority passed to the new provincial court. *Leges XII tabularum*, written according to tradition in 450, formulated Roman consuetudinary law. The interpretation of its regulations laid the foundations of continental legal science, while the interpretation of its ancient language provided a basis for philology.

b84a196a-5e80-5eb5-a98e-69bd61c9145d.name: View of the Sanctuary
b84a196a-5e80-5eb5-a98e-69bd61c9145d.description: The walls of the nave are divided only by the shallow niches for altars between the pilasters topped by a cornice, with a dome above. Such characteristics tell of a designer educated in the tradition of the great Viennese architects of the first half of the 18th century, but also of one familiar with contemporary e achievements in Vienna.
b84a196a-5e80-5eb5-a98e-69bd61c9145d.location: Parish Church of St. Mary Magdalene

b84fc6dd-27c1-5511-a9e0-c67a19c076d7.name: *Our Lady of the Rosary*
b84fc6dd-27c1-5511-a9e0-c67a19c076d7.description: The sculpture of Our Lady with Christ accompanied by two angels is characterised by the harmony of the statuary and the pictorial treatment of the surface.
b84fc6dd-27c1-5511-a9e0-c67a19c076d7.location: Altar of Our Lady of the Rosary
b84fc6dd-27c1-5511-a9e0-c67a19c076d7.artist: Alvise Tagliapietra (1670–1747) and his son Ambrogio (b. 1701)

b85348b2-d909-56ff-a0a5-f045a0d7908e.name: Statues
b85348b2-d909-56ff-a0a5-f045a0d7908e.description:
The small statues (about 60cm high) on the three altars, by Joseph Matthias Götz, are baroque masterpieces. There are umpteen figures on every altar, made of alabaster and delicately carved.  
The statues on the ornament-like bases to the left and to the right of the tabernacles reflect the swing of the epoch. It looks as if a baroque storm would blow through their clothes. Even the tinier statues (about 40cm high) on the tabernacles are of high sculptural quality and execute strong movements.  
The (larger) figures at the altars´ sides represent allegoric scenes, while the smaller ones on and around the tabernacles depict the Fathers of the Church, prophets, evangelists, saints, angels and allegoric scenes as well as Christ and guardian angels fighting with verve against the evil.
b85348b2-d909-56ff-a0a5-f045a0d7908e.location: On and around tabernacles and altars

b9250751-a918-5753-8ef7-c308b77cd4dd.name: Fountain Design
b9250751-a918-5753-8ef7-c308b77cd4dd.artist: Johann Bernhard Fischer von Erlach (1656, Graz – 1723, Vienna)

b9439e08-f605-525b-ab57-a6bd68cb7344.name: *Plato and Aristoteles*
b9439e08-f605-525b-ab57-a6bd68cb7344.description:
This representation is depicted in one of the seven lunettes of the main room. In this room the central theme is the *Ascension to the Mountain of Knowledge*. The allegories of several disciplines (Philosophy, Mathematics, Moral Philosophy, Theology, History and Law) are flanked by pairs of their significant representatives. The lunettes allude to the books held in the bookshelves below.  
In this lunette, illustrating Philosophy, Plato and Aristoteles are sitting on the sides of a central basis. They are supporting a monochrome standing female figure. She is holding in her right hand three circles of different diameter and in her left hand a round vessel with a burning a flame.

b94d6ba6-4d5d-506c-a98a-300337f08cd0.name: High altar
b94d6ba6-4d5d-506c-a98a-300337f08cd0.description: The high altar acquires its dignity and elegance by lateral columns. They frame plastically the altarpiece that depicts the Assumption of Mary. Via crossing media she is approached above the cornice by Christ who is part of the sculpted group of the Holy Trinity. The patrons of the church are only represented by lateral statues.
b94d6ba6-4d5d-506c-a98a-300337f08cd0.artist: Architecture and sculptures: Johann Baptist Straub (1704–84); Altarpiece: Balthasar Augustin Albrecht (1687–1765)

b985235f-025a-5eed-a7b8-96646d281fd8.name: The Triumph of Religion and Spirituality
b985235f-025a-5eed-a7b8-96646d281fd8.description: The Triumph of Religion and Spirituality, where Science, holding a book on the one hand and fire on the other, gazes at the Heaven above, the true source of knowledge. Down next to her, Religion holding a tripod.

b9abc8a0-1fc1-59ad-9b41-3194b57afd27.name: Throne Room
b9abc8a0-1fc1-59ad-9b41-3194b57afd27.description: The Throne Room, also known as the Great Room, is the largest of the palace's three state rooms. Construction began in 1768 when the marriage of Dom Pedro to the future Queen Maria I demanded a large area for official audiences. Designed by the architect, Jean-Baptiste Robillion, the new room was built in the Rococo style with carvings by the sculptor and wood carver, Silvestre de Faria Lobo. The paintings on the ceiling represent Faith, Sun, Hope, War, Justice and Charity and were executed under the direction of the painter, João de Freitas Leitão. Manuel da Costa, António Berardi and Manuel do Nascimento assisted him.
b9abc8a0-1fc1-59ad-9b41-3194b57afd27.artist: Jean Baptiste Robillion (active 1758–1782); carving: Silvestre de Faria Lobo; painters: João de Freitas Leitão, Manuel da Costa, António Berardi, Manuel do Nascimento, whose dates are unknown.

ba5ce20b-93ed-5c78-aff9-153a607a9783.name: Façade Sculptures
ba5ce20b-93ed-5c78-aff9-153a607a9783.description: The main body of the façade is furnished by allegoric sculptures of Faith, Devotion, Gratitude and Liberality, and in the lower level, on the side, there are niches within which are St. Teresa of Avila and St. Mary Magdalene of Pazzi. On the upper section there are sculptures of St. Elijah and St. John of Cross. The central high -relief of the Sacred Heart of Jesus is flanked by two angels.
ba5ce20b-93ed-5c78-aff9-153a607a9783.artist: Joaquim Machado de Castro (1731–1822)and his workshop: Alexandre Gomes [n.d.], João José Elveni (active 1747), José Joaquim Leitão (1731–1811), José Patrício (active 1779–1789) Faustino José Rodrigues [n.d.], Giovanni Chiari (active 1807–08; 1812–17).

bad50899-194a-53f5-8b17-f81567ff0b42.name: High altar
bad50899-194a-53f5-8b17-f81567ff0b42.description: The bundle of columns of the powerful main altar made of stucco marble forms an imposing frame for the topics of the altarpiece, namely the Trinity and Redemption. To the sides, larger-than-life stucco figures of the apostles Peter and Paul in ecstatically-moved depictions admonish the faithful, while respectively, the painting reflects on the secret of faith. On either side are the figures of the holy bishops Ulrich and Conrad, both of whom were patrons of the Swabian bishoprics of Augsburg and Konstanz.
bad50899-194a-53f5-8b17-f81567ff0b42.artist: Johann Michael Feichtmayr (1696–1772); Johann Joseph Christian (1706–1777); Johann Jakob Zeiller (1708–1783)

bb4dd8ab-cc0e-5fac-aef4-60091ca7be8d.name: The Four Latin Church Fathers
bb4dd8ab-cc0e-5fac-aef4-60091ca7be8d.description: The statues of the Four Latin Church Fathers, still animated with restrained Baroque pathos, rank as the best works of their creator.
bb4dd8ab-cc0e-5fac-aef4-60091ca7be8d.location: Column pairs in the lay church on the sides of the transept

bbb068e0-786d-5185-ae89-0a937e547d94.name: Ceiling fresco of the Dining Room
bbb068e0-786d-5185-ae89-0a937e547d94.description: The enchanting fresco on the ceiling of the Dining Room shows Odysseus’ arrival at the nymph Calypso’s island guarded in heaven by gods. It was painted primarily during the reign of Max III Joseph.
bbb068e0-786d-5185-ae89-0a937e547d94.location: New Palace, ground floor of the central wing

bbf2ac31-f420-5547-903d-485e39009fa1.name: Arches over the Alcântara valley
bbf2ac31-f420-5547-903d-485e39009fa1.description: The structure uses the pointed arch in some of the larger arches crossing the Alcântara valley. Curiously, some of the stones of the Aqueduct are inscribed with the masons' initials, a custom that was all but lost but which was revived here.

bc51144d-7f51-569b-98c3-5440f70f3532.name: Ceiling stucco in the vestibule of the large summer dining hall
bc51144d-7f51-569b-98c3-5440f70f3532.description: The rich ornamentation consists of strapwork, grids, bells and festoons of flowers. G. M. Fontana came from a large north-Italian family active in Moravia from the 1660s. He also worked on the decoration of the chateau frontage. The room originally featured tapestries with scenes by P. Brueghel Sr.

bd498b1e-10d8-51ed-a9f6-dcb8b3eca124.name: Octagonal  dome
bd498b1e-10d8-51ed-a9f6-dcb8b3eca124.description: The dome with Baroque and Rococo features is topped by a small lantern and four large windows together with some *trompe l'oeil* windows too. The dome is composed of white stonework – which at one time was polychrome – and is ornamented with spiralling motifs.
bd498b1e-10d8-51ed-a9f6-dcb8b3eca124.artist: Father João Baptista [n.d.] and Manuel Gomes

bd83431f-3b68-50c1-b369-a3b63fc107e1.name: Staircase
bd83431f-3b68-50c1-b369-a3b63fc107e1.description: A two-shouldered staircase with stucco decoration is overlooked by a ceiling painting of *The Fall of the Titans*. A number of Italian artists who had settled in Vienna worked for Count Questenberk in the 1720s and 30s.

bdb9b063-8eae-579f-839d-ba9aea3eaa63.name: Worship of the name of Jesus through the four continents
bdb9b063-8eae-579f-839d-ba9aea3eaa63.description: The theme of the ceiling painting is the Triumph of Christ in heaven as on earth. The monogram “IHS” becomes a form of throne for the Infant Jesus and his mother. Sun and moon stand for the universal sovereignty over space and time; in the clouds the church patron St. Vitus with a host of angels. The globe is surrounded by personifications of the continents in honour and worship of Jesus. At the west end, antipodal to the Triumph of faith, the Fall of Satan and hell, whose impotence is shown through his subjugation by the archangel Michael in the form of a putto.
bdb9b063-8eae-579f-839d-ba9aea3eaa63.location: Ceiling fresco in the congregation room

bdc1f2b1-fc9e-59d3-ae94-399c2dcd7e7c.name: Collegiate church, stucco
bdc1f2b1-fc9e-59d3-ae94-399c2dcd7e7c.description: The exceedingly rich stuccowork is an important example of the Early Baroque Munich school of stucco with panels structured in classical forms, which in the choir are also enriched with figurative reliefs. The work, under the direction of the sculptor Onofrius Weigl, was also executed by stucco masons of the Wessobrunn school.

bdc92e89-8fcf-5e5f-b4a5-e6fce434d540.name: Ceiling paintings
bdc92e89-8fcf-5e5f-b4a5-e6fce434d540.description: In the central field of the painting surrounded by angels sits a winged woman dressed in a white robe and blue cloak. Her attributes – a crown on her head, a triangle on her breast symbolising the Holy Trinity, a rope and a ring in her hands, flames around her head and a mirror (without stain) – match the iconography of the Immaculate Conception and the Blessed Virgin Mary, being here also a symbol of the Church.

bde4f2f2-d40b-57af-b5d6-cd1f3f422f2f.name: High altar
bde4f2f2-d40b-57af-b5d6-cd1f3f422f2f.description: The high altar, erected almost two decades after the church was consecrated, bears only light traces of the Classicist style; this is only apparent in the somewhat stiff, angular form of the altar crown, not the overall form: a column altar with, in part, free-standing supporting elements. The altar from Anton Simeth is probably based on the design from Petrus Schmid who completed a number of figures before suffering a fatal accident in 1787.
bde4f2f2-d40b-57af-b5d6-cd1f3f422f2f.dates: Erected in 1805 utilising statues from before 1787; altarpiece 1807
bde4f2f2-d40b-57af-b5d6-cd1f3f422f2f.artist: Anton Simeth [n.d.]; Petrus Schmid [n.d]; Andreas Nesselthaler (1748–1821)

be223737-7c12-50b0-a7e8-cdae4ef617f5.name: Staircase
be223737-7c12-50b0-a7e8-cdae4ef617f5.description: Monti designed a so-called “macchina per salire” (machine to  ascend) that transformed the loggia into a theatrical stage, with stuccos by Carlo Nessi. The staircase consist of two symmetrical and opposite flights where the windows are open on illusionistic perspectives.
be223737-7c12-50b0-a7e8-cdae4ef617f5.location: Hall, ground floor, Palazzo Marescotti Brazzetti

be3b668a-5d87-5793-9bef-a8d5f0482e41.name: Panoramic view of the church interior
be3b668a-5d87-5793-9bef-a8d5f0482e41.description: Commissioned by the wealthy merchant, Manuel Álvares Azeitado, this is the first *scarto* known in Portugal, forming part of the International Baroque program. The panoramic view of the interior shows the *trompe l'œil* architecture of the barrel-vaulted ceiling, which appears to be a continuation of the walls. The *trompe l'œil,* centred towards one focal point, creates the illusion of deep recession, heavenly sphere or even an open sky.
be3b668a-5d87-5793-9bef-a8d5f0482e41.artist: Woodcarvers: João de Touro Freitas, António de Oliveira (1675–n.d.), Manuel João da Fonseca and Francisco da Silva (1684-n.d.); painters: António de Oliveira Bernardes (1662–1732) and Pedro Figueira; azulejos painters: Gabriel del Barco (1649–c.1703)

be663194-99e6-5792-bcaf-1232ec907783.name: Nave
be663194-99e6-5792-bcaf-1232ec907783.description: An oval-shaped nave with four altars.

beb103e2-c3d8-5595-a211-c4be2ed2c8ce.name: Bernhardisaal (Fürstensaal)
beb103e2-c3d8-5595-a211-c4be2ed2c8ce.description: Architecturally, the Bernhardisaal, extending over two storeys, is a simple rectangular room whose distinguishing feature is a rectangular opening in the ceiling with perimeter balustrade, a “hypaethral space” which gives the illusion of an opening onto heaven. It is the wall and ceiling paintings, covering the entire surface, that first turn the room into a ceremonial hall. A sequence of scenes from the life of the founder of the order, St. Bernhard of Clairvaux, culminates in the Christmas vision above the ceiling opening.
beb103e2-c3d8-5595-a211-c4be2ed2c8ce.location: Central pavilion of the western monastery wing, the so called “Bernhardibau”, Cistercian Monastery of Stams
beb103e2-c3d8-5595-a211-c4be2ed2c8ce.artist: Johann Martin Gumpp the elder (1643–1729) and Georg Anton Gumpp (1682–1754); Franz Michael Hueber (?–1746), Anton Zoller (1695–1768)

bf66d04d-bf53-5799-aa15-41c2f4772599.name: Caesar Fountain
bf66d04d-bf53-5799-aa15-41c2f4772599.description: The rearing horse with rider stands on a rock; at the horse’s feet lie two figures of bearded men, water deities, representing the rivers Morava and Danube. Their joined hands and forward movement indicate the confluence of the two rivers. The men hold the emblems of Moravia and Lower Austria, symbolising the alliance of the two countries and their joint future in loyalty (personified by a resting dog) to the emperor.
bf66d04d-bf53-5799-aa15-41c2f4772599.artist: Jan Jiří Schauberger (?, before 1725 Vienna, active in Olomouc – 1744 Brno)

bf8d5dd6-621c-537a-a14f-13c5c7464cea.name: Gardens
bf8d5dd6-621c-537a-a14f-13c5c7464cea.description: Expansion of the garden was possible after resolution of the uneven land quotas and the relatively rough excavation. The garden's first designer was the Dutchman, Jan van der Kolke, who followed the plans of Robillion. The expansion followed a structure typical of the Portuguese “farm”, purchasing the surrounding land to create a formal garden, a recreational garden and a large area for cultivation, the *Quinta Real*.
bf8d5dd6-621c-537a-a14f-13c5c7464cea.artist: Jean Baptiste Robillion (active 1758–1782); Garden statues: John Cheere (1709-1787)

bfde98ff-c1bf-5790-801d-18b84b741f38.name: Ceiling frescos: *Care of the Arts* – *Theological Truth* – *Profane Truth*
bfde98ff-c1bf-5790-801d-18b84b741f38.description: The central ceiling image of the library hall displays Theological Truth through Divine Revelation. In the next fresco, Parnassus as the Mountain of the Muses with feminine allegories shows the close relationship between the arts, and likewise, the close relationship between the monastery and the modern sciences. On the other side Truth, in the sense of profane critical science, is taken as a theme illustrating the “unveiling of truth”, which at the same time underlines the quintessence of the entire programme. The depiction is based on the title page of Diderot's *Encyclopédie*, the famous encyclopedia of the Enlightenment, which was perceived at the time to bring together the entirety of knowledge from the sciences, the arts and the trades. Provost Fanciscus Töpsl leaves behind his intellectual legacy by using his coat-of-arms: he sees himself not only as the third founder and decisive reformer of his foundation, but likewise, as father of its enlightened mission to instruct and inform.
bfde98ff-c1bf-5790-801d-18b84b741f38.location: Vault of the Library Hall, Augustinian Canons’ Convent of the Holy Saviour

bfed794d-33a3-554d-8ce9-82eccf3e5f7b.name: Crucifixion Altar (High Altar)
bfed794d-33a3-554d-8ce9-82eccf3e5f7b.description: The mighty high altar with three columns on either side is constructed as a stage altar in which the themes of the religious observance can be theatrically illustrated following the Diessen model. According  to the patrocinium, the altar piece shows Christ on the cross whereas the two winding columns, connected above by volute brackets to form a canopy, refer to those in the Roman St. Peter’s Church, thus, together with the statues of the apostle leaders Peter and Paul, claim the leadership of the papacy.
bfed794d-33a3-554d-8ce9-82eccf3e5f7b.artist: Altar Architecture: Dominikus Bergmüller (1707–73); Sculptures: Franz Xaver Schmädl (1705–77); Altarpiece: Johann Baptist Baader (1717–80)

c033a142-ba63-5940-81e3-bdf3db2aed83.name: *Allegories of the Four Seasons, Four Temperaments and Four Elements*
c033a142-ba63-5940-81e3-bdf3db2aed83.description: Four allegories representing the Four Seasons, the Four Stages of Life, the Four Elements, Four Tempers and, finally, the Four Senses, painted by Anton Jožef Lerchinger after prints by Johann Georg Bergmüller (Turkheim, Schwaben 1688 – Augsburg 1762) from Augsburg.
c033a142-ba63-5940-81e3-bdf3db2aed83.location: Wall of the working cabinet, Ratkaj Palace

c18e8d6d-69e1-5154-b742-7142e553dfce.name: Stuccowork
c18e8d6d-69e1-5154-b742-7142e553dfce.description: Stucco floral ornamentation and figurative scenes depict the life of the patron saint and saints to which the side chapels were dedicated between 1713 and 1726. The stuccowork, by the Italian master Anton Joseph Quadrio, was constructed between 1713 and 1721, and an anonymous Italian master between 1724 and 1726. With this exquisite work, St. Catherine's reached the ideal of *bel composto*, the characteristic Baroque unity of architecture, sculpture and painting.

c1acfc20-ced7-5631-9eba-98e3d6d38ec3.name: Wall covered with bones
c1acfc20-ced7-5631-9eba-98e3d6d38ec3.description: The Baroque sensibility reinforces a tendency arising from the late Middle Ages, which makes death and even funerals a spectacle aimed at showing the deceased, as far as possible, cheered up until the final destination: his or her grave and eternal resting place. The concept of a *Boa Morte* “Gentle Death” is the point of the prayers to Nossa Senhora da Boa Morte, whose origins go back to this tradition.

c1c0b0de-8c2c-564c-abd8-1b7bab473b05.name: Vault
c1c0b0de-8c2c-564c-abd8-1b7bab473b05.description: A cylindrical vault with intersecting segments is decorated austerely with stucco rods with “mirror” frames. The vault pedestal is marked by a ledge frieze supported by pilasters; this approach was typical of the second half of the 17th century.
c1c0b0de-8c2c-564c-abd8-1b7bab473b05.location: Dominican Church of St. Michael, Brno

c1efc606-bb1a-5e6b-a789-0a668d5179a7.name: Interior of the church
c1efc606-bb1a-5e6b-a789-0a668d5179a7.description: High Baroque longitudinal single-nave type with lateral chapels and dominant sanctuary

c256056a-455e-5666-97c9-214e4f117e0d.name: Ceiling painting: *Competition of the Magician Simon with Peter and Paul*
c256056a-455e-5666-97c9-214e4f117e0d.description: Victory over evil and unbelief, which frequently commences the programme of pictures, is here drawn from the story of the two church patrons: The apostles demonstrate the truth of the Christian faith in front of the entire people, evil in the form of the magician is destroyed. In a spatial image made up of a range of perspectives, different levels are combined with virtuosity to form an overall impression: Late Baroque pictorial rhetoric employing clear colours and audacious composition.

c2794ae5-2bd4-58c8-894b-a8fbe7024d22.name: Oršić Castle, Central Hall Frescoes
c2794ae5-2bd4-58c8-894b-a8fbe7024d22.description: *Trompe l'œil* window frescos articulate the walls of the Central hall. Within the windows are painted landscapes.
