c27eb774-cc9f-55db-b3e3-343e34b005f2.name: Middle room balcony railings
c27eb774-cc9f-55db-b3e3-343e34b005f2.description: Each room has a different colour scheme and decorative emphasis with multicoloured bookshelves of different lacquered finishes in green, red and black decorated with *chinoiserie* motifs. Each of the rooms is two-storeys high, with a balcony and stairs incorporated into the furniture.
c27eb774-cc9f-55db-b3e3-343e34b005f2.location: Interior, Biblioteca Joanina da Universidade de Coimbra
c27eb774-cc9f-55db-b3e3-343e34b005f2.artist: Design and execution: Francesco Gualdini, João Rodrigues de Almeida; supervisor: Gaspar Ferreira; painting and gilding of woodwork: Manuel da Silva [dates unknown]

c2a04a59-d483-5172-86bf-965cfc076d63.name: Side altars depicting St. Stephen and St. Sebastian
c2a04a59-d483-5172-86bf-965cfc076d63.description:
As imports of Venetian painting, the pictures on the two middle altars embody the cosmopolitan taste of the Provost, Herculan Karg. Giovanni Pittoni painted the Protomartyr Stephen. Likewise, Giovanni Tiepolo, Pittoni’s even more renowned colleague, painted St. Sebastian who is the patron saint of plague victims.  
By intentionally eschewing the typical retable architecture, the sumptuous altarpieces appear to the viewer as being pictures in a gallery, unveiled by puttos through means of sculpted drapery which seems to be pulled aside. The flanking sculptures belong to a cycle depicting the 12 Apostles who are distributed among the side altars.
c2a04a59-d483-5172-86bf-965cfc076d63.location: The third pair of altars from the chancel. St. Stephen is on the left and St. Sebastian on the right.
c2a04a59-d483-5172-86bf-965cfc076d63.artist: Architecture and sculpture on the altars: Johann Baptist Straub (1704–84);  Altarpieces: Giovanni Battista Pittoni (1687–1767) and Giovanni Battista Tiepolo (1696–1770)

c2d63c5b-d4ae-5888-8cde-752a7081e65c.name: *St. Blaise*
c2d63c5b-d4ae-5888-8cde-752a7081e65c.description: A freestanding figure of the patron saint of the church and of Dubrovnik itself St. Blaise.

c2e53467-4a58-5c0a-a5ef-e7fb0a384dbf.name: *Stigmata of St. Francis*
c2e53467-4a58-5c0a-a5ef-e7fb0a384dbf.description: Central place in the lower part of the composition belongs to the unconscious saint and angels. Separated by light accents on the dark landscape the brother Leon, in the background, witnesses the stigmatisation. Among the clouds in the upper part of the composition a winged Seraphim carries the Crucified Jesus, followed by a group of angels.
c2e53467-4a58-5c0a-a5ef-e7fb0a384dbf.location: The painting, made originally for the Altar of St. Frances in the church, is in the monastery corridor in the present day.

c2fa115e-3ff1-53bd-a4fb-c6aa6c675900.name: Examples of *Via Crucis* chapels: Chapel of the Flagellation and the Mercury Fountain; Chapel of the Crucifixion and the interior of the Chapel of the Falls
c2fa115e-3ff1-53bd-a4fb-c6aa6c675900.description: The Stairway of the Five Senses leads up to the Crucifixion Chapel. On the way up are other chapels one of which, the Chapel of the Flagellation, reinforces the Suffering of Christ or the *Via Crucis* as an element of purification.
c2fa115e-3ff1-53bd-a4fb-c6aa6c675900.location: The Stairway of the Five Senses, Bom Jesus de Braga (Bom Jesus do Monte)

c2fbeb88-8a77-582a-a431-c3d1fbc93542.name: Main fresco
c2fbeb88-8a77-582a-a431-c3d1fbc93542.description: The nave frescos of the monastery church are typologically woven into one another, depicting the life of the founder of the Cistercian Order, Bernhard of Clairvaux, and likewise, the Life of Christ. Using the solemnity of the church year from west to east the position of the Cistercians within God’s divine plan for salvation is accented: the Birth of Christ and Saint Bernhard’s vision of it; the Resurrection with its sermon for the Duke of Aquitaine; the Ascent to Heaven with the entrance of the saint into the Citeaux Monastery as well as the despatch of the Holy Ghost with Bernhard’s visions of Christ Crucified and the Virgin Mary.

c3248f90-1efb-5523-aeb8-e0dc9f500316.name: Main portal
c3248f90-1efb-5523-aeb8-e0dc9f500316.description: The monastery was established in 1350 by Margrave Jan Jindřich of Luxembourg, brother of Emperor Charles IV. The church was meant to house the tombs of the Luxembourg dynasty, but only Jan Jindřich and his son, Jošt, are buried here; their statues flank the entrance to the prefecture. It is the only five-axis palace portal in Moravia.
c3248f90-1efb-5523-aeb8-e0dc9f500316.location: Augustinian Monastery, Hermits of St. Thomas the Apostle
c3248f90-1efb-5523-aeb8-e0dc9f500316.artist: František Antonín Grimm (1710 Brno – 1784 Brno) – Josef Leonard Weber (? Svidnica – after 1766 Trnava)

c382e187-dfa2-5c42-8797-e81a3eeb61e8.name: The way to Calvary
c382e187-dfa2-5c42-8797-e81a3eeb61e8.description:
This crowded and airless way to Calvary with soldiers and executioners all around Christ is in the typical caricature style of Francesco Brizio (c. 1574–1623).  
He most likely developed this style in the workshop of Bartolomeo Passerotti (1529–1592), a specialist in genre scenes with caricatures.
c382e187-dfa2-5c42-8797-e81a3eeb61e8.location: Oratory of the Madonna dell’Orazione, entrance wall

c411bbf2-f8fa-5be5-91ee-30d88c519c1c.name: General View of the Interior and three lateral chapels
c411bbf2-f8fa-5be5-91ee-30d88c519c1c.description: General view of the single-nave interior with three of the four lateral “Lady” chapels: Chapel of Our Lady of Glory (the *Apocalypse* in low relief in the tympanum), Chapel of Our Lady of Conception and the Chapel of Our Lady of Assistance, all of which have gilt-wood retables.
c411bbf2-f8fa-5be5-91ee-30d88c519c1c.artist: Architects: Mateus do Couto (“uncle”; active 1660), Carlos Baptista Garvo stone carvers: António Pereira, Vicente Soares, Manuel Rodrigues; woodcarvers: António Martins Calheiros, António Luís, Claude Laprade, Manuel Álvares [dates unknown]

c4949ddb-d9d5-551d-b5df-1849fe2e8307.name: Ceremonial Façade (main façade)
c4949ddb-d9d5-551d-b5df-1849fe2e8307.description: Perhaps one of the best palace façades of the Portuguese Baroque, it combines traditional Portuguese features with Classical precision. The triangular pediment, adorned at the tympanum with garlands, averts the solemnity of a façade which is the keynote of the garden views.
c4949ddb-d9d5-551d-b5df-1849fe2e8307.location: Exterior view from the Pênsil Garden
c4949ddb-d9d5-551d-b5df-1849fe2e8307.artist: Jean Baptiste Robillion (active 1758–1782), Mateus Vicente de Oliveira (1706–1786)

c50c530f-8856-58b7-b0c8-6a852549828b.name: *St. John of Nepomuk*
c50c530f-8856-58b7-b0c8-6a852549828b.description: This painting by A. Schoonjans, an itinerant Flemish artist, is on a side altar covering an entrance to the Chapel of the Holy Cross. A court painter in Vienna and Berlin, he was active in Moravia where he worked in particular for the Znojmo Premonstratensians. The altar by J. J. Schauberger was removed from the chapel and now closes the former entrance to the chapel with a Thaumaturga.
c50c530f-8856-58b7-b0c8-6a852549828b.location: Augustinian Monastery, Hermits of St. Thomas the Apostle

c5d4ce83-28e3-57fb-bebd-32c994976202.name: Choir with high altar
c5d4ce83-28e3-57fb-bebd-32c994976202.description: The massive high altar, built by Martin Lengauer in 1756, forms the focal point of a graduated prospect whereby the simple ground plan of fore choir (transverse rectangle) and choir (semi-circular apse) is not visible from the nave. Protruding pilasters set at an angle between the fore choir and the apse form the framework for the altar, which, with its lively structure, completely fills this niche in accordance with the side-altars in the nave niches.
c5d4ce83-28e3-57fb-bebd-32c994976202.location: View from the nave into the choir
c5d4ce83-28e3-57fb-bebd-32c994976202.artist: Abraham Millauer (c. 1680–1758), Philipp Millauer (1710–53), Leonhard Millauer [n.d.]

c6225da7-41a1-5706-82f3-6f3e9e2d0c24.name: Façade
c6225da7-41a1-5706-82f3-6f3e9e2d0c24.description: The façade, originally planned with bolder mouldings and greater richness, is only distantly related to that of the Innsbruck parish church (since 1964 St. Jacob’s Cathedral). The architectural idea in Wilten is a different one: While at St. Jacob’s the central section between the towers is set back, here a lightly rounded, projecting broken pediment sets column-like accents. These form the framework for the central section with its shallow concave form. United under a tail gable the central section forms the main motif, while in contrast, at the Innsbruck parish church the central section was clearly subordinated to the pair of towers. The statue of the Mary Immaculata and the portal are the work of Joseph Stapf.
c6225da7-41a1-5706-82f3-6f3e9e2d0c24.artist: Franz de Paula Penz (1702–1772), Joseph Stapf [n.d.]

c6cb3e56-81b8-5635-ab45-fa274e89c1c4.name: Ceiling fresco
c6cb3e56-81b8-5635-ab45-fa274e89c1c4.description: Following his apprenticeship, Schöpf, a student of Knoller, is considered one of the most important masters of fresco painting during the transition to Early Classicism. The composition of the large cupola fresco depicting the Coronation of the Virgin Mary follows the Late Baroque scheme with a crown of clouds and vision of light in the centre, however the painting style, above all in the case of the figures, is characterised by concentration and devout earnestness. Baroque pathos is replaced by a salutary pictorial narrative.

c6e385c3-ce5d-59a2-9749-9c9b67369cb0.name: St. Cyril
c6e385c3-ce5d-59a2-9749-9c9b67369cb0.description: The six statues on the central section represent Slavic saints: Methodius, the first Moravian bishop; Cyril (Konstantin); Vojtěch the Bishop of Prague and founder of the first Benedictine Monastery in Bohemia; John of Nepomuk; John Sarkander, tortured to death in Olomouc in 1620; and St. Blasius to whom the Olomouc Church, considered the oldest Baroque church in the country, was dedicated.

c77b1fdd-77c1-5393-bb6e-34d3a79f55ad.name: Main chapel and High Altar Altarpiece
c77b1fdd-77c1-5393-bb6e-34d3a79f55ad.description:
The high altar features an altarpiece depicting St. Catherine, St. Paul and St. Bulão, made during the reign of King João V. It marks the transition in taste of the altarpiece genre, adopting large monumental structures partially inspired by Italian architecture.  
The stucco ceiling depicts an allegory of the Holy Trinity, and on the walls are paintings by Andre Gonçalves.
c77b1fdd-77c1-5393-bb6e-34d3a79f55ad.artist: Retable: woodcarver: Santos Pacheco; stucco ceiling painting: António Pimenta Rolim (c. 1759/1851); painting: André Gonçalves (1685–1762).

c7eaf695-c32d-5a9b-abe4-003a1cc59469.name: Column and vault with bones
c7eaf695-c32d-5a9b-abe4-003a1cc59469.description: A spectacular image of the shortness of Life and the inevitability of Death. The skull and bones are the earthly evidence of the Death of the Body, in opposition to the aesthetic Joy of Redemption or Salvation. This trend for exhibiting naked bones – so called *Morte Secca* (“Dry Death”) – encompasses the allegory of Christian meditation: “Life is just a short passage; this world is not the ultimate destiny; the final destiny is the salvation of the soul.”

c7fb890b-5f07-5f95-9ff8-9c8c19735fbc.name: *St. Francis Takes off his Worldly Clothes in front of the Bishop*
c7fb890b-5f07-5f95-9ff8-9c8c19735fbc.description: The scenes, painted in the small ceiling medallions in 1683, are characteristically well-organised, dynamic compositions.

c808701e-fb13-501f-b5ef-7e36dad27a4e.name: Pulpit
c808701e-fb13-501f-b5ef-7e36dad27a4e.description: A creative reinterpretation of the pulpit by J. B. Straub of 10 years earlier, it stands out in the pantheon of Baroque sculpture in northern Croatia at a time when sculpture and imaginatively and skilfully executed ornamental work were on the threshold of the Rococo.
c808701e-fb13-501f-b5ef-7e36dad27a4e.location: North side of the nave, Parish Church of Our Lady of the Snow

c8223071-8449-5de7-8edc-1087729762f4.name: Tile-Painting Masters’ signature, P.M.P.
c8223071-8449-5de7-8edc-1087729762f4.description: The signature P.M.P is probably that of Padre Manuel Pereira, who was a clergyman, amateur architect (in the 18th century he designed the palace of the Tristão da Cunha family) and *azulejos* painter. Padre Manuel Pereira was patron of a large workshop in Lisbon. He had several disciples that produced *azulejos* for palaces and churches all over Portugal and Brazil.
c8223071-8449-5de7-8edc-1087729762f4.artist: Tile-Painting Master P.M.P., probably Padre Manuel Pereira [n.d.]

c84f6b86-bda2-5650-b91c-dba0814eb447.name: Remedy Fountain
c84f6b86-bda2-5650-b91c-dba0814eb447.description: Situated in the centre of the Courtyard of the Kings, overlooking the staircase, is an obelisk fountain known as the Remedy Fountain. The obelisk in the centre of the fountain is 14 metres high.
c84f6b86-bda2-5650-b91c-dba0814eb447.location: Courtyard of the Kings, Sanctuary of Our Lady of Good Remedy

c8702876-ac37-5902-bf15-743a186cb380.name: Gates of St Anthony (Santo António) - exterior and interior
c8702876-ac37-5902-bf15-743a186cb380.description: Gates designed in the Classical style of French military architecture.

c8bccff1-9c81-5fca-adb1-b9407b328f8e.name: Church’s plan
c8bccff1-9c81-5fca-adb1-b9407b328f8e.description: Greek cross plan with four symmetrical towers united by undulating walls.

c8d4755a-5654-5a9a-b873-e0c0966909ab.name: High altar
c8d4755a-5654-5a9a-b873-e0c0966909ab.description: The high altar, a structure composed of a loose grouping of freestanding marble pillars enclosing the altarpiece framed by pilasters, fits in perfectly to the semi-circle of the eastern apse. The painting from Zeiller depicts the church patron St. Vitus as a martyr ascending into heaven. The actual martyrdom is depicted in the choir fresco. In addition, the white painted sculptures of St. Peter and St. Paul are attributed to Franz Xaver Nißl.
c8d4755a-5654-5a9a-b873-e0c0966909ab.artist: Franz Xaver Nißl (1731–1804); Franz Graßmayr [n.d.]; Franz Anton Zeiller (1716–1794)

c8fcc521-c8fd-5169-9a79-20dd33d8158d.name: *St Francis Visiting the Home of Katarina Galović During his Stay in Zagreb*
c8fcc521-c8fd-5169-9a79-20dd33d8158d.description: The meeting between the Zagreb citizen, Katarina Galović, and St. Francis supposedly took place in 13th century but the cityscape in the background is Baroque, and on the church tower the year 1683 is recorded.

c90e1ce2-788c-5c71-b79a-bfbec589dc17.name: Façade
c90e1ce2-788c-5c71-b79a-bfbec589dc17.description: The south façade, lacking any significant architectural features, becomes the viewing side by virtue of Knoller’s frescos. The edges are accentuated by colossal pilasters that appear to support the real principal cornice. The five windows and the portal are fitted with frames and the unstructured area of wall in the centre above the portal is occupied by an aureole of the church patron in a sweeping cartouche.
c90e1ce2-788c-5c71-b79a-bfbec589dc17.location: Exterior view from the south (the church is oriented towards the north)

c9398419-e8fd-51e0-a09b-6998a0522cf3.name: Pulpit
c9398419-e8fd-51e0-a09b-6998a0522cf3.description: The pulpit, richly decorated with gilded rocaille, possibly also a work of Stapf, is decorated by two sculptures, a relief on the pulpit featuring Moses in front of the Burning Bush (meaning: Moses hears the word of God as the faithful the sermon); and the statue of the Apocalyptical Angel with the Tablets of the Law on the baldachin (proclamation of the Will of God and portent of the impending Day of Judgement).

c98afbe4-8f44-5607-bb49-a1a56098da61.name: Library
c98afbe4-8f44-5607-bb49-a1a56098da61.description: The entrance to the library, with a ceiling-painting of the 12-year-old Jesus in the temple disputing with the elders (the first example of Jesus’ preaching), opens with Prudence and Knowledge; Wisdom is painted on the door. The library, with its well-preserved furniture, is among the most significant Baroque libraries in Czech lands.

c997623c-dc1e-5f87-b598-a6ef85003af7.name: Coronation of the Virgin Mary
c997623c-dc1e-5f87-b598-a6ef85003af7.description: The scene depicting the Coronation of the Virgin Mary with its plethora of figures was executed with little regard to viewing from below. Within a quatrefoil-shaped frame a series of picture levels are differentiated, ascending in sequence to the holy spirit in the form of a dove in an aureole, however this would also be clear when viewed frontally. In this case no effort has been made to create an impression of space or an imaginary heavenly opening when viewed from below using exaggerated perspective effects. Instead, traditional pictorial techniques have been employed.

c9e437ac-0abc-54f8-bdb1-c612628c79a0.name: Celebration of the Althann Dynasty
c9e437ac-0abc-54f8-bdb1-c612628c79a0.description: Illusionary elements of a balustrade and carpet provide a link between the earth and the celestial sphere. Ancient gods and allegorical figures show a path to honour and glory. The family’s celestial triumph is accompanied by scenes depicting aristocratic virtues. The major component is not stuccowork but painting, in contrast to more recent decorations. The fresco as one of the first pieces by an artist who later became famous.

c9e49af2-234e-5264-88ea-43e004a7108c.name: High altar
c9e49af2-234e-5264-88ea-43e004a7108c.description: The double altar, crowned by the dove of the Holy Spirit in a nimbus, provides both a Late Gothic miraculous image – a *pietà* – in its lower part and an altarpiece depicting the Assumption of the Virgin Mary in its upper part where both the Virgin’s suffering and triumph are evident. Slim columns connect the two levels.

ca4be14d-93e9-596d-b076-3472190bbd99.name: Left hand-side altar
ca4be14d-93e9-596d-b076-3472190bbd99.description: The left hand-side altar built after 1682 differs fundamentally from the other altars. Its superstructure forms a frame for the two inset paintings; the larger of the two, the actual altarpiece, is the work of Michael Waldmann from 1677 and depicts St. Anthony in front of the Infant Jesus with the portrait of the picture’s donor, the musician Karl Boussier from Innsbruck. The picture was brought to Landeck in 1682. Each side of the altar’s outer frame forms seven small niches with figures of the fourteen Holy Helpers, probably the work of Adam Payr.
ca4be14d-93e9-596d-b076-3472190bbd99.location: Northeast nave on the triumphal arch wall
ca4be14d-93e9-596d-b076-3472190bbd99.artist: Adam Payr (?–1682); Michael Waldmann the younger (1640–1682)

cb0bfb98-65d7-5e00-ac6e-f7448d4fefe4.name: Feudal Hall
cb0bfb98-65d7-5e00-ac6e-f7448d4fefe4.description: Following the fire of 1752, J. Stern decorated both library and chapel ceilings. The restoration of the Feudal Hall (Courtroom) took place in parallel; its decoration featuring key scenes from the history of the Olomouc bishopric and the apotheosis of the builder, Bishop Egkh. A virtuoso fresco with a striking colour scheme, it is considered one of the most impressive of its kind in Central Europe.
cb0bfb98-65d7-5e00-ac6e-f7448d4fefe4.artist: Franz Anton Maulbertsch (1724 Langenargen am Bodensee – 1796 Vienna), František Ondřej Hirnle (1726, Prague – 1774, Kroměříž)

cb4fde26-f723-5c3f-926c-8f4ec43eb1b2.name: Crucifix
cb4fde26-f723-5c3f-926c-8f4ec43eb1b2.description: A further special feature of the interior work is the so-called “Wundheiland” or “Tropfheiland”, an expressive “plague cross” suspended from the apex of the triumphal arch. The body is covered in wounds from which blood flows. The suffering Christ as the symbol of all pain and its overcoming is presented to the itinerant workers as a sign of consolation and warning.
cb4fde26-f723-5c3f-926c-8f4ec43eb1b2.location: Choir arch, Catholic Guild Church of St. Joseph

cb50ee45-d844-5c38-ae52-e6a8120cbd02.name: “Black Chapel”
cb50ee45-d844-5c38-ae52-e6a8120cbd02.description: F. A. Rottal had a memorial chapel with a family tomb added to the parish church. Life-size portraits of the investor and his wife adorn the side altars, presenting them as art-loving and pious aristocrats. Together with a relief of Christ on the Mount of Olives, they are considered some of the best work by Gottfried Fritsch, a pupil of G. Donner. At the death of F. A. Rottal, the family died out.

cb6a0376-8eca-5065-8e51-3daf911b8733.name: *Crowning of St. Gaetano and Flight of Satan*
cb6a0376-8eca-5065-8e51-3daf911b8733.description: Three angels lift a red drape showing the Glory of St. Gaetano, honoured by the Trinity thanks to the intercession of the Virgin. Some of the saints looking at the scene are arriving at the head of a procession exiting from the gates of Bologna. Opposite Satan is chased away.
cb6a0376-8eca-5065-8e51-3daf911b8733.location: Dome above the presbiterium, general view

cb712c93-18a3-58c8-9f29-cfea9d8f2763.name: *Mystical Supper of the Holy Family*
cb712c93-18a3-58c8-9f29-cfea9d8f2763.description:
Inscription on the bottom right-hand side:  
*Facta a Fr. Serafino Schön O.M.S. franc. Croatiae Carnioliae An. 1640. Refacta vero a DD. Josepho Candito Italo Neapolitano et Georgio Esperlinn Germano Helveto anno 1777. Mense Augusto.* (Painted by the Franciscan lay brother Seraphin Schön in August 1777; repaired by Italian Joseph (Giuseppe) Candito and German-Swiss Georgio Esperlinn).  
The theme of the painting is the Sacrifice of Christ presented in a tripartite composition in which the central part belongs to the quiet meal of the Holy Family. The food they are eating has a symbolic meaning. On the left, another set table symbolises Christ's Passion carefully arranged by angels and archangels led by St. Michael. On the right-hand side, two large angels are frying fish, while the two small ones are playing with birds, making clear that this painting belongs to the Franciscan Order.
cb712c93-18a3-58c8-9f29-cfea9d8f2763.location: Summer Refectory, west wall, Franciscan Church and Monastery of Our Lady of Trsat

cc396419-f1b0-581a-b241-9a82f942b0ab.name: Main Altar Altarpiece
cc396419-f1b0-581a-b241-9a82f942b0ab.description: Late Baroque gilt wood carved altarpiece.
cc396419-f1b0-581a-b241-9a82f942b0ab.artist: Luís Pereira da Costa (active 1724–?), João Lopes da Maia [n.d.], Domingos Martins Moreira (active 1746–1750)

cc3aa5b9-a146-5ee6-b9a4-5560a9f85e69.name: Altar of the Virgin Mary (high altar)
cc3aa5b9-a146-5ee6-b9a4-5560a9f85e69.description: The high altar, designed by Hans Krumpper, is an early example of a combined retable and tabernacle – the latter manufactured on the explicit demand of the Prince-Bishop by Philipp Dirr. The Rubens’ altarpiece is a replica (the original has been conserved in Munich since 1927). It shows the “Madonna on the Crescent Moon” with the archangel Michael triumphant over evil, especially paganism.
cc3aa5b9-a146-5ee6-b9a4-5560a9f85e69.artist: Hans Krumpper (c. 1570–1634); Philipp Dirr (c. 1582–1633); Pieter Paul Rubens (1577–1640)

cc3d0593-4799-50e0-9f3d-44bc2af39e0e.name: Staircase
cc3d0593-4799-50e0-9f3d-44bc2af39e0e.description: The Imperial-style staircase has three flights. It bears characteristics typical of the 1780s, consisting of superimposed columns, strips and cornices originally painted in a marble paint finish, while the railing has a decorative motif of a square meander, which also points to the Early Classical language of architecture.
cc3d0593-4799-50e0-9f3d-44bc2af39e0e.location: Central area (opposite the entrance hall), Palace of the Sugar Refinery

ce3032c2-5138-591d-bcc6-d2a6badb1886.name: Allegorical Sculptures
ce3032c2-5138-591d-bcc6-d2a6badb1886.description: Along the intermediate terrace are allegorical sculptures identified with captions. Around the main lake are the Three Theological Virtues: Hope, Faith and Charity, and the Four Cardinal Virtues: Justice, Fortitude, Temperance and Prudence.

ce3e1a26-65b3-5643-a5eb-b18a3b8d53e4.name: Assumption of Mary
ce3e1a26-65b3-5643-a5eb-b18a3b8d53e4.description: Upon electoral request, the altarpiece of the once Early Baroque high altar depicts the Assumption of Mary according to the saint’s patronage of the church. The Munich painter portrayed himself as the apostle Johannes looking out of the painting. Theme and composition follow a copperplate depiction of the high altarpiece of Peter Paul Rubens in the Cathedral of Antwerp.

ce8830d8-b822-5a73-b84f-3d1865e4c511.name: Workshops and houses for craftsmen
ce8830d8-b822-5a73-b84f-3d1865e4c511.description: The narrow streets of the hamlet with houses on both sides remind the urban structure of the medieval town of Bologna.

cee30618-4395-58d9-9364-6ae0526dbf95.name: Church of St. Margaret
cee30618-4395-58d9-9364-6ae0526dbf95.description: The church, with an oval nave, presbytery and vestibule, is 20.2 m long, 14.8 m wide and 44 m high. Its fresco decoration is the apotheosis of St. Margaret. She is accompanied by two angels, crypto-portraits of the investor and his wife, Marie Antonie of Friedberg–Scheer. The nave contains six side altars. The two front altars feature reliquaries of two young martyrs, Saints Vincent and Reparata, presented by Pope Innocent XII to the count during his journey to Rome. The church joined the chateau and the area below it. The concept is not only of architectural importance but also manifests the connection between the sovereign and the people, considered an aspect of “beneficent reign”.
cee30618-4395-58d9-9364-6ae0526dbf95.artist: Johann Lucas von Hildebrandt (1668 Genoa – 1745 Vienna), František Antonín Findt, Karel František Tepper (1682–1738), Kaspar Ober

cf22d135-ac5c-5d43-9ae5-2d9a94f522fa.name: Detail of interior
cf22d135-ac5c-5d43-9ae5-2d9a94f522fa.description:
Detail of the magnificent inlaid marble work on the walls, dome and floor, remarkable for its precocious use of marble inlaid with white and other colours.  
The 18th-century organ with carved gilt wood casing was made by the Portuguese school of Joaquim António Peres Fontanes.
cf22d135-ac5c-5d43-9ae5-2d9a94f522fa.artist:
João Antunes (1643–1712)  
Organ: Joaquim António Peres Fontanes \[n.d.\]

cf7f7c95-7ab3-53df-bee6-0f5d4ff05dea.name: St. John the Evangelist
cf7f7c95-7ab3-53df-bee6-0f5d4ff05dea.description: The flowing gown accentuates the spiral movement of the figure and its volume. Attributes, such as a book and an eagle (the right hand lacks a quill, probably lost), spread the matter of the statue into space. The straightened shapes and angular folds of the gown bear witness of the influence of O. Zahner, with whom Kammereit, son-in-law of the artist J. K. Handke, collaborated several times.

cfc8b095-24f6-594f-a08a-a320412bd52e.name: Interior of the church
cfc8b095-24f6-594f-a08a-a320412bd52e.description: The interior is a perfect blend of different arts and techniques. The colours of the frescoes harmonise perfectly with the white and gold stucco decorations and with the soft light coming from the windows.

cfe4e76b-dae8-5b07-88b5-6d61d4cac871.name: Relic chapel
cfe4e76b-dae8-5b07-88b5-6d61d4cac871.description: What is commonly known as the *Achbergkapelle* (Relic Chapel), so-called due to a miraculous sculptured image of the Virgin Mary, contains a splendid stucco marble altar wall with integrated relic shrines and atmospheric Neapolitan-influenced oil paintings on the ceiling depicting the Life of Christ.
cfe4e76b-dae8-5b07-88b5-6d61d4cac871.location: Ground floor of the choir, to the right of the presbytery, Augustinian Canons’ Convent of the Holy Saviour

cffaa59d-b1cb-5e23-8802-313d1d732a07.name: Gilded wood, carved retable
cffaa59d-b1cb-5e23-8802-313d1d732a07.description: This 17th-century retable is considered to be one of the most remarkable Jesuit examples in Portugal.
cffaa59d-b1cb-5e23-8802-313d1d732a07.artist: Attributed to the workshop of Manuel Pereira (active 1648–1660)

cffb34f2-f0c0-53a2-a788-0817dd101e89.name: Fresco
cffb34f2-f0c0-53a2-a788-0817dd101e89.description: Mölck’s ceiling paintings depicting scenes from the life of Mary in large panels are integrated in an ornamental system of decoration which partly replaces and partly extends the stucco (of Simon Wachter). The large choir fresco depicts the acceptance of Mary into heaven, echoing the picture of the Assumption of the high altar.

d0ab1550-cbd5-5935-b8c4-fe0633742da9.name: Neptune Fountain
d0ab1550-cbd5-5935-b8c4-fe0633742da9.description: The Neptune Fountain is perhaps one of the most remarkable pieces of 17th-century Baroque stonework in Portugal. Originating during the period of the Castelo Melhor, the fountain was commissioned in Rome shortly after 1675 , 1675 by Luis de Meneses, Count of Ericeira and Portuguese Ambassador in Rome, and made specifically for his Lisbon palace of Anunciada where it was installed in the gardens. After the earthquake of 1755, the fountain fell into the hands of other owners and ended up in several different locations. It was finally purchased by the state and placed in the gardens of Queluz in the first half of the 20th century. Today we know it was probably commissioned from Gian Lorenzo Bernini (the *“vernino*” as he is referred to in Portuguese documentation) who delegated work on it to Ercole Ferrata.

d0dcd65e-a0b7-5d6e-a06f-2003e1ddadea.name: Ceiling fresco
d0dcd65e-a0b7-5d6e-a06f-2003e1ddadea.description: The painting of the great oval choir cupola represents an important step in the development of Baroque fresco painting in the Tyrol. The heaven of the saints of the Augustinians, with the order’s members and saints venerating the Holy Trinity, has been executed as a pure figure composition and thus establishes a link to the form of cupola painting founded by Corregio in Parma designed for viewing from below. Painted architecture is completely absent.

d1138bd2-9ece-57a8-a87f-358caf766c14.name: *Azulejos*
d1138bd2-9ece-57a8-a87f-358caf766c14.description: *Azulejos* illustrating the story of Joseph in Egypt captioned in Latin. At the bottom of each panel the Miracles of S. Gonçalo of Amarante are represented.
d1138bd2-9ece-57a8-a87f-358caf766c14.location: Four *Azulejos* panels (two per side) line the lower register of the church walls, interrupted by the pulpit and stairs.
d1138bd2-9ece-57a8-a87f-358caf766c14.artist: Attributed to Teotónio dos Santos [n.d.], Lisbon tile production

d1c1eb40-6c20-5043-8872-8d70084736b5.name: *Pastoral theme*
d1c1eb40-6c20-5043-8872-8d70084736b5.location: Wall of the working cabinet, Ratkaj Palace

d2984278-366b-5283-9f1a-506cabf83a53.name: Façade and tower
d2984278-366b-5283-9f1a-506cabf83a53.description: Together with the west tower, the façade forms a delightful ensemble, a simplified version of the double-tower façade of Wilten parish church (since 1964 St. Jacob’s Cathedral). The few sculptural architectural elements – mouldings, tail gable and portal aedicule – are supplemented by painting and sculpture. The gable panel features an *Ecclesia triumphans*, painted by Günther, together with the church patrons in the niches of the façade wall from Schnegg (the triumphant Catholic Church, founded by Peter and Paul).
d2984278-366b-5283-9f1a-506cabf83a53.artist: Franz Singer (1724–1789); Johann Schnegg (1724–1784); Matthäus Günther (1705–1788)

d2a0bb6d-e271-5430-bd69-fba3a45eaf85.name:
Bronze Equestrian Statue of King José I  
(copper engraving by Carneiro da Silva made before the unveiling in 1774)
d2a0bb6d-e271-5430-bd69-fba3a45eaf85.description: The statue by Joaquim Machado de Castro was unveiled on 27 May 1775 on King José I’s birthday. The copper engraving by Joaquim Carneiro da Silva was made a year prior to this in 1774 to commemorate the unveiling. Other commemorative items include china decorated with reproductions of the statue.
d2a0bb6d-e271-5430-bd69-fba3a45eaf85.location: Terreiro do Paço (Palace Square) or Praça do Comércio (Commerce  Square)

d2a7f2b6-6580-5dae-8336-b155d38a911d.name: Interior, facing east
d2a7f2b6-6580-5dae-8336-b155d38a911d.description: The interior of the Burschlkirche is characterised by the contrast between plane architecture, employing an antiquated repertoire of forms, and the masterfully executed, rich ensemble of the three altars. The two-bay choir with a 3/6 termination in the continuation of the Gothic tradition is separated from the nave by a heavily tapered ogival triumphal arch. This in turn is a simple oblong hall which the panelled ceiling lends the character of a secular festive hall of the Renaissance period.

d2aaaa35-322e-55c8-aa9a-d4c8876f0303.name: Staircase
d2aaaa35-322e-55c8-aa9a-d4c8876f0303.description: The wide, double flight of stairs is the first monumental Baroque staircase in Innsbruck. From the vestibule on the ground floor it leads upwards to the first and second floors. The rich stucco ornamentation in the form of Baroque strapwork originates from Anton Gigl, Johann Singer, Paul Wachter and Andreas Gratl, the sculptures in the niches of the round arches on the second floor are from Nikolaus Moll (Apollo and Artemis) and Ingenium Lechleitner (busts of Zeus and Hera). On the ceiling in front of the parliament hall Lechleitner also depicted the map of Tyrol in stucco, supported by an eagle, the state’s heraldic animal.
d2aaaa35-322e-55c8-aa9a-d4c8876f0303.location: Main wing, connection between first and second floors
d2aaaa35-322e-55c8-aa9a-d4c8876f0303.artist: Georg Anton Gumpp (1682–1754); Nikolaus Moll (1676–1754); Ingenuin Lechleitner (1676–1731); Anton Gigl (1700–1769); Johann Singer [n.d.]

d2ac0900-9922-5fbf-886a-0210952ff6cd.name: High Altar
d2ac0900-9922-5fbf-886a-0210952ff6cd.description: Perceived as his most monumental work, it is characterised by a light architectural construction that comes out particularly in the concluding, weight-bearing elements where the altar wall is abandoned.
d2ac0900-9922-5fbf-886a-0210952ff6cd.location: Sanctuary, Parish Church of Our Lady of the Snow

d33bac06-e82c-5db0-b385-be388a6eeb7a.name: Tritons’ Fountain
d33bac06-e82c-5db0-b385-be388a6eeb7a.description: Václav Render, who also created several other fountains and columns, was an Olomouc burgher and stonemason, inspired by Bernini’s fountain in Rome. The Olomouc fountain represents the descendants and servants of Neptune, the ruler of the sea. Triton, half-man half-fish, son of Neptune and Amphitrite, would sound his conch if there was a storm at sea.The fountain may therefore symbolise a warning against the watery elements, far from unjustified in the vicinity of the mighty and unpredictable River Morava. The fountain originally dominated a crossroads.

d3bb32df-1032-585b-bb84-e5c3b1bb0836.name: *Immaculate Conception*
d3bb32df-1032-585b-bb84-e5c3b1bb0836.location: Ceiling painting in the sanctuary, Votive church of St. Mary of Jerusalem, Trški Vrh, near Krapina

d3d037ed-e8e5-5ff3-85c2-555bbabfcf8d.name: New Festival Hall (Princely Hall; now the convent chapel of the Salesian monastery)
d3d037ed-e8e5-5ff3-85c2-555bbabfcf8d.description: The Festival Hall, ideally conceptualised for the reception of Bavarian electoral princes as sovereigns, is decorated in the courtly Régence style. The central ceiling painting illustrates the establishment of the abbey as if it occurred in the present day at the time. This reinforces the ambivalent relationship between monastic allegiance and welfare provided by the sovereign.
d3d037ed-e8e5-5ff3-85c2-555bbabfcf8d.location: First floor in the south wing of the arcade court
d3d037ed-e8e5-5ff3-85c2-555bbabfcf8d.artist: Stucco and frescoes: Johann Baptist (1680–1758) and Johann Joseph (1707–43) Zimmermann

d40aa2ad-09f7-51fd-ae9a-a8ee9cc91264.name: Altar of St. Stephen (high altar)
d40aa2ad-09f7-51fd-ae9a-a8ee9cc91264.description: The high altar with its column superstructure, curved entablature and towering, gilded altar crown, forms the magnificent focal point of the enfilade. The altarpiece depicts the decisive event in the life of the church patron, the stoning of St. Stephen. In the moment of his death St. Stephen sees the heavens open. Thus the scene forms part of the pictorial programme continued in the ceiling frescos, while illustrating the function of the saint as mediator between heaven and earth, analogue to the Eucharist sacrament.

d41d9ab1-acd5-514f-884e-67ecf8eccd1a.name: Interior of the church of St. John the Baptist
d41d9ab1-acd5-514f-884e-67ecf8eccd1a.description: The church has a very simple plan with a main chapel and two side ones that convey the impression of a wide, central space.

d487f118-f333-59e5-a4ba-127152098431.name: The former summer refectory, today: Minoritensaal (Minorites' hall)
d487f118-f333-59e5-a4ba-127152098431.description:
The former summer refectory´s one and a half storey aisle was built by Joachim Carlone. He crowned the windows in the main floor with alternating segmental and triangular gables as it was done by Bramante at a church´s façade in Todi (near Perugia). Climbing up the staircase with stone balustrade and putti one reaches the hall, nowadays called Minoritensaal.  
The excellent stucco work from the end of the 17th century is reminiscent of Joseph Antonio Serenio´s style. The fresco paintings by Antonio Maderni represent the Holy Virgin worshipped by the nine angel choirs. On the South wall there is a huge interestingly T-shaped painting: the Miraculous Multiplication of the Loaf by Johannes Baptist Raunacher. The painters of the paintings at both long sides of the hall remain anonymous. They represent Franciscan and Dominican saints, such as St Anthony of Padua during the vision of the Blessed Virgin.
d487f118-f333-59e5-a4ba-127152098431.dates: From 1691 construction of the former summer refectory, the so-called Minoritensaal; from 1697 ceiling stucco decoration; 1702 ceiling fresco paintings; 1732 painting of the Miraculous Multiplication of the Loaf and completion of the summer refectory´s int
d487f118-f333-59e5-a4ba-127152098431.location: Part of the monastery building in the West of the church
d487f118-f333-59e5-a4ba-127152098431.artist: Former summer refectory, today Minoritensaal: architecture: Joachim Carlone; ceiling stucco: in the style of Joseph Antonio Serenio; fresco paintings: Antonio Maderni; painting The Miraculous Multiplication of the Loaf: Johann Baptist Raunacher

d48c2807-4183-5a04-813a-e3b0c161d099.name: Altar of St. Anton of Padua
d48c2807-4183-5a04-813a-e3b0c161d099.location: Nave (south wall), Church of St. George in Purga Lepoglavska

d4c28ae8-32bb-5728-b823-2fbca193bbeb.name: The Tree-of-Jesse Monstrance
d4c28ae8-32bb-5728-b823-2fbca193bbeb.description: The masterpiece of a local goldsmith features busts within a 122cm tall arabesque depicting Christ's family tree growing from Jesse. Christ’s body is present as the consecrated host in an ostensory which is fitted in St Mary’s lap.

d51ec020-734f-58d3-8f56-248b568ae3b8.name: Monumental gallery, vault decoration with episodes of the history of the Aldrovandi Family (“I fasti degli Aldrovandi”)
d51ec020-734f-58d3-8f56-248b568ae3b8.description: The subjects chosen by Pompeo for the decoration of the ceiling are related to the lives of his ancestors Nicolò, Giovanni Francesco, Pietro and Ulisse. Two of them represent episodes of the Cardinal’s own life.
d51ec020-734f-58d3-8f56-248b568ae3b8.location: Interior, first floor, palazzo Aldrovandi Montanari
d51ec020-734f-58d3-8f56-248b568ae3b8.artist: Vittorio Maria Bigari and Stefano Orlandi

d554971f-f508-52e4-999c-e09207ee45b2.name: Ceiling of the Galleria del Senato
d554971f-f508-52e4-999c-e09207ee45b2.description: The personification of Bologna is standing on a chariot pulled by two lions, which symbolize the power of the City. She is guided by Cybele, the goddess of nature, to the glory of Olympus, where Jupiter welcomes her.

d57919ad-92e5-5973-9707-042b48266da3.name: Mercury
d57919ad-92e5-5973-9707-042b48266da3.description: The chateau frontage is segmented by windows and niches with statues – allegories of the seasons and figures of ancient gods.
d57919ad-92e5-5973-9707-042b48266da3.artist: Jan Jirí Schauberger (? before 1725 Vienna, active in Olomouc – 1744 Brno)

d580e261-d346-5245-927b-14f58847eed8.name: Interior
d580e261-d346-5245-927b-14f58847eed8.description: The overall impression generated by the building’s interior, in fact merely a domed transept square with slanting piers and four barrel-vaulted cross arms, is surprisingly rich. Thanks to the painting, which also includes illusionistic stucco on all the framing, Penz’s clear, well proportioned spatial structure acquires an intricate and appealing character. Architecture and painting thus fuse to form a unity of intricate detail and systematic architectural stringency.
d580e261-d346-5245-927b-14f58847eed8.location: Interior facing south (in the direction of the choir)
d580e261-d346-5245-927b-14f58847eed8.artist: Franz de Paula Penz (1707–1772); Christoph Anton Mayr (c. 1720–1771)

d5bb0a84-dc09-524d-955d-6f8930019c18.name: Chapel
d5bb0a84-dc09-524d-955d-6f8930019c18.description: The fresco of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary is one of the lesser-known works of renowned Viennese master, Mildorfer. A sketch for the painting is preserved in the Reuschel Collection in Munich. Cartouches contain *putti* with symbols of St. John of Nepomuk.

d5cd6b83-9aac-5c7c-a74a-83cd7db62062.name: The former summer refectory´s staircase
d5cd6b83-9aac-5c7c-a74a-83cd7db62062.description:
The former summer refectory´s staircase is an interesting part of the building complex. The Minorites are a mendicant order, their monks have always stuck to strict rules, concerning life and architecture. Facades were meant to be simple, buildings should be purposeful and not pompous. Nevertheless, there is a magnificent staircase such as those in princely residences. The one and only answer why it is there, must be that it was Prince Johann Seyfried of Eggenberg’s idea. He was used to having representative staircases in his residences and gave the Minorites one as he gave the whole building complex.  
Via the staircase with stone balustrade, putti and a railing made of wrought iron on the gallery, one gets from the ground floor to the former summer refectory above. The fresco paintings on the ceiling represent the life of St Francis of Assisi. Pope Clemens XIV can be seen on a portrait on the North wall while a frameless portrait of the donor, Prince Johann Seyfried von Eggenberg, crowns the hall´s entrance. He is represented with models of the former summer refectory and his summer palace Schloss Eggenberg, then outside Graz.
d5cd6b83-9aac-5c7c-a74a-83cd7db62062.dates: From 1691 construction; end of the 17th century ceiling stucco; beginning of the 18th century ceiling fresco paintings; 1703 portrait of Prince Johann Seyfried von Eggenberg; about 1715/20 putti
d5cd6b83-9aac-5c7c-a74a-83cd7db62062.location: In the North of the building complex
d5cd6b83-9aac-5c7c-a74a-83cd7db62062.artist: Architecture: Joachim Carlone; ceiling stucco: in the style of Joseph Antonio Serenio; ceiling fresco paintings: in the style of Antonio Maderni; anonymous: portrait of Prince Johann Seyfried von Eggenberg; putti: in the style of Johann Jakob Schoy

d5e8c54b-73a6-5832-bef5-a3fcec29071a.name: Crucifixion
d5e8c54b-73a6-5832-bef5-a3fcec29071a.description: This Crucifixion with the deposition from the cross and the fading Madonna on the lower right is clearly the work of Lucio Massari (1569–1633). This painter has been considered for a long time a mediocre artist. Today we tend to appreciate his luminous palette and the style, reminiscent of Annibale Carracci. After the restorations of 2000 the soldiers playing dice on Jesus’ clothes became visible again.
d5e8c54b-73a6-5832-bef5-a3fcec29071a.location: Oratory of the Madonna dell’Orazione, entrance wall

d6106d67-8053-5953-b8d3-21dcd5e36a0d.name: Mãe d’ Água das Amoreiras reservoir
d6106d67-8053-5953-b8d3-21dcd5e36a0d.description: Mãe d' Água das Amoreiras reservoir was designed by Carlos Mardel. Due to its monumentality, the Mãe d'Água constitutes a true civic temple to the *águas livres* (free waters). An antechamber precedes the vast rectangle which contains a deep reservoir.

d6131cce-c6f1-5f7e-be6f-984c9b39096b.name: Apotheosis of St. John Sarkander
d6131cce-c6f1-5f7e-be6f-984c9b39096b.description: St. John Sarkander Moravian was a martyr worshipped by the demesne owners, the Kuefstein family. The bridge was a project that would “express their thanks to the Almighty and to celebrate His name always and everywhere”. The picture comes from the side altar in the Chapel of St. Anne, in an infirmary (1743–1745) established as a home for the elderly servants and subjects of the Námešť demesne. A parsonage constructed in parallel was decorated by J. Winterhalder Sr. and K. J. Aigen. The artist P. Troger took part in the decoration of the adjacent church. He was probably introduced to the count – that he had painted a tomb in Röhrenbach for in 1737 – by his friend Winterhalder.
d6131cce-c6f1-5f7e-be6f-984c9b39096b.location: Náměšť nad Oslavou, St. Anne Chapel

d66a89c1-4e7d-50bb-8edb-6b7c02fa1341.name: Pulpit
d66a89c1-4e7d-50bb-8edb-6b7c02fa1341.description: On the corners of the pulpit set on pillars, the figures of the evangelists are shown in high-spirited movement; between them, also plastically very highly emphasised, are *rocaille* cartouches with reliefs in which the central figure is Moses: *Moses Dancing Around the Golden Calf, Moses Receives the Law, Moses and the Bronze Serpent*. Monumentality and dynamism are the main features of the sculptural composition at the top of the baldachin too, showing the *Transfiguration of Christ on Mount Tabor*, the scene enriched with figures of the Prophets *Moses* and *Elijah* either side.
d66a89c1-4e7d-50bb-8edb-6b7c02fa1341.location: North wall of the church, Parish Church of Our Lady of the Snow

d67fc781-3f54-55c3-84af-e3c9847918be.name: Pier arcades and aisle
d67fc781-3f54-55c3-84af-e3c9847918be.description: The arrangement of large columns in the main space corresponds to pilaster-type constructions in longitudinal buildings. The edges are occupied by pilasters supporting a powerful entablature bent at right angles. The vault arches ascend above an attic zone and mark the ends of the barrel-vaulted aisles. The rear wall with a large, round arched window functions solely as a panel wall without architectural structure. Pilasters and vault arches generate eight fully formed arcades which encircle the central space like a crown, opening up on all sides like gateways.
d67fc781-3f54-55c3-84af-e3c9847918be.location: Main room, view into the aisle

d6a6bbee-1004-5fe5-93a3-c845fe7b8380.name: Library
d6a6bbee-1004-5fe5-93a3-c845fe7b8380.description:
A significant Enlightenment Library with around 36,000 volumes amassed through royal commission. It has a cruciform layout with a multi-coloured limestone floor and Rocaille shelves.  
Some rare works furnish its shelves to this day: the *Nuremberg Chronicle* (1493) or the *Theatrvm Orbis Terrarvm* by Ortelius (1595) and a nucleus of scores from musicians such as João de Sousa Carvalho or Marcos Portugal, composed expressly to be played on the Basilica's six organs.

d6a7f708-c180-5d4e-8436-b72c783cd20a.name: Virtues and Praise of God
d6a7f708-c180-5d4e-8436-b72c783cd20a.description: Allegorical representations are mounted on the elegantly curved balustrades of the two-storey gallery. On the first floor, reserved for the faithful, the cardinal virtues of wisdom, temperance, courage and justice are shown as aspects of an allegory of the church, complemented by faith, love and hope on the underside of the gallery. The pictorial theme of the upper storey, appropriately as an organ gallery, refers to the praise of God by angels making music. As part of the ceiling frescoes, the context includes St. Cecelia, King David and the Prophet Jeremiah.

d6b2cb6a-1495-5fd3-9836-145bd04a8474.name: Frescos and stucco
d6b2cb6a-1495-5fd3-9836-145bd04a8474.description: The High Baroque interior work significantly changed the original spatial impression. In the vault the bay borders were masked with overlapping stucco and the introduction of colourful ceiling pictures in small panels provided a contrast to the Early Baroque colour scheme of white, gold and black. The vault’s heavenly zone is characterised by stucco putti, garlands of fruit and acanthus vine, the series of pictures depict, amongst other things, scenes from the life of the Virgin Mary (choir) and the Church patrons (nave).

d6d9c08d-bc42-54cc-90c2-ca572c64044c.name: Svatý Kopeček (Holy Hill)
d6d9c08d-bc42-54cc-90c2-ca572c64044c.description: Part of Cardinal Dietrichstein’s Counter-Reformation strategy was the construction of the Church of St. Sebastian on Tanzberg Hill. This pilgrimage church, with 13 chapels of the Stations of the Cross, was intended to turn a rocky hill, redolent with pagan legend, into a “Holy Mount” modelled on Varallo in northern Italy. The original church (G. G. Tencalla) was re-established after 1663 and in 18th and 19th centuries.

d6e25877-b660-5efc-8f7a-d50ee03a2ca2.name: Church (architecture and interior)
d6e25877-b660-5efc-8f7a-d50ee03a2ca2.description:
Baroque started in Rein with the baroquization of the tower, then part of the Romanesque church. Architectonically it was never a tower itself as Cistercians were only allowed to have roof turrets. It is superimposed upon two naves’ walls and has no substructure. During the early Baroque era the winter church with rich stucco decoration was attached to the church whose baroquization started sixty years later. Architect Johann Georg Stengg was commissioned with the planning and the building. The forth- and back-swinging façade was like many others in this epoch influenced by Francesco Borromini´s church San Carlo alle Quattro Fontane in Rome. It is vertically decorated with statues, mighty columns, strongly protruding capitals and delicate stucco frames. Horizontally the façade is structured in a pedestal zone and a one and a half column storey. This zone is separated by a curved architrave from the (third) Attica zone with the protruding so-called hornwork. It looks like the pipes of an organ but reproduced only one chord.  
Going inside the church one is in the dark Romanesque entrance hall, the former sanctuary, with the baroque organ gallery above it. Both open to the wide and bright nave and presbytery, completely covered with fresco paintings by Joseph Adam von Mölck. The illusionistic architecture has its origin in Andrea Pozzo´s *Perspectiva pictorum et architectorum,* an instruction manual for painters. The high altar with columns and statues fills the width of the choir. The painting, an adoration of the shepherds, was originally made for another church. In 1819 it replaced the original painting representing the Assumption of the Holy Virgin.
d6e25877-b660-5efc-8f7a-d50ee03a2ca2.dates: 1650: replacing the Medieval tower (above the Southern/left part of the church) with an early baroque one; 1682: stucco decoration in the Old Sacristy (winter chapel); 1739–47: church building, structural changes and baroquization; 1742–47: church´s façad
d6e25877-b660-5efc-8f7a-d50ee03a2ca2.location: In the Northwest of the monastery complex, the church's main façade is in the great court.
d6e25877-b660-5efc-8f7a-d50ee03a2ca2.artist: Architecture: façade, baroquization of the tower and of the Gothic church: Johann Georg Stengg; statues at the façade: Johann Matthias Leitner Interior: walls´ and ceiling´s fresco paintings: Joseph Adam von Mölck; painting at the high altar: Martin Johann Schmidt; statutes at the high altar: Jakob Payer Marienkapelle/Lady Chapel (former sacristy, winter church): stucco decoration: attributed to Alexander Serenio

d721d07e-af8d-5c90-a2d1-60b3a0ac2fd3.name: Altar of the Holy Kinship
d721d07e-af8d-5c90-a2d1-60b3a0ac2fd3.description: The Altar of the Holy Family (or more broadly the Holy Kinship), with its altarpiece, is a reference to the Bavarian dynasty and the future of Christian Bavaria. The theme of the Annunciation of the Virgin is carried through in the imagery of the altar; the painting, the figures of saints either side, and the predella panel at the bottom. The altar can be seen therefore to indicate the birth of the Crown Prince and reiterate the dedicational background of the church. At one time the altarpiece in the choir (now destroyed) also picked up on this votive purpose.

d7d09131-18f8-5efb-b8f0-72baf37a8096.name: Interior
d7d09131-18f8-5efb-b8f0-72baf37a8096.description: The special feature of the three-bayed pilaster hall with barrel vault is the double-layered construction of the three-storey wall with narrow circumferential choir lofts and a powerful denticular cornice at the foot of the vault. The wall piers are faced with double pilasters. The Baroque interior thus acquires a strictly organised wall arrangement. The crossing is of the St. Peter’s type with tapered piers supporting the cupola.
d7d09131-18f8-5efb-b8f0-72baf37a8096.location: View through the nave from the west

d8289a89-1170-5ec0-a741-c5175017f870.name: Chapel of the Holy Trinity
d8289a89-1170-5ec0-a741-c5175017f870.description: This chateau chapel, with a subterranean family tomb, is a conceptual and compositional counterpart to the Hall of the Ancestors. The cylindrical central nave, with six oval apses around the perimeter, is decorated with paintings – the Last Judgment, Heaven and Paradise – drawing attention to the ephemeral nature of existence, the end of human life and its continuation in eternity. The cupola fresco represents the Archangel Michael, the family’s patron saint and protector of the Church.
d8289a89-1170-5ec0-a741-c5175017f870.artist: Johann Bernhard Fischer von Erlach (1656 Graz – 1723 Vienna), Ignaz Heinitz of Heintzenthal (1657–1742, Vienna)

d874eff0-55c2-5243-9c49-5d45221a42f9.name: *St. Paul in Ephesus burns the books of magic*
d874eff0-55c2-5243-9c49-5d45221a42f9.description: In Ephesus there was a famous shrine dedicated to the pagan goddess Arthemis. When St. Paul arrived in Ephesus, he decided to stop there for three years, but his words sent him to prison.
d874eff0-55c2-5243-9c49-5d45221a42f9.location: Right transept, San Paolo Maggiore, Bologna

d8c1fd87-1ac6-5fe2-b25b-54927d0e8b27.name: Ecce Homo (“day’s work” or *giornata* of the presbytery fresco)
d8c1fd87-1ac6-5fe2-b25b-54927d0e8b27.description: The Ecce Homo group over the high altar with the statue of the Scourged Christ represents Jesus as the victor over earthly tribulations. The contours outline the “day's work” – *giornata –* showing individual phases of the painting for which fresh plaster had to be applied and into which the artist could paint for up to three days. The sections also show the division of labour between the artist of the illusionary architecture and the painter of the figures.
d8c1fd87-1ac6-5fe2-b25b-54927d0e8b27.location: Pilgrimage Church of the Scourged Saviour, Dyje
d8c1fd87-1ac6-5fe2-b25b-54927d0e8b27.artist: Franz Anton Maulbertsch (1724 Langenargen am Bodensee – 1796 Vienna) and associates

d8eb5e02-b29c-5131-ae4d-9d51da74a14f.name: *St. Charles Borromeo*, *St. Roch*, *St Francis Xavier* and *St. John Nepomuk* (detail)

d91086bf-1c10-54ef-9ee9-fd787e402072.name: Pagan gods
d91086bf-1c10-54ef-9ee9-fd787e402072.description: Although these are reminiscent of antique statues, the gods fit perfectly in the illusionistic architecture, painted by the artist to create artificial effects in order to amaze the visitors.

d91846ba-1200-5b0a-820b-a4e5e1687ce1.name: *Ensemble d’époque*: Kitchen
d91846ba-1200-5b0a-820b-a4e5e1687ce1.description: Re-creation of an 18th-century kitchen set up in what was the original palace kitchen. Lined with *azulejos* (tile panels) of random figures alluding to culinary themes (for example, a bad cook and hanging game), it is equipped with a wide-mouthed chimney, stone tables and contemporary kitchen utensils.

d982fe8c-5b31-5e71-98c1-24e9b98b2b9a.name: Light-bearer
d982fe8c-5b31-5e71-98c1-24e9b98b2b9a.description: Light played a major role in Baroque iconography as a symbol of the Holy Spirit and was synonymous with holiness. Angels, the mediators of God's Will, are represented on the bottom balustrade of the staircase as decorative *putti*, messengers and guardians of the light.
d982fe8c-5b31-5e71-98c1-24e9b98b2b9a.artist: Ondřej Zahner (1709 Ettershausen – 1752 Olomouc) and workshop

d996062b-2320-5362-a028-3354728f180e.name: The Mercy Seat
d996062b-2320-5362-a028-3354728f180e.description: Four winding columns, deliberately imitating the ciborium of St. Peter’s Basilica in Rome, form a pictorial space in front of the upper high altar. There, instead of the modern glory window, a relief of the church’s patron once hung. It is into this space that the Holy Trinity seems to descend in the company of angels. This array of sculptures follows the iconography of the Mercy Seat: God the Father is shown presenting His crucified Son. Moreover, the papal crown that He is wearing, together with the winding columns, symbolizes the Catholic Church’s claim to religious leadership.

d9b298ce-e8bd-5aff-a2be-6532a7d43266.name: Stucco
d9b298ce-e8bd-5aff-a2be-6532a7d43266.description: The bold foliage stucco with long acanthus vines, often highly delicate and filigree is a work of Paolo d’Allo, who was a relative of Diego Francesco Carlone. He worked as part of Carlone’s retinue in southern Germany and Austria.

d9ce9f71-0281-5cf2-8079-e3f3766d7daa.name: Altar of the Cross (High Altar)
d9ce9f71-0281-5cf2-8079-e3f3766d7daa.description: The elegant high altar of Augsburg origin contains a three-dimensional representation of the crucifixion of Christ with the Virgin Mary and John instead of an altarpiece. Since it is usually portrayed in the altarpiece, the martyrdom of the church patrons Gordian and Epimachus already depicted in the ceiling frescoes gives way for the “original” martyr Christ, in whose succession the two saints, present at the side in the form of statues, stand with their work and death.

d9da836f-3e6b-5c2a-b9e8-6a9d2289580c.name: Main façade
d9da836f-3e6b-5c2a-b9e8-6a9d2289580c.description: The façade facing Maria-Theresien-Straße forms the buildings’ main, monumental visible side. Modelled on the scheme of the Palazzo Chigi Odescalchi in Rome, only the central projection is distinguished by colossal pilasters, a massive temple-like front elevated above the rusticated ground floor. The central projection is extended by a mezzanine storey and flanked by three-storey sections whose horizontal plane is augmented by powerful mouldings. The central Borrominian window enriches the austere, massive design with flowing forms. The design of the façade clearly expresses combativeness and sovereign dignity.

da426277-fa80-5d6b-bf9e-deb7c0f1f1c4.name: Detail of the alcove, putto
da426277-fa80-5d6b-bf9e-deb7c0f1f1c4.description:
It was probably realised after 1704, surely before 1739, when it is mentioned in a biography dedicated to its author, the sculptor Giuseppe Mazza, here working together with the painter Ercole Graziani senior.  
Coming back from Venice, the artist was probably engaged by the Zaniboni family, owner of the palace, to create this superb nuptial bedroom lavishly decorated with stuccoes and sculptures (among them *Venus* and *Apollo,* allusive to abundance and fertility); every element contributes here to a very dynamic composition inspired by typically baroque concepts.

da692340-65dd-57c1-b904-cdc5e0421125.name: High altar
da692340-65dd-57c1-b904-cdc5e0421125.description: Occupying the whole width and height of the concluding wall of the sanctuary, the altar fits very successfully into the highly articulated setting of the Gothic sanctuary with Ranger’s Baroque painting. Through the choice of an altar design with marked architectural features – with fluted columns repeated in the forms of the tabernacle – a monumental unit was created revealing obvious Classicist tendencies. There is a depiction of the Virgin of Częstocowa, the patron saint of the Paulists, in the central intercolumniation and four figures of the Fathers of the Church in more than life size in the lower part of the altar. In the gable, there is a figure of God the Father in a gloriole interwoven with clouds and angels.

da6bb370-648e-50af-8a64-8954bf78f1e2.name: Exterior
da6bb370-648e-50af-8a64-8954bf78f1e2.description: The design of the exterior is ambitious and rich in forms. The entrance side is distinguished by a single-tower façade whose main storey is framed by massive double pilasters, between which there is a portal surmounted by a window, both in curved forms. This arrangement of windows and pilasters is repeated throughout the entire building exterior. The combination of cupola with skylight turret and the onion tower form a charming ensemble, even when viewed from afar.

da8631fc-2904-5fa9-8e88-60dc987c0a59.name: *St. Francis Xavier* (detail)
da8631fc-2904-5fa9-8e88-60dc987c0a59.location: Upper inner rim of the monument

dacfc5e3-35c3-5c79-b422-4ca07ca8248a.name: Illusionistic dome
dacfc5e3-35c3-5c79-b422-4ca07ca8248a.location: Nave ceiling, Church of St. George in Purga Lepoglavska

db34ddd0-baae-5ed6-b464-91cb094254c6.name: Entrance portal
db34ddd0-baae-5ed6-b464-91cb094254c6.description: V. Render and his workshop executed all the stonemasonry for both the exterior and interior. Columns on pedestals bring an element of movement and suspense – rather rare in Moravian Baroque architecture – to the five-axis, undulating frontage, broken by windows and niches within which are statues of the saints (D. Zürn, 1720). The approach was part of a comprehensive iconographic programme for the university church. Columns in the frontage evoke the Temple of Solomon. Set in a cartouche is the Jesuit trigram: *IHS*, indicating also the coming of the Saviour. The principal element of the concept, synonymous with wisdom, is the union of the secular and spiritual, and its restoration after religious schisms.

dbaffd3f-8c80-55c5-8dff-c3db51a61236.name: Courtyard
dbaffd3f-8c80-55c5-8dff-c3db51a61236.description: Countess Marie Anna Pignatelli took up the reconstruction of the residence after 1722. She commissioned the court architect A. E. Martinelli to build a three-wing chateau, adjust the entrance bridge, parts of the castle front, and the chapel frontage and interior. The two-shouldered staircase of the ceremonial courtyard is set with sculptures of Hercules fighting Antaios and Aeneas Rescuing his Father, Anchises, from Burning Troy.

dbc2275f-b4d6-5495-9692-57254afc887e.name: Cupola
dbc2275f-b4d6-5495-9692-57254afc887e.description: The cupola is divided into six segments by stucco bands. The stuccowork was executed according to the designs of Hans Schor from Augsburg in around 1650. The austere arrangement with borders of bead moulding, in imitation of classical antiquity, is loosened by curved cartouches which frame the approximately vertical oval, i.e. round fresco panels above. The frescos, with their strong northern Italian influence, one of the earliest cycles of ceiling frescos in the whole of the southern German-speaking territories, depict the life of the Virgin Mary in the large panels, and in the small panels, primarily scenes from the Old Testament. The highly crowded scenes were conceived with little regard to viewing from below.
dbc2275f-b4d6-5495-9692-57254afc887e.dates: Stuccowork: c. 1650–1689, completion of the frescos

dbe72ec3-54b3-559a-ab0d-40fbc548afc5.name: Fresco paintings in the cupola and on the walls
dbe72ec3-54b3-559a-ab0d-40fbc548afc5.description:
The fresco paintings in the cupola and on the walls were done by Carlo Carlone (figures) and Francesco Messenta (illusionistic architecture) who created therewith a fantastic paradisiacal scenery.  
Looking upwards, through the illusionistic balustrade to the sky, one thinks one is standing in the courtyard of a baroque pavilion and watching a spectacle in Heaven. A myriad of blessed and angels worship the Holy Trinity, while there is a buzz of putti (little angels) in the centre and on top of the lantern marvelling at the dove with its aureole (= the Holy Spirit).  
Mighty illusionistic columns on the walls frame the altars. They are crowned with curved entablature and gable parts which look as if they are human beings and would like to break out. The indicated curvature alludes to the hemicycle of the altar niches. Above, there are cupolas with illusionistic architecture and circular balustrades through which one can see little angels in Heaven.
dbe72ec3-54b3-559a-ab0d-40fbc548afc5.location: In the dome and on the walls behind the altars

dcb4b1e9-8570-58ec-bfd9-2967dc807b70.name: Ballroom with frescoes
dcb4b1e9-8570-58ec-bfd9-2967dc807b70.description:
The most famous fresco of the palace is that of the ballroom located on the the first floor, it represents the *Apotheosis of Marescotti's family* and was painted  by Giuseppe and Antonio Rolli. It shows  Wisdom, with  Glory on her left,  holding up a pyramid. The circle on the pyramid symbolizes eternity. The main scene is surrounded by oval medaillons with allegorical figures of cities connected with the Marescottis (Bologna, Rome, Siena) and the personification of Scotland.  
The family portraits on the walls were painted in 1709 by Giovanni Battista Caccioli.
dcb4b1e9-8570-58ec-bfd9-2967dc807b70.location: Salone Marescotti, first floor, Palazzo Marescotti Brazzetti
dcb4b1e9-8570-58ec-bfd9-2967dc807b70.artist: Giuseppe Rolli; Antonio Rolli; Giovanni Battista Caccioli

dce2de76-9422-577c-8181-1a405908be1f.name: Main staircase
dce2de76-9422-577c-8181-1a405908be1f.description: Corresponding with its traditional role in court ceremonies, the staircase is central to the chateau. The architect supplied the drawings for the balustrade in 1729, at which time he was also working on the interior design.
dce2de76-9422-577c-8181-1a405908be1f.artist: Johann Lucas von Hildebrandt (1668 Genoa – 1745 Vienna)

dd9d98d4-ce14-5cb3-81aa-86c331412c4e.name: Altar of St. Frances Borgia
dd9d98d4-ce14-5cb3-81aa-86c331412c4e.description: The Altar of St. Francis Borgia is characterised by its conservative, two-storey architectural structure with symmetrically deployed statues. The caryatids of the bottom, the spiral columns, and the acanthus ornaments – which were actually first brought by Komersteiner to Zagreb and northern Croatia in the 1680s – introduce Baroque accents into the church. On the Altar of St. Franics Borgia, softly rounded acanthus leaves sparsely furnish the load-bearing areas and mouldings, more abundantly on the narrow wings. The design of the altarpiece is attributed to H. A. Weissenkircher.
dd9d98d4-ce14-5cb3-81aa-86c331412c4e.location: The first side chapel of St. Frances Borgia on the right-hand (south) side of the nave

ddbe9286-c279-56fc-8d46-01cf14d5ad37.name: The Chapel of St. John of Nepomuk
ddbe9286-c279-56fc-8d46-01cf14d5ad37.description: One of the two chapels to the side is dedicated to St. Johann of Nepomuk, the patron saint of the Mittenwald log drivers  on the Isar river. The fresco situated above the chapel’s vault depicts the resurrected martyr, who is crowned by five stars, floating above the Vltava river. A padlock, hanging on the left arm which is gripping a devotional cross, refers to his secrecy.
ddbe9286-c279-56fc-8d46-01cf14d5ad37.location: The southern alcove of the nave

ddf00c3a-e980-51f1-baa7-12826cbb65c4.name: *St. Anne with Saints and the Rovere Family*
ddf00c3a-e980-51f1-baa7-12826cbb65c4.description: The Virgin Mary with the Infant Jesus and St. Anne in the mid-ground of the composition form the characteristic motif known as "St Anne Selfthird" meaning St Anne with two others (in German, *Die heilige Anna selbdritt*), an iconographic convention that began in the 14th century. On the right-hand side of the composition are members of the Rovere family together with their saint-protectors. On the left-hand side, a Franciscan monk is seen in profile.
ddf00c3a-e980-51f1-baa7-12826cbb65c4.location: Left-hand side altarpiece in St. Anne’s Chapel
ddf00c3a-e980-51f1-baa7-12826cbb65c4.artist: Giovanni Pietro de Pomis (active 1569, Lodi–1633, Graz)

de217671-b0c6-5d52-a68e-4da53f3ccb53.name: Church Façade
de217671-b0c6-5d52-a68e-4da53f3ccb53.description: The late 18th-century Rococo façade is divided into three parts, separated by Corinthian pilasters with capitals, and surmounted by a magnificent pediment built in the 19th century. The two towers, designed in 1848, were completed at the beginning of the 20th century. The pediment dates to around 1890. The first section of the stairway can also be seen in the photograph.
de217671-b0c6-5d52-a68e-4da53f3ccb53.dates: c. 1750; towers: 1848; final design façade: 1880; pediment: c.1890
de217671-b0c6-5d52-a68e-4da53f3ccb53.location: Exterior, Sanctuary of Our Lady of Good Remedy
de217671-b0c6-5d52-a68e-4da53f3ccb53.artist: Church: António Mendes Coutinho (active 1750 ); stairs: Manuel Faustino Loureiro (active1782); Towers: Augusto de Matos Cid (active1880).

de4bf7f6-639e-5b76-a737-c2879b0b1c85.name: Monumental Staircase
de4bf7f6-639e-5b76-a737-c2879b0b1c85.description: The double flight staircase was built between 1726 and 1738 by Domenico Trifogli following the model of Bolognese senatorial residences staircases; the sculptures are by Francesco Janssens and the stucco decorations by Giambattista Verda.
de4bf7f6-639e-5b76-a737-c2879b0b1c85.artist: Domenico Trifogli; Francesco Janssens; Giambattista Verda

de6db7d5-6d7b-5926-ad6b-637eedb72f0d.name: Monochrome roundel with the *Birth of the Virgin*
de6db7d5-6d7b-5926-ad6b-637eedb72f0d.description: The use of monochrome painting in the roundels at the foot of the dome shows Mitelli’s and Colonna’s elegant taste together with their will to emphasise the contrast between the different worlds of the stories of the Virgin and the heavenly vision above. The scene represented in this roundel is strongly indebted to the classicizing style of Guido Reni.
de6db7d5-6d7b-5926-ad6b-637eedb72f0d.location: Dome of the square antechamber of the chapel of the Rosary, Basilica di San Domenico, Bologna
de6db7d5-6d7b-5926-ad6b-637eedb72f0d.artist: Angelo Michele Colonna and Agostino Mitelli

deb66bb9-f9a7-5754-b548-8fe682e92195.name: The Last Judgement
deb66bb9-f9a7-5754-b548-8fe682e92195.description: The brightly coloured main fresco promisingly and obviously thematises the Last Judgement as the goal of Christ’s redemption, whose passion began with His suffering leading up to His crucifixion. Opposite the gate to eternity, before which a toppled Chronos symbolises the end of time, is the throne prepared for Christ as the Judge of the World.

df155207-91c9-565d-8f2e-e745a4c8648a.name: Ulisse Aldrovandi giving a lecture at Bologna University
df155207-91c9-565d-8f2e-e745a4c8648a.description: The famous naturalist Ulisse Aldrovandi was a true protagonist of Bolognese culture. He donated his naturalistic collection to the City and today it is exhibited in the Palazzo Poggi Museum.
df155207-91c9-565d-8f2e-e745a4c8648a.location: Interior, first floor, palazzo Aldrovandi Montanari
df155207-91c9-565d-8f2e-e745a4c8648a.artist: Vittorio Maria Bigari and Stefano Orlandi

df6b10ce-46a5-5015-8d2f-07ed83b9bdeb.name: Fresco and stucco
df6b10ce-46a5-5015-8d2f-07ed83b9bdeb.description: Perhaps of greatest aesthetic interest is the decorated vault. The fine Wessobrunn stucco with its combination of late-period strapwork and emerging rocailles is the height of the prevailing fashion and is indicative of the transition to Rococo. It probably originates from Franz Xaver Feichtmayr. Thanks to their small format and their general failure to account for viewing from below, the frescos, depicting scenes from the life of the church patroness, appear like inserted folk art pictures. The landscapes depict the environs of Eben. The attribution is contested.
df6b10ce-46a5-5015-8d2f-07ed83b9bdeb.artist: Johann Georg Höttinger (c. 1690–after 1645) or Christoph Anton Mayr (c. 1720–1771); Franz Xaver Feichtmayr (1698–1763)

df780fc9-d9b2-5161-911e-4c3bf1d7dfca.name: Anatomical Theatre
df780fc9-d9b2-5161-911e-4c3bf1d7dfca.description: This room, known as Teatro Anatomico, was built to house the lessons of anatomy. It is made of pine wood and decorated with wooden statues of the most celebrated medicine professors of the past. In the coffered ceiling are represented Apollo and the signs of the Zodiac. According to contemporary astrological beliefs these symbols were considered connected with the human body rhythms.
df780fc9-d9b2-5161-911e-4c3bf1d7dfca.location: Palazzo of the Archiginnasio, first floor

dfafe781-3027-548f-92da-7716b132333a.name: Invokings and Glories of St. Anthony of Padua
dfafe781-3027-548f-92da-7716b132333a.description: With its capriccio-like tendencies, Holzer’s masterly combination of earthly sceneries and the visionary “celestial realm” follows the concept of illusionistic architecture and marks the peak of the Late Baroque ceiling paintings in Bavaria. The elegance and pathos of the figural depictions are unprecedented. Delicately painted clouds and poetic, brilliant colour shifts account for the enchanting character of the visual experience. As an appeal to the pilgrims, they are encircled by pictorial representations of peoples’ physical and spiritual afflictions: death, fallacy, misery, obsession, plagues, disease, distress at sea, captivity, lameness, material damages and eye conditions; from these ailments the invocation of St. Anthony promises salvation. In this context, there are regional and time-related references, such as: a healed man dragging away his mattress, which is considered to be a self-portrait of the artist; and the merchants that were typical for the social structure of a market town. They are holding a fabric bale and immediately strike the eye when entering the church.

dfe1817b-f94e-59bb-b55c-9eb4977a08bc.name: View of the west section of Zelný trh (Vegetable Market)
dfe1817b-f94e-59bb-b55c-9eb4977a08bc.description: The upper section of the vegetable market is dominated by the Dietrichstein Palace. This was constructed on the site of five burgher houses by the Olomouc Cardinal, František of Dietrichstein, in 1614–20 and rebuilt in 1739 to 1740 to the designs of G. G. Tencalla. Empress Maria Theresa stayed at No. 9 during her visit to Brno. The empress took part in, among other events, the Procession of Corpus Christi in 1748. The aristocracy and prelates that came to Brno for sessions of the Provincial Assembly constructed and reconstructed a large number of buildings in the city after the Thirty Years’ War, making Brno the third major centre of palace culture in the monarchy after Vienna and Prague.

e0af94ab-1e8f-5c03-a9d4-caad48b4c0a1.name: Church and Monastery Façade
e0af94ab-1e8f-5c03-a9d4-caad48b4c0a1.description: The church façade is typical of the Late Baroque style, disguising the original volumes of the building and strictly unifying the front of the complex. The entrance to the church is through a porch with three Corinthian columns.

e0b22be9-8f6f-536c-91f7-27d4bf5ef96f.name: *Abraham and the Three Angels*
e0b22be9-8f6f-536c-91f7-27d4bf5ef96f.description: In the third story of the frieze the painter shows the three angels appearing to Abraham to announce the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah as well as his miraculous paternity in old age.

e0deac61-1689-5102-865c-bbe744a184c6.name: Death of St. Augustine in Hippo
e0deac61-1689-5102-865c-bbe744a184c6.description: The main fresco extends across two bays and is highlighted by a golden stucco frame. Matthäus Günther aesthetically contrasts the horrors of the Siege of Hippo by the Vandals to Augustine’s immensely towering deathbed and his ascent into heavenly glory as a theme of redemption. The artist obviously immortalises himself as the chronicler in the painting.

e1205084-57bd-571b-9800-802c7784d032.name: *The Coronation of the Emperor Charles V*
e1205084-57bd-571b-9800-802c7784d032.description: This scene documents one of the most important episodes in the history of Bologna and Europe: Pope Clement VII crowning Emperor Charles V in 1530. The sumptuous ceremony took place in Bologna in the church of San Petronio, facing the main square, next to the Municipal Palace.

e145a80f-139b-5a44-a72d-22942e7995d1.name: St. Cecilia
e145a80f-139b-5a44-a72d-22942e7995d1.description: This statue of St. Cecilia, an early Christian martyr and patron saint of musicians, was probably created with the intention of commemorating Countess Cecílie Kollonitsch. With her striking attribute (the organ) and female attire, the statue stands out among markedly vertical figures of closed outlines. Her arms stretched forward, and with a cloak thrown over the shoulder, the figure, with the head slightly tilted back, has great emotional appeal.

e18d8bb6-3bd7-5475-b27b-3e786ad79e26.name: Church’s architecture
e18d8bb6-3bd7-5475-b27b-3e786ad79e26.description:
Though there was everywhere a huge desire to erect buildings during the Baroque era, it was different in Wilhering. The Cistercians had to (re)build the church and monastery buildings after a big fire. The destroyed parts were reconstructed using the remaining Romanesque walls, the original Romanesque portal is even visible. The new buildings got similarly designed Baroque facades with structuring pilasters. The church’s main façade with the tower is richly decorated. There are capitals and entablature above the pilasters, statues and Rococo skylight windows, continuously setting throughout the upper floor of the building.  
According to the church’s main façade, the interior is similarly designed. The walls have pilasters (and pillars) with capitals, entablature and figurative decoration. Flat vaults sit on prominent columns whose continuous cornice divide the church into a celestial and a terrestrial part.
e18d8bb6-3bd7-5475-b27b-3e786ad79e26.location: In the centre of the monastery’s courtyard
e18d8bb6-3bd7-5475-b27b-3e786ad79e26.artist: Johann Haslinger probably after plans by Joseph Matthias Götz (Johann Michael Prunner? and/or Joseph Munggenast?)

e2638706-bdcf-5e4a-9bd3-dcc016217e9e.name: Observatory
e2638706-bdcf-5e4a-9bd3-dcc016217e9e.description: After centuries of disputes between the representatives of the Roman Catholic Church and those of natural sciences, there was finally an acceptation by the church. In consequence, academic institutions, such as the Kremsmünster observatory, arose. In this case, the building of the observatory was even planned by a Benedictine monk. Being the first high-riser in today’s Austria it was not only unique for its height but also as a building where natural research had a home. It houses several collections (mineralogical, zoological, anthropological, physical, astronomical instruments), a chapel and a spacious panoramic terrace.
e2638706-bdcf-5e4a-9bd3-dcc016217e9e.dates: 1748–59 construction of tower; 1697 stucco work on ceiling
e2638706-bdcf-5e4a-9bd3-dcc016217e9e.artist: Pater Anselm Desing: architecture; stucco work on ceiling: Franz Joseph Ignaz Holzinger

e2b776c2-de6a-5d29-a03c-25866587d681.name: Nave fresco, detail: *Angel blowing a trumpet*
e2b776c2-de6a-5d29-a03c-25866587d681.description: The angel announces the dawn of the age of salvation with a quote from the Epistle to the Galatians “Venit plenitudo temporis” (When the fullness of time has come) on a standard. With this spirited and powerful figure, compositionally integrated in the heavenly scenery, the viewer is immediately introduced to the picture’s theme, the triumph of Christ’s work of salvation as manifested in his church. The angel functions as a pictorial-rhetorical introduction presenting the motto.
