e2f80c3c-ab05-5f27-aeeb-0c7c30fb8fa9.name: Stucco and ceiling paintings
e2f80c3c-ab05-5f27-aeeb-0c7c30fb8fa9.description: During the course of the Baroque redesign of the monastery church, which was vaulted between 1607 and 1609, ceiling pictures and stucco were also added to the nave and choir. The picture cycle in accordance with the preferences of the order, depict Marian themes as well as the life of the order’s founder. They are the work of the fresco artist Wolcker from Augsburg which is characterised by audacious illusionistic architecture. The stuccowork of the Wessobrun school is in the late strapwork style, at the transition to Rococo.
e2f80c3c-ab05-5f27-aeeb-0c7c30fb8fa9.artist: Georg Anton Gumpp (1682–1754, attributed to); Johann Georg Wolcker (1700–1766); Franz Xaver Feichtmayr the elder (1698–1763), Joseph Fischer [n.d.]

e3219bac-8d55-51be-9446-ae37aba26277.name: Ceiling paintings *Judith and Holofernes* and *Apocalyptic Madonna*
e3219bac-8d55-51be-9446-ae37aba26277.description: The ceiling frescos in Wilten, which are among the most significant achievements of the Director of the Augsburg Academy, are pictorial worlds executed with virtuosity: heavenly visions open up above grandiose architectural backdrops, which rather than extending the real architecture form part of the visionary event breaking into the space of the church. Like the rhetoric of a Late Baroque preacher, the pictorial content draws a number of references. Here Judith, who presents the head of Holofernes to the people as a symbol of her victory over evil, is interpreted as the precursor of Mary, who at the end of time appears as the “Madonna of the Apocalypse”, the over-comer of all evil. The transcendence of space and time within the picture support this statement.
e3219bac-8d55-51be-9446-ae37aba26277.location: Vault of the west nave bay

e4463aab-b7e7-5517-b782-78afcfe70848.name: *Salvation of the Cross*
e4463aab-b7e7-5517-b782-78afcfe70848.description: The large-scale circumferential main fresco of the church typologically introduces the Holy plan for salvation derived from both the New and Old Testaments. The adjacent choir fresco shows the *Salvation of the Cross* within the illusionistic cupola architecture.
e4463aab-b7e7-5517-b782-78afcfe70848.location: Vault of the nave, side aisles and choir, Catholic Parish and Pilgrimage Church of the Exaltation of the Cross and Our Lady of Sorrows

e4945fc7-7c58-505c-b4ee-a58561295954.name: Church
e4945fc7-7c58-505c-b4ee-a58561295954.description: The church is built in the Late Classical style, the interior following the model of Jesuit churches. Due to the design, the sanctuary is attributed to João Antunes, an attribution that is probable because he was at the time the architect of the Casa do Infantado nearby. The ceiling painting of Our Lady of the Assumption was painted by Lourenço da Cunha in 1740.
e4945fc7-7c58-505c-b4ee-a58561295954.location: Sanctuary of Our Lady of Cape Espichel, West End
e4945fc7-7c58-505c-b4ee-a58561295954.artist: Architecture attributed to João Antunes (1642–1712); painting to Lourenço da Cunha (active 1740–1743)

e4c124f4-c90f-54be-b229-5dc62e2547dc.name: Celebration of St. Aloysius
e4c124f4-c90f-54be-b229-5dc62e2547dc.description: A member of the influential Gonzaga family in Italy who renounced his social status (indicated by the hat and armour at his feet), St. Aloysius joined the Jesuit order. Treating victims of a plague epidemic he contracted the disease and died in 1591. The lily held by an angel symbolises moral purity. The pyramidal chiaroscuro composition opens with the figure of an angel who draws in the viewer and enhances the psychological effect of the picture. The saint is a mediator of pleas and prayers to Christ and the Virgin Mary. A sketch for the picture is preserved in the collections of the Moravian Gallery in Brno.

e4d031d0-15bc-59fc-817c-694868cfef89.name: Ceiling painting *Miracle of Pentecost*
e4d031d0-15bc-59fc-817c-694868cfef89.description: In great contrast to the choir cupola is Joseph Anton Zoller’s composition for the central cupola employing the entire range of High Baroque devices. Here the Pentecost scene takes place against the background of a huge architectural backdrop which is calculated for viewers in the rear congregation room and signifies the gate to the city of God. The apostle and Mary function as mediators between heaven and earth and thus connect the vision to the real space of the church.

e4db2e14-2c80-5dda-9994-a2e49390ee72.name: Marienaltar (High Altar)
e4db2e14-2c80-5dda-9994-a2e49390ee72.description: The two-levelled high altar, finished by Feichtmayr, fits into the double-shelled choir apse according to a scenographic plan. The two levels are united through slender column pairs between which the stucco figures of *St. Ulrich* and *St. Norbert* are placed, together with a whimsically cambered attic. All this forms an arcade, which, in turn, frames the slightly removed high altar with its painting of the *Ascension of the Virgin Mary.*
e4db2e14-2c80-5dda-9994-a2e49390ee72.artist: Johann Georg Üblher (1703–1763), Franz Xaver Feichtmayr, the Younger (1735–1803); Franz Georg Hermann, the Younger (1692–1768)

e617b4a6-da47-5007-89ac-f0ffc254183c.name: High altar
e617b4a6-da47-5007-89ac-f0ffc254183c.description: The richly structured ciborium above six pillars with curved entablature and altar crown, together with the portals for the offertory procession, extend across the whole width of the choir. Its structure is clearly drawn from the high altar in Götzens. Zeiller’s altarpiece depicts the church patron Gall worshipping Mary and the Infant Jesus. The statues of six saints which flank it and the figures in the altar crown, God the Father with aureole between angels, are masterful works of an unknown sculptor.

e63e4169-7728-579b-8318-a18d9572838d.name: *St. Kümernissa*
e63e4169-7728-579b-8318-a18d9572838d.description: The bearded St. Kümerrnissa was particularly popular in Tyrol. She was known variously as *Liberatrix, Wilgefortis*, *Ontkomer* and *Hülpe* and can be traced back to the Middle Ages. Her unusual looks relate to the *Volto Santo* from the Tuscan city of Lucca (a wooden cross bearing the corpus of Christ cloaked in the long priest's robe – *colobium*). The development of trade and dissemination of graphic prints representing the famous Tuscan sculpture resulted in an incorrect interpretation of the figure and replacement of the iconography with that of St. Kümerrnissa.

e6d1474a-473c-5669-a0d5-a4ba232d0192.name: Interior, facing east
e6d1474a-473c-5669-a0d5-a4ba232d0192.description: The actual sacred centre of the church is the Chapel of Mercy with the devotional picture of Mary, an oval structure at the central axis of the nave. The hall of the church is surmounted by a depressed barrel vault in which deep lunettes are cut. The walls are structured by simple pilasters. The heavily retracted choir of steeper proportions receives considerably more light than the nave and thus stages the high altar as the second focal point of the space, opposite the Chapel of Mercy.

e776e04a-2c10-552c-8dee-90065c1de43f.name: Villa Ghisilieri
e776e04a-2c10-552c-8dee-90065c1de43f.description: The villa was not only a place for leisure but also the administrative centre of many commercial and rural activities. The villa of the patron had its own courtyard, separated from the hamlet. This is where a weekly market took place.

e782bf6e-5adc-5df3-a2ab-2d9db58b30af.name: Gates of São Francisco (St. Francis) – exterior and interior gates
e782bf6e-5adc-5df3-a2ab-2d9db58b30af.description: Main entrance following the designs of Salomon de Brosse.

e7b338c4-14b0-537a-a5cd-6a0cb1516281.name: General View, Church Interior
e7b338c4-14b0-537a-a5cd-6a0cb1516281.description: One of the finest examples of a Portuguese Baroque Golden Church. The panel ceiling of the nave is adorned with paintings depicting the Life of St. Dominic.
e7b338c4-14b0-537a-a5cd-6a0cb1516281.dates: Late 17th century and first third of the 18th century

e7e6dced-0a81-539b-82a2-a013d4574cd9.name: Presbytery vaulting
e7e6dced-0a81-539b-82a2-a013d4574cd9.description: The stucco decoration is 30 cm deep in places. The designs for the cartouche frescos were created by M. A. Lublinský, an Olomouc canon and artist. The vault frescos symbolise the invocation of the Loreto litanies. The painting of the Holy Trinity above the altar is accompanied by the Celebration of the Lord by the Three Virtues and the Assumption of the Virgin Mary.
e7e6dced-0a81-539b-82a2-a013d4574cd9.artist: Quiricho Castelli, Domenico Gagina, Carlo Borsa, Matteo Contessa, Martin Antonín Lublinský (1636 Lesnica – 1690 Olomouc).

e83f959c-c5a5-5804-9244-9b13dbf232e5.name: Imperial Hall
e83f959c-c5a5-5804-9244-9b13dbf232e5.description: The architectonic and artificial painting arrangement of the ceremonial hall celebrates the idea and dignity of the Holy Roman Empire as well as the fidelity to the empire and the potential sovereignty of the abbey. The ceiling fresco shows the Coronation of Emperor Charlemagne in 800; four pictures to the sides describe the empire's functions in relation to its services for the church: *Ecclesiae propagatori* (propagator of the Church), *Ecclesiae propugnatori* (defender of the Church), *Hostium debellatori* (combatant against enemies) and *Scientiae fautori* (patron of science). Larger-than-life statues of the last 16 emperors, placed in front of the pompous columns of the wall decoration, show respectful reverence to the ruling House of Habsburg.
e83f959c-c5a5-5804-9244-9b13dbf232e5.location: Central projection of the west wing (3rd floor), Benedictine Abbey of St. Theodor and Alexander
e83f959c-c5a5-5804-9244-9b13dbf232e5.artist: Andrea Maini (b. 1683); Jakob Karl Stauder (1694–1751/56); Franz Anton Sturm (1690–1757)

e8770573-d328-5834-b1d9-a0c8ce5da0f6.name: Bom Jesus Church
e8770573-d328-5834-b1d9-a0c8ce5da0f6.description: At ground level there are two sculptural figures of the prophets, Jeremiah and Isaiah. Over the cornice, on the upper section, are the four evangelists.
e8770573-d328-5834-b1d9-a0c8ce5da0f6.location: Façade of the church in the Neo-Classical style, Bom Jesus de Braga (Bom Jesus do Monte)

e88898ac-b98e-5bad-81d8-2344a9fd7fed.name: Angel pointing to the Virgin with Child
e88898ac-b98e-5bad-81d8-2344a9fd7fed.description: The beautiful side angels made by Mazza for the former altar were reused in this new version with the help of the sculptor himself.

e89d5689-d3ce-555d-b58f-cb9630485edd.name: Altar of St. Bernard
e89d5689-d3ce-555d-b58f-cb9630485edd.description: Commissioned by the Archdeacon of the Chapter in Dubrovnik, Bernard Dordić, this opulent inlaid altar is the work of Neapolitan sculptor, Carlo degli Frangi. In the shape of a triumphal arch with protruding stripes, it has double Corinthian columns and a segmented, broken gable into which an attic has been inserted. The angels and the dove of the Holy Spirit in the attic were probably the work of the Venetian sculptor, Marino Gropelli, while the *Virgin and Child with St Bernard* altarpiece was the work of local Dubrovnik painter, Petar Mattej. The notable feature of this altar is in the application of inlay in various coloured marbles. This type of decoration, which is particular to southern Italy, was not common in Venice, and in spite of this Ragusan exception, was not commonly seen in Dalmatia either.
e89d5689-d3ce-555d-b58f-cb9630485edd.location: Transept of the Cathedral, northern side
e89d5689-d3ce-555d-b58f-cb9630485edd.artist: Inlay on altarpiece: Carlo Degli Frangi [n.d.]; statues: Marino Gropelli (1662–1728); painter of altarpiece: Petar Matej [n.d.]

e8bde714-42f2-5dcd-81ba-9973e29e6a61.name: Pulpit
e8bde714-42f2-5dcd-81ba-9973e29e6a61.description: Reliefs on the baldachin present stories from the Old Testament: *the Sacrifice of Abraham*, *Moses and the Burning Bush*, *The legend of Tobias* and *Daniel in the Lion's Den*, accompanied by statues of the *Four Apostles*. The decorative motifs are characteristic of Stjepan Severin's work.

e93c0684-321e-58c9-b7f4-2505ffdc37b6.name: Playing Putti
e93c0684-321e-58c9-b7f4-2505ffdc37b6.description: In the side lunettes of the Room of Fortune are depicted playing putti.
e93c0684-321e-58c9-b7f4-2505ffdc37b6.location: Ceiling decoration of a room of the first floor of the palace, detail, Palazzo Ranuzzi

e9b3c366-6e58-520e-b2f0-8115391ee915.name: High altar
e9b3c366-6e58-520e-b2f0-8115391ee915.description: This altar is typically baroque with its elegant curved lines and its open shape, embracing the space. It is a good example of different artistic techniques (sculpture, architectural painting, architecture and figural painting) and of different materials (stucco, painted and gilded wood, fresco, and oil on canvas). It is perfectly in harmony with the space of the church blending the frescoes on the ceiling, the elegant balustrade, the organs and side pillars. This imposing altar frames a fresco fragment of the Virgin with Child, worshipped in the church of Santa Maria di Galliera since the fifteenth-century. The church was completely remodelled in the eighteenth-century and the main altar was rebuilt twice. Giuseppe Maria Mazza built the first version between 1691, when the Filippines fathers inherited a large sum of money in order to refurbish the main chapel, and 1706, when the decoration is mentioned in a guidebook for the first time. This altar, made of stucco, looked like great curtain suspended to the wall and held by two angels and some putti. Before 1739 the decoration was destroyed in order to build a new altar which was designed by Francesco Bibiena. This altar was decorated with two wooden statues of Justice and Peace, carved by the Tuscan Silvestro Giannotti, and two putti, moulded by Angelo Gabriello Piò. The central part of the altar is decorated with a picture by Giuseppe Rolli of angels carrying the medieval Madonna and Child, framed by a rich baroque carving.
e9b3c366-6e58-520e-b2f0-8115391ee915.artist: Francesco Bibiena, Giuseppe Maria Mazza, Giuseppe Rolli, Angelo Gabriello Piò, Silvestro Giannotti

e9ee182e-3c06-5ca0-afa2-0e2ef8d51fa6.name: Monumental staircase
e9ee182e-3c06-5ca0-afa2-0e2ef8d51fa6.description: Commissioned by Earl Vincenzo Bargellini, the monumental staircase was realised by the architect Alfonso Torreggiani in 1730. The project represents the synthesis resulting from the combination of the designs suggested by various architects contacted by the Earl. Besides Torreggiani, one can see the hints of the work of Carlo Francesco Dotti and Antonio Conti, whose drawings are still preserved. The plastic decorations are the work of Giuseppe Borelli a member of an important Swiss family of stucco decorators, working in Bologna for many noble families. The staircase was recently restored.

ea9fdd0d-171f-533d-b39d-9aff5b4b8568.name: Pulpit
ea9fdd0d-171f-533d-b39d-9aff5b4b8568.description: The baptismal font, organ and particularly the pulpit, are remarkable carved pieces. Contrary to common practice they are not made of stone or stucco, and the pulpit is situated on the right decorated with plant garlands and tendrils with pomegranates. The ambo with semi-relief herm has the figures of the four Evangelists in its niches.

eafb2529-446c-50ef-b77c-af336401eab9.name: Church´s façade and square in front of the church
eafb2529-446c-50ef-b77c-af336401eab9.description:
The vertically high extending church with two-storied façade and three-storied towers has a stone-faced exterior and towers with onion-shaped roofs and patriarchal crosses on top. These emblems – the building´s height, the stone-faced façade and the patriarchal crosses – may allude to the provosts´ (territorial) claim to power. They probably would therewith refer that they are on the one hand subordinate to the prince-bishops of Bamberg and on the other hand emphasize the independence on the Habsburgs´ rule.  
The elegant façade is decorated with stone statues in niches and above the portal: in the middle storey one can see the Mother of God holding the Infant Jesus, in the base storey there are the apostles Peter and Paul. The sculptor Severin Träxl created the statues (1725). God the Father, sitting enthroned, as well as the figures of the founder Emperor Henry II, Bishop Otto II of Bamberg and the angels above the entrance were done by Josef Hochedlinger (1728–30).  
In 1771, Veit Königer created the trinity column on the square in front of the church. It is surrounded by a picket fence and stone posts to enclose an outer holy district. All wrought ironwork (grids, gates and window grilles) was presumably done by Matthäus Lindemayr (1756).
eafb2529-446c-50ef-b77c-af336401eab9.artist: Johann Michael Prunner, Severin Träxl, Josef Hochedlinger, Veit Königer, Matthäus Lindemayr

eb2c6bd8-523c-5da1-ab39-330d09fffdc5.name: The Triumph of Intelligence over Brutality
eb2c6bd8-523c-5da1-ab39-330d09fffdc5.description: The Triumph of Intelligence, represented as Minerva, over Brutality, symbolized by the Giants.

eb503e88-060a-52e9-9182-c489847066be.name: Frontage
eb503e88-060a-52e9-9182-c489847066be.description: The portal to the third courtyard of the residence lends emphasis to the central section: the main hall, chapel and the count’s quarters, the oldest part of the complex. The count would greet his subjects from the balcony. Beduzzi’s decoration of the frontage was part of the second phase of the reconstruction; he was also responsible for some of the iconography of the residence. Beduzzi designed the sculpted decoration of the chateau and chapel interiors.
eb503e88-060a-52e9-9182-c489847066be.artist: Antonio Maria Nicolao Beduzzi (1675 Bologna – 1735 Vienna)

eb5ab3da-2f42-5a92-b0f9-42a687e8b2c2.name: *St. Macarius*
eb5ab3da-2f42-5a92-b0f9-42a687e8b2c2.description: The painting of the Egyptian hermit, St. Macarius the Great, forms part of a complex iconographic cycle of 24 oil-on-panel paintings built into the backs of the choir stalls on which eremitic figures and motifs are shown – an iconographic choice that refers to the spiritual models of the Paulist community.

eb77d416-fa55-5898-86cc-7b23bc0e41c1.name: High altar
eb77d416-fa55-5898-86cc-7b23bc0e41c1.description: The superstructure of the high altar, which, with its loose, light-flooded rows of columns is integrated into the semi-circular choir apse, is based on the design of the stucco sculptor Franz Xaver Feichtmayr. It is composed of a total of six columns above a high pedestal which are united by an entablature bent at right angles and curved in places. The crowning baldachin and the stucco figure of St. Joseph in the centre are modern additions in the style of the period.

eb7a0351-f4ca-5902-b8bb-572d211a56e6.name: Carmo Fountain
eb7a0351-f4ca-5902-b8bb-572d211a56e6.description: From the Mãe d' Água das Amoreiras reservoir, a secondary aqueduct spreads out around the city terminating in fountains, many of them like this one still extant. Built by the engineer, Miguel Ângelo Blasco in 1769, it was redesigned by Reinaldo Manuel dos Santos in 1786.
eb7a0351-f4ca-5902-b8bb-572d211a56e6.artist: Attributed to the engineer, Miguel Ângelo Blasco (1769–1770) and the architect, Reinaldo Manuel dos Santos [n.d.]

eb86b19e-ab63-5c13-b4c8-efb32827e0c8.name: *Choirs of angels with a double crown of flowers and stars*
eb86b19e-ab63-5c13-b4c8-efb32827e0c8.description: Above the extraordinary altar containing the statue of the Virgin Mitelli, and Colonna painted a monumental baroque building, with courts, balconies, friezes and floral decorations. The sky opens over two choirs of angels holding a crown made of flowers, symbolizing earthly grace, and a crown made of stars, a symbol of divine glory. The skilled use of perspective, the vivid colours and the employ of gold leaf in the decorations lead to a strongly visual result.
eb86b19e-ab63-5c13-b4c8-efb32827e0c8.location: Semi dome of the chapel of the Rosary, Basilica di San Domenico, Bologna
eb86b19e-ab63-5c13-b4c8-efb32827e0c8.artist: Angelo Michele Colonna and Agostino Mitelli

ec109625-0feb-560f-9046-bdb7068fb85c.name: Panels’ Room
ec109625-0feb-560f-9046-bdb7068fb85c.description: In the Panels’ Room are Dutch tiles depicting mythological themes, rural scenes and river landscapes. On the same floor is the Library with a barrel vault decorated with the pagan god, Mercury and neo classical stucco.

ec147545-1850-5a97-9755-1387bdc2cc89.name: *Celebration of the Serényi family*
ec147545-1850-5a97-9755-1387bdc2cc89.description: The spectacular rectangular hall, referred to as the large summer dining hall, spans two storeys. The subject of wall and ceiling frescos is the triumph of the imperial army in the struggle against the Turks at the turn of the 17th century. The illusionary architecture blends with portraits of family members: Jan Karel Serényi (d.1691) took part in the victorious Siege of Vienna in 1683 and became a Commander-in-Chief in Munich. The figure of Hercules enthroned and the depictions of his deeds in the presence of ancient gods, along with the allegories of the Arts and Sciences, celebrate the military past and aristocratic nobility of the family. Above Jan Karel, András Serényi (d.1345) with allegories of Victory and Eternal Fame is depicted. The central figure is Emperor Charles VI portrayed as Apollo, surrounded by the Zodiac, Aurora, Luna and Chronos. The painter pays tribute to the family in his self-portrait. He is seen pointing to the Baptism of an Aristocrat, a scene that illustrates a family legend about an ancestor from a noble family of Hungarian origin known as Temnurtus (“The Dark”), who was baptised in 965 and adopted the name Serenus (“The Powerful”). Representations of Habsburg sovereigns, Czech kings and ancient rulers supplement the celebration of the Serényi family. Family history and its mythologization are major iconographic elements in Baroque residences.
ec147545-1850-5a97-9755-1387bdc2cc89.artist: František Ignác Řehoř Eckstein (1689 Židovice – 1741 Lviv)

ed2e5596-037a-5738-8eaa-d795beb82ba9.name: High Altar
ed2e5596-037a-5738-8eaa-d795beb82ba9.description:
The sculptor, António Bellini of Pádua, was responsible for the decoration of the chancel. He endowed it with a sense of immateriality and a subtle notion of “suspension” seen in, for example, the main altar where angels worship on top of the white marble pediment flanking the cedar sculpture of Christ by Manuel Dias.  
In the central panel is the *Assumption of the Virgin*, signed and dated 1731 by Agostino Masucci. This is surrounded by other paintings of the *Nativity,* *Conception*, *Adoration of the Shepherds* and the *Coronation,* all of which were painted in his workshop.
ed2e5596-037a-5738-8eaa-d795beb82ba9.artist: The angels, the *Four Virtues*, the pediment over the main arch and busts of *St. Peter and St. Paul* are by João António Bellini de Pádua (active 1725–1748); the paintings are by the workshop of Agostino Masucci

ed6f3189-e588-5b12-a94c-6f71f36b6d21.name: Hercules
ed6f3189-e588-5b12-a94c-6f71f36b6d21.description: Although these figures are reminiscent of antique statues, the gods fit perfectly in the illusionistic architecture, painted by the artist to create artificial effects in order to amaze the visitors.

edf71a35-ca15-58ff-b59d-2908cc032376.name: St Catherine's church interior
edf71a35-ca15-58ff-b59d-2908cc032376.description:
By 1687 Johann Bernhard Fischer von Erlach was working on the plans for the church´s and the burial chapel's interior design. They are considered to be his earliest documented work. Maybe the church’s main altar also originates from him. Marx Schokotnigg, who received many orders from Fischer, created the statues for the main altar and for the side altar. The figure in the centre of the main altar is St Catherine, the church’s and the Jesuit university’s patron saint. The former university building is directly opposite the mausoleum and today houses the seminary.  
Franz Steinpichler was presumably commissioned with the ceiling frescoes. They represent “The Glourious Winner (emperor Leopold I) over the Osmans”, a then actual topic that was for sure requested from the court in Vienna. Fischer von Erlach designed the stucco decoration for walls and ceilings and the tall statues at the lower edge of the cross vault. The stucco work was executed by Joseph Antonio Serenio, Girolamo Rossi and Antonio Quadrio.
edf71a35-ca15-58ff-b59d-2908cc032376.dates: 1687 interior design; n.d. ceiling frescoes; 1688–89 stucco work; about 1695 main altar; 1697–99 statues on the main altar; 1697–1701 altar of the Virgin Mary; n.d. statues of St Michael, angels and putti on the altar of the Virgin Mary
edf71a35-ca15-58ff-b59d-2908cc032376.location: Northern part of the mausoleum complex
edf71a35-ca15-58ff-b59d-2908cc032376.artist: Johann Bernhard Fischer von Erlach: interior design and main altar(?); Marx Schokotnigg: statues for the main altar and for the altar of the Virgin Mary; probably Franz Steinpichler: ceiling fresco paintings; Joseph Antonio Serenio, Girolamo Rossi and Antonio Quadrio: stucco work

ee0459a7-7135-59f3-8a2f-96ace2250f9f.name: Ceiling fresco
ee0459a7-7135-59f3-8a2f-96ace2250f9f.description: Already on the staircase, the profession, rank and claim to power of von Liebenhofen are demonstrated. The ceiling is decorated with an oval fresco by Guglielmi, framed within gold-plated stucco. Its theme is the benefices of trade for the arts and sciences.

ee2e4059-1d67-5430-b35e-06d85eea2b0e.name: *Trompe l’oeil* paintings on the walls and ceiling
ee2e4059-1d67-5430-b35e-06d85eea2b0e.description: *Trompe l'oeil* paintings of Our Lady of Aires decorate the ceiling, while on the walls they recall the Our Lady Litany.

ee7acbfb-30b7-5d16-a232-731decd3979e.name: Main Altar, marble sculptures
ee7acbfb-30b7-5d16-a232-731decd3979e.description: Marble sculpture of St. Domingos (left) and St. Francis of Assisi (right).

ee906e22-472a-58c7-bafa-8ad9e8d52d69.name: Interior of the church
ee906e22-472a-58c7-bafa-8ad9e8d52d69.description: What really defines the internal space is the adoption of half and free standing columns conveying the impression of a cross-shaped plan. The use of free standing columns is a *leitmotiv* of Bolognese architecture during the modern age, when designers appreciated the monumental character of this solution. Stucco decoration and sculptures were realised by Angelo Piò with the help of Antonio Borelli and Giovanni Callegari. Mural paintings of the chapel of the Virgin were commissioned to Vittorio Maria Bigari and Claudio Ferroni.
ee906e22-472a-58c7-bafa-8ad9e8d52d69.location: Santuario della Beata Vergine di san Luca
ee906e22-472a-58c7-bafa-8ad9e8d52d69.artist: Carlo Francesco Dotti; Angelo Piò; Antonio Borelli; Giovanni Callegari; Vittorio Maria Bigari; Claudio Ferroni

ee9947e9-d8a3-563b-bf75-08af587efa7d.name: Martyrdom of Saint Peter and Saint Paul
ee9947e9-d8a3-563b-bf75-08af587efa7d.description: The church’s circular main fresco impressively illustrates the lives of its two patrons, St. Peter and St. Paul, in front of a surrounding architectural backdrop. The fresco displays a subtle colourfulness in a surreal stylization. With dramatic clarity, Günther depicts the martyrdom of the two apostles along the periphery of the fresco with Heaven looking on from the centre. The flat dome, which gives the illusion of being voluminous, is flanked by four pendentives, each of them containing an image of one of the four evangelists.

eea8e4f8-9634-582d-b793-e4253daa1b61.name: *Our Lady of Snow with Donors*
eea8e4f8-9634-582d-b793-e4253daa1b61.description: In the painted medallion are the kneeling figures of Adam Najšić, the chief notary of the Banovina of Croatia, and his wife, both of whom were donors of the church. Above them, on a cloud, sits Mary of the Snow with Christ on her lap. Below her, in the centre of the composition created as a skilful *trompe**\-**l'œil*, is the Roman Church of Santa Maria Maggiore in outline.
eea8e4f8-9634-582d-b793-e4253daa1b61.location: Ceiling, Parish Church of Our Lady of the Snow

eef79b76-d9e7-54b4-9f5c-c341259d92f0.name: Ballroom
eef79b76-d9e7-54b4-9f5c-c341259d92f0.description: The perspective illusionism of the ceiling emphasizes the false columns, embraced by leaves painted on the walls. The chequered floor, dating to the seventeenth-century, is an homage to the Pepoli coat of arms.
eef79b76-d9e7-54b4-9f5c-c341259d92f0.artist: Domenico Maria Canuti and Domenico Santi known as Mengazzino

ef4b7c84-1839-5809-9275-619d28e3878a.name: Battle of the Milvian Bridge
ef4b7c84-1839-5809-9275-619d28e3878a.description: The ceiling painting, which covers the entire surface of the chancel vault, shows the battle of Emperor Constantine the Great, led by a vision of the Christian Cross, against Maxentius, his rival to the throne, at the Tiber Bridge north of Rome. The dramatic figural composition, surging around a bridge arch, is based on a famous model by paraphrasing the Battle of the Amazons by Pieter Paul Rubens.

ef57f78a-4a61-572b-9295-1a1a823103d5.name: Ballroom
ef57f78a-4a61-572b-9295-1a1a823103d5.description: This great hall is considered one of the most peculiar interiors in Italian Baroque architecture. It is a triple volume hall with several balustrades, culminating with the lantern on the top (33 m. height and about 800 square feet surface). There is no painted decoration, only white stucco mouldings that emphasise the extreme lightness of the architecture.

ef5ad0a6-fe89-5362-8d56-f6086ab50208.name: Bulwark
ef5ad0a6-fe89-5362-8d56-f6086ab50208.description: The Bulwark of St. João de Deus for 28 cannons with casemates.
ef5ad0a6-fe89-5362-8d56-f6086ab50208.artist: Pierre Gilles de Saint-Paul and others

ef97269c-7f1c-524a-b766-0796d7d80956.name: *Apotheosis of the Work of St. Ignatius*
ef97269c-7f1c-524a-b766-0796d7d80956.description: The central figure of St. Ignatius is painted most probably after a print depicting the marble statue of the saint made by Camillo and Giuseppe Rusconi in 1733 for the Basilica of St. Peter’s in Rome.

ef9ea3ed-fa20-5118-8e8e-67dcd70aa609.name: Caesar
ef9ea3ed-fa20-5118-8e8e-67dcd70aa609.description: The central motif of the fountain is a figure of G. J. Caesar considered, from the 15th century onwards as the founder of the city. The sculptor J. J. Schauberger, chiefly active in Olomouc and Brno, created his masterpieces, this equestrian statue, which was possibly inspired by Bernini's *Constantine the Great* in the Vatican. Caesar's dynasty was allegedly linked to the mythical Hercules. Together with a fountain dedicated to Hercules (1688), the statue celebrates a legend of the establishment of the town. Hercules holds a shield bearing an eagle, symbol of Olomouc, in his left hand.
ef9ea3ed-fa20-5118-8e8e-67dcd70aa609.artist: Jan Jiří Schauberger (?, before 1725 Vienna, active in Olomouc – 1744 Brno)

f0686b3a-434d-5606-a50c-295938c43bcd.name: Ceiling fresco
f0686b3a-434d-5606-a50c-295938c43bcd.description: The large cupola fresco is considered to be Franz Anton Zeiller’s magnum opus. It depicts the veneration of the Holy Trinity by prophets and saints of the Old and New Testament, a total of approximately 100 figures who, in a huge panorama, are arranged in the celestial sphere in order of hierarchy. On the eastern side of the cupola, between angels playing music, the patrons of the diocese of Salzburg, Rupert and Virgil, are prominently featured.

f16e1653-232d-58b1-9c5a-9e463ced20a3.name: The Baptism of Christ
f16e1653-232d-58b1-9c5a-9e463ced20a3.description: The vault of the nave is roofed by a celestial sphere abounding in figures of saints and angels carrying symbols of the Old and New Testament. The central motif is the Baptism of Christ, while the scenes by the ledge are from the life of St. John; the composition culminates in a figure of God the Father. The vaults of the altar niches feature framed scenes with the patron saints, to which individual altars are dedicated. As is typical of Etgens, the decorative components – cartouches, decorative vases and illusionary architecture – are essential:  The monumental fresco is the final work of this prominent Moravian artist. The church decoration was completed by J. Stern.

f2c3e5c1-e11f-5d98-af35-9b30d507c062.name: High altar
f2c3e5c1-e11f-5d98-af35-9b30d507c062.description: The high altar includes a picture of the Saviour (*Salvatore*) given blessing in Laterano, near Rome, where the original is to be found. In front of the high altar are two tombstones covering the entrance to an underground crypt. The right one commemorates F. M. Šubíř of Chobyně founder of the church, the left one his wife and children. On a side altar to the left is a glass coffin containing the remnants of St. Felician, a martyr from the period of the first Christians, which was acquired in 1735. On the right is an altar of tools of the Lord's martyrdom with a replica of the Turin Shroud. The ceiling painting is modern.
f2c3e5c1-e11f-5d98-af35-9b30d507c062.location: Interior, Pilgrimage Church of the Elevation of the Holy Cross, Jaroměřice u Jevíčka

f2e3163a-4308-51ca-8274-354207600f17.name: General view of the Sacristy
f2e3163a-4308-51ca-8274-354207600f17.description: The redesigned sacristy with marble floor and a marble table. The coat of arms of the Franciscans and of the Royal family are fashioned in *Azulejos,* above which are a series of paintings with religious themes. A Brazilian ebony chest of drawers with a Rococo gilded carved back furnishes one end.
f2e3163a-4308-51ca-8274-354207600f17.artist: Woodcarver: Félix Adauto da Cunha (1649–c.1703); painter André Gonçalves (1685–1762)

f2fd7abc-465f-5f55-a1af-5082af90fafa.name: Sacristy
f2fd7abc-465f-5f55-a1af-5082af90fafa.description: The sacristy holds a large chest of drawers form the 17th century. On its wooden back board is a set of 20 paintings from the Life of St. Francis Xavier.
f2fd7abc-465f-5f55-a1af-5082af90fafa.location: Church interior, Sacristy, Church of São Roque

f3472803-8a49-5d58-b72d-b03b7f910c1b.name: “Amtshof” or the Ceremonial Courtyard
f3472803-8a49-5d58-b72d-b03b7f910c1b.description: In 1719 a fire destroyed the chateau interiors. Reconstruction was undertaken by C. A. Oedtl, who unified the chateau complex with a single frontage. He also rebuilt several other houses in the town. A ballroom was converted into a winter riding hall, and the theatre hall was reconstructed into a library; a *sala terrena* with a terrace was added and the ceremonial courtyard was refurbished, lined with busts of ancient emperors, and further decorated with *putti* and ornamental vases. The wrought-iron gates by H. G. Forster are original.
f3472803-8a49-5d58-b72d-b03b7f910c1b.artist: Christian Alexander Oedtl (1654 Paznaun – 1731 Vienna), Ignaz Lengelacher (1698 Unter Peissenberg – 1780 Baden), Heinrich Gottfried Forster

f449f193-96dc-53bd-8945-39e4c9c7af05.name: Church plan
f449f193-96dc-53bd-8945-39e4c9c7af05.location: Parish Church of St. Mary Magdalene

f47caf01-f716-5553-985a-bd104d027662.name: Ceiling fresco *Miracle of the Loaves*
f47caf01-f716-5553-985a-bd104d027662.description: The Early Classicist, enlightened spirit is most clearly evident in the ceiling pictures which are a late work of the court painter of Brixen Franz Anton Zeiller. The large nave fresco has been painted without reference to viewing from below and has the appearance of a wall painting that has been transferred to the ceiling. The scene is set in a steep rocky landscape with several groups of figures. Although the composition draws on Baroque traditions, the scene and visual language is executed with didactic clarity.

f4b1a4d2-e15b-5664-9e0d-e52316a45737.name: Churchyard and doorway
f4b1a4d2-e15b-5664-9e0d-e52316a45737.description: The churchyard and stone doorway follow a precise architectural design, which is significant in the architectural context of this Church. By using an elegant Baroque design, the anonymous architect added a special status to a vernacular building.

f4cd8092-6856-50bc-98ac-2704192e2c1c.name: Staircase
f4cd8092-6856-50bc-98ac-2704192e2c1c.description: View of one of the two stair flights that bring to the loggia.
f4cd8092-6856-50bc-98ac-2704192e2c1c.location: Ground floor, on the front of the villa

f4f070b1-0f56-5450-aac0-06133e74f60e.name: The Glory of St. Laurence
f4f070b1-0f56-5450-aac0-06133e74f60e.description: Cobalt-blue on white *azulejos* decorate the vault. The *quadratura* setting shows an architectural perspective, *di sotto* *in sù* (“above from below”) at the centre of which is the image of St. Laurence being carried by angels to Heaven.

f4f82fea-ac97-5110-bd7d-d89aa7791475.name: Plan of the chateau and garden
f4f82fea-ac97-5110-bd7d-d89aa7791475.description: In 1650 Jan Rottal was appointed Imperial Secret Councillor. He was also the Supreme War Commissioner, Supreme Provincial Judge of Moravia and the Episcopal Court, Supreme Administrator of Orphans' Property, Chairman of the Royal Tribunal and Provincial Governor! Unsurprisingly, he maintained very close contacts with the court in Vienna. Luchese, in imperial service, made his reputation as a hydrological civil engineer. In Holešov, he designed broad canals along the flower parterre and divided it into four sections. These were adjoined by a kitchen garden and an orchard. The layout of the garden, in its time considered the most beautiful in Moravia, matched that of the chateau.

f5088f41-3c02-57b5-88f0-03125f08fe8f.name: Ceiling fresco: *St. Gall heals a demoniac*
f5088f41-3c02-57b5-88f0-03125f08fe8f.description: The eastern nave fresco is designed in the tradition of Andrea Pozzo (1642–1709), however the cupola’s monumental illusionistic architecture is not closed, instead it opens up to reveal a view of a whole series of vaulted rooms. The grand, highly monumental architectural backdrop elevates the scene from the legend of Gall healing a demoniac to that of the triumph of the church and the history of salvation.

f5580fad-17e7-50ed-b62a-e9bc0f688102.name: View to the sanctuary
f5580fad-17e7-50ed-b62a-e9bc0f688102.location: Votive church of St. Mary of Jerusalem, Trški Vrh, near Krapina
f5580fad-17e7-50ed-b62a-e9bc0f688102.artist: Architect: Josef Hoffer (1700–1764); builder: Josip Javornik (active c. 1750); painter: Anton Joseph (Jožef) Lerchinger (Lerhinger) (c. 1720–after 1787)

f573d604-cfd6-5857-836a-96a9afe10782.name: *Supper at the House of the Pharisee*
f573d604-cfd6-5857-836a-96a9afe10782.description: The inscription reads: “GASPAR PETRI VECCHIA FILIVS FACI(EB)AT VENETIS AN(N)O MDCCXI”.

f57686f8-103f-571f-8a35-6086284443ef.name: Carved Wood and Gilded Retable (High Altar)
f57686f8-103f-571f-8a35-6086284443ef.description: Surmounted by a cupola covered with tiles, the carved wood and gilded retable or high altar was designed as an architectural structure and, in order to make the most of the available space is concave. The elevation, with Solomon Temple columns and a pyramidal throne, has steps to accommodate the image of St. Laurence. In the arched attic are two archivolts decorated with scrolls and angels. The topmost angel holds a grill, symbol of the saint's martyrdom.

f59127bb-d24a-50dc-95ab-b32b7ebbe922.name: Pilgrimage Altar (High Altar)
f59127bb-d24a-50dc-95ab-b32b7ebbe922.description: The two-storey pilgrimage altar, here designed due to the concept of a deeply staggered baldachino architecture, is a type commonly used in Bavaria for pilgrimages. In addition to the altar of mercy at ground level, it contains at gallery level a further celebration altar with an altarpiece that shows the Holy Family. The doughy moulded pedestals and entablatures stand in deliberate contrast to the faked marble materials.
f59127bb-d24a-50dc-95ab-b32b7ebbe922.artist: Altar Architecture: Dominikus Zimmermann (1685–1766) Sculptures: Ägid Verhelst (1696–1749) Altarpiece: Balthasar Augustin Albrecht (1687–1765)

f63aef53-1a4f-5d5f-b041-51c0d6fd9736.name: *Annunciation and Transportation of the Holy House*
f63aef53-1a4f-5d5f-b041-51c0d6fd9736.description:
Signed: *XTOFORO TASCA, 1714*  
The inscription beneath the painting reads *Munificentia Ilustrissimi Dni, Dni Francisci Ignatii Lib. Bar. de Androcha, Dni in Kostell., Kruppa etc. Haec Imago in honorem Miraculosissimae Virginis Tersactanae erecta fuit”; “Virgo sanCtIssIMa, HVIC BENEFACTORI NVnC IN artICVLO VLTae sVae, aC PERPEtVo Tva PIETaTE TVIsqVe GRATIIS PROPITIARE*. (By efforts of the noble Francis Ignatius Androcha, the baron of Androhia, the lord of Kostell, Kruppa etc. this image was painted in honour of the miraculous virgin of Trsat …)
f63aef53-1a4f-5d5f-b041-51c0d6fd9736.location: Triumphal Arch, Franciscan Church and Monastery of Our Lady of Trsat

f640898f-741e-5753-a96c-401f6705b7f8.name: High altar
f640898f-741e-5753-a96c-401f6705b7f8.description: The massive altar superstructure from stucco marble occupies the centre of the polygon, extending to the vault. Portals for the offertory procession connect to the side walls of the choir. The altarpiece depicting the martyrdom of the church patron St. Andrew is framed by unconnected groups of free-standing columns supporting curved sections of entablature. This results in a direct transition between the altarpiece (*Acceptance of the Cross by St. Andrew*, Anton Zoller 1761) and the altar crown, which forms the heavenly zone, so to speak. Here *God the Father* is enthroned before the window, surrounded by numerous angels and putti. The church patron is thus staged as the mediator between earth and heaven.

f644b45d-6304-57e5-a71b-e23ab0fa362c.name: Archangel Raphael
f644b45d-6304-57e5-a71b-e23ab0fa362c.description: The railing opens, fan-like, onto the bridgehead, where the entrance is guarded by two angels on either side. Raphael accompanying little Tobias is, apart from St. Anne teaching the Virgin Mary, the only statue group on the bridge. The angel personifies the guardian spirit believed to accompany pilgrims and travellers. His name means “God heals” and he is identified with the angel who rippled the waters of Lake Bethesda, on the banks of which the diseased used to lie. The water of the lake was believed to have miraculous healing properties.

f6a68291-eff4-59de-8f5e-1783ed8a9228.name: Church’s architecture
f6a68291-eff4-59de-8f5e-1783ed8a9228.description:
The Trinity Church is considered to be Johann Michael Prunner’s masterwork, a creation of highest perfection in both architectural and theological sense. It is very special because it was planned and constructed as a symbolic edifice with many allusions to the Holy Trinity.  
Being typically South German as a building, it stands out in many ways, with the symbolic program and Italian influence. Francesco Borromini was an artistic idol to most architects of this time, such as to Johann Michael Prunner. His oeuvre was not only very popular but generally acknowledged.  
Borrominesque are the forth- and back-swinging outer walls and towers, and the even floor plan with three semicircular altar niches (in the towers) that respond to the circular central room. And the indirect light, flooding from above and from the sides, illuminates the altar paintings and the tiny fresco in the lantern.  
Breaking through the walls behind the altars, the use of indirect light and the interior design go back to Francesco Messenta in his role as interior architect (he also did the illusionistic painting in the church, s. below: Fresco paintings in the cupola and on the walls) who symbolically bowed, like the architect, to Borromini.
f6a68291-eff4-59de-8f5e-1783ed8a9228.location: On a hill in Stadl-Paura next to the river Traun

f7450b1c-6382-5c9c-a528-e4c11c55aa74.name: Ideal design for the residence
f7450b1c-6382-5c9c-a528-e4c11c55aa74.description: Martinelli’s design for reconstruction included the development of a major part of the town and a new parish church. The chateau, on a U-shaped ground plan with a ceremonial courtyard, reflected the status of the investor who thus laid the foundations for the future ambitions of the dynasty. The building director, Petruzzi, adjusted the design to local conditions, paying attention in particular to new functions and taste in accordance with a design by I. Valmaggini, later a building director in Vienna. Maxmilián Kounic, son of Dominik Ondřej and Secretary to Charles VI as well as a secret councillor, became a provincial governor and preferred a more austere design in the French style. The design included the segmentation of the garden with pools, parterres and mazes.

f78d544f-2dff-5ee2-bb44-142887c4b8d2.name: *St. Roch* (detail)
f78d544f-2dff-5ee2-bb44-142887c4b8d2.location: Upper inner rim of the monument

f8bfdb91-7d16-5af5-b1fa-a2b2d52eea27.name: Altar of the Crucifixion and the Shrine of St. Valerius
f8bfdb91-7d16-5af5-b1fa-a2b2d52eea27.description: Positioned on the altar of the Holy Cross is a glass shrine decorated with Rococo ornaments. It is holding the relics of a Roman catacomb saint, St. Valerius. Above, angels reside gracefully pointing at the martyr as well as the crucifix and thus represent the succession of Christ by the martyrdom. The original crucifix of Günther is separated from the shrine today, just like the corresponding Mother of Sorrows which was put up in the Chapel of St. James.
f8bfdb91-7d16-5af5-b1fa-a2b2d52eea27.location: In front of the central wall pillar on the right-hand side, parts of it in the first side chapel and outside the abbey church in the Chapel of St. James.

f8e1ad0b-17de-5672-8ca1-f12a32ae2481.name: Altar of St. Anthony (High Altar)
f8e1ad0b-17de-5672-8ca1-f12a32ae2481.description: With its Late Baroque shapes, the high altar contrasts strongly with the coloured side altars as it is fully gold-plated, a rare occurrence in Bavaria. In its centre, it bears a precious altarpiece. With a clear design and subdued colours, it depicts one of the main visions of the church patron: the blessed embrace of the Christ child. The imported art piece from Venice is characteristic for the market town of Partenkirchen as it is located near an important transit route in the Alps.

f97c18af-c344-543d-9c05-9aae43476c0f.name: Interior
f97c18af-c344-543d-9c05-9aae43476c0f.description: The space was planned by Hagenauer as a longitudinal building with a uniform sequence of four dome bays. Hueber reduced this to three, the central of which he configured as the main space above a quadratic ground plan with bevelled corner piers. Layers of pilasters and bold projecting cornices are further echoes of the Late Baroque. A sharp contrast is established by the ceiling stucco from Peter Plauder in true Early Classicist style executed in a highly two-dimensional manner, as does the austere composition of the high altar and pulpit, virtually devoid of ornamentation.
f97c18af-c344-543d-9c05-9aae43476c0f.artist: Wolfgang Hagenauer (1726–1801), Andrä Hueber [n.d.]; Peter Pflauder (1733–1811)

f9b4fa4a-dd10-5ab8-8d3c-1f5cc6d4e3cb.name: Fish pools
f9b4fa4a-dd10-5ab8-8d3c-1f5cc6d4e3cb.description:
Aside from the observatory, an unusually innovative building in that time, the earlier erected fish pools are another baroque attraction. Carlo Antonio Carlone built the three westerly pools and a fourth, situated ten steps lower. Jakob Prandtauer who was later working for Kremsmünster demolished this pool, raised the terrain level and added two pools at the same level of the older ones to achieve symmetry. In the mid of the pools are water-spouting statues, the earlier westerly ones were done by a sculptor from Salzburg who was then very popular.  
The pools are surrounded by roofed arcades on every side. They run along the walls and between the pools, thereby separating them. Originally there were illusionistic fresco paintings on the sidewalls, doubling the arcades. Only a small part on the ceiling has survived. Art and architecture have created a perfect theatre scenery. No wonder that the place was used for theatre performances. It must have been a fantastic art experience watching a play or listening to a concert in the cool arcades in summer.
f9b4fa4a-dd10-5ab8-8d3c-1f5cc6d4e3cb.dates: 1690–92: construction of the fish pools; 1692: four fountain figures; 1717: extension of the fish pools; n.d. fresco paintings
f9b4fa4a-dd10-5ab8-8d3c-1f5cc6d4e3cb.location: In the North of the monastery complex
f9b4fa4a-dd10-5ab8-8d3c-1f5cc6d4e3cb.artist: Carlo Antonio Carlone: construction; Jakob Prandtauer: alteration and extension; Andreas Götzinger: four fountain figures; Johann Michael Feichtmayr (the older or the younger) and Melchior Steidl: fresco paintings (most of them destroyed)

f9e1619f-ad4c-5283-96ab-edde611f3de0.name: The Baptism of Christ
f9e1619f-ad4c-5283-96ab-edde611f3de0.description: The high altarpiece, supplied by a professor of the Vienna Academy, M. Unterberger, was hailed as the best in Moravia at the time. It is framed by statues of the Prophets Isaiah and Zachary, father of John the Baptist, which are mirror transcriptions of the Apostles Peter and Paul in the Rajhrad Monastery Church. Two *bozzetos* for these monumental statues by I. Lengelacher have survived (Moravian Gallery), and may well have provided direct inspiration for the Kroměříž statues. Volute consoles hold allegories of the Old and New Testaments. Unterberger also painted the two side altarpieces.
f9e1619f-ad4c-5283-96ab-edde611f3de0.artist: Michelangelo Unterberger (1695 Cavalese – 1758 Vienna), Wolfgang Träger (1714 Pilsen – 1763 Olomouc)

fa0f2509-a770-50de-bf2a-adc4110e9d91.name: Main Altarpiece
fa0f2509-a770-50de-bf2a-adc4110e9d91.description: The Main altarpiece is decorated with gilded wood carving in the Rococo style, similar to that of Tibães Monastery, although adapted to a narrower space. The entire structure is elevated. Five steps lead up to the throne occupied by the image of Our Lady that is under a baldachin.
fa0f2509-a770-50de-bf2a-adc4110e9d91.location: Church Interior, Chancel, Sanctuary of Our Lady of Good Remedy
fa0f2509-a770-50de-bf2a-adc4110e9d91.artist: Frei José de Santo António Ferreira (act.1764–66), Luís Manuel da Silva (act.1766)

fa7c0328-2962-5882-b92a-503ddeb0baf9.name: High altar
fa7c0328-2962-5882-b92a-503ddeb0baf9.description: Fontana, who was acquainted with Bernini’s work, made the rich figurative and decorative components give way to an image of the Virgin Mary Adored. The baldachin is topped with a sculpture of God the Father. Through the interplay of light and colour, and the transition of altar architecture into the stucco decoration of the vault, the baldachin accentuates the centrepiece of this pilgrimage complex.
fa7c0328-2962-5882-b92a-503ddeb0baf9.artist: Baldassare Fontana (1661–1733, Chiasso), Johannes Spillenberger (1628 Košice – 1679 Engelhartszell), Johann Hagenmüller, Bernard Antonio Fossati, Mikuláš Indegrenz

faaf94f7-ce33-5ca8-89fa-ac7eebd8c1c7.name: Cycle: The Life of Princess Santa Joana
faaf94f7-ce33-5ca8-89fa-ac7eebd8c1c7.description: A cycle of Baroque paintings in the naïve style made in 1729 by Emanuel Ferreira e Sousa. They depict scenes from the Life of Princess Santa Joana with characters in 18th-century costume acting out episodes from the 15h century.
faaf94f7-ce33-5ca8-89fa-ac7eebd8c1c7.location: Church interior, main chapel side walls

fb2c16ce-05ab-5038-b941-2740a8a0e2cb.name: Detail of ceiling painting
fb2c16ce-05ab-5038-b941-2740a8a0e2cb.description: The *Trompe l'oeil* ceiling painting depicts three manifestations of Wisdom: an allegory of the library (*Bibliotheca*), of the university (*Universitas*) and of the encyclopaedia (*Encyclopaedia*).
fb2c16ce-05ab-5038-b941-2740a8a0e2cb.location: Interior, Biblioteca Joanina da Universidade de Coimbra
fb2c16ce-05ab-5038-b941-2740a8a0e2cb.artist: António Simões Ribeiro and Vicente Nunes [n.d.]

fb3fdb2d-573f-563d-9108-61663265d16a.name: Portrait of João V
fb3fdb2d-573f-563d-9108-61663265d16a.description: The portrait of the King João V emerges from a sort of a “*rideau de scène*” in carved wood, upheld by angels. The oil on canvas painting is by Domenico Duprà, royal painter in Lisbon before 1730.
fb3fdb2d-573f-563d-9108-61663265d16a.location: Interior, Biblioteca Joanina da Universidade de Coimbra

fb69020a-86ca-5884-8fbe-a4756b55b391.name: St. Fidelius of Sigmaringen
fb69020a-86ca-5884-8fbe-a4756b55b391.description: This picture of St. Fidelius of Sigmaringen was first painted by Kracker for the Capuchin Monastery in Znojmo. Sandrart lived in the monastery before being summoned to work for the Bishop of Jager. The Brno piece was probably an unfinished painting by J. T. Rotter in whose workshop Kracker worked after graduating from the Vienna Academy.
fb69020a-86ca-5884-8fbe-a4756b55b391.location: Capuchin Monastery and the Church of the Invention of the Holy Cross, Brno

fba45a53-75fe-54df-af59-5265c31ccabf.name: Church Vault with scenes from the Life of the Virgin Mary and Jesus.
fba45a53-75fe-54df-af59-5265c31ccabf.description: *Azulejos* decorate the chancel with scenes from the Life of the Virgin Mary and Jesus, signed by Policarpo de Oliveira Bernardes.

fbd7ae30-ddfc-55f0-8ed5-3d2ff8b47311.name: Church (architecture and interior)
fbd7ae30-ddfc-55f0-8ed5-3d2ff8b47311.description:
In the first Baroque building period at the begin of the 17th century the two secondary apses were extended and the altars (formerly attached to the pillars) installed on the nave’s sides.  
By 1677, 900 years after the abbey’s foundation, the second Baroque building period began. Carlo Antonio Carlone added a chapel and the new main/west façade. The four storey front with pillars, altane, atticas and gables was erected in front of the towers. It looks like a separate (profane) pavilion architecture.  
The church’s interior was totally baroquised: the late Roman/early Gothic columns were covered with decorative stucco work and got a mighty winding entablature on top. The fresco paintings on the ceiling were framed with sculptural stucco garlands. The side altars were newly built. The altar paintings originate from this epoch and got sumptuous frames. They are complemented with angels of marble who present the paintings’ biblical scenes to the viewer. Gian Lorenzo Bernini created this altar type, first of all, for the church Santa Maria del Popolo in Rome. It was here applied for the first time outside Italy.  
With the order of the painting for the high altar in 1699, the third Baroque phase began. Because of its huge dimension it took thirteen years to get it, as there was no suitable canvas in size. The high altar, complementing angels, the tabernacle, the two statues of the saints Benedict and Scholastika and the pulpit completed the Baroque interior that has stayed untouched for over 300 years.
fbd7ae30-ddfc-55f0-8ed5-3d2ff8b47311.dates: 1614: two secondary apses enlarged; 1680/1681: main/west façade and stucco work in the church; as of 1682–86: most statues on the altars; 1699–1712: painting at the high altar
fbd7ae30-ddfc-55f0-8ed5-3d2ff8b47311.artist: Marx Martin Spaz: secondary apses; Carlo Antonio Carlone: main/west façade; Giovanni Battista Colomba and Giovanni Battista Barberini: stucco work; Michael Zürn the younger: most statues on the altars; Johann Andreas Wolf: painting at the high altar

fc094f04-ed4e-5c5a-b47f-7bcc11b75d8f.name: The Chapel of Santo António  or Ante-Choir
fc094f04-ed4e-5c5a-b47f-7bcc11b75d8f.description: The beautiful floors of the Chapel of Santo António are of inlaid Brazilian wood. *Azulejo* panels – representing scenes from the lives of the hermit saints Anthony and Paul – adorn the walls on the lower register, while on the upper register are paintings depicting the Miracles of St Anthony of Lisbon. Behind a monumental door is the Madre de Deus crib, comprising a set of 42 sculpted polychrome terracotta figures.
fc094f04-ed4e-5c5a-b47f-7bcc11b75d8f.artist: André Gonçalves (1685–1762); terracotta figures in crib: António Ferreira [n.d.] and Dionísio Ferreira [n.d.]

fc6666e7-92e7-5cea-b28d-61769637fca5.name: Interior of the collegiate church
fc6666e7-92e7-5cea-b28d-61769637fca5.description: The collegiate church in the style of the Italian Late Renaissance is modelled on North Italian prototypes (Venice). The four-bay nave has a barrel vault with lunettes ascending above a powerful entablature. The vertical structure is composed of red marble pilasters from the first building phase. The vault of the heavily retracted choir is interrupted by a ten-cornered lantern from 1691/92.
fc6666e7-92e7-5cea-b28d-61769637fca5.location: Interior, view from north to south
fc6666e7-92e7-5cea-b28d-61769637fca5.artist: Giovanni Lucchese [n.d.], Alberto Lucchese [n.d.]; Onofrius Weigl [n.d.]

fc8bfebb-e43c-5126-a7e6-2c4df02c56a9.name: The Saint John of Reims (+around 545), Benedictine Abbot
fc8bfebb-e43c-5126-a7e6-2c4df02c56a9.description: The side-altar statues come from the famous Brno workshop of O Schweigl and Benedikt Edel.

fc8fe75f-aa42-5aa6-8958-3321f68494d9.name: Frontage
fc8fe75f-aa42-5aa6-8958-3321f68494d9.description: The convex-concave frontage traces the ground plan. The blind central entrance is particularly remarkable certainly holding symbolic meaning and probably embodying the third gate of St. John’s Revelation. Stone coats of arms of the church’s founder and his wife appear above the staircase, while a central cartouche features the bull of Pope Clement XI. Ledges that sit above crosses in shallow niches may symbolise Christ’s crown of thorns.
fc8fe75f-aa42-5aa6-8958-3321f68494d9.location: Pilgrimage Church of the Elevation of the Holy Cross, Jaroměřice u Jevíčka
fc8fe75f-aa42-5aa6-8958-3321f68494d9.artist: František Benedikt Klíčník? (1677 Ivanovice na Hané – 1755 Brno)

fc9843fd-105c-5026-84d3-61960e070c6c.name: Holy Relatives
fc9843fd-105c-5026-84d3-61960e070c6c.description: The *modello* for this side-altar painting is preserved in the collections of the Moravian Gallery in Brno, while a preparatory sketch is in the collection of the Ukrainian Academy of Science, Lviv. The central figure is St. Anne, accompanied by her three daughters with husbands and children including John the Baptist, Thaddeus Jude, Apostle James, and the Virgin Mary, mother of Jesus.

fcb82c11-f675-5384-8e4d-b3ba97dcb563.name: *The Revelation of St. Thomas*
fcb82c11-f675-5384-8e4d-b3ba97dcb563.description: The painting, depicting the revelation of the Apostle Thomas who doubted Christ’s resurrection is enhanced by the sculpted component of St. Augustine with a burning heart, which becomes almost part of the miraculous scene. The figure of St. Matthew is a crypto-portrait of Abbot M. Pertscher, under whom the monastery was completed and furnished. He was active during the Catholic Enlightenment and was among a small group of clergymen closely linked with the court of Maria Theresa.
fcb82c11-f675-5384-8e4d-b3ba97dcb563.location: Augustinian Monastery, Hermits of St. Thomas the Apostle
fcb82c11-f675-5384-8e4d-b3ba97dcb563.artist: Josef Winterhalder Sr. (1702 Vöhrenbach – 1769 Vienna), Franz Anton Maulbertsch (1724 Langenargen am Bodensee – 1796 Vienna), Jakub Scherz (active in the third quarter of the 18th century, Brno)

fcc7b9d9-0238-5ac6-acff-da0ef5f94db3.name: High altar
fcc7b9d9-0238-5ac6-acff-da0ef5f94db3.description: The austere Classicist high altar, flanked by double columns, was executed by Pflauder according to the design of Hagenauer and Nesselthaler. In contrast, Schöpf’s masterfully executed altarpiece depicting The Assumption of Mary with its Baroque contrasts of light and shade and wealth of figures radiates calm in respect of both composition and expressive content.
fcc7b9d9-0238-5ac6-acff-da0ef5f94db3.artist: Wolfgang Hagenauer (1726–1801); Peter Pflauder (1733–1811); Joseph Schöpf (1745–1822), Andreas Nesselthaler (1748–1821)

ff2f7e9c-b837-54ae-88c0-9b70a0b56098.name: Monastic wings
ff2f7e9c-b837-54ae-88c0-9b70a0b56098.description: The newly renovated large corridors of these wings portray the eloquence of the great baroque monastic spaces, not due to the excessive ornamentations, but rather due to its size, its infinite passages and the repetitive and monotonous spans of the cells with its partition walls.

ff582151-3b73-57fb-86ef-7b3ab9f3c119.name: St. Joachim
ff582151-3b73-57fb-86ef-7b3ab9f3c119.description: This larger-than-life statue which is made still more impressive by emotional gesture and facial expression, is further enhanced by a spiral movement of the body with the lower part emphasised. St. Joachim, father of the Virgin Mary, holds in his right hand a dove brought as a sacrifice to the temple in Jerusalem. Sketches for the statues of Archangel Michael, St. Andrew and St. Joachim have been preserved in the collections of the Moravian Gallery in Brno; only slight modifications were made in the final execution.
